l-m-h3-b0c33-01.title: Raise and then lower by di same percentage: e go back to di original?
l-m-h3-b0c33-01.goal: Check whether di claim say to raise and then lower value by di same percentage return am to di original value dey always true, and find one case wey e no true (a counterexample) and explain am.
l-m-h3-b0c33-01.material: Claim: If you raise value by p% and then lower am by p% again, e dey always return to di original value. Find one case wey show say dis claim wrong.
l-m-h3-b0c33-01.s.s1.r.a: To raise and lower by di same amount dey carry you back. E no be percentage, so e no be counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0c33-01.s.s1.r.c: Di change na 0%, so e remain di same. Dis example fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c33-01.s.s1.r.d: 0 dey stay 0 no matter wetin percent you change am by, so dis example fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c33-01.s.s1.explain: To raise 100 by 50% give 150, and to lower 150 by 50% give 75. When you dey lower, di base change to 150, so e no return to di original value.
l-m-h3-b0c33-01.s.s2.model.0: To raise 100 by 50% give 150, and to lower 150 by 50% give 75, so e no return to di original value, 100.
l-m-h3-b0c33-01.s.s2.model.1: When you dey lower, di value after di raise, 150, na di base, so to lower by 50% give 75, no be 100.

l-m-h3-b0c33-02.title: Higher interest rate dey always mean more interest?
l-m-h3-b0c33-02.goal: Check whether di claim say di deposit wey get higher annual interest rate pay more interest dey always true, and find one case wey e no true (a counterexample) and explain am.
l-m-h3-b0c33-02.material: Claim: When dem deposit money for di same period, di deposit wey get higher annual interest rate dey always pay more interest. Di principals fit differ (simple interest, 1 year). Find di pair wey break di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c33-02.s.s1.prompt: Choose di pair of deposits wey go against di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c33-02.s.s1.o.a: 5% per year on 100×10,000 won vs 3% per year on 100×10,000 won
l-m-h3-b0c33-02.s.s1.r.a: Di interest na 5×10,000 won and 3×10,000 won, so di higher rate give more. E fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c33-02.s.s1.o.b: 6% per year on 50×10,000 won vs 1% per year on 50×10,000 won
l-m-h3-b0c33-02.s.s1.r.b: Di interest na 3×10,000 won and 0.5×10,000 won, so di higher rate give more. E fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c33-02.s.s1.o.c: 5% per year on 100×10,000 won vs 3% per year on 300×10,000 won
l-m-h3-b0c33-02.s.s1.o.d: 4% per year on 200×10,000 won vs 2% per year on 200×10,000 won
l-m-h3-b0c33-02.s.s1.r.d: Di interest na 8×10,000 won and 4×10,000 won, so di higher rate give more. E fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c33-02.s.s1.explain: 5% on 100×10,000 won na 5×10,000 won, and 3% on 300×10,000 won na 9×10,000 won. Interest na principal × rate, so you must look di principal too.
l-m-h3-b0c33-02.s.s2.model.0: 3% on 300×10,000 won give 9×10,000 won for interest, and 5% on 100×10,000 won give 5×10,000 won, so di lower rate give more interest.
l-m-h3-b0c33-02.s.s2.model.1: Interest na principal × rate, so if di principal big 3 times, di interest fit big pass even with lower rate.

l-m-h3-b0c33-03.title: If you raise di price, total revenue dey only go down?
l-m-h3-b0c33-03.goal: Check whether di claim say if you raise di price and sales fall, total revenue go decrease too dey always true, and find one case wey e no true (a counterexample) and explain am.
l-m-h3-b0c33-03.material: Claim: If you raise di price and sales fall, total revenue (price × quantity sold) must fall too. For first, dem sell 100 items for 1,000 won. Find one case wey break di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c33-03.s.s1.r.a: Total revenue fall to 75,000 won. Dis example fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c33-03.s.s1.r.b: Total revenue fall to 84,000 won. Dis example fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c33-03.s.s1.r.c: Total revenue fall to 88,000 won. Dis example fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c33-03.s.s1.explain: 1,200×90=108,000 won, wey big pass di original 100,000 won. Di price fit rise by bigger proportion than di quantity wey dem sell go fall.
l-m-h3-b0c33-03.s.s2.model.0: 1,200 won×90=108,000 won, wey big pass di original 100,000 won, so total revenue no must fall.
l-m-h3-b0c33-03.s.s2.model.1: Di price rise 20% but di quantity wey dem sell fall only 10%, so total revenue actually rise and di claim break.

l-m-h3-b0c33-04.title: If you sell below di list price, e always mean loss?
l-m-h3-b0c33-04.topic: Profit, loss, and list price (di price wey dem write)
l-m-h3-b0c33-04.goal: Check whether di claim say to sell below di list price mean loss na always true, and find and explain one case wey e no be so (one counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c33-04.material: Claim: If you sell below di list price, you always go lose. Loss dey happen wen di selling price low pass di cost price. Find one case wey go against di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c33-04.s.s1.r.b: Di selling price low pass di cost, so na loss. Dis example fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c33-04.s.s1.r.c: Di selling price low pass di cost, so na loss. Dis example fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c33-04.s.s1.r.d: Di selling price low pass di cost, so na loss. Dis example fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c33-04.s.s1.explain: Di selling price of 9,000 won big pass di cost of 8,000 won, so na profit of 1,000 won. Profit or loss dey compare di cost and di selling price, no be di list price.
l-m-h3-b0c33-04.s.s2.model.0: Di selling price of 9,000 won big pass di cost of 8,000 won, so even if you sell below di list price e still give profit of 1,000 won, and di claim wrong.
l-m-h3-b0c33-04.s.s2.model.1: Profit or loss dey compare di cost and di selling price, so even if di price dey below di list price, na profit if e dey above di cost.

l-m-h3-b0c34-01.title: If item get higher tax rate, you always pay more tax?
l-m-h3-b0c34-01.goal: Check whether di claim say item wey get higher tax rate get more tax na always true, and find and explain one case wey e no hold (one counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c34-01.material: Claim: Between two items, di one wey get higher tax rate always get more tax. Di tax na price × tax rate. Find di pair wey break di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c34-01.s.s1.r.a: Di taxes na 1,500 won and 4,500 won, so di one wey get higher rate pay more.
l-m-h3-b0c34-01.s.s1.r.b: Di taxes na 5,000 won and 10,000 won, so di one wey get higher rate pay more.
l-m-h3-b0c34-01.s.s1.r.c: Di taxes na 1,000 won and 8,000 won, so di one wey get higher rate pay more.
l-m-h3-b0c34-01.s.s1.explain: 100,000×10%=10,000 won and 20,000×20%=4,000 won. Even with higher rate, di tax fit small if di price low.
l-m-h3-b0c34-01.s.s2.model.0: 10% of 100,000 won na 10,000 won and 20% of 20,000 won na 4,000 won, so di item wey get higher rate get less tax.
l-m-h3-b0c34-01.s.s2.model.1: Di tax na price × tax rate, so if di prices different well well, di tax fit small even with higher rate.

l-m-h3-b0c34-02.title: If di expected values na di same, di two choices na di same?
l-m-h3-b0c34-02.goal: Check whether di claim say two choices wey get di same expected value na di same na always true, and find and explain one case wey e no hold (one counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c34-02.material: Claim: Two choices wey get di same expected value get di same possible outcomes, so no difference dey which one you pick. (For one coin and one die, heads/tails and even/odd each get probability 1/2.) Find di pair wey break di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c34-02.s.s1.r.a: Di outcomes of di two choices na di same. Dis one na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c34-02.s.s1.o.b: Heads 200 won, tails 0 won versus heads 0 won, tails 200 won
l-m-h3-b0c34-02.s.s1.r.b: Di kinds of outcomes and dia probabilities na di same. Dis one na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c34-02.s.s1.o.c: Heads or tails both 100 won versus even or odd both 100 won
l-m-h3-b0c34-02.s.s1.r.c: Both choices give sure 100 won. Dis one na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c34-02.s.s1.o.d: Sure 100 won versus heads 200 won, tails 0 won
l-m-h3-b0c34-02.s.s1.explain: Both get expected value of 100 won, but di first one na always exactly 100 won while di second one na 200 won or 0 won, so di outcomes different.
l-m-h3-b0c34-02.s.s2.model.0: Sure 100 won and one coin toss both get expected value of 100 won, but di second one fit give 0 won, so di outcomes different.
l-m-h3-b0c34-02.s.s2.model.1: Di expected value na only average, so if di outcomes wey you fit get spread out different way, di two choices no be di same.

l-m-h3-b0c34-03.title: Di one wey get bigger discount rate always cheap pass?
l-m-h3-b0c34-03.goal: Check whether di claim say product wey get bigger discount rate get lower final price na always true, and find and explain one case wey e no hold (one counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c34-03.material: Claim: Between two products, di one wey get bigger discount rate also get lower final price. Di list prices fit different. Find di pair wey break di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c34-03.s.s1.o.a: List price 100,000 won with 30% off versus list price 40,000 won with 10% off
l-m-h3-b0c34-03.s.s1.o.b: List price 80,000 won with 25% off versus list price 80,000 won with 5% off
l-m-h3-b0c34-03.s.s1.r.b: Di final prices na 60,000 won and 76,000 won, so di one wey get bigger discount rate cheap pass.
l-m-h3-b0c34-03.s.s1.o.c: List price 50,000 won with 20% off versus list price 50,000 won with 10% off
l-m-h3-b0c34-03.s.s1.r.c: Di final prices na 40,000 won and 45,000 won, so di one wey get bigger discount rate cheap pass.
l-m-h3-b0c34-03.s.s1.o.d: List price 30,000 won with 15% off versus list price 30,000 won with 0% off
l-m-h3-b0c34-03.s.s1.r.d: Di final prices na 25,500 won and 30,000 won, so di one wey get bigger discount rate cheap pass.
l-m-h3-b0c34-03.s.s1.explain: 30% discount on 100,000 won give 70,000 won, and 10% discount on 40,000 won give 36,000 won. You must look di list price too.
l-m-h3-b0c34-03.s.s2.model.0: Di price after 30% discount on list price of 100,000 won na 70,000 won, and 10% discount on list price of 40,000 won give 36,000 won, so di one wey get bigger discount rate cost more.
l-m-h3-b0c34-03.s.s2.model.1: Di final price na di list price times di share wey remain, so if di list prices different well well, bigger discount rate fit still cost more.

l-m-h3-b0c34-04.title: Compound interest always give more interest than simple interest?
l-m-h3-b0c34-04.goal: Check whether di claim say compound interest big pass simple interest na always true, and find and explain one case wey e no hold (one counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c34-04.material: Claim: If di principal and di yearly rate (5%) na di same, compound interest always big pass simple interest. After you deposit 100 × 10,000 won, check whether e depend on how many years later you look.
l-m-h3-b0c34-04.s.s1.prompt: Choose di time wey go against di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c34-04.s.s1.r.b: Simple interest na 10 × 10,000 won and compound na 10.25 × 10,000 won, so compound big pass.
l-m-h3-b0c34-04.s.s1.r.c: Simple interest na 15 × 10,000 won and compound na about 15.76 × 10,000 won, so compound big pass.
l-m-h3-b0c34-04.s.s1.r.d: Simple interest na 50 × 10,000 won and compound na about 62.9 × 10,000 won, so compound big pass.
l-m-h3-b0c34-04.s.s1.explain: After 1 year, simple and compound interest both na 5 × 10,000 won, so dem equal and di claim say compound 'big pass' fail. Di difference start from year 2.
l-m-h3-b0c34-04.s.s2.model.0: After 1 year, di simple and compound interest both na 5 × 10,000 won and equal, so di claim say compound big pass fail.
l-m-h3-b0c34-04.s.s2.model.1: Interest on interest for compound interest start for di second year, so for di first year e na di same as simple interest, and dat one na di counterexample.

l-m-h3-b0c35-01.title: If di price go up, total sales go up too?
l-m-h3-b0c35-01.goal: Check whether di claim "if di price go up, total sales go up too" na always true, and find and explain one case wey e no be so (one counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c35-01.material: Claim: Wen product price go up, total sales (price × quantity wey dem sell) always go up. Here are records from four shops where di quantity wey dem sell change after di price go up.
l-m-h3-b0c35-01.s.s1.prompt: Which shop show say di claim wrong?
l-m-h3-b0c35-01.s.s1.r.a: Sales rise from 10,000 to 11,000 won, so dis one na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c35-01.s.s1.r.c: Sales rise from 100,000 to 104,500 won, so dis one na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c35-01.s.s1.r.d: Sales rise from 8,000 to 9,000 won, so dis one na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c35-01.s.s1.explain: 500×200=100,000 won, but 600×150=90,000 won, so e drop. If di quantity wey dem sell fall by more, sales go down.
l-m-h3-b0c35-01.s.s2.model.0: Di price go up, but sales drop from 100,000 won to 90,000 won, so dis shop na di counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0c35-01.s.s2.model.1: Di quantity wey dem sell fall by 25%, wey pass di 20% price increase, so sales fall and di claim break.

l-m-h3-b0c35-09.title: If di expected value high pass, di loss go small too?
l-m-h3-b0c35-09.goal: Check whether di claim "di one wey get higher expected value also get lower chance of loss" na always true, and find and explain one case wey e no be so (one counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c35-09.material: Claim: Between two products, di one wey get higher expected value (average profit) also get lower probability of loss. For each pair, dem give di expected values (for 10,000 won) and loss probabilities of A and B.
l-m-h3-b0c35-09.s.s1.prompt: Which pair show say di claim wrong?
l-m-h3-b0c35-09.s.s1.r.a: A get higher expected value and lower loss probability, so e fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c35-09.s.s1.r.c: B dey ahead for both, so dis one na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c35-09.s.s1.r.d: A dey ahead for both, so dis one na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c35-09.s.s1.explain: A get higher expected value, but im loss probability na 40% too, wey big pass B own 5%. Even with high average, di risk fit big.
l-m-h3-b0c35-09.s.s2.model.0: A get higher expected value of 50, but im loss probability of 40% big pass B own 5%, so na counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0c35-09.s.s2.model.1: Di expected value na only average, so like A, even with high average di loss probability fit reach 40%.

l-m-h3-b0c35-17.title: If di total price cheap, di price for each item cheap too?
l-m-h3-b0c35-17.goal: Check whether di claim 'di pack wey get cheaper total price get cheaper price for each item too' dey always true, then find and explain one case wey e no true (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c35-17.material: Claim: Between two packs, di one wey get cheaper total price get cheaper price for each item too. Dem write each pair of packs as (number of items, total price).
l-m-h3-b0c35-17.s.s1.r.a: Di cheaper pack na 500 won for each item and di other one na 600 won, so e fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c35-17.s.s1.r.c: Di cheaper pack na 500 won for each item and di other one na 600 won, so e fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c35-17.s.s1.r.d: Di cheaper pack cost 500 won for each item against 600 won, so e cheaper for each item and e fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c35-17.s.s1.explain: Di 6-item pack wey cost 4,800 won get cheaper total price, but e cost 800 won for each item, and di 10-item pack wey cost 7,000 won cost 700 won for each item.
l-m-h3-b0c35-17.s.s2.model.0: 4,800 won cheap pass 7,000 won, but e na 800 won for each item, and 7,000÷10=700 won, so na counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0c35-17.s.s2.model.1: When di number of items no be di same, total price alone no go tell you di price for each item, so di 6-item pack wey cost 4,800 won cost more for each item.

l-m-h3-b0c35-25.title: If di growth rate big pass, di amount of increase big pass too?
l-m-h3-b0c35-25.topic: Growth rate and amount of increase
l-m-h3-b0c35-25.goal: Check whether di claim 'di one wey get bigger growth rate get bigger amount of increase too' dey always true, then find and explain one case wey e no true (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c35-25.material: Claim: Between two shops, di one wey get bigger sales growth rate get bigger increase in amount too. Each pair give A and B sales from last month to dis month (for units of 10,000 won).
l-m-h3-b0c35-25.s.s1.r.a: A: 20% and 10 ×10,000 won; B: 10% and 8 ×10,000 won. Dis one fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c35-25.s.s1.r.b: A: 50% and 100 ×10,000 won; B: 20% and 80 ×10,000 won. Dis one fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c35-25.s.s1.r.c: A: 50% and 5 ×10,000 won; B: 10% and 4 ×10,000 won. Dis one fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c35-25.s.s1.explain: A grow 30%, wey be 30 ×10,000 won, while B grow 20% but by 200 ×10,000 won. Growth rate and amount of increase different.
l-m-h3-b0c35-25.s.s2.model.0: A rise 30% for increase of 30 ×10,000 won, while B rise 20% for increase of 200 ×10,000 won; B increase in amount big pass, so na counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0c35-25.s.s2.model.1: When di starting value big, even low growth rate fit become big amount, so B 20% grow pass A 30%.

l-m-h3-b0c36-01.title: The sum of two vectors wey get magnitudes 3 and 4
l-m-h3-b0c36-01.goal: Check whether the claim 'the sum of two vectors wey get magnitudes 3 and 4 always get magnitude 5' dey true always, then find and explain one case wey e no true (a counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c36-01.material: Claim: If you add vector of magnitude 3 and vector of magnitude 4, the sum vector go always get magnitude 5. Find one addition wey show say this claim wrong.
l-m-h3-b0c36-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose the sum of vectors wey go against the claim (a counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c36-01.s.s1.r.a: The magnitude of the sum (−3,4) na 5, so e na example wey fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c36-01.s.s1.r.c: The magnitude of the sum (4,3) na 5, so e na example wey fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c36-01.s.s1.r.d: The magnitude of the sum (3,4) na 5, so e na example wey fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c36-01.s.s1.explain: (3,0)+(4,0)=(7,0), and the magnitude na 7. When the directions same, the magnitudes dey add up, so e no be 5.
l-m-h3-b0c36-01.s.s2.model.0: (3,0) and (4,0) get magnitudes 3 and 4, but the sum (7,0) get magnitude 7, no be 5, so e na counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0c36-01.s.s2.model.1: When the directions same, the magnitudes just dey add, so the magnitude of the sum na 7 and the claim break.

l-m-h3-b0c36-02.title: P(A|B) and P(B|A) dey always equal?
l-m-h3-b0c36-02.goal: Check whether the claim 'the two conditional probabilities P(A|B) and P(B|A) always equal' dey true always, then find and explain one case wey e no true (a counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c36-02.material: We survey 100 students and count how many fit events A and B. Claim: P(A|B) and P(B|A) always equal. Find survey results wey break this claim.
l-m-h3-b0c36-02.s.s1.prompt: Choose the survey result wey go against the claim (a counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c36-02.s.s1.o.a: A 20 students, B 20 students, both 8 students
l-m-h3-b0c36-02.s.s1.r.a: Both probabilities na 8/20, the same. E na example wey fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c36-02.s.s1.o.b: A 30 students, B 10 students, both 10 students
l-m-h3-b0c36-02.s.s1.o.c: A 12 students, B 12 students, both 3 students
l-m-h3-b0c36-02.s.s1.r.c: Both probabilities na 3/12, the same. E na example wey fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c36-02.s.s1.o.d: A 40 students, B 40 students, both 15 students
l-m-h3-b0c36-02.s.s1.r.d: Both probabilities na 15/40, the same. E na example wey fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c36-02.s.s1.explain: P(A|B)=10/10=1 and P(B|A)=10/30=1/3, so dem differ. When the events wey form the denominator get different number of people, the values go differ too.
l-m-h3-b0c36-02.s.s2.model.0: P(A|B) na 10/10=1 but P(B|A) na 10/30, so dem different and e na counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0c36-02.s.s2.model.1: The denominators differ—10 people for B and 30 for A—so the two probabilities no equal.

l-m-h3-b0c36-03.title: Point wey the derivative na 0, e always be the minimum?
l-m-h3-b0c36-03.goal: Check whether the claim 'point wey the derivative na 0 always be the minimum' dey true always, then find and explain one case wey e no true (a counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c36-03.material: Claim: For function f, point wey the derivative f'(x) na 0 always be the point wey f get im smallest value. Find one function and one point wey break this claim.
l-m-h3-b0c36-03.s.s1.prompt: Choose the function and point wey go against the claim (a counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c36-03.s.s1.r.a: The minimum na 1 for x=2. E na example wey fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c36-03.s.s1.r.b: f dey for im minimum for x=0. E na example wey fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c36-03.s.s1.r.d: The minimum na 3 for x=0. E na example wey fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c36-03.s.s1.explain: The derivative 3x² of x³ na 0 for x=0, but smaller values dey for x<0, so e no be the minimum.
l-m-h3-b0c36-03.s.s2.model.0: f'(0)=0, but x³ na −1 for x=−1, wey small pass 0, so x=0 no be the minimum and e na counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0c36-03.s.s2.model.1: x³ dey increase all the time, so even though point wey get slope 0 dey, e no get minimum, and the claim break.

l-m-h3-b0c36-04.goal: Check whether the claim 'classification model wey get 95% accuracy always dey useful' dey true always, then find and explain one case wey e no true (a counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c36-04.material: Claim: Disease classification model wey get 95% accuracy dey always useful. For four models wey all get 95% accuracy for 1000 tests, find the one wey break this claim.
l-m-h3-b0c36-04.s.s1.prompt: Choose the model wey no fit work even though im accuracy na 95%.
l-m-h3-b0c36-04.s.s1.o.a: 500 patients, 500 healthy people, 475 correct for each
l-m-h3-b0c36-04.s.s1.r.a: E find 95% of the patients too, so e dey useful. Na example wey match the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c36-04.s.s1.o.b: 50 patients, 950 healthy people, e no identify even one patient correct
l-m-h3-b0c36-04.s.s1.o.c: 100 patients, 900 healthy people, 95% correct for each
l-m-h3-b0c36-04.s.s1.r.c: E find 95% of the patients, so e dey useful. Na example wey match the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c36-04.s.s1.r.d: E find 95% of the patients, so e dey useful. Na example wey match the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c36-04.s.s1.o.d: 200 patients, 800 healthy people, 95% correct for each
l-m-h3-b0c36-04.s.s1.explain: Even if e just talk 'healthy' for everybody, 950 go correct and accuracy go be 95%, but e no find even one patient.
l-m-h3-b0c36-04.s.s2.model.0: Even if e miss all the 50 patients, e still get the 950 healthy cases correct, so accuracy na 95%, and na so e take be counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0c36-04.s.s2.model.1: Most people healthy, so if you answer healthy for everybody e go still give 95%, and e mean say accuracy alone no fit show how useful the model be.

l-m-h3-b0c37-01.title: Di square of matrix wey all im entries no be 0
l-m-h3-b0c37-01.goal: Examine whether di claim say di square of matrix wey no entry equal 0 also no get entry wey equal 0 dey always true, then find and explain one case wey e no true (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c37-01.material: Claim: If you square 2×2 matrix A wey all im entries no be 0, A² no get entries wey equal 0 either. Find matrix wey break dis claim.
l-m-h3-b0c37-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose di matrix A wey go against di claim (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c37-01.s.s1.r.a: A²=(2 2; 2 2) no get entries wey equal 0. Na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c37-01.s.s1.r.b: A²=(5 4; 4 5) no get entries wey equal 0. Na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c37-01.s.s1.r.c: A²=(−1 8; −4 7) no get entries wey equal 0. Na example wey fit.
l-m-h3-b0c37-01.s.s1.explain: If A=(1 −1; 1 −1), then A² na di zero matrix wey every entry na 0. Even if di entries no be 0, di square fit be 0.
l-m-h3-b0c37-01.s.s2.model.0: If you calculate A², every entry become 0, but none of di entries of A na 0, so na counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0c37-01.s.s2.model.1: Terms dey cancel each other, like (1)(1)+(−1)(1)=0, so A² na di zero matrix and di claim break.

l-m-h3-b0c37-02.title: We fit always just add to get di probability of union of events?
l-m-h3-b0c37-02.goal: Examine whether di claim say di probability of di union of two events na P(A)+P(B) dey always true, then find and explain one case wey e no true (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c37-02.material: Draw one card from cards wey dem number 1 to 10. Claim: P(A∪B)=P(A)+P(B) hold for any two events A and B. Find two events wey break dis claim.
l-m-h3-b0c37-02.s.s1.prompt: Choose di two events wey di claim no hold for.
l-m-h3-b0c37-02.s.s1.r.a: No card overlap, so 10/10=5/10+5/10. E hold.
l-m-h3-b0c37-02.s.s1.o.b: A: 5 or less, B: 8 or more
l-m-h3-b0c37-02.s.s1.r.b: No card overlap, so 8/10=5/10+3/10. E hold.
l-m-h3-b0c37-02.s.s1.r.d: No card overlap, so 6/10=4/10+2/10. E hold.
l-m-h3-b0c37-02.s.s1.explain: Dem count di 6, wey be even and multiple of 3, two times. When overlap dey, di sum go big pass di real value.
l-m-h3-b0c37-02.s.s2.model.0: 6 na even and multiple of 3, so dem add am two times; so e na 7/10, no be 5/10+3/10=8/10, and na counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0c37-02.s.s2.model.1: Di two events overlap, so di probability of di union small pass P(A)+P(B), and di claim break.

l-m-h3-b0c37-03.title: If di MSE na di same, di MAE na di same too?
l-m-h3-b0c37-03.goal: Examine whether di claim say if two models get di same MSE dem get di same MAE too dey always true, then find and explain one case wey e no true (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c37-03.material: Claim: Two models wey get di same mean of squared errors (MSE) get di same mean of absolute errors (MAE) too. Among four pairs of error records of two models, find di one wey break di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c37-03.s.s1.prompt: Choose di pair wey go against di claim (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c37-03.s.s1.r.a: Both MSE and MAE na di same, 1. Na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c37-03.s.s1.r.b: MSE 4 and MAE 2, both na di same. Na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c37-03.s.s1.r.c: MSE 9/4 and MAE 3/4, both na di same. Na example wey fit.
l-m-h3-b0c37-03.s.s1.explain: Di MSE of both sides na 4, but di MAE na 2 and 1. When di errors gather for one place, di MAE dey different even if di MSE na di same.
l-m-h3-b0c37-03.s.s2.model.0: (2,2,2,2) get MSE 4 and MAE 2, and (0,0,0,4) get MSE 4 and MAE 1, so di MAE different even though di MSE na di same, and na counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0c37-03.s.s2.model.1: When di errors gather for one place, di mean of absolute values dey become smaller even if di MSE na di same because of squaring, so di claim break.

l-m-h3-b0c37-04.title: If recall high, precision high too?
l-m-h3-b0c37-04.goal: Examine whether di claim say if recall na 90% or more then precision na 90% or more too dey always true, then find and explain one case wey e no true (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c37-04.material: Claim: Model wey get recall of 90% or more get precision of 90% or more too. Di models below all get recall of 90% or more. (TP = sick people wey dem find, FN = sick people wey dem miss, FP = healthy people wey dem count as sick) Find di model wey break di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c37-04.s.s1.prompt: Choose di model wey im precision dey below 90%.
l-m-h3-b0c37-04.s.s1.r.a: Recall 0.9 and precision 0.9, so na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c37-04.s.s1.r.b: Recall 0.9 and precision 0.9, so na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c37-04.s.s1.r.c: Recall 0.9 and precision 0.9, so na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c37-04.s.s1.explain: If you call everybody sick, recall na 100% but precision na 50/200=25%. Recall alone no fit tell you about false alarms.
l-m-h3-b0c37-04.s.s2.model.0: With TP 50 and FP 150, precision na 50/200=25% while recall na 100%, so na counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0c37-04.s.s2.model.1: If you call almost everybody positive so that you no go miss any sick person, recall go high but plenty false alarms go dey, so precision go low.

l-m-h3-b0c38-01.title: If the dot product na 0, e mean say one vector na the zero vector?
l-m-h3-b0c38-01.goal: Check whether the claim say if the dot product of two vectors na 0, one of dem na the zero vector, always true, and find and explain one case where e no true (a counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c38-01.material: Claim: if the dot product of two vectors na 0, at least one of dem na the zero vector (0,0). Find two vectors wey show say this claim wrong.
l-m-h3-b0c38-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose the pair of vectors wey go against the claim (a counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c38-01.s.s1.r.a: The dot product na 0 and zero vector dey. Na example wey match the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c38-01.s.s1.r.c: The dot product na 3, so e no be 0. E no meet the condition.
l-m-h3-b0c38-01.s.s1.r.d: The dot product na 5, so e no be 0. E no meet the condition.
l-m-h3-b0c38-01.s.s1.explain: (1,2)·(2,-1)=2-2=0, but none of dem na the zero vector. Dot product of 0 only mean say dem dey perpendicular.
l-m-h3-b0c38-01.s.s2.model.0: (1,2)·(2,-1)=0, but none of the vectors na zero vector, so na counterexample to the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c38-01.s.s2.model.1: Dot product of 0 only mean say dem dey perpendicular, so (1,2) and (2,-1), wey no be zero vectors, na counterexample too.

l-m-h3-b0c38-09.goal: Examine whether the claim say the result of matrix product dey the same when dem swap the order dey always true, and find and explain one case wey e no true (a counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c38-09.material: Claim: for two 2×2 matrices A and B, AB=BA always hold. Find one pair of matrices wey show say this claim wrong. (; mean new line)
l-m-h3-b0c38-09.s.s1.prompt: Choose one pair of matrices wey AB≠BA.
l-m-h3-b0c38-09.s.s1.r.a: For diagonal matrices, AB=BA. This na example wey match the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c38-09.s.s1.r.b: For the same matrix, AB=BA. This na example wey match the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c38-09.s.s1.r.d: With the identity matrix, the order of multiplying no matter.
l-m-h3-b0c38-09.s.s1.explain: AB=[2 1; 1 1] and BA=[1 1; 1 2], wey different from each other.
l-m-h3-b0c38-09.s.s2.model.0: AB=[2 1; 1 1] and BA=[1 1; 1 2], so the two results different and this na counterexample to the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c38-09.s.s2.model.1: For matrix product, the rows and columns wey dem use for the calculation dey change with the order, so for this pair AB and BA come out different.

l-m-h3-b0c38-14.title: If the correlation high, na the cause?
l-m-h3-b0c38-14.goal: Examine whether the claim say high correlation mean say one na the cause of the other dey always true, and find and explain one case wey e no true (a counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c38-14.material: Claim: if the correlation coefficient of two variables near 1, one na the cause of the other. Find one situation wey show say this claim wrong.
l-m-h3-b0c38-14.s.s1.prompt: Choose one situation wey contradict the claim (a counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c38-14.s.s1.o.a: The harder dem push the pedals, the faster the bicycle go
l-m-h3-b0c38-14.s.s1.r.a: The pedals na the cause of the speed. This na example wey match the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c38-14.s.s1.o.b: When the temperature rise, ice cream and fan sales increase together
l-m-h3-b0c38-14.s.s1.o.c: When dem turn on the switch, the light come on
l-m-h3-b0c38-14.s.s1.r.c: The switch na the cause. This na example wey match the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c38-14.s.s1.o.d: When dem give more water, the plant for the pot grow more
l-m-h3-b0c38-14.s.s1.r.d: The water dey act as the cause. This na example wey match the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c38-14.s.s1.explain: The temperature just affect both sales and dem no be cause of each other. Even if the correlation high, e fit no be causation.
l-m-h3-b0c38-14.s.s2.model.0: The temperature just raise both sales together, and ice cream no be the cause of fan sales, so this na counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0c38-14.s.s2.model.1: Even if two values dey move together, e fit be because of 3rd factor, so you no fit say high correlation mean cause.

l-m-h3-b0c38-21.s.s1.r.b: Di slope na 0 and e na di actual minimum. Dis one na example wey fit di claim.

l-m-h3-b0c38-27.s.s1.o.a: Model wey get 50% defective and 99% accuracy
l-m-h3-b0c38-27.s.s1.r.a: If half na defective, for 99% e also find at least 98% of the defects.

l-m-h3-b0c41-01.s.s2.model.1: Dem dey find area by to multiply di width and di height, so di conversion ratio dey square too, and dat one make am 10000cm².

l-m-h3-b0c41-02.goal: Examine whether di claim "di side wey get lower defect rate get fewer defective items too" dey always true, then find and explain one case wey e no true (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c41-02.material: Claim: The factory wey get lower defect rate also get fewer defective items. Find the one among the production records of the two factories wey break this claim.
l-m-h3-b0c41-02.s.s1.prompt: Choose the record wey go against the claim (a counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c41-02.s.s1.o.a: Factory A: 10 of 500, Factory B: 25 of 500
l-m-h3-b0c41-02.s.s1.r.a: A get lower rate and smaller count. Na example wey match the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c41-02.s.s1.o.b: Factory A: 1 of 100, Factory B: 8 of 400
l-m-h3-b0c41-02.s.s1.r.b: A na 1% and B na 2%, and A also get smaller count.
l-m-h3-b0c41-02.s.s1.o.c: Factory A: 40 of 2000, Factory B: 10 of 200
l-m-h3-b0c41-02.s.s1.o.d: Factory A: 30 of 1000, Factory B: 40 of 1000
l-m-h3-b0c41-02.s.s1.r.d: A na 3% and B na 4%, and A also get smaller count.
l-m-h3-b0c41-02.s.s1.explain: A na 40÷2000=2% and B na 10÷200=5%. A get lower defect rate, but e get more defective items, 40.
l-m-h3-b0c41-02.s.s2.model.0: A defect rate na 2%, lower than B own 5%, but im 40 defective items pass B own 10, so na counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0c41-02.s.s2.model.1: The production amounts differ by 10 times, so even with lower defect rate, the number of defective items fit big pass.

l-m-h3-b0c41-03.title: If the error small, the measurement more accurate?
l-m-h3-b0c41-03.goal: Examine whether the claim "measurement wey get smaller error more accurate" always true, and find and explain one case where e no true (a counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c41-03.material: Claim: Measurement wey get smaller wrong amount (error) always more accurate. Compare two measurements and find the case where this claim break.
l-m-h3-b0c41-03.s.s1.prompt: Choose the pair of measurements wey show say the claim wrong.
l-m-h3-b0c41-03.s.s1.o.a: Measured 50m, off by 3cm; measured 20cm, off by 1cm
l-m-h3-b0c41-03.s.s1.o.b: Measured 30cm, off by 3mm; measured 30cm, off by 1mm
l-m-h3-b0c41-03.s.s1.r.b: Dem measure the same length, so the one wey get smaller error more accurate.
l-m-h3-b0c41-03.s.s1.r.c: Dem measure the same length, so the one wey get smaller error more accurate.
l-m-h3-b0c41-03.s.s1.o.c: Measured 10m, off by 2cm; measured 10m, off by 5cm
l-m-h3-b0c41-03.s.s1.o.d: Measured 1m, off by 1cm; measured 2m, off by 4cm
l-m-h3-b0c41-03.s.s1.r.d: The first one smaller for both error and ratio (1%, 2%). E fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c41-03.s.s1.explain: Dem dey judge accuracy by the ratio of the error to the size wey dem measure. 3cm÷50m na 0.06%, and 1cm÷20cm na 5%.
l-m-h3-b0c41-03.s.s2.model.0: 3cm÷5000cm na 0.06% and 1cm÷20cm na 5%, so the first one, wey get larger error, more accurate, wey make am counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0c41-03.s.s2.model.1: You no suppose look only the size of the error, but the ratio to the length wey dem measure, so this pair break the claim.

l-m-h3-b0c42-01.title: For systematic sampling, dem fit pick any two students together?
l-m-h3-b0c42-01.goal: Examine whether di claim 'for systematic sampling, dem fit pick any two students together' dey always true, then find and explain one case wey e no true (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c42-01.material: Systematically sample 10 students from students wey dem number 1 to 100. Randomly choose starting number from 1 to 10 and keep dey add 10. Claim: Any two students fit dey inside di same sample together. Find two students wey show say dis claim wrong.

l-m-h3-b0c42-01.s.s1.r.c: Di difference na 40, so if di starting number na 7, dem go pick dem together.
l-m-h3-b0c42-01.s.s1.r.d: Di difference na 90, so if di starting number na 2, dem go pick dem together.
l-m-h3-b0c42-01.s.s1.explain: Numbers inside di sample dey differ by multiples of 10. No. 5 and No. 6 differ by 1, so dem no fit pick dem together.
l-m-h3-b0c42-01.s.s2.model.0: No. 5 and No. 6 differ by 1, but numbers inside di sample differ by 10, so dem no fit pick dem together, and dat one make dem counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0c42-01.s.s2.model.1: Once dem set di starting number, na only numbers wey add 10 each time dem go pick, so numbers wey follow each other no fit dey inside di same sample.

l-m-h3-b0c42-30.material: Claim: The side wey get higher overall pass rate go get higher pass rate for any department wey you compare. Department X: 48 of 80 men and 14 of 20 women pass. Department Y: 6 of 20 men and 20 of 80 women pass. Overall na 54% for men and 34% for women.

l-m-h3-b0c42-30.s.s1.o.c: Compare the overall pass rates of men and women
l-m-h3-b0c42-30.s.s1.r.c: Men 54% and women 34% na just where the claim start from, e no be counterexample.

l-m-h3-b0c42-30.s.s1.explain: For X, women's 70% high pass men's 60%. Even if men high overall, e fit be opposite for each department.

l-m-h3-b0c42-30.s.s2.model.1: Overall men high at 54%, but if you look Department X only, women high at 70%, so the claim break.

l-m-h3-b0c44-01.material: Claim: The bigger the size of sample, the better e always represent all the students for the school. Find one case wey this claim wrong, for situation where we wan know the daily reading time of all the students.

l-m-h3-b0c44-04.title: If correlation strong, e mean say one cause the other?
l-m-h3-b0c44-04.goal: Check whether the claim “If strong correlation dey, one thing cause the other” dey always true, then find and explain one case wey e no true (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c44-04.material: Claim: If two sets of data show strong correlation, one cause the other. Find one case wey strong correlation dey but neither one cause the other.
l-m-h3-b0c44-04.s.s1.o.a: How much fertilizer dem use and how tall plants for test pots grow
l-m-h3-b0c44-04.s.s1.r.a: If na experiment wey dem control the fertilizer amount directly, dem fit see am as the cause.
l-m-h3-b0c44-04.s.s1.o.b: Ice cream sales each month and number of water-play accidents
l-m-h3-b0c44-04.s.s1.o.c: How hard person press brake and how far the car travel before e stop
l-m-h3-b0c44-04.s.s1.r.c: The force of pressing brake na direct cause of the shorter stopping distance.
l-m-h3-b0c44-04.s.s1.o.d: How many hours people use heater and how room temperature rise
l-m-h3-b0c44-04.s.s1.r.d: Heater na direct cause of the room temperature rising.
l-m-h3-b0c44-04.s.s1.explain: Hot weather dey increase both. Even if the two dey rise together, one no cause the other.
l-m-h3-b0c44-04.s.s2.model.0: Hot weather dey increase ice cream sales and water play, so even if correlation strong, e no mean say one cause the other.
l-m-h3-b0c44-04.s.s2.model.1: If ice cream sales reduce, e no go reduce accidents, so correlation alone no fit show say one cause the other.

l-m-h3-b0c44-05.title: If you add one value, average go always change?
l-m-h3-b0c44-05.goal: Check whether the claim “If you add one value, average go always change” dey always true, then find and explain one case wey e no true (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c44-05.material: Claim: If you add one new value to the data 4, 6, 8, the average go always change. The original average na 6. Find one case wey this claim no correct.
l-m-h3-b0c44-05.s.s1.prompt: Choose the new value wey no agree with the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c44-05.s.s1.r.a: The new average change to 28÷4=7. This example follow the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c44-05.s.s1.r.c: The new average change to 20÷4=5. This example follow the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c44-05.s.s1.r.d: The new average change to 18÷4=4.5. This example follow the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c44-05.s.s1.explain: If the new value equal the original average 6, dividing the total 24 by 4 still give 6, so the average no change.
l-m-h3-b0c44-05.s.s2.model.0: If you add the new value 6, the total go from 18 to 24 and the count go from 3 to 4, so 24÷4=6 and the average no change.
l-m-h3-b0c44-05.s.s2.model.1: If the value wey you add equal the average, the total distance from the average no increase, so the average no change.

l-m-h3-b0c45-01.title: If we share 60 minutes equally, e go always be whole number of minutes?
l-m-h3-b0c45-01.goal: Check if the claim say one part go be whole number of minutes, no matter how you share 60 minutes equally, always true; then find and explain one case wey no true (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c45-01.material: 60 get many divisors, so e easy to share. Babylonians use base-60 system. Claim: No matter how you share 1 hour (60 minutes) equally, one part go be whole number of minutes.
l-m-h3-b0c45-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose the equal sharing wey go go against this claim (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c45-01.s.s1.o.a: Share am into 6 equal parts (10 minutes each)
l-m-h3-b0c45-01.s.s1.r.a: 10 minutes na whole number, so e be example wey fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c45-01.s.s1.o.b: Share am into 4 equal parts (15 minutes each)
l-m-h3-b0c45-01.s.s1.r.b: 15 minutes na whole number, so e be example wey fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c45-01.s.s1.o.c: Share am into 3 equal parts (20 minutes each)
l-m-h3-b0c45-01.s.s1.r.c: 20 minutes na whole number, so e be example wey fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c45-01.s.s1.explain: 60÷7 na about 8.57, wey no be whole number. 7 no be divisor of 60, so e no divide evenly into whole minutes.
l-m-h3-b0c45-01.s.s2.model.0: 60 no divide by 7, so sharing am into 7 equal parts make one part about 8.57 minutes. Na why e be counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0c45-01.s.s2.model.1: 7 no be divisor of 60, so 60÷7 no be whole number. Sharing am into 3, 4, or 6 equal parts give whole numbers, so those no be counterexamples.

l-m-h3-b0c45-02.title: Ratio of neighboring Fibonacci numbers dey always bigger than golden ratio?
l-m-h3-b0c45-02.goal: Check whether the claim say ratio of neighboring Fibonacci numbers dey always bigger than 1.618 always true, then find and explain a case wey no true (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c45-02.material: For Fibonacci numbers 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, …, bigger number ÷ smaller number for two numbers wey near each other dey close to golden ratio, about 1.618. Claim: this ratio dey always bigger than 1.618.
l-m-h3-b0c45-02.s.s1.r.a: 2 bigger than 1.618, so e be example wey fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c45-02.s.s1.r.c: 1.625 bigger than 1.618, so e be example wey fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c45-02.s.s1.r.d: 1.667 bigger than 1.618, so e be example wey fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c45-02.s.s1.explain: 8÷5=1.6 smaller than 1.618. This ratio dey get closer by going above and below 1.618 one after another.
l-m-h3-b0c45-02.s.s2.model.0: 8÷5=1.6, and 1.6 smaller than 1.618, so the claim say 'e dey always bigger' no hold.
l-m-h3-b0c45-02.s.s2.model.1: The ratio dey change above and below 1.618, so even one small value like 1.6 be counterexample.

l-m-h3-b0c45-03.title: We fit always cover flat surface with only one kind of regular polygon?
l-m-h3-b0c45-03.goal: Check whether the claim say we fit cover flat surface without gaps using one kind of regular polygon always true, then find and explain a case wey no true (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c45-03.material: You wan cover floor with tiles, using only one kind of regular polygon, with no gap or overlap. Claim: any regular polygon fit cover floor if you use only one kind.
l-m-h3-b0c45-03.s.s1.prompt: Choose the regular polygon wey go against the claim (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c45-03.s.s1.r.b: When 3 meet for one point, dem make 360°, so dem fill the space.
l-m-h3-b0c45-03.s.s1.r.c: When 4 meet for one point, dem make 360°, so dem fill the space.
l-m-h3-b0c45-03.s.s1.r.d: When 6 meet for one point, dem make 360°, so dem fill the space.
l-m-h3-b0c45-03.s.s1.explain: Each angle for regular pentagon na 108°. 360÷108 no be whole number, so dem no fit meet for one point without gap.
l-m-h3-b0c45-03.s.s2.model.0: Each angle for regular pentagon na 108° and 360÷108 no be whole number, so dem no fit meet for one point without gap.
l-m-h3-b0c45-03.s.s2.model.1: 3 of dem make 324° and 4 make 432°, so dem no fit ever make exactly 360°. Na why regular pentagon be counterexample.

l-m-h3-b0c45-04.goal: Check whether the claim say every year wey divide by 4 na leap year always true, then find and explain a case wey no true (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c45-04.material: For Gregorian calendar, year wey divide by 4 na leap year, but year wey divide by 100 and no divide by 400 na normal year. Claim: every year wey divide by 4 na leap year.
l-m-h3-b0c45-04.s.s1.prompt: Choose the year wey go against the claim (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c45-04.s.s1.r.a: E divide by 400, so e be leap year. E be example wey fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c45-04.s.s1.r.b: E divide by 4 and na leap year, so e be example wey fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c45-04.s.s1.r.c: E divide by 4 and na leap year, so e be example wey fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c45-04.s.s1.explain: 1900 divide by 4 and 100 but no divide by 400, so na normal year.
l-m-h3-b0c45-04.s.s2.model.0: 1900 divide by 4, but e be multiple of 100 and no be multiple of 400, so na normal year and counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0c45-04.s.s2.model.1: 2000 too be multiple of 100, but e be multiple of 400, so na leap year. So na only 1900 go against the claim.

l-m-h3-b0c46-01.material: You wan gather some paper equilateral triangles for one point to make pointed vertex of solid. Claim: if you gather 3 or more equilateral triangles for one point, dem always make vertex of solid.
l-m-h3-b0c46-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose di number wey go against di claim (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c46-01.s.s1.r.a: Di angles add up to 180°, wey less than 360°, so dem make vertex.
l-m-h3-b0c46-01.s.s1.r.b: Di angles add up to 240°, wey less than 360°, so dem make vertex.
l-m-h3-b0c46-01.s.s1.r.c: Di angles add up to 300°, wey less than 360°, so dem make vertex.

l-m-h3-b0c46-02.s.s1.r.d: 127 na prime, so e be example wey fit di claim.

l-m-h3-b0c47-01.goal: Check whether claim 'ratio of two neighboring terms (later term ÷ earlier term) always bigger than 1.6' always true, and find and explain a case wey no true (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0c47-01.material: For Fibonacci sequence 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, …, ratio of two neighboring terms (later ÷ earlier) dey close to golden ratio 1.618. Claim: this ratio always bigger than 1.6.

l-m-h3-b0c47-01.s.s1.r.d: 1.615 bigger than 1.6, so e fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c47-01.s.s1.explain: 3÷2=1.5 smaller than 1.6. Ratios for first terms dey go up and down around 1.618.
l-m-h3-b0c47-01.s.s2.model.0: 3÷2=1.5 smaller than 1.6. Since some ratios na 1.6 or less, this counter the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c47-01.s.s2.model.1: All other ratios bigger than 1.6, but 3÷2 na 1.5, so claim no always true.

l-m-h3-b0c50-18.title: Big sample always accurate?
l-m-h3-b0c50-18.goal: Check if claim bigger sample always more accurate always true, find and explain counterexample if not.
l-m-h3-b0c50-18.material: Claim: More survey people always make result more accurate. Find where claim wrong when you want know what whole school thinks.
l-m-h3-b0c50-18.s.s1.o.a: Survey 300 random people instead of 30 random people
l-m-h3-b0c50-18.s.s1.r.a: Bigger random sample, so e fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c50-18.s.s1.o.b: Survey 1000 random people instead of 100 random people

l-m-h3-b0c50-18.s.s1.o.c: Survey 200 random people instead of 50 random people
l-m-h3-b0c50-18.s.s1.r.c: Sample bigger and more accurate, so e fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c50-18.s.s1.o.d: Survey 1000 volunteers instead of 100 random people
l-m-h3-b0c50-18.s.s1.explain: 1000 volunteers fit mostly share certain views. Plenty people no make am accurate if sample biased.
l-m-h3-b0c50-18.s.s2.model.0: 1000 volunteers fit include students with strong opinions, so no say dem more accurate than 100 random people.
l-m-h3-b0c50-18.s.s2.model.1: Even with many people, biased selection fit make am worse than 100 random people, so this counterexample.

l-m-h3-b0c50-22.title: Sum of two irrational numbers always irrational?
l-m-h3-b0c50-22.topic: Operations with irrational numbers and counterexamples
l-m-h3-b0c50-22.goal: Check if sum of two irrational numbers always irrational, find and explain counterexample if not.
l-m-h3-b0c50-22.material: Claim: Add two irrational numbers and sum always irrational too. Find two numbers to show claim wrong.
l-m-h3-b0c50-22.s.s1.prompt: Which pair of irrational numbers counter the claim?
l-m-h3-b0c50-22.s.s1.r.a: √2+√3 irrational, so e fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c50-22.s.s1.r.b: 3π irrational, so e fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c50-22.s.s1.r.c: 3√2 irrational, so e fit the claim.
l-m-h3-b0c50-22.s.s1.explain: √2+(-√2)=0, and 0 rational. Sometimes two irrational numbers fit sum to rational number.
l-m-h3-b0c50-22.s.s2.model.0: √2 and -√2 both irrational, but sum na 0, rational, so this go against claim.
l-m-h3-b0c50-22.s.s2.model.1: Sum 0 rational, so claim that two irrational numbers always sum to irrational one wrong.

l-m-h3-b0d07-01.title: Convergent sequence always move one direction?
l-m-h3-b0d07-01.goal: Check if di claim say convergent sequence always dey increase or always dey decrease correct, and find and explain one case wey no be so (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0d07-01.material: Claim: If sequence {aₙ} converge, then aₙ always increase or always decrease. Find sequence wey show say claim wrong.
l-m-h3-b0d07-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose sequence wey converge but go against di claim.
l-m-h3-b0d07-01.s.s1.r.a: E converge to 2 and continue to increase. E fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0d07-01.s.s1.r.c: E dey change between 1 and −1 and no converge. E no be convergent sequence.
l-m-h3-b0d07-01.s.s1.r.d: E converge to 0 and continue to reduce. E fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0d07-01.s.s1.explain: (−1)ⁿ/n na −1, 1/2, −1/3, … and e converge to 0, but e dey go up and down.
l-m-h3-b0d07-01.s.s2.model.0: Sign of (−1)ⁿ/n dey alternate, so e dey go up and down, but e converge to 0, so na counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0d07-01.s.s2.model.1: Terms dey go up and down, −1, 1/2, −1/3, but dem dey close to 0, so claim wrong.

l-m-h3-b0d07-10.title: If terms go to 0, series go converge too?
l-m-h3-b0d07-10.goal: Check whether claim say if general term go to 0, series converge always true, then find and explain one case wey no true (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0d07-10.material: Claim: If sequence aₙ converge to 0, then series Σaₙ must converge too. Find one aₙ wey show say dis claim wrong.
l-m-h3-b0d07-10.s.s1.prompt: Which one go to 0 but its series no converge?
l-m-h3-b0d07-10.s.s1.r.a: Di series converge (sum about 1.64). Na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0d07-10.s.s1.r.b: Di series converge (sum 1). Na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0d07-10.s.s1.r.c: Di series converge (sum 1). Na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0d07-10.s.s1.explain: 1/n go to 0, but groups like 1/3+1/4>1/2 and 1/5+…+1/8>1/2 each bigger than 1/2, so sum grow without limit.
l-m-h3-b0d07-10.s.s2.model.0: 1/n go to 0, but when you group as 1/3+1/4, 1/5+…+1/8, each group at least 1/2, so sum dey grow forever, making am counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0d07-10.s.s2.model.1: Even when general term dey close to 0, added terms reduce too slowly, so series 1/n diverge. Na why di claim wrong.

l-m-h3-b0d07-15.goal: Check if di claim say derivative of exponential function always positive correct, then find and explain one case wey no be true (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0d07-15.material: Claim: Derivative of y=aˣ (a>0, a≠1) positive for all x. Find exponential function wey make dis claim wrong.
l-m-h3-b0d07-15.s.s1.prompt: Which function go against di claim?
l-m-h3-b0d07-15.s.s1.r.a: Derivative 10ˣ ln 10 always positive. E fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0d07-15.s.s1.r.b: Derivative 2ˣ ln 2 always positive. E fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0d07-15.s.s1.r.d: Derivative na eˣ, wey always positive. E fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0d07-15.s.s1.explain: (aˣ)'=aˣ ln a. If 0<a<1, then ln a<0, so derivative negative.
l-m-h3-b0d07-15.s.s2.model.0: Derivative of (1/2)ˣ na (1/2)ˣ ln(1/2), and since ln(1/2)<0 e always negative, so na counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0d07-15.s.s2.model.1: When base less than 1, function dey reduce, so derivative negative. Na why (1/2)ˣ break di claim.

l-m-h3-b0d10-01.title: Di 2 distances to foci must be different?
l-m-h3-b0d10-01.goal: Check if claim say distances from point on ellipse to 2 foci always different correct, then find and explain case wey fail (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0d10-01.material: Claim: For point P on ellipse x²/25 + y²/9 = 1, distances to foci F(4, 0) and F′(−4, 0) always different. Find point wey show claim wrong.
l-m-h3-b0d10-01.s.s1.r.b: PF=1 and PF′=9 different, so dis example fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0d10-01.s.s1.r.c: PF=9 and PF′=1 different, so dis example fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0d10-01.s.s1.r.d: PF=2.6 and PF′=7.4 different, so dis example fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0d10-01.s.s1.explain: At (0,3), PF=PF′=5. When point on ellipse dey on y-axis (end of minor axis), distances to 2 foci equal.
l-m-h3-b0d10-01.s.s2.model.0: (0,3) dey on curve, and PF=√(16+9)=5=PF′, so 2 distances equal. Dis na counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0d10-01.s.s2.model.1: Y-axis na symmetry line wey pass middle of 2 foci, so any point on am get same distance to both foci.

l-m-h3-b0d10-02.title: Line through origin always meet hyperbola?
l-m-h3-b0d10-02.goal: Check if claim "line through origin meet hyperbola" always correct, and find and explain one case wey no be so (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0d10-02.material: Claim: Every line through origin meet hyperbola x²/4 − y²/9 = 1. Find line wey show claim wrong.
l-m-h3-b0d10-02.s.s1.r.b: One x fit make 5x²/36=1 true, so line meet curve.
l-m-h3-b0d10-02.s.s1.r.c: One x fit satisfy x²/4−x²/36=1, so line meet curve.
l-m-h3-b0d10-02.s.s1.explain: Put y=2x and get x²/4−4x²/9=−7x²/36=1, wey no get solution. Line steeper than asymptotes (slope ±3/2) no meet hyperbola.
l-m-h3-b0d10-02.s.s2.model.0: Put y=2x and get −7x²/36=1, but left side 0 or less, so no solution. Dis na counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0d10-02.s.s2.model.1: Slope 2 steeper than asymptote slope 3/2, so dis line never meet hyperbola.

l-m-h3-b0d10-15.title: Dot product of two parallel vectors always positive?
l-m-h3-b0d10-15.topic: Parallel vectors and the dot product
l-m-h3-b0d10-15.goal: Check whether claim “dot product of two parallel vectors positive” always true, then find and explain one case wey no be true (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0d10-15.material: Claim: If two nonzero vectors a and b parallel, then a·b > 0. Find a and b wey show say claim wrong.
l-m-h3-b0d10-15.s.s1.r.b: Dem no parallel. Dot product na 0, so dem perpendicular.
l-m-h3-b0d10-15.s.s1.r.c: Dem parallel in same direction, and dot product na 10>0, wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0d10-15.s.s1.r.d: Dem parallel in same direction, and dot product na 15>0, wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0d10-15.s.s1.explain: (1,2) and (−2,−4) parallel, but dem face opposite ways, so dot product na −10, wey negative.
l-m-h3-b0d10-15.s.s2.model.0: b=−2a, so dem parallel, but dot product na 1·(−2)+2·(−4)=−10, no be positive, so na counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0d10-15.s.s2.model.1: Parallel includes opposite directions too. Then angle between dem na 180°, so cos na −1 and dot product negative.

l-m-h3-b0d10-16.title: Absolute value of dot product equal product of lengths?
l-m-h3-b0d10-16.goal: Check whether claim |a·b|=|a||b| always true, then find and explain one case wey no be true (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0d10-16.material: Claim: For two nonzero vectors a and b, absolute value of dot product |a·b| always equal |a||b|. Find a and b wey show say claim wrong.
l-m-h3-b0d10-16.s.s1.r.a: Dem parallel, so |a·b|=6=3·2, wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0d10-16.s.s1.r.c: Dem parallel, so |a·b|=10=√5·√20, wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0d10-16.s.s1.r.d: Dem parallel, so |a·b|=5=1·5, wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0d10-16.s.s1.explain: (1,0)·(0,1)=0, so |a·b|=0, but |a||b|=1. Di 2 values equal only when vectors parallel.
l-m-h3-b0d10-16.s.s2.model.0: |a·b|=0, but |a||b|=1·1=1, so dem no equal. Dis na counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0d10-16.s.s2.model.1: |a·b|=|a||b||cosθ|, so if vectors perpendicular (cos90°=0), e be 0, different from product of lengths.

l-m-h3-b0d10-29.material: Claim: Two planes β and γ wey perpendicular to plane α parallel to each other. When α na xy-plane, find two planes wey show claim wrong.
l-m-h3-b0d10-29.s.s1.prompt: Which two planes go against di claim?
l-m-h3-b0d10-29.s.s1.r.b: Di two planes parallel, so na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0d10-29.s.s1.r.c: Di two planes parallel, so na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h3-b0d10-29.s.s1.r.d: Plane parallel to xy-plane no perpendicular to xy-plane.
l-m-h3-b0d10-29.s.s1.explain: xz-plane and yz-plane both perpendicular to xy-plane, but dem meet along z-axis, so dem no parallel.
l-m-h3-b0d10-29.s.s2.model.0: xz-plane and yz-plane both perpendicular to xy-plane and meet along z-axis, so dem no parallel. Dis na counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0d10-29.s.s2.model.1: Planes perpendicular to one plane fit face many directions, so you no fit say dem parallel to each other.

l-m-h3-b0d10-30.goal: Check whether claim “segment keep its length when orthogonally projected” always true, then find and explain case wey no be so (counterexample).
l-m-h3-b0d10-30.material: Claim: Segment keep its length when you orthogonally project am onto plane. When you project onto xy-plane, find segment wey show say claim wrong.
l-m-h3-b0d10-30.s.s1.prompt: Which segment go against di claim?
l-m-h3-b0d10-30.s.s1.r.a: E dey inside plane, so its length stay same after projection.
l-m-h3-b0d10-30.s.s1.r.b: E parallel to plane, so its length stay di same after projection.
l-m-h3-b0d10-30.s.s1.r.c: E parallel to plane, so its length stay di same after projection.
l-m-h3-b0d10-30.s.s1.explain: Projection of (3,4,5) na (3,4,0), so its length na 5. Dat different from original length √50≈7.07.
l-m-h3-b0d10-30.s.s2.model.0: After projection length na 5, but original length na √50≈7.07, so dem different and dis na counterexample.
l-m-h3-b0d10-30.s.s2.model.1: If segment tilt against plane, its height part disappear, so projected length shorter.

l-m-h3-b0c33-05.title: Which information you must get to find di profit for each item?
l-m-h3-b0c33-05.goal: Find out which standard (information) you must get to find di profit wey remain from selling one item, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c33-05.material: You wan know how much profit one shop dey make from selling one item. Profit na di selling price minus di cost. Think about which information dem must get.
l-m-h3-b0c33-05.s.s1.prompt: Which information dem must get to know di profit for each item?
l-m-h3-b0c33-05.s.s1.o.a: Only di list price and di discount rate (cost nobody know)
l-m-h3-b0c33-05.s.s1.r.a: If you no know di cost, you no fit tell whether di selling price big pass di cost.
l-m-h3-b0c33-05.s.s1.o.b: Di cost and selling price of dat item
l-m-h3-b0c33-05.s.s1.o.c: Number wey dem sell for one day and number of customers
l-m-h3-b0c33-05.s.s1.r.c: Di number alone no fit tell you di money wey remain for each item.
l-m-h3-b0c33-05.s.s1.o.d: Di shop rent and number of workers
l-m-h3-b0c33-05.s.s1.r.d: Dem no connect directly to di profit for one item.
l-m-h3-b0c33-05.s.s1.explain: Profit na selling price − cost, so dem need both values. Di list price and discount rate only give di selling price.
l-m-h3-b0c33-05.s.s2.model.0: Dem find profit by subtracting di cost from di selling price, so you must get di cost and di selling price. Rent and number of customers no fit decide di profit for one item.
l-m-h3-b0c33-05.s.s2.model.1: Di list price and discount rate only give di selling price, so without di cost you no fit know how much remain.

l-m-h3-b0c33-06.title: Information wey dem need for take-home pay after tax
l-m-h3-b0c33-06.goal: Find out which standard (information) you must get to find di amount wey remain for hand after dem collect tax, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c33-06.material: You wan know di amount wey you really receive after dem collect tax from your pay. Dem decide tax by multiplying di pre-tax amount by di tax rate. Think about which information dem must get.
l-m-h3-b0c33-06.s.s1.prompt: Which information dem must get to find di take-home pay?
l-m-h3-b0c33-06.s.s1.o.a: Only di tax rate (pre-tax amount nobody know)
l-m-h3-b0c33-06.s.s1.r.a: Di tax rate alone no tell you how much money e be.
l-m-h3-b0c33-06.s.s1.o.b: Only di pre-tax amount (tax rate nobody know)
l-m-h3-b0c33-06.s.s1.r.b: If you no know di tax rate, you no know how much dem collect.
l-m-h3-b0c33-06.s.s1.o.c: Di total tax wey dem pay last month
l-m-h3-b0c33-06.s.s1.r.c: Last month tax no tell you dis month rate.
l-m-h3-b0c33-06.s.s1.o.d: Di pre-tax amount and di tax rate wey apply
l-m-h3-b0c33-06.s.s1.explain: Tax = pre-tax amount × tax rate, so you need both. Na only dat time you fit find take-home pay = pre-tax amount − tax.
l-m-h3-b0c33-06.s.s2.model.0: Dem find tax by multiplying di pre-tax amount by di tax rate, so you must know both to find di take-home pay.
l-m-h3-b0c33-06.s.s2.model.1: If you know only di tax rate, you no know di amount, and if you know only di amount, you no know di rate wey dem collect, so dem need both together.

l-m-h3-b0c33-07.title: Wetin else you need to find compound interest?
l-m-h3-b0c33-07.goal: Find out which standard (information) you must get to find di total amount (principal plus interest) wey compound interest grow, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c33-07.material: You deposit principal of 500×10,000 won at 4% per year. Think about which other information dem must get to find di amount wey compound interest grow.
l-m-h3-b0c33-07.s.s1.prompt: Which additional information dem must get?
l-m-h3-b0c33-07.s.s1.o.a: Only how long di deposit stay (how often dem add interest no matter)
l-m-h3-b0c33-07.s.s1.r.a: Di same rate give different amounts with yearly compounding and monthly compounding.
l-m-h3-b0c33-07.s.s1.o.b: Di name of di deposit product
l-m-h3-b0c33-07.s.s1.r.b: One name no decide di amount.
l-m-h3-b0c33-07.s.s1.o.c: Di interest rate of one deposit for another bank
l-m-h3-b0c33-07.s.s1.r.c: E no be information wey decide di amount for my deposit.
l-m-h3-b0c33-07.s.s1.o.d: How long di deposit stay and how often dem add interest to di principal
l-m-h3-b0c33-07.s.s1.explain: For compound interest, di amount depend on how long di time be and how often dem add interest to di principal. Dem don already give di rate and di principal.
l-m-h3-b0c33-07.s.s2.model.0: Di longer di time, di more interest dem earn on interest, and di amount depend on how often dem add interest, so dem need both.
l-m-h3-b0c33-07.s.s2.model.1: Dem already know di rate of 4% per year and di principal, so wetin miss na how long di time be and how often dem add interest.

l-m-h3-b0c33-08.title: Which information you need to find di break-even point?
l-m-h3-b0c33-08.topic: Break-even point (where income and cost equal)
l-m-h3-b0c33-08.goal: Find out which standard (information) you must get to find di sales quantity wey income equal cost, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c33-08.material: One small shop sell one product. Think about which information dem must get to find di sales quantity wey income and cost go equal.
l-m-h3-b0c33-08.s.s1.prompt: Which set of information dem must get?
l-m-h3-b0c33-08.s.s1.o.a: Fixed cost and selling price for each item (variable cost nobody know)
l-m-h3-b0c33-08.s.s1.r.a: If you no know di variable cost for each item, you no know how much remain for each item.
l-m-h3-b0c33-08.s.s1.o.b: Variable cost for each item and selling price for each item (fixed cost nobody know)
l-m-h3-b0c33-08.s.s1.r.b: If you no know di fixed cost, you no know how much dem must cover.
l-m-h3-b0c33-08.s.s1.o.c: Fixed cost, variable cost for each item, and selling price for each item
l-m-h3-b0c33-08.s.s1.o.d: Last year total sales quantity and total income
l-m-h3-b0c33-08.s.s1.r.d: Total income alone no tell you di cost structure.
l-m-h3-b0c33-08.s.s1.explain: Di money wey remain for each item (selling price − variable cost) must cover di fixed cost, so dem need all three.
l-m-h3-b0c33-08.s.s2.model.0: If you subtract di variable cost from di selling price for each item, e give di money wey remain for each item, and dat one must cover di fixed cost, so dem need all three.
l-m-h3-b0c33-08.s.s2.model.1: If di fixed cost or di variable cost miss, you no fit decide di quantity wey income and cost go equal, so dem need all.

l-m-h3-b0c34-05.topic: Demand function (how demand dey change with price)
l-m-h3-b0c34-05.title: Which records we need to decide one linear demand equation?
l-m-h3-b0c34-05.goal: Find out which criteria (information) dem must get to find di linear equation wey connect price and sales, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c34-05.material: You wan write as equation di linear relationship where sales dey fall by steady amount as di price dey rise. Think about which records dem must get.
l-m-h3-b0c34-05.s.s1.prompt: Which records dem must get to decide di equation?
l-m-h3-b0c34-05.s.s1.o.a: Two days of sales at di same price
l-m-h3-b0c34-05.s.s1.r.a: Di same price na just one point, so we no fit know di slope.
l-m-h3-b0c34-05.s.s1.o.b: One price and di sales at dat price
l-m-h3-b0c34-05.s.s1.r.b: With one point, endless lines dey wey pass through am.
l-m-h3-b0c34-05.s.s1.o.c: Di shop location and business hours
l-m-h3-b0c34-05.s.s1.r.c: Dem no tell us about di relationship between price and sales.
l-m-h3-b0c34-05.s.s1.o.d: Two different prices and di sales at dose prices
l-m-h3-b0c34-05.s.s1.explain: Two different points dey decide one line. You need two different prices and dia sales to find di slope and di intercept.
l-m-h3-b0c34-05.s.s2.model.0: Two different points dey decide one line, so dem must get two different prices and dia sales.
l-m-h3-b0c34-05.s.s2.model.1: One single point or records at di same price no fit tell us di slope, so you need two records at different prices.

l-m-h3-b0c34-06.title: Which information dem must get for di expected value of one game?
l-m-h3-b0c34-06.goal: Find out which criteria (information) dem must get to find di average prize wey you fit expect for one game, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c34-06.material: Na game where you draw one slip of paper from one box and get prize. Think about which information dem must get to find di prize wey you fit expect (di expected value) for one play.
l-m-h3-b0c34-06.s.s1.o.a: Only di number of possible prizes
l-m-h3-b0c34-06.s.s1.r.a: Di number of kinds alone no tell us how often each prize dey show.
l-m-h3-b0c34-06.s.s1.r.b: Without di other prizes and di probabilities, we no fit find di average.
l-m-h3-b0c34-06.s.s1.o.c: Only di number of people wey don play until now
l-m-h3-b0c34-06.s.s1.r.c: Di number of players no tell us di sizes or probabilities of di prizes.
l-m-h3-b0c34-06.s.s1.o.d: Di amount and di probability of each possible prize
l-m-h3-b0c34-06.s.s1.explain: Di expected value na di sum of (prize × im probability), so dem need both di amounts and di probabilities of di prizes.
l-m-h3-b0c34-06.s.s2.model.0: Di expected value dey multiply each prize by im probability and add dem up, so dem must get di amount and di probability of each prize.
l-m-h3-b0c34-06.s.s2.model.1: Di number of kinds or di biggest prize alone no tell us how often each one dey show, so we no fit decide di average.

l-m-h3-b0c34-07.title: Wetin we need to compare rates of return?
l-m-h3-b0c34-07.topic: Rate of return (how much profit compared to money wey you put)
l-m-h3-b0c34-07.goal: Find out which criteria (information) dem must get to find di rates of return of two investments, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c34-07.material: You wan know which one between Investment A and Investment B get higher rate of return. Di rate of return na di money wey you earn divided by di money wey you put in. Think about which information dem need.
l-m-h3-b0c34-07.s.s1.o.a: Di money wey you put in and di money wey you earn for each one
l-m-h3-b0c34-07.s.s1.o.b: Only di money wey you earn for each one
l-m-h3-b0c34-07.s.s1.r.b: If di money wey you put in different, we no fit compare di ratios by di money wey you earn alone.
l-m-h3-b0c34-07.s.s1.o.c: Only di money wey you put in for each one
l-m-h3-b0c34-07.s.s1.r.c: If we no know di money wey you earn, we no fit find di ratio.
l-m-h3-b0c34-07.s.s1.o.d: Only di date wey each investment start
l-m-h3-b0c34-07.s.s1.r.d: Di dates alone no tell us di ratio of di money wey you earn.
l-m-h3-b0c34-07.s.s1.explain: Di rate of return = money wey you earn ÷ money wey you put in, so both investments need di money wey you put in and di money wey you earn.
l-m-h3-b0c34-07.s.s2.model.0: Di rate of return na di money wey you earn divided by di money wey you put in, so we need both di money wey you put in and di money wey you earn for each one.
l-m-h3-b0c34-07.s.s2.model.1: Even if di money wey you earn na di same, di ratio dey change if di money wey you put in different, so we no fit compare by di money wey you earn alone.

l-m-h3-b0c34-08.title: Wetin we need to know whether real income don grow?
l-m-h3-b0c34-08.goal: Find out which criteria (information) dem must get to find di change for di real purchasing power of one salary, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c34-08.material: Di salary go up from last year, but prices go up too. Think about wetin you need to know whether di amount wey you fit really buy (real purchasing power) don grow.
l-m-h3-b0c34-08.s.s1.o.a: Di rate of salary increase and di rate of price increase
l-m-h3-b0c34-08.s.s1.o.b: Only di rate of salary increase
l-m-h3-b0c34-08.s.s1.r.b: If prices rise even more, di amount wey you fit buy fit go down.
l-m-h3-b0c34-08.s.s1.o.c: Only di amount of dis year salary
l-m-h3-b0c34-08.s.s1.r.c: If we no compare with last year, we no fit tell whether e grow.
l-m-h3-b0c34-08.s.s1.o.d: Only di rate of price increase
l-m-h3-b0c34-08.s.s1.r.d: If we no know how much di salary go up, we no fit compare.
l-m-h3-b0c34-08.s.s1.explain: You must compare di rate wey di salary rise with di rate wey prices rise to know whether di amount wey you fit really buy don grow.
l-m-h3-b0c34-08.s.s2.model.0: We must compare di rate wey di salary rise with di rate wey prices rise, so dem must get both rates of increase.
l-m-h3-b0c34-08.s.s2.model.1: If only di salary rise and prices rise too, di amount wey you fit buy fit stay di same, so you need to know di rate of price increase.

l-m-h3-b0c35-02.title: How to find di amount wey you go receive wen di deposit mature?
l-m-h3-b0c35-02.goal: Find out which basis (information) dem must get to find di amount wey you receive wen one deposit mature, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c35-02.material: You deposit one principal for bank and you wan calculate before time di amount (principal + interest) wey you go receive wen e mature after some years. Think about which information dem must get.
l-m-h3-b0c35-02.s.s1.prompt: Which information dem must get to decide di maturity amount?
l-m-h3-b0c35-02.s.s1.o.a: Principal, yearly interest rate, period, and whether na simple or compound interest
l-m-h3-b0c35-02.s.s1.r.b: If you no know di interest rate, you no fit know how big di interest be.
l-m-h3-b0c35-02.s.s1.o.c: Yearly interest rate and di bank name
l-m-h3-b0c35-02.s.s1.r.c: Without di principal and di period, dem no fit decide di interest.
l-m-h3-b0c35-02.s.s1.o.d: Principal and yearly interest rate only
l-m-h3-b0c35-02.s.s1.r.d: If di period and di calculation method change, di amount go change too.
l-m-h3-b0c35-02.s.s1.explain: Di principal, di rate, and di period dey decide di interest, and di amount different for di same conditions depending on whether na simple or compound interest.
l-m-h3-b0c35-02.s.s2.model.0: You need di principal, rate, and period to find di interest, and simple and compound interest give different amounts, so dem need di calculation method too.
l-m-h3-b0c35-02.s.s2.model.1: Without even one of di rate or di period you no fit find di interest, so dem need all four, and each of di other choices miss one.

l-m-h3-b0c35-10.title: Information wey dem need to find di expected loss
l-m-h3-b0c35-10.goal: Find out which basis (information) dem must get to find di expected loss from when dem steal bicycle, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c35-10.material: Suppose say dem fit steal one bicycle. You wan find di average loss (expected loss) wey you suffer from theft over 1 year.
l-m-h3-b0c35-10.s.s1.prompt: Which information dem must get to find di expected loss?
l-m-h3-b0c35-10.s.s1.o.a: Di insurance premium and how long di coverage be
l-m-h3-b0c35-10.s.s1.r.a: Dem dey use di premium wen dem dey compare insurance, and dem no need am for di expected loss itself.
l-m-h3-b0c35-10.s.s1.o.b: Di probability of theft and di amount wey dem lose wen dem steal am
l-m-h3-b0c35-10.s.s1.o.c: Di name and color of di shop wey dem buy di bicycle
l-m-h3-b0c35-10.s.s1.r.c: Dis na information wey no relate to di size or probability of di loss.
l-m-h3-b0c35-10.s.s1.o.d: Only di price wey dem pay last year
l-m-h3-b0c35-10.s.s1.r.d: You fit guess di amount wey dem lose, but di probability of theft miss.
l-m-h3-b0c35-10.s.s1.explain: Expected loss = probability × amount wey dem lose. You need both values, and dem dey use di premium afterward for comparison.
l-m-h3-b0c35-10.s.s2.model.0: Di expected loss na di average of probability times amount wey dem lose, so dem must get di probability of theft and di amount wey dem lose.
l-m-h3-b0c35-10.s.s2.model.1: Dem need di premium wen dem dey compare whether to sign up and dem no need am to find di expected loss, so dem no choose am.

l-m-h3-b0c35-24.title: For linear cost model to fit
l-m-h3-b0c35-24.goal: To work out whether dem fit express total cost as linear function, decide which standard (information) must dey, then explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c35-24.material: One workshop want express im total cost as C=a+bx (x na di number wey dem make). Think about which property dis linear expression need make e be suitable model.
l-m-h3-b0c35-24.s.s1.prompt: Which property must dey for linear model to fit?
l-m-h3-b0c35-24.s.s1.o.a: One fixed cost and one cost for each item wey dey stay constant no matter di number
l-m-h3-b0c35-24.s.s1.o.b: Di cost for each item dey change as di number dey grow
l-m-h3-b0c35-24.s.s1.r.b: If di cost for each item dey change, e no be linear expression.
l-m-h3-b0c35-24.s.s1.o.c: Di number wey dem make na 100 or more
l-m-h3-b0c35-24.s.s1.r.c: Wetin matter no be di size of di number but whether di cost structure constant.
l-m-h3-b0c35-24.s.s1.o.d: Di selling price high pass di cost
l-m-h3-b0c35-24.s.s1.r.d: Dat one na about profit and e no get anything to do with di shape of di cost model.
l-m-h3-b0c35-24.s.s1.explain: Di fixed cost a and di cost for each item b must be constant make di cost grow steadily as di number dey grow, and dat one go make linear expression.
l-m-h3-b0c35-24.s.s2.model.0: Di cost for each item must be constant so that di cost go rise by di same b every time di number go up by 1, and dat one make linear expression suitable.
l-m-h3-b0c35-24.s.s2.model.1: Di fixed cost a must be constant and di cost for each item b must be constant too, so dat property dey needed, and di selling price no get anything to do with di cost model.

l-m-h3-b0c35-31.goal: To know whether to continue one course wey dem no dey refund, decide which standard (information) important pass and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c35-31.material: You don already pay 15 ×10,000 won fee for one cooking class wey dem no fit refund. After you try few sessions e no good, and you wan decide whether to continue.
l-m-h3-b0c35-31.s.s1.prompt: Which information suppose be the standard to decide whether to continue?
l-m-h3-b0c35-31.s.s1.o.a: The name of the place wey dey run the course
l-m-h3-b0c35-31.s.s1.r.a: E no get anything to do with the cost or benefit of the choice.
l-m-h3-b0c35-31.s.s1.o.b: The time and cost to come, and the benefit wey you go get
l-m-h3-b0c35-31.s.s1.o.c: The 15 ×10,000 won wey you don already pay
l-m-h3-b0c35-31.s.s1.r.c: Money wey you no fit recover no be standard to decide whether to continue.
l-m-h3-b0c35-31.s.s1.o.d: The reason wey make you choose this course for the first place
l-m-h3-b0c35-31.s.s1.r.d: E na about the past, no be something wey you go gain for the future.

l-m-h3-b0c35-31.s.s2.model.0: The 15 ×10,000 won no fit come back whether you continue or you quit, so na only future costs and benefits be the standard.

l-m-h3-b0c36-05.title: For two matrices to fit multiply
l-m-h3-b0c36-05.goal: To know whether you fit calculate the product AB of two matrices, decide which standard (information) dey essential and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c36-05.material: If dem give matrices A and B, we wan first check whether the product AB dey defined. Think which information about the two matrices we must look.
l-m-h3-b0c36-05.s.s1.prompt: Which information dey essential to know whether AB dey defined?
l-m-h3-b0c36-05.s.s1.o.a: Number of rows in A and columns in B
l-m-h3-b0c36-05.s.s1.r.a: E only decide the size of the product, e no decide whether e dey defined.
l-m-h3-b0c36-05.s.s1.o.b: Columns in A and rows in B
l-m-h3-b0c36-05.s.s1.o.c: Sum of entries in A and B
l-m-h3-b0c36-05.s.s1.r.c: The values of the entries no get anything to do with whether the product dey defined.
l-m-h3-b0c36-05.s.s1.o.d: Whether all the entries of A and B na integers
l-m-h3-b0c36-05.s.s1.r.d: Whether the entries na integers no get anything to do with whether multiplication fit happen.
l-m-h3-b0c36-05.s.s1.explain: To multiply each A row by each B column entry by entry and add, A column count gats equal B row count.
l-m-h3-b0c36-05.s.s2.model.0: The entries of one row of A must pair and multiply with the entries of one column of B, so the number of columns of A and the number of rows of B must be equal.
l-m-h3-b0c36-05.s.s2.model.1: If the counts no match, some entries go remain without partner, so na only the numbers of columns and rows dey decide whether multiplication fit happen, and we no need the entry values.

l-m-h3-b0c36-06.title: To check whether two events dey independent
l-m-h3-b0c36-06.goal: To know whether two events A and B dey independent, decide which standard (information) dey essential and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c36-06.material: We wan use data check whether events A and B dey independent of each other. Think which probability information dey essential.
l-m-h3-b0c36-06.s.s1.prompt: Which information dey essential to judge independence?
l-m-h3-b0c36-06.s.s1.r.a: If you no get P(A∩B) to compare with the product P(A)P(B), you no fit judge.
l-m-h3-b0c36-06.s.s1.o.b: Whether A and B don ever happen at the same time
l-m-h3-b0c36-06.s.s1.r.b: Even if dem don happen together, you still must check the product before you fit know whether dem dey independent.
l-m-h3-b0c36-06.s.s1.o.d: Whether the sample sizes of A and B the same
l-m-h3-b0c36-06.s.s1.r.d: Even if the sample sizes the same, e no get anything to do with independence.
l-m-h3-b0c36-06.s.s1.explain: You must compare whether P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B). You need to know all three values to compare with the product.
l-m-h3-b0c36-06.s.s2.model.0: If dem dey independent, P(A∩B) must equal the product of P(A) and P(B), so we need all three probabilities.
l-m-h3-b0c36-06.s.s2.model.1: If na only P(A) and P(B) you get, you go only fit get the product and nothing to compare am with, so we need P(A∩B) too.
