l-m-h3-b0c36-07.title: To decide the next position for gradient descent
l-m-h3-b0c36-07.goal: To know the next position for gradient descent, decide which standard (information) dey essential and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c36-07.material: We dey use gradient descent find where f(x) dey near im minimum. To take one step from the current x and decide the next position, think wetin we need to know.
l-m-h3-b0c36-07.s.s1.prompt: Which information dey essential to decide the next position?
l-m-h3-b0c36-07.s.s1.r.a: If you no get the slope for the current position, you no fit decide the direction and size.
l-m-h3-b0c36-07.s.s1.o.b: The slope for the current position and the learning rate
l-m-h3-b0c36-07.s.s1.r.c: Dem no dey use the y-intercept decide the next position.
l-m-h3-b0c36-07.s.s1.o.d: Wetin be the minimum value of f
l-m-h3-b0c36-07.s.s1.r.d: Even if you no know the minimum value, you fit still take step if you know the slope.
l-m-h3-b0c36-07.s.s1.explain: x_new = x − (learning rate)×(slope). The slope give direction and size, and the learning rate decide the step width.
l-m-h3-b0c36-07.s.s2.model.0: The slope show the downhill direction and the learning rate decide the step size, so the two of dem dey essential.
l-m-h3-b0c36-07.s.s2.model.1: We dey search without knowing the minimum value, so we must decide the next position with only the slope for the current position and the learning rate.

l-m-h3-b0c36-08.title: To know whether e miss patients
l-m-h3-b0c36-08.goal: To know whether the model miss patients, decide which standard (information) dey essential and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c36-08.material: We dey evaluate disease test model. Wetin we wan know na how many of the real patients the model find as patients.
l-m-h3-b0c36-08.s.s1.prompt: Which measure dey tell us this one?
l-m-h3-b0c36-08.s.s1.o.a: Share of correct answers out of all answers
l-m-h3-b0c36-08.s.s1.r.a: With accuracy, the patients wey dem miss fit hide under the correct healthy answers.
l-m-h3-b0c36-08.s.s1.o.b: The share of real patients among those wey dem call positive
l-m-h3-b0c36-08.s.s1.r.b: Na precision be this one, e dey check whether false alarms few. E no show the patients wey dem miss.
l-m-h3-b0c36-08.s.s1.o.c: The share of real patients wey dem find as positive
l-m-h3-b0c36-08.s.s1.o.d: The time wey the model take train
l-m-h3-b0c36-08.s.s1.r.d: Training time no get anything to do with the ability to find patients.
l-m-h3-b0c36-08.s.s1.explain: Recall na the share of real patients wey dem find. The fewer the patients wey dem miss, the higher the recall.
l-m-h3-b0c36-08.s.s2.model.0: Wetin we dey ask about na the share of real patients wey dem find, so we suppose look recall, wey im denominator na real patients.
l-m-h3-b0c36-08.s.s2.model.1: Accuracy mix the correct healthy answers inside, and precision get the positive predictions as im denominator, so none of dem show how many patients dem miss.

l-m-h3-b0c37-05.title: To know whether two vectors dey perpendicular
l-m-h3-b0c37-05.goal: To find out whether two vectors dey perpendicular to each other, work out which standard (information) dey absolutely necessary, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c37-05.material: We wan know whether two nonzero vectors a and b dey perpendicular. The dot product na the value wey you get when you multiply the matching entries and add dem. Think which information dey absolutely necessary.
l-m-h3-b0c37-05.s.s1.prompt: Which information dey absolutely necessary to know whether dem dey perpendicular?
l-m-h3-b0c37-05.s.s1.r.a: The sizes alone no fit tell you the relation of direction.
l-m-h3-b0c37-05.s.s1.o.b: Number of entries in di two vectors
l-m-h3-b0c37-05.s.s1.r.b: Even if the number of entries the same, you no fit know whether dem dey perpendicular.
l-m-h3-b0c37-05.s.s1.o.c: The value wey you get from adding all the entries of the two vectors
l-m-h3-b0c37-05.s.s1.r.c: The sum of the entries no fit tell you the relation of direction between the two vectors.
l-m-h3-b0c37-05.s.s1.o.d: Dot product of di two vectors
l-m-h3-b0c37-05.s.s1.explain: Two nonzero vectors dey perpendicular only when the dot product na 0. One dot product value dey enough to decide.
l-m-h3-b0c37-05.s.s2.model.0: If dem dey perpendicular, the dot product na 0, and if the dot product na 0, dem dey perpendicular, so with only the dot product value you fit decide.
l-m-h3-b0c37-05.s.s2.model.1: The sizes and the number of entries no get anything to do with direction, so you need the dot product value, wey hold the relation of direction inside one number.

l-m-h3-b0c37-06.title: Information wey dem need for confidence interval of mean
l-m-h3-b0c37-06.goal: To find the 95% confidence interval of the population mean, work out which standard (information) dey absolutely necessary, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c37-06.material: When dem know the population standard deviation, we wan estimate the population mean with 95% confidence interval. The interval na sample mean ± 1.96×(population standard deviation ÷ √sample size). Think which information dem need.
l-m-h3-b0c37-06.s.s1.prompt: Which information dey absolutely necessary to build the interval?
l-m-h3-b0c37-06.s.s1.r.a: The range alone no fit give the standard error.
l-m-h3-b0c37-06.s.s1.o.b: Sample mean, population standard deviation, and sample size
l-m-h3-b0c37-06.s.s1.o.c: Only sample mean and sample size
l-m-h3-b0c37-06.s.s1.r.c: The population standard deviation wey show the spread no dey, so dem no fit decide the width.
l-m-h3-b0c37-06.s.s1.r.d: The spread and the sample size wey dem need to decide the margin of error no dey.
l-m-h3-b0c37-06.s.s1.explain: The center na the sample mean, and the width na 1.96×σ÷√n. You need all three values to decide the two ends of the interval.
l-m-h3-b0c37-06.s.s2.model.0: The center of the interval na the sample mean and the population standard deviation and the sample size dey decide the width, so dem need all three values.
l-m-h3-b0c37-06.s.s2.model.1: If na only the sample mean you get, you no know the width, so the interval no dey decided; the population standard deviation and the size dey decide the width.

l-m-h3-b0c37-07.goal: To find out whether the quadratic function f(x)=ax²+bx+c get minimum, work out which standard (information) dey absolutely necessary, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c37-07.material: We wan find out whether the quadratic function f(x)=ax²+bx+c (a≠0), wey dey show error, get minimum. Think which information you absolutely need to know.
l-m-h3-b0c37-07.s.s1.prompt: Which information you absolutely need to know to know whether minimum value dey?
l-m-h3-b0c37-07.s.s1.r.b: c only dey move the graph up or down. E no dey change which way e open.
l-m-h3-b0c37-07.s.s1.r.c: The sign of b dey affect where the vertex dey, but e no fit decide which way the graph open.
l-m-h3-b0c37-07.s.s1.r.d: The discriminant only dey tell you how many times the graph meet the x-axis. Na different thing from minimum value.
l-m-h3-b0c37-07.s.s1.explain: If a>0, the graph open upward and e get minimum value. If a<0, e open downward and e no get minimum value. You only need the sign of a.
l-m-h3-b0c37-07.s.s2.model.0: Graph only get minimum value when e open upward, and the sign of a dey decide that direction, so to know a dey enough.
l-m-h3-b0c37-07.s.s2.model.1: b and c only dey move the graph and dem no dey change which way e open, so the sign of a alone dey decide whether minimum value dey.

l-m-h3-b0c37-08.title: To find out about overfitting
l-m-h3-b0c37-08.goal: Decide which criterion (information) dey absolutely needed to find out whether model dey lean toward im training data only, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c37-08.material: You wan find out whether classification model dey correct only because e memorize the answers inside the training data (overfitting). Think which information you need to look together.
l-m-h3-b0c37-08.s.s1.prompt: Which information you absolutely need to know whether overfitting dey?
l-m-h3-b0c37-08.s.s1.o.a: The accuracy for the training data and for new test data
l-m-h3-b0c37-08.s.s1.r.b: The number of items alone no tell you which data e get correct or how much.

l-m-h3-b0c38-10.title: Wetin we need to find conditional probability?
l-m-h3-b0c38-10.goal: Work out which standard (information) dem must get to find the conditional probability of event A happening given event B, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c38-10.material: We dey build spam filter. We wan find the probability P(A|B) say email na spam (A) when e get the word 'free' (B). Make we work out which two probabilities dem must get.
l-m-h3-b0c38-10.s.s1.prompt: Which two values dem must get to find P(A|B)?
l-m-h3-b0c38-10.s.s1.r.a: With just these two, P(A|B) no dey determined. You need the intersection.
l-m-h3-b0c38-10.s.s1.r.b: Dem dey use these two to find P(B|A). The reference na the other way round.
l-m-h3-b0c38-10.s.s1.r.d: The union alone no tell you the intersection.
l-m-h3-b0c38-10.s.s1.explain: P(A|B)=P(A∩B)/P(B). Na the proportion, among the cases wey B happen, wey A also happen.
l-m-h3-b0c38-10.s.s2.model.0: E dey use only the cases wey B happen as the reference, so the denominator na P(B) and the numerator need P(A∩B), the probability say both happen together.
l-m-h3-b0c38-10.s.s2.model.1: With P(A) and P(B) alone, you no know how often the two dey happen together, so e no dey determined, and dem need the intersection.

l-m-h3-b0c38-22.goal: Work out which standard (information) dem absolutely need to find di information wey dem require to decide di next w by gradient descent, then explain why you choose am.

l-m-h3-b0c38-22.s.s1.r.b: Di maximum no dey decide di direction and size of di update.
l-m-h3-b0c38-22.s.s1.o.c: Di position of di minimum of di loss
l-m-h3-b0c38-22.s.s1.r.c: If you know dat one, you no go need to update.
l-m-h3-b0c38-22.s.s1.o.d: Di current w, di current slope, and di learning rate
l-m-h3-b0c38-22.s.s1.explain: New w = current w − learning rate × current slope. With dis three values you fit calculate am.
l-m-h3-b0c38-22.s.s2.model.0: Dem dey get di new w when dem subtract learning rate × slope from di current w, so dem absolutely need dis three things.
l-m-h3-b0c38-22.s.s2.model.1: If you already know di position of di minimum, you no go need to update, so dat one no be necessary information.

l-m-h3-b0c38-28.goal: Work out which standard (information) dem must get to find how much of the defects dem find without miss any (recall), then explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c38-28.material: How much of the real defects one defect-detection model find na im dem dey call recall. Make we work out which two pieces of information dem must get to find recall.

l-m-h3-b0c38-28.s.s1.o.a: The number wey dem judge defective and the number of those wey correct
l-m-h3-b0c38-28.s.s1.r.a: Na the information for precision be that. The standard different.
l-m-h3-b0c38-28.s.s1.o.b: The total number of products and the number wey dem judge correct
l-m-h3-b0c38-28.s.s1.r.b: Na the information for accuracy be that. You must look the defects separate.

l-m-h3-b0c38-28.s.s1.r.c: The number of defects wey dem find no dey, so you no fit find the ratio.
l-m-h3-b0c38-28.s.s1.o.d: The real number of defects and the number of those wey dem find
l-m-h3-b0c38-28.s.s1.explain: Recall = number of real defects wey dem find ÷ number of real defects. The denominator na all the real defects.
l-m-h3-b0c38-28.s.s2.model.0: Recall na the proportion of the real defects wey dem find, so you need the real number of defects and the number of those wey dem find.
l-m-h3-b0c38-28.s.s2.model.1: If you use the number wey dem judge as the standard e go become precision, so recall must use the real defects as the standard.

l-m-h3-b0c40-05.material: Dem measure one pipe length and e come out 3 mm off. You wan judge whether this error dey on the big side.
l-m-h3-b0c40-05.s.s1.prompt: Which information dem must get to judge whether e big?
l-m-h3-b0c40-05.s.s1.r.a: Weight no be standard to judge the size of length error.
l-m-h3-b0c40-05.s.s1.o.b: The total length of the pipe wey dem measure
l-m-h3-b0c40-05.s.s1.o.c: The number of people wey measure
l-m-h3-b0c40-05.s.s1.r.c: The number of people no get anything to do with how big the error be.
l-m-h3-b0c40-05.s.s1.r.d: Price no be standard to judge the size of error.
l-m-h3-b0c40-05.s.s1.explain: If 3 mm come from 20 mm, na big error, and if e come from 3 m, na small error. You must compare am with the total length.
l-m-h3-b0c40-05.s.s2.model.0: You fit know whether error big or small only by comparing am with the length wey dem measure, so the total length na must.
l-m-h3-b0c40-05.s.s2.model.1: Even for the same 3 mm, e na 15% of 20 mm and 0.1% of 3 m, so you must know the total length to judge.

l-m-h3-b0c40-06.title: Wetin you need to decide how many bolts to order?
l-m-h3-b0c40-06.goal: To find out the number of extra bolts to order, identify which standard (information) dem must get, then explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c40-06.material: Bolts don short for the workshop, so you wan order more. The amount wey dem go use this week don fix. You must decide how many to order.
l-m-h3-b0c40-06.s.s1.prompt: Which information dem must get to decide the order quantity?
l-m-h3-b0c40-06.s.s1.o.a: Current stock and price of one bolt
l-m-h3-b0c40-06.s.s1.r.a: If you no know the amount wey dem need, you no fit know how much short.
l-m-h3-b0c40-06.s.s1.o.b: One bolt price and supplier location
l-m-h3-b0c40-06.s.s1.r.b: Price and location no fit decide the number to order.
l-m-h3-b0c40-06.s.s1.o.c: The amount wey dem need this week and the price of one bolt
l-m-h3-b0c40-06.s.s1.r.c: Dem dey use price for the amount of money and e no decide the number to order.
l-m-h3-b0c40-06.s.s1.o.d: The amount wey dem need this week and the current stock
l-m-h3-b0c40-06.s.s1.explain: The order quantity na the shortage, the amount wey dem need minus the stock. So you need to know the amount wey dem need and the stock.
l-m-h3-b0c40-06.s.s2.model.0: The shortage na the amount wey dem need minus the current stock, so dem fit decide the order quantity only with the two pieces of information.
l-m-h3-b0c40-06.s.s2.model.1: Dem no dey use the price and the supplier location to decide the number, so dem no necessary. The amount wey dem need and the stock na the key.

l-m-h3-b0c40-07.title: Wetin go tell you whether two quantities dey directly proportional?
l-m-h3-b0c40-07.goal: To find out whether two quantities dey directly proportional, identify which standard (information) dem must get, then explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c40-07.material: Table dey wey pair the working time x with the pay y. You wan set standard to judge whether the two quantities dey directly proportional.
l-m-h3-b0c40-07.s.s1.prompt: Wetin you must check to know if dem dey directly proportional?
l-m-h3-b0c40-07.s.s1.o.a: Whether y also increase when x increase
l-m-h3-b0c40-07.s.s1.r.a: Even if dem increase together, e no directly proportional if y÷x change.
l-m-h3-b0c40-07.s.s1.o.b: Whether the value of y÷x always the same
l-m-h3-b0c40-07.s.s1.o.c: Whether the value of y−x always the same
l-m-h3-b0c40-07.s.s1.r.c: When the difference the same, na relationship of adding the same amount, and e no directly proportional.
l-m-h3-b0c40-07.s.s1.o.d: Whether x and y both na natural numbers
l-m-h3-b0c40-07.s.s1.r.d: The kind of numbers no get anything to do with judging direct proportion.
l-m-h3-b0c40-07.s.s1.explain: If dem directly proportional, y÷x always the same. To just increase together no make am directly proportional.
l-m-h3-b0c40-07.s.s2.model.0: Direct proportion na relationship wey the value of y÷x constant, so you must check say y÷x the same for every pair.
l-m-h3-b0c40-07.s.s2.model.1: To just increase together no enough because e also include cases wey get base fee. You must see whether y÷x the same.

l-m-h3-b0c40-08.title: Which information no necessary to find the number of boxes?
l-m-h3-b0c40-08.goal: For the problem of how to divide water bottles into boxes, identify which standard (information) dem must get, then explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c40-08.material: For the warehouse, dem pack 144 water bottles 24 for one box. One bottle cost 600 won. You find the number of boxes wey dem need.
l-m-h3-b0c40-08.s.s1.prompt: Which information dem no use to find the number of boxes?
l-m-h3-b0c40-08.s.s1.o.a: Say wetin you wan find na the number of boxes
l-m-h3-b0c40-08.s.s1.r.a: To know wetin you dey find dey set the direction of the solution.
l-m-h3-b0c40-08.s.s1.r.b: Dem must get the total number to find the number of boxes.
l-m-h3-b0c40-08.s.s1.r.d: The number wey dem put for one box na the divisor, so e necessary.
l-m-h3-b0c40-08.s.s1.explain: The number of boxes na 144÷24=6. Dem no use the 600 won price of one bottle for counting.
l-m-h3-b0c40-08.s.s2.model.0: Dem find the number of boxes by 144÷24=6 and dem no use the price, so 600 won na information wey no necessary.
l-m-h3-b0c40-08.s.s2.model.1: With the total number and the number for each box, the answer don settle, so the price no matter. Dem dey use the price only when dem dey find the total amount of money.

l-m-h3-b0c41-05.title: To know how many m 6cm for the drawing really be
l-m-h3-b0c41-05.goal: Identify which standard (information) dey absolutely necessary to find the real length of length wey dem draw for plan, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c41-05.material: Dem draw one wall as 6cm for the plan. We wan find the real length of this wall before construction.
l-m-h3-b0c41-05.s.s1.prompt: Which information dey absolutely necessary to find the real length?
l-m-h3-b0c41-05.s.s1.o.a: The size of the drawing paper
l-m-h3-b0c41-05.s.s1.r.a: The paper size no tell you the ratio of reduction.
l-m-h3-b0c41-05.s.s1.o.b: The paint color for the wall
l-m-h3-b0c41-05.s.s1.o.c: The date wey dem draw the plan
l-m-h3-b0c41-05.s.s1.r.c: The date no tell you the ratio of reduction.
l-m-h3-b0c41-05.s.s1.o.d: The scale of the plan (for example, 1:50)
l-m-h3-b0c41-05.s.s1.explain: If the scale na 1:50, 1cm for the plan na 50cm for real life. So 6cm na 300cm, wey be 3m.
l-m-h3-b0c41-05.s.s2.model.0: You need to know the scale to know how much 1cm for the plan be for real life, so the scale dey absolutely necessary.
l-m-h3-b0c41-05.s.s2.model.1: The paper size, the color, and the date no tell you the ratio of reduction, so dem no need dem.

l-m-h3-b0c41-06.title: Information wey dem need to find the cost per item
l-m-h3-b0c41-06.goal: Identify which standard (information) dey absolutely necessary to find the average cost of making one item, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c41-06.material: One handmade soap workshop make several soaps at once. We wan find the cost of making one soap (cost per item).
l-m-h3-b0c41-06.s.s1.prompt: Which information dey absolutely necessary to find the cost per item?
l-m-h3-b0c41-06.s.s1.o.a: The selling price and the number of soaps wey dem sell
l-m-h3-b0c41-06.s.s1.r.a: The selling price na the money wey dem receive, no be the money wey dem spend to make dem.
l-m-h3-b0c41-06.s.s1.o.b: Only the number wey dem make
l-m-h3-b0c41-06.s.s1.r.b: If na only the number you know, you no know the total cost, so you no fit divide.
l-m-h3-b0c41-06.s.s1.r.c: If na only the total cost you know, you no know how many to divide by.
l-m-h3-b0c41-06.s.s1.o.d: The total cost wey dem spend and the number wey dem make
l-m-h3-b0c41-06.s.s1.explain: The cost per item na the total cost ÷ the number wey dem make. If one of dem miss, you no fit find am.
l-m-h3-b0c41-06.s.s2.model.0: You must divide the total cost by the number wey dem make to get the cost per item, so dem need the two pieces of information.
l-m-h3-b0c41-06.s.s2.model.1: The selling price na the money wey dem earn from selling, wey different from the cost of making, so dem no need am.

l-m-h3-b0c41-07.goal: Identify which standard (information) dey absolutely necessary to see how monthly sales dey change, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c41-07.material: We wan report how cafe sales for 12 months dey change. Make we think about the standard to choose type of graph.
l-m-h3-b0c41-07.s.s1.prompt: Which one na the most suitable standard to choose graph?
l-m-h3-b0c41-07.s.s1.o.a: Whether e be shape wey easy to draw
l-m-h3-b0c41-07.s.s1.r.a: To fit the purpose matter pass to be easy to draw.
l-m-h3-b0c41-07.s.s1.o.b: Whether the colors bright and dey catch eye
l-m-h3-b0c41-07.s.s1.r.b: Decoration no be standard wey dey help to read data.
l-m-h3-b0c41-07.s.s1.o.c: Whether the change over time clear at one glance
l-m-h3-b0c41-07.s.s1.o.d: Whether dem fit write plenty numbers as text
l-m-h3-b0c41-07.s.s1.r.d: To write plenty numbers no dey make the change visible.
l-m-h3-b0c41-07.s.s1.explain: To show change, line graph wey connect the points and show the rise and fall suitable.
l-m-h3-b0c41-07.s.s2.model.0: E must show the values dey rise and fall over time, so the standard na whether the change clear at one glance.
l-m-h3-b0c41-07.s.s2.model.1: Color and ease no get anything to do with the purpose of the report, so the standard suppose be whether the change visible.

l-m-h3-b0c41-08.title: If the same value show 5 times, the scale accurate?
l-m-h3-b0c41-08.goal: Identify which standard (information) dey absolutely necessary to find out whether scale accurate, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c41-08.material: Dem put standard weight for the same scale 5 times, and e show the same 98g every time. We wan find out whether this scale accurate.
l-m-h3-b0c41-08.s.s1.prompt: Which information dey absolutely necessary to judge whether e accurate?
l-m-h3-b0c41-08.s.s1.o.a: The real mass of the standard weight
l-m-h3-b0c41-08.s.s1.o.b: The fact say all 5 values the same
l-m-h3-b0c41-08.s.s1.r.b: To dey consistent and to dey close to the true value na different thing.
l-m-h3-b0c41-08.s.s1.o.c: The price of the scale and the company wey make am
l-m-h3-b0c41-08.s.s1.r.c: Price no get direct connection with the accuracy of the measurement result.
l-m-h3-b0c41-08.s.s1.o.d: The number of people wey put the weight
l-m-h3-b0c41-08.s.s1.r.d: The number of people no tell you how far e dey from the true value.
l-m-h3-b0c41-08.s.s1.explain: You must compare with the true value (the real mass of the standard weight). If the real mass na 100g, this scale short by 2g every time.
l-m-h3-b0c41-08.s.s2.model.0: You fit only know how wrong e be by comparing the measured value with the true value, so dem need the real mass of the standard weight.
l-m-h3-b0c41-08.s.s2.model.1: Even if the value always the same, e fit far from the true value, so the fact say e the same alone no fit show say e accurate.

l-m-h3-b0c42-02.goal: Work out which information (criterion) dem absolutely need to find out how to compare school lunch satisfaction by grade, then explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c42-02.material: After dem collect di school lunch satisfaction survey, we want compare di satisfaction of Grades 1, 2, and 3. Think about which information di survey suppose ask for.
l-m-h3-b0c42-02.s.s1.prompt: Which information dem absolutely need for comparison by grade?
l-m-h3-b0c42-02.s.s1.o.a: Di order number wey dem receive di survey
l-m-h3-b0c42-02.s.s1.r.a: Di order number no dey tell di grade.
l-m-h3-b0c42-02.s.s1.r.c: Color no dey tell di grade.
l-m-h3-b0c42-02.s.s1.r.d: Di time alone no dey tell which grade e be.

l-m-h3-b0c42-02.s.s2.model.0: Dem must write di grade for each response to divide by grade, so di respondent grade na something dem absolutely need.
l-m-h3-b0c42-02.s.s2.model.1: Di time or di order number no dey tell di grade, so dem no fit use dem for comparison by grade.

l-m-h3-b0c44-08.title: Information wey you need for binomial distribution probability
l-m-h3-b0c44-08.goal: Decide which rule or information important to find the values wey you need to calculate probability with binomial distribution, then explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c44-08.material: Dem roll fair die plenty times, and X na the number of times 6 show. Think about the information wey important to find P(X=2) with the binomial distribution B(n, p) wey X follow.
l-m-h3-b0c44-08.s.s1.o.a: Number of rolls n and the chance p to get 6 for one roll
l-m-h3-b0c44-08.s.s1.o.b: The colour of the die dem roll
l-m-h3-b0c44-08.s.s1.r.b: The die colour no get anything to do with the chance to get 6.
l-m-h3-b0c44-08.s.s1.o.c: The number wey show just before
l-m-h3-b0c44-08.s.s1.r.c: Each try dey independent, so earlier results no change the chance.
l-m-h3-b0c44-08.s.s1.o.d: How hard dem throw the die
l-m-h3-b0c44-08.s.s1.r.d: With fair die, the chance dey the same no matter how hard dem throw am.
l-m-h3-b0c44-08.s.s1.explain: Number of tries n and chance p of success for one try dey determine binomial distribution. With these two values, you fit find P(X=2).
l-m-h3-b0c44-08.s.s2.model.0: n and p dey determine binomial distribution, so you need know the number of rolls and the chance 1/6 to get 6 to find P(X=2).
l-m-h3-b0c44-08.s.s2.model.1: The die colour and earlier results no change the chance, so na only n and p you need.

l-m-h3-b0c44-09.title: Information wey you need to build confidence interval
l-m-h3-b0c44-09.topic: Confidence interval for the population average
l-m-h3-b0c44-09.material: When population standard deviation dey known, we wan build 95% confidence interval for population average from sample average. Think about the other important information apart from sample average.
l-m-h3-b0c44-09.s.s1.prompt: Choose the important information apart from sample average.
l-m-h3-b0c44-09.s.s1.o.a: Sample size and population standard deviation
l-m-h3-b0c44-09.s.s1.o.b: The date wey dem gather the sample data
l-m-h3-b0c44-09.s.s1.r.b: The date no get anything to do with the interval width.
l-m-h3-b0c44-09.s.s1.o.c: Total number of people for the whole population
l-m-h3-b0c44-09.s.s1.r.c: If the population big reach, you no need am to calculate the interval.
l-m-h3-b0c44-09.s.s1.o.d: The biggest value for the sample
l-m-h3-b0c44-09.s.s1.r.d: The biggest value alone no dey determine the interval width.
l-m-h3-b0c44-09.s.s1.explain: The interval width dey come from 1.96×(population standard deviation÷√sample size), so you need sample size and population standard deviation.
l-m-h3-b0c44-09.s.s2.model.0: The interval width dey proportional to population standard deviation divided by √n, so sample size and population standard deviation dey needed.
l-m-h3-b0c44-09.s.s2.model.1: The biggest value or the date no fit determine the width, so you fit build the interval with only sample size and population standard deviation.

l-m-h3-b0c45-05.goal: Work out the standard (information) we really need to find tower height using shadows, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c45-05.material: One old story talk say Thales measure height of tall tower using ratio of stick length to the shadow. For the same time of day, with sunlight coming down slant, you wan find the height.
l-m-h3-b0c45-05.s.s1.prompt: Wetin information we really need to find tower height?
l-m-h3-b0c45-05.s.s1.o.a: Only the length of the tower shadow
l-m-h3-b0c45-05.s.s1.r.a: No standard to compare with the stick, so we no fit know the height.
l-m-h3-b0c45-05.s.s1.o.b: The stick length, the stick shadow, and tower shadow length
l-m-h3-b0c45-05.s.s1.o.c: Only the date we measure the shadows and the weather
l-m-h3-b0c45-05.s.s1.r.c: Date and weather alone no fit tell us ratio of lengths.
l-m-h3-b0c45-05.s.s1.o.d: Thickness of the stick and color of tower shadow
l-m-h3-b0c45-05.s.s1.r.d: Thickness and color no get anything to do with height.
l-m-h3-b0c45-05.s.s1.explain: For the same time of day, ratio of height to shadow length na the same. If you know that ratio from the stick, you fit find height from tower shadow.
l-m-h3-b0c45-05.s.s2.model.0: For the same time of day, ratio of height to shadow na the same, so you need stick length, stick shadow, and tower shadow to find the height.
l-m-h3-b0c45-05.s.s2.model.1: Tower shadow alone no enough because we no know the ratio. We need stick values to work out the ratio.

l-m-h3-b0c45-06.goal: Work out the standard (information) we really need to find whether one candidate win majority of people wey vote, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c45-06.material: For vote with three or more candidates, you wan know whether candidate A get more than half of people wey vote. Think about wetin information we really need.
l-m-h3-b0c45-06.s.s1.o.a: A position and number of candidates
l-m-h3-b0c45-06.s.s1.r.a: Even if candidate come 1st, e fit no get more than half.
l-m-h3-b0c45-06.s.s1.o.b: A number of votes and election date
l-m-h3-b0c45-06.s.s1.r.b: The date no get anything to do with share of votes.
l-m-h3-b0c45-06.s.s1.o.c: A number of votes and total number of votes
l-m-h3-b0c45-06.s.s1.o.d: Number of candidates and number of polling places
l-m-h3-b0c45-06.s.s1.r.d: These two numbers no fit tell us A votes.
l-m-h3-b0c45-06.s.s1.explain: Majority mean more than half of the whole, so you need compare A votes with total votes.
l-m-h3-b0c45-06.s.s2.model.0: Whether na majority depend on whether A votes pass half of all votes, so you need A number of votes and total number of votes.
l-m-h3-b0c45-06.s.s2.model.1: Coming 1st no mean say person get more than half, so you need compare with total votes instead of position.

l-m-h3-b0c45-07.goal: Work out the standard (information) we really need to find if rectangle na golden rectangle, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c45-07.material: Rectangle wey ratio of width to height na golden ratio (about 1.618 : 1) na golden rectangle. You wan identify which rectangles be golden rectangles.
l-m-h3-b0c45-07.s.s1.prompt: Wetin information we really need to tell dem apart?
l-m-h3-b0c45-07.s.s1.r.a: Even with the same area, ratio of width to height fit be many different things.
l-m-h3-b0c45-07.s.s1.r.b: Even with the same perimeter, ratio of width to height fit be many different things.
l-m-h3-b0c45-07.s.s1.r.c: Even with the same diagonal, ratio of width to height fit be many different things.
l-m-h3-b0c45-07.s.s1.explain: To find ratio, you need know both width and height. Area, perimeter, or diagonal alone no decide the ratio.
l-m-h3-b0c45-07.s.s2.model.0: Ratio dey compare two lengths, so you need both width and height to check if e equal 1.618.
l-m-h3-b0c45-07.s.s2.model.1: Area or perimeter na one value, so ratio of width to height fit come out different ways, meaning say dem no fit be the standard.

l-m-h3-b0c45-08.goal: Work out the standard (information) we really need to find whether two notes dey one octave apart, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c45-08.material: Note wey dey one octave higher get 2 times the frequency. If you know frequencies of two notes, you wan tell whether dem dey one octave apart.
l-m-h3-b0c45-08.s.s1.prompt: Wetin standard we really need to tell dem apart?

l-m-h3-b0c45-08.s.s1.r.a: Even with the same instrument, ratio of pitches fit be different.
l-m-h3-b0c45-08.s.s1.r.b: Even if the difference na the same, 100 and 200 dey one octave apart, but 900 and 1000 no be.
l-m-h3-b0c45-08.s.s1.o.c: Frequency of the higher note ÷ frequency of the lower note
l-m-h3-b0c45-08.s.s1.o.d: How long the two notes make sound

l-m-h3-b0c45-08.s.s1.explain: One octave mean say frequency ratio na 2:1. You must judge with ratio, no be difference.
l-m-h3-b0c45-08.s.s2.model.0: Octave mean frequency na 2 times, so just check whether higher note divide by lower note give ratio of 2.

l-m-h3-b0c46-07.material: One survey send questionnaires to millions of people wey dem choose from list wey favor one side, but result far from reality. You wan know whether sample represent everybody.
l-m-h3-b0c46-07.s.s1.prompt: Wetin information you suppose check first?
l-m-h3-b0c46-07.s.s1.o.a: How many questions the survey get
l-m-h3-b0c46-07.s.s1.r.a: Number of questions no fit tell if sample represent everybody.
l-m-h3-b0c46-07.s.s1.o.b: Only whether number of people wey answer big
l-m-h3-b0c46-07.s.s1.r.b: Even if number big, choosing only one kind of people go make result biased.
l-m-h3-b0c46-07.s.s1.o.d: Date wey dem send the questionnaires
l-m-h3-b0c46-07.s.s1.r.d: Date hardly get anything to do with whether sample represent everybody.
l-m-h3-b0c46-07.s.s1.explain: If the way dem choose people favor one side, no matter how big sample be, e no represent everybody.
l-m-h3-b0c46-07.s.s2.model.0: Even big sample get bias if dem choose only certain people, so the way dem choose am matter pass.
l-m-h3-b0c46-07.s.s2.model.1: Big number alone no guarantee say sample represent everybody, so you must check whether dem choose people fairly by chance.

l-m-h3-b0c46-08.title: Wetin you need know to solve Caesar cipher?
l-m-h3-b0c46-08.goal: Choose which standard (information) we really need to find the original text of Caesar cipher message, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c46-08.material: Caesar cipher change alphabet by shifting each letter certain number of places. Person wey receive coded message wan know the original text.
l-m-h3-b0c46-08.s.s1.o.a: Size of paper wey dem write coded message on
l-m-h3-b0c46-08.s.s1.r.a: Paper size no get anything to do with the rule wey change the letters.
l-m-h3-b0c46-08.s.s1.o.b: Number of letters for coded message
l-m-h3-b0c46-08.s.s1.r.b: Number of letters alone no fit tell how many places dem shift am.
l-m-h3-b0c46-08.s.s1.o.c: How many places dem shift am and which direction
l-m-h3-b0c46-08.s.s1.o.d: Time wey dem send coded message
l-m-h3-b0c46-08.s.s1.r.d: Time wey dem send am no get anything to do with rule for changing letters.
l-m-h3-b0c46-08.s.s1.explain: If you know number of places and direction dem shift am, you fit shift back the other way to get original letters.
l-m-h3-b0c46-08.s.s2.model.0: Dem shift each letter by certain number of places, so if you know the number and direction, you fit shift backward to find original text.
l-m-h3-b0c46-08.s.s2.model.1: Time, paper size, and number of letters no be the changing rule, so dem no dey needed to solve am.

l-m-h3-b0c47-06.title: Wetin you need know to tell if pattern get rotational symmetry?
l-m-h3-b0c47-06.goal: To know if pattern get rotational symmetry, decide wetin be necessary information, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c47-06.material: You wan check if traditional pattern get rotational symmetry. Rotational symmetry na when you turn pattern around one point by angle smaller than 360°, e fit exactly on top di original.
l-m-h3-b0c47-06.s.s1.prompt: Wetin information you really need to know if e get rotational symmetry?
l-m-h3-b0c47-06.s.s1.o.a: Length of di pattern outside edge
l-m-h3-b0c47-06.s.s1.r.a: Edge length alone no fit tell you whether e go match when you turn am.
l-m-h3-b0c47-06.s.s1.o.b: Time wey dem make di pattern
l-m-h3-b0c47-06.s.s1.r.b: Time wey dem make am no get anything to do with whether e match when you turn am.
l-m-h3-b0c47-06.s.s1.o.c: Number of colors dem use for di pattern
l-m-h3-b0c47-06.s.s1.r.c: Number of colors no tell you whether e match when you turn am.
l-m-h3-b0c47-06.s.s1.o.d: Whether e match when dem turn am around chosen center
l-m-h3-b0c47-06.s.s1.explain: Rotational symmetry mean say when you choose center and turn by certain angle, e fit on top di original.
l-m-h3-b0c47-06.s.s2.model.0: Rotational symmetry na when e fit on top di original after you turn am, so choose center and angle, turn am, and see whether e match.
l-m-h3-b0c47-06.s.s2.model.1: Color, perimeter, and time no get anything to do with di result of turning, so na only whether e match after you turn am you need check.

l-m-h3-b0c47-07.title: Wetin be di rule to decide place-value number system?
l-m-h3-b0c47-07.goal: To know if number system na place-value system, decide wetin be necessary information, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c47-07.material: Each number system use different symbols and methods. Roman numerals no be place-value system, but Babylonian base-60 system and today's base-10 system be place-value systems.
l-m-h3-b0c47-07.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di rule to decide whether na place-value system?
l-m-h3-b0c47-07.s.s1.o.a: Whether dem write di characters from left to right
l-m-h3-b0c47-07.s.s1.r.a: Writing direction no get anything to do with how dem determine value.
l-m-h3-b0c47-07.s.s1.o.b: Whether same symbol get different value depending on where e dey
l-m-h3-b0c47-07.s.s1.r.c: Babylonian numerals get far fewer symbols and still be place-value system.
l-m-h3-b0c47-07.s.s1.o.d: Whether di symbols come from pictures
l-m-h3-b0c47-07.s.s1.r.d: Shape or origin of symbols no be di rule.
l-m-h3-b0c47-07.s.s1.explain: Whether same symbol get different value depending on where e dey na di key to place-value system.
l-m-h3-b0c47-07.s.s2.model.0: For base 10, 2 mean 2 for ones place and 20 for tens place, so di rule na whether di value change based on place.
l-m-h3-b0c47-07.s.s2.model.1: System fit be place-value system even if number of symbols or writing direction different, so you need check how value change by place.

l-m-h3-b0c47-08.title: School Lunch Survey: Wetin We Need to Say It Represents Everybody?
l-m-h3-b0c47-08.goal: To know if survey results represent di whole school, decide wetin be necessary information, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c47-08.material: To find di share of all students for school wey want better school lunch, dem ask 100 students and 62 support am. Think if e okay to say na opinion of all students be dis result.
l-m-h3-b0c47-08.s.s1.prompt: Wetin information you really need to judge whether e represent everybody?
l-m-h3-b0c47-08.s.s1.o.a: Number of people among di 100 wey support am
l-m-h3-b0c47-08.s.s1.r.a: You don already know how many support am. If you no know how dem choose dem, you no fit judge whether e represent everybody.
l-m-h3-b0c47-08.s.s1.o.b: How dem choose di 100 students from di whole school
l-m-h3-b0c47-08.s.s1.o.c: Average height of di 62 wey agree
l-m-h3-b0c47-08.s.s1.r.c: Height no get anything to do with whether e represent di share of people wey support am.
l-m-h3-b0c47-08.s.s1.o.d: Time wey dem give out di questionnaires
l-m-h3-b0c47-08.s.s1.r.d: Time alone no fit tell you whether e represent everybody.
l-m-h3-b0c47-08.s.s1.explain: If di way dem choose people get bias, di results too go get bias. Whether dem choose randomly na key to representativeness.
l-m-h3-b0c47-08.s.s2.model.0: If di way dem choose people get bias, di results too get bias, so you really need know whether dem choose randomly.
l-m-h3-b0c47-08.s.s2.model.1: You don know di number of people wey support am, so to know if e represent everybody, check how dem choose di 100 instead of height or time. Na why you need dat information.

l-m-h3-b0c47-09.goal: Work out the standard (information) we really need to find whether two notes dey one octave apart, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c47-09.material: Do and Do wey one octave higher sound like notes with same name. To use numbers judge if 2 notes one octave apart, think wetin information you really need.
l-m-h3-b0c47-09.s.s1.r.a: Even for same instrument, frequency dey determine relationship between di pitches.
l-m-h3-b0c47-09.s.s1.o.b: Ratio between frequency of di 2 notes
l-m-h3-b0c47-09.s.s1.r.c: Loudness no get anything to do with pitch of note.
l-m-h3-b0c47-09.s.s1.o.d: Difference between frequency of di 2 notes
l-m-h3-b0c47-09.s.s1.r.d: 220Hz and 440Hz, and 440Hz and 660Hz, get same difference, but na only di first pair be one octave apart.
l-m-h3-b0c47-09.s.s1.explain: One octave mean say frequency ratio na 2:1. Judge with di ratio, no be di difference.
l-m-h3-b0c47-09.s.s2.model.0: If frequency ratio na 2:1, na one octave, so you need know di ratio wey you get when you divide di 2 frequencies.
l-m-h3-b0c47-09.s.s2.model.1: 220 and 440 relate by 2 times, so dem one octave apart, but 440 and 660 get same difference yet dem relate by 1.5 times, so difference no fit tell you.

l-m-h3-b0c48-09.material: Report: "Class A average na 78 and Class B average na 75, so Class A do better." Di 2 classes do same test. Think which information really necessary before you trust dis conclusion.
l-m-h3-b0c48-09.s.s1.prompt: Which information you need most to trust di conclusion?
l-m-h3-b0c48-09.s.s1.o.a: Highest score of one student for Class A
l-m-h3-b0c48-09.s.s1.r.a: You no fit use one student's score compare di whole class.
l-m-h3-b0c48-09.s.s1.o.b: Font size dem use for test paper
l-m-h3-b0c48-09.s.s1.r.b: Font no get anything to do with comparing scores.
l-m-h3-b0c48-09.s.s1.o.c: Date wey dem calculate di average
l-m-h3-b0c48-09.s.s1.r.c: Date no tell you whether you fit trust di difference between averages.
l-m-h3-b0c48-09.s.s1.o.d: Number of students for each class and how spread out di scores be
l-m-h3-b0c48-09.s.s1.explain: To judge whether 3-point difference for average big, you need know how spread out di scores be and how many students dey.
l-m-h3-b0c48-09.s.s2.model.0: If scores spread out plenty, 3-point difference fit happen by chance, so you need know di spread.
l-m-h3-b0c48-09.s.s2.model.1: Highest score or font no tell you about difference across di whole class, so dem no necessary.

l-m-h3-b0c49-05.goal: To find effect of tire air pressure on distance wey bicycle travel, choose which information really necessary and explain why you choose am.

l-m-h3-b0c49-05.s.s1.r.a: Air pressure na variable wey we dey change, so we no fit keep am di same.
l-m-h3-b0c49-05.s.s1.o.c: Name of person wey dey measure
l-m-h3-b0c49-05.s.s1.r.c: Name no get anything to do with distance.
l-m-h3-b0c49-05.s.s1.r.d: Color no affect di distance wey e roll.
l-m-h3-b0c49-05.s.s1.explain: Na only when air pressure be di only difference we fit blame di distance difference on am. If starting speed and slope different, dem fit be di cause.
l-m-h3-b0c49-05.s.s2.model.0: If starting speed and slope change, we no fit know if distance difference come from air pressure, so dem must stay di same.
l-m-h3-b0c49-05.s.s2.model.1: Air pressure na di variable we dey change, so we no fit keep am di same, and things like color no concern di distance.

l-m-h3-b0c49-06.s.s1.r.a: E only include students wey come early, so e hard to represent everybody.
l-m-h3-b0c49-06.s.s1.r.b: Na students with similar taste fit gather.
l-m-h3-b0c49-06.s.s1.r.c: If na only students wey wan answer join, opinions go lean one side.
l-m-h3-b0c49-06.s.s1.o.d: Choose 100 students randomly from list of all students
l-m-h3-b0c49-06.s.s1.explain: Every student must get equal chance to be chosen so sample no lean one side.
l-m-h3-b0c49-06.s.s2.model.0: If you choose randomly from list, every student get equal chance, so e fit represent everybody.
l-m-h3-b0c49-06.s.s2.model.1: Students for front of queue, friends, and volunteers only include some students, so opinions dey lean and representativeness low.

l-m-h3-b0c49-07.goal: To find out about ice cream sales and number of swimming accidents, choose which information really necessary and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c49-07.material: For summer, ice cream sales rise every month, and swimming accidents too rise. Think which information necessary to judge if conclusion "ice cream cause accidents" correct.
l-m-h3-b0c49-07.s.s1.prompt: Wetin information really necessary to judge di conclusion?
l-m-h3-b0c49-07.s.s1.r.a: Shop name no get anything to do with relationship between di 2 values.
l-m-h3-b0c49-07.s.s1.o.b: Entry fee for pool wey accident happen
l-m-h3-b0c49-07.s.s1.r.b: Entry fee alone no fit tell why di 2 values rise together.
l-m-h3-b0c49-07.s.s1.o.c: Records of other things wey fit make both values rise together
l-m-h3-b0c49-07.s.s1.o.d: Prices for each type of ice cream
l-m-h3-b0c49-07.s.s1.r.d: Prices alone no fit tell why di 2 values change together.
l-m-h3-b0c49-07.s.s1.explain: Another factor like temperature fit increase both sales and accidents. Na only with dat record we fit judge.

l-m-h3-b0c49-07.s.s2.model.1: Shop name or price no tell why di 2 values rise together, so dem no necessary.

l-m-h3-b0c49-08.title: Linear Model or Exponential Model: Wetin Separate Dem?
l-m-h3-b0c49-08.goal: To find di type of model wey fit data, choose which information really necessary and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c49-08.material: We measure y when x na 1, 2, 3, 4. We wan decide whether to describe di points with linear model (y=ax+b) or exponential model wey change by same multiple each time. Think which rule needed.
l-m-h3-b0c49-08.s.s1.prompt: Wetin rule really necessary to separate di models?
l-m-h3-b0c49-08.s.s1.o.a: Position of point with biggest y value
l-m-h3-b0c49-08.s.s1.r.a: Position of one point no fit tell how e dey change.
l-m-h3-b0c49-08.s.s1.o.b: Whether number of points na even or odd
l-m-h3-b0c49-08.s.s1.r.b: Whether count even or odd no get anything to do with how e dey change.
l-m-h3-b0c49-08.s.s1.o.c: Whether, when x increase by 1, y change by constant amount or constant multiple
l-m-h3-b0c49-08.s.s1.o.d: Whether y values be whole numbers
l-m-h3-b0c49-08.s.s1.r.d: Being whole number no be rule wey separate di 2 models.
l-m-h3-b0c49-08.s.s1.explain: Line change by same amount, and exponential model change by same multiple. Check di difference to choose model.
l-m-h3-b0c49-08.s.s2.model.0: If y difference stay constant when x rise by 1, na linear; if ratio stay constant, na exponential, so you need dis rule.
l-m-h3-b0c49-08.s.s2.model.1: Position of biggest point and whether e be whole number no show how e change, so dem no fit be di rule.

l-m-h3-b0c49-09.title: Wetin we need to disprove claim wey start with "every"?
l-m-h3-b0c49-09.goal: To find one example wey break claim wey start with “every,” identify which condition (information) you really need, then explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c49-09.material: Claim: “Every odd number na prime.” Think which example you really need to show say dis claim wrong.
l-m-h3-b0c49-09.s.s1.prompt: Which example you really need to break di claim?
l-m-h3-b0c49-09.s.s1.o.a: One number wey no be odd and no be prime
l-m-h3-b0c49-09.s.s1.r.a: E no be odd, so e no concern di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c49-09.s.s1.o.b: One number wey even and prime
l-m-h3-b0c49-09.s.s1.r.b: Even number no be di odd number wey di claim dey talk about.
l-m-h3-b0c49-09.s.s1.o.c: One number wey odd and no be prime
l-m-h3-b0c49-09.s.s1.r.d: No matter how many examples wey fit di claim you collect, di claim no break.
l-m-h3-b0c49-09.s.s1.explain: To break “every odd number,” one number wey odd but no be prime dey enough. For example, 9.
l-m-h3-b0c49-09.s.s2.model.0: 9 odd, but e be 3×3, so e no be prime, and dat one example dey enough to break di claim.
l-m-h3-b0c49-09.s.s2.model.1: Examples wey fit di claim, no matter how many, no fit break am. So you need one example wey meet di condition but make di conclusion wrong.

l-m-h3-b0c50-13.topic: Types of Data and Representative Values
l-m-h3-b0c50-13.goal: Work out which condition (information) really necessary to find representative value for data on how students come to school, then explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0c50-13.material: Dem survey 40 students about how dem come to school (walking, bus, bicycle). You wan choose one representative value for dis data.
l-m-h3-b0c50-13.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di most suitable condition to choose representative value?
l-m-h3-b0c50-13.s.s1.o.a: How big di biggest value be
l-m-h3-b0c50-13.s.s1.r.a: No big value dey for how students come to school.
l-m-h3-b0c50-13.s.s1.o.b: Whether di data get even number of values
l-m-h3-b0c50-13.s.s1.r.b: Whether count even only matter when you find median.
l-m-h3-b0c50-13.s.s1.o.c: Whether di values na names (categories) or numbers
l-m-h3-b0c50-13.s.s1.o.d: Alphabetical order of names of students wey answer
l-m-h3-b0c50-13.s.s1.r.d: Order of names no get anything to do with nature of di values.
l-m-h3-b0c50-13.s.s1.explain: How students come to school na names, no be numbers, so you no fit calculate mean or median. Use mode, di value wey show most often.
l-m-h3-b0c50-13.s.s2.model.0: Di values na names, like walking and bus, so you no fit calculate mean. Therefore, whether dem be names or numbers na di condition you really need.
l-m-h3-b0c50-13.s.s2.model.1: You no fit add or arrange categorical data in order, so you must use di value wey show most often as representative value.

l-m-h3-b0c50-25.goal: Work out information absolutely needed to know sum of interior angles for every triangle na 180 degrees, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c50-25.material: You measure interior angles of some triangles with protractor and confirm sums all about 180 degrees. Now you wan generalize say e true for all triangles.
l-m-h3-b0c50-25.s.s1.r.a: No matter how many you measure, you no fit check every triangle.
l-m-h3-b0c50-25.s.s1.r.b: Even if precise, e no give reason for all triangles.
l-m-h3-b0c50-25.s.s1.o.c: Give logical reason wey work for any triangle
l-m-h3-b0c50-25.s.s1.o.d: Pick and measure only equilateral triangles
l-m-h3-b0c50-25.s.s1.r.d: You no fit generalize from special triangles only.

l-m-h3-b0c50-25.s.s2.model.0: Measurement only check some triangles, so generalization need logical reason wey work for every triangle.
l-m-h3-b0c50-25.s.s2.model.1: If you show with properties of parallel lines that sum be 180 degrees for every triangle, na enough; logic matter pass adding more examples.

l-m-h3-b0d07-03.title: Whether rⁿ Converges: What Do We Need to Know About r?
l-m-h3-b0d07-03.goal: Work out which condition (information) really necessary to find range of r where geometric sequence rⁿ converges, then explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0d07-03.material: You wan decide whether sequence {rⁿ} converge or diverge. Wetin you need know about common ratio r?
l-m-h3-b0d07-03.s.s1.prompt: Which information fully settle whether e converge, without leaving anything out?
l-m-h3-b0d07-03.s.s1.r.b: If r=1, e converge to 1, and dis condition alone go miss am.
l-m-h3-b0d07-03.s.s1.r.c: r=2 positive but diverge, and r=−0.5 negative but converge.
l-m-h3-b0d07-03.s.s1.r.d: r=1/2 no be integer but e converge to 0.
l-m-h3-b0d07-03.s.s1.explain: If −1<r<1, e converge to 0; if r=1, e converge to 1; and if r≤−1 or r>1, e diverge.
l-m-h3-b0d07-03.s.s2.model.0: When r=1, sequence also converge to 1, while if r≤−1 or r>1, e diverge. So you need know whether −1<r≤1.
l-m-h3-b0d07-03.s.s2.model.1: If you only check |r|<1, you miss r=1, so check whether −1<r≤1 to decide exactly if sequence converge.

l-m-h3-b0d07-12.s.s1.r.a: If a=0.5 and r=1, terms stay 0.5, so series diverge.
l-m-h3-b0d07-12.s.s1.r.b: Even if a positive, series diverge when r=2; even if a negative, e converge when r=1/2.

l-m-h3-b0d07-12.s.s1.r.d: If −1<r<0, e converge even though signs dey alternate.
l-m-h3-b0d07-12.s.s1.explain: When a≠0, geometric series converge if |r|<1 and sum na a/(1−r). If |r|≥1, e diverge.
l-m-h3-b0d07-12.s.s2.model.0: For terms to go to 0, |r|<1 must hold. Then partial sums dey close to a/(1−r), so size of common ratio na di condition.
l-m-h3-b0d07-12.s.s2.model.1: Changing a no change whether e converge, so a no be di rule. Whether absolute value of r less than 1 decide convergence.

l-m-h3-b0d08-03.s.s1.explain: Limit na 1/max(a, b). Power of bigger one control numerator and denominator.

l-m-h3-b0d08-03.s.s2.model.1: If a>b, then (b/a)ⁿ→0, so limit na 1/a; if a=b too, na 1/a, so knowing which one bigger determine limit.

l-m-h3-b0d10-31.title: How we measure angle between two planes?
l-m-h3-b0d10-31.goal: Decide what information really needed to find angle formed by two planes, then explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0d10-31.material: We wan find size of angle formed by two intersecting planes (dihedral angle). Decide which two rays to use to measure am.
l-m-h3-b0d10-31.s.s1.prompt: Which rays correct to measure dihedral angle?
l-m-h3-b0d10-31.s.s1.o.a: Two rays drawn on top each other along intersection line
l-m-h3-b0d10-31.s.s1.r.a: If you draw dem along intersection line, both rays point same way, so no angle dey.
l-m-h3-b0d10-31.s.s1.o.b: Two rays drawn perpendicular to intersection line, one on each plane
l-m-h3-b0d10-31.s.s1.o.c: Two rays drawn anyhow, one on each plane
l-m-h3-b0d10-31.s.s1.r.c: Angle between random rays change depending how you choose dem.
l-m-h3-b0d10-31.s.s1.o.d: Two longest segments on each plane
l-m-h3-b0d10-31.s.s1.r.d: Long segment no get fixed direction inside plane.
l-m-h3-b0d10-31.s.s1.explain: From point on intersection line, draw one ray on each plane, both perpendicular to intersection line. Angle between two rays na di dihedral angle.
l-m-h3-b0d10-31.s.s2.model.0: If you use rays perpendicular to intersection line, angle same no matter where you choose point, so angle between planes get one fixed value.
l-m-h3-b0d10-31.s.s2.model.1: Angle of random rays change depending direction you choose, so standard na two rays wey perpendicular to intersection line.

l-m-h3-b0d10-32.title: How we know if sphere and plane meet?
l-m-h3-b0d10-32.goal: Decide which information really needed to find position relationship between sphere and plane, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h3-b0d10-32.material: We wan know how sphere (x−1)² + (y−2)² + (z−3)² = 25 and plane z = k dey positioned (meet, tangent, or no meet). Wetin we suppose compare?
l-m-h3-b0d10-32.s.s1.prompt: Wetin we suppose compare to decide position relationship?
l-m-h3-b0d10-32.s.s1.r.a: Whether k even or odd no concern sphere and plane position.
l-m-h3-b0d10-32.s.s1.o.b: Distance from center to plane, and radius
l-m-h3-b0d10-32.s.s1.o.c: Sum of x-coordinate and y-coordinate for center
l-m-h3-b0d10-32.s.s1.r.c: Position with plane z=k depend on z-coordinate.
l-m-h3-b0d10-32.s.s1.o.d: Volume of sphere and area of plane
l-m-h3-b0d10-32.s.s1.r.d: Plane stretch forever, so you no fit compare its area.
l-m-h3-b0d10-32.s.s1.explain: Distance from center (1,2,3) to plane z=k na |k−3|. If e less than 5 dem meet, if equal dem tangent, and if bigger dem no meet.
l-m-h3-b0d10-32.s.s2.model.0: Sphere and plane position depend on whether distance |k−3| from center to plane bigger or smaller than radius 5, so compare those two.
l-m-h3-b0d10-32.s.s2.model.1: If |k−3|=5 dem tangent, and if e less than 5, circular cross-section form, so we need compare distance with radius.

l-m-h3-b0c33-09.material: You deposit principal of 100×10,000 won at 3% per year simple interest. After 1 year e become 103×10,000 won, after 2 years 106×10,000 won, and after 3 years 109×10,000 won. Find di rule and predict di amount after 5 years.
l-m-h3-b0c33-09.s.s1.prompt: How much be di total amount (principal plus interest) after 5 years?
l-m-h3-b0c33-09.s.s1.r.a: Dat one na di value after 4 years. Dem count one year too few.
l-m-h3-b0c33-09.s.s1.r.c: You multiply by 3% each year. For simple interest, di amount wey dem add dey constant.
l-m-h3-b0c33-09.s.s1.r.d: Dat one na di value after 6 years. Dem count one year too many.
l-m-h3-b0c33-09.s.s1.explain: E dey grow by 3×10,000 won each year, so after 5 years e na 100+3×5=115×10,000 won. For simple interest, only di principal dey earn interest.
l-m-h3-b0c33-09.s.s2.model.0: E dey grow by 3×10,000 won each year, so after 5 years e na 100+3×5=115×10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c33-09.s.s2.model.1: Dem only dey add 3×10,000 won, wey be 3% of di principal, every year, so after 5 years e na 115×10,000 won, wey be 12×10,000 won more than di 103×10,000 won after year 1.

l-m-h3-b0c33-10.material: You deposit principal of 100×10,000 won at 10% per year compound interest. After 1 year e become 110×10,000 won, after 2 years 121×10,000 won, and after 3 years 133.1×10,000 won. Find di rule and predict di amount after 4 years.

l-m-h3-b0c33-10.s.s1.r.b: You add only 10×10,000 won as di last year interest.

l-m-h3-b0c33-10.s.s1.explain: Each year e become 1.1 times di year before, so 133.1×1.1=146.41×10,000 won. Di amount wey dem add dey grow: 10, 11, 12.1.
l-m-h3-b0c33-10.s.s2.model.0: Each year e become 1.1 times di previous year, so after 4 years e na 133.1×1.1=146.41×10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c33-10.s.s2.model.1: Di amount wey dem add dey grow as 10, 11, 12.1, so you must multiply by 1.1 each time instead of to add like simple interest.

l-m-h3-b0c33-11.material: Shop records: at price of 1,000 won, dem sell 90 items for one day, at 1,200 won 80 items, and at 1,400 won 70 items. Find di rule and predict di sales quantity at 1,800 won.

l-m-h3-b0c33-11.s.s1.r.a: Dat one na di value at 1,600 won. You go one step too few.
l-m-h3-b0c33-11.s.s1.r.b: You estimate am roughly halfway. Di rule be say e dey fall by 10 items for every 200 won.
l-m-h3-b0c33-11.s.s1.r.d: Dat one na di value at 2,000 won. You go one step too many.
l-m-h3-b0c33-11.s.s1.explain: Each time di price rise by 200 won, di quantity dey fall by 10. If you go two more steps from 70 at 1,400 won, e give 50.
l-m-h3-b0c33-11.s.s2.model.0: Each time di price rise by 200 won, di quantity dey fall by 10, so at 1,800 won, wey be 400 won more than 1,400 won with 70 items, e na 50.

l-m-h3-b0c33-12.material: Factory records: even if dem make 0 items, di cost na 300×10,000 won, with 10 items 600×10,000 won, with 20 items 900×10,000 won, and with 30 items 1,200×10,000 won. Find di rule and predict di cost to make 50 items.
l-m-h3-b0c33-12.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di total cost to make 50 items?
l-m-h3-b0c33-12.s.s1.r.a: Dat one na di value for 40 items. You go one step too few.
l-m-h3-b0c33-12.s.s1.r.c: You treat di cost as proportional to di quantity. Fixed cost of 300×10,000 won dey.
l-m-h3-b0c33-12.s.s1.r.d: You add di fixed cost of 300×10,000 won one extra time.
l-m-h3-b0c33-12.s.s1.explain: E dey grow by 300×10,000 won for every 10 items and e na 300×10,000 won even at 0 items, so 50 items na 300+30×50=1,800×10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c33-12.s.s2.model.0: E dey grow by 300×10,000 won for every 10 items and e cost 300×10,000 won even at 0 items, so 50 items na 300+1,500=1,800×10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c33-12.s.s2.model.1: Each item cost 30×10,000 won more and fixed cost of 300×10,000 won dey, so di cost of 50 items na 30×50+300=1,800×10,000 won.

l-m-h3-b0c34-09.goal: Find and talk di rule from plenty cases of di quantity supplied wey dey change with price, and check dat rule with one new case.
l-m-h3-b0c34-09.material: Supply records: at price of 100 won, dem supply 20 units, at 200 won, 50 units, and at 300 won, 80 units. Find di rule and predict di quantity supplied wen di price na 500 won.
l-m-h3-b0c34-09.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di quantity supplied at 500 won?
l-m-h3-b0c34-09.s.s1.r.a: 20 units at 100 won, so dem treat am as proportional, 5 times dat one, 100 units.
l-m-h3-b0c34-09.s.s1.r.b: You go only one more step. From 300 won to 500 won na two steps.
l-m-h3-b0c34-09.s.s1.r.d: You go three more steps. 500 won na two steps from 300 won.
l-m-h3-b0c34-09.s.s1.explain: Each time di price go up by 100 won, di quantity go up by 30 units. If you go two more steps from 80 units at 300 won, e give 140 units.
l-m-h3-b0c34-09.s.s2.model.0: Each time di price go up by 100 won, di quantity go up by 30 units, so 500 won, wey be 200 won above 300 won own 80 units, give 80+60=140 units.
l-m-h3-b0c34-09.s.s2.model.1: Di rule na steady increase of 30 units for every 100 won, so if you start from 20 units and rise 400 won to 500 won, e give 20+120=140 units.

l-m-h3-b0c34-10.material: Wen di price na 20, 30, 40, and 50 won, di quantity demanded na 80, 70, 60, and 50 units, and di quantity supplied na 20, 35, 50, and 65 units. Find di rule and work out di price wey di two quantities go become equal.
l-m-h3-b0c34-10.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di price wey di quantity demanded and di quantity supplied equal?
l-m-h3-b0c34-10.s.s1.r.a: At 40 won, di demand na 60 units and di supply na 50 units, so dem still different.
l-m-h3-b0c34-10.s.s1.r.c: At 45 won, di demand na 55 units and di supply na 57.5 units, so dem different.
l-m-h3-b0c34-10.s.s1.r.d: At 50 won, di demand na 50 units and di supply na 65 units, so dem different.
l-m-h3-b0c34-10.s.s1.explain: Di demand dey fall by 10 units for every 10 won, and di supply dey rise by 15 units. At 44 won, di demand and di supply both na 56 units, so dem equal.
l-m-h3-b0c34-10.s.s2.model.0: Di quantity demanded na 100 − price, and di quantity supplied na 1.5 times di price minus 10, so di price wey dem equal na 44 won.

l-m-h3-b0c34-11.topic: Progressive tax (tax wey rise as income rise)
l-m-h3-b0c34-11.goal: Find and talk di rule from plenty cases of tax wey dey change with income brackets, and check dat rule with one new case.
l-m-h3-b0c34-11.material: If di income na 500 × 10,000 won, di tax na 50 × 10,000 won; for 1,000 × 10,000 won, e na 100 × 10,000 won; for 1,500 × 10,000 won, 200 × 10,000 won; and for 2,000 × 10,000 won, 300 × 10,000 won. Find di rule and predict di tax for 3,000 × 10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c34-11.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di tax wen di income na 3,000 × 10,000 won?
l-m-h3-b0c34-11.s.s1.r.a: You apply 10% to everything. Di part wey pass 1,000 × 10,000 won get different rate.
l-m-h3-b0c34-11.s.s1.r.b: You add only 10% for di excess. Di part wey pass 1,000 × 10,000 won na 20%.
l-m-h3-b0c34-11.s.s1.r.d: You apply 20% to everything. Di first 1,000 × 10,000 won na 10%.
l-m-h3-b0c34-11.s.s1.explain: Up to 1,000 × 10,000 won na 10%, and di part wey pass dat one na 20%. 100 × 10,000 won + (2,000 × 10,000 won × 20%) = 500 × 10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c34-11.s.s2.model.0: Dem dey tax up to 1,000 × 10,000 won at 10%, wey be 100 × 10,000 won, and dem dey tax di 2,000 × 10,000 won wey pass dat one at 20%, wey be 400 × 10,000 won, so di total na 500 × 10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c34-11.s.s2.model.1: After 1,000 × 10,000 won, di tax dey rise by 100 × 10,000 won for every 500 × 10,000 won, so dem add 200 × 10,000 won more to di 300 × 10,000 won at 2,000 × 10,000 won, wey make 500 × 10,000 won.

l-m-h3-b0c34-12.title: Wetin go happen if you keep going up 20% and down 20%?
l-m-h3-b0c34-12.goal: Find and talk di rule from plenty cases of values wey dey go up and down again and again, and check dat rule with one new case.
l-m-h3-b0c34-12.material: One value of 100 go up 20% to become 120, then go down 20% to become 96, and go up 20% again to become 115.2. If you follow dis rule, wetin be di next value if e go down 20% dis time?
l-m-h3-b0c34-12.s.s1.r.b: You think say 96 dey repeat. Di base dey change, so e no be di same value.
l-m-h3-b0c34-12.s.s1.r.c: You think say e dey return to di original value.
l-m-h3-b0c34-12.s.s1.r.d: You raise am 20% again. Dis time e must go down.
l-m-h3-b0c34-12.s.s1.explain: 80% of 115.2 na 92.16. Di more e dey go up and down, di more di value dey shrink small small (×1.2×0.8=0.96).
l-m-h3-b0c34-12.s.s2.model.0: Dis time na di turn to go down, so 115.2×0.8=92.16.
l-m-h3-b0c34-12.s.s2.model.1: Each time e go up and then down, di value become 0.96 times, so like 100, 96, 92.16 e no dey return to di original value and e dey keep shrinking.

l-m-h3-b0c35-03.title: Di rule of one deposit wey dey grow every year
l-m-h3-b0c35-03.goal: Find and talk di rule from plenty cases of how one compound-interest deposit dey change each year, and check di rule with one new case.
l-m-h3-b0c35-03.material: You deposit 100 × 10,000 won at 5% every year compound interest, and e become 105 × 10,000 won after 1 year, 110.25 × 10,000 won after 2 years, and about 115.76 × 10,000 won after 3 years. Di same rule dey continue.
l-m-h3-b0c35-03.s.s1.prompt: Which one closest to di amount after 4 years?
l-m-h3-b0c35-03.s.s1.r.a: Dat one na di amount after 3 years. You need to calculate one more year.
l-m-h3-b0c35-03.s.s1.r.b: Dat one na di simple-interest value wey add 5 × 10,000 won each year. Di increase dey get bigger.
l-m-h3-b0c35-03.s.s1.r.d: You notice say di increase dey get bigger but you no use di multiplication rule.
l-m-h3-b0c35-03.s.s1.explain: Each year na 1.05 times di year before, so 100×1.05⁴≈121.55 × 10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c35-03.s.s2.model.0: Di amount dey become 1.05 times each year, so if you multiply di 115.76 × 10,000 won after 3 years by 1.05, e give about 121.6 × 10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c35-03.s.s2.model.1: Di increases dey get bigger: 5, 5.25, 5.51 × 10,000 won, so e na about 121.6 × 10,000 won, more than di simple-interest 120 × 10,000 won.

l-m-h3-b0c35-11.title: Di rule for sales wen di price go up
l-m-h3-b0c35-11.goal: Find and talk di rule from plenty cases of how lunchbox sales dey change with price, and check di rule with one new case.
l-m-h3-b0c35-11.material: Each time dem change di lunchbox price, dem record di daily sales. At 2,000 won e na 900, at 2,500 won e na 800, at 3,000 won e na 700, and at 3,500 won e na 600.
l-m-h3-b0c35-11.s.s1.prompt: If di same rule continue, wetin be di sales at 4,500 won?
l-m-h3-b0c35-11.s.s1.r.a: You make di decrease dey get bigger and bigger.
l-m-h3-b0c35-11.s.s1.r.c: You make di decrease dey get smaller and smaller.
l-m-h3-b0c35-11.s.s1.r.d: Dat one na di value at 4,000 won. At 4,500 won e go down one more time.
l-m-h3-b0c35-11.s.s1.explain: Each time di price rise by 500 won, sales dey fall by 100. At 4,000 won e na 500, and at 4,500 won e na 400.
l-m-h3-b0c35-11.s.s2.model.0: Each time di price rise by 500 won, sales dey fall by 100, so from 600 at 3,500 won e fall two more times to 400.
l-m-h3-b0c35-11.s.s2.model.1: Di change for sales na always −100, di same, so 4,000 won give 500 and 4,500 won give 400.

l-m-h3-b0c35-18.goal: Find and state di rule from some cases of population wey dey reduce every year, then check di rule for one new case.
l-m-h3-b0c35-18.material: One town population na 50,000 for 2020, 47,500 for 2021, and 45,125 for 2022. Suppose e continue to change by di same rule.
l-m-h3-b0c35-18.s.s1.prompt: Which one near di population for 2023 pass?
l-m-h3-b0c35-18.s.s1.r.a: Dis one na di value wey you go get if you multiply by 0.9 wrongly.
l-m-h3-b0c35-18.s.s1.r.b: Dis one na di value wey you go get if you subtract 2,500 every year. Di amounts of decrease no be di same.
l-m-h3-b0c35-18.s.s1.r.d: Dis one just use di 2022 value as e dey.
l-m-h3-b0c35-18.s.s1.explain: E dey reduce by 5% each year, so dem go multiply am by 0.95. 45,125×0.95≈42,869, so e be about 42,900.
l-m-h3-b0c35-18.s.s2.model.0: Di population dey become 0.95 times as big each year, so if you multiply 45,125 by 0.95, e go be about 42,900.
l-m-h3-b0c35-18.s.s2.model.1: Di decreases of 2,500 and 2,375 no be di same, so dem calculate am as 5% decrease, no be constant decrease.

l-m-h3-b0c35-29.title: How to find the break-even point from profit table
l-m-h3-b0c35-29.goal: Find and talk the rule from some cases for profit table by sales volume, then check the rule with new case.
l-m-h3-b0c35-29.material: One shop daily sales and profit be like this: 0 items −6,000 won, 10 items −3,500 won, 20 items −1,000 won, and 30 items +1,500 won. As sales dey rise, profit dey change by one steady rule.
l-m-h3-b0c35-29.s.s1.prompt: For which sales volume profit first go pass 0 won?
l-m-h3-b0c35-29.s.s1.r.a: For 24 items, profit na 0 won, wey be the break-even point. E never pass 0 won yet.
l-m-h3-b0c35-29.s.s1.r.c: Profit dey, but profit also show for smaller number of items.
l-m-h3-b0c35-29.s.s1.r.d: Na the first profit value wey show for the table. The rule fit help you find smaller number.
l-m-h3-b0c35-29.s.s1.explain: E dey grow by 2,500 won every 10 items, wey be 250 won for each item. E na 0 won for 24 items and 250 won for 25 items.
l-m-h3-b0c35-29.s.s2.model.0: Profit dey grow by 2,500 won every 10 items, wey be 250 won for each item, and e na 0 won for 24 items, so e pass 0 from 25 items.
l-m-h3-b0c35-29.s.s2.model.1: If you start from −6,000 and add 250 won for each item, e go reach 0 for 24 items and e first go positive for 25 items.

l-m-h3-b0c35-34.title: How to find the rule of price and quantity supplied
l-m-h3-b0c35-34.goal: Find and talk the rule from some cases of how the quantity supplied dey change with price, then check the rule with new case.
l-m-h3-b0c35-34.material: One farm set im daily supply (boxes) as 10, 16, 22, 28 when the price (thousand won) na 30, 40, 50, 60. Suppose the same rule continue.
l-m-h3-b0c35-34.s.s1.prompt: When the price na 70 thousand won, how much be the supply?
l-m-h3-b0c35-34.s.s1.r.a: E think say the increase go reduce to 4 instead of 6.
l-m-h3-b0c35-34.s.s1.r.c: E think say the increase go grow to 8.
l-m-h3-b0c35-34.s.s1.explain: Every time the price rise by 10, the supply dey grow by 6 boxes. E na 28 for 60, so for 70 e go be 34 boxes.
l-m-h3-b0c35-34.s.s2.model.0: Every time the price rise by 10, the supply dey grow by 6, so na 28 plus 6, wey be 34 boxes.
l-m-h3-b0c35-34.s.s2.model.1: 10, 16, 22, 28 all differ by the same 6, so the next value na 28+6=34.

l-m-h3-b0c36-09.title: Wetin happen to the entries when you raise matrix to powers?
l-m-h3-b0c36-09.goal: Find and state the rule from several cases of how the upper-right entry dey change for matrix powers, then check the rule for one new case.
l-m-h3-b0c36-09.material: When M=(1 2; 0 1), M²=(1 4; 0 1), M³=(1 6; 0 1), and M⁴=(1 8; 0 1). Find the rule for how the upper-right entry dey change.
l-m-h3-b0c36-09.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be the upper-right entry of M⁵?
l-m-h3-b0c36-09.s.s1.r.b: You confuse am with the square of the exponent 5.
l-m-h3-b0c36-09.s.s1.r.c: Although dem dey add 2 every time, you see am as e dey grow by factor of 2 every time.
l-m-h3-b0c36-09.s.s1.r.d: You assume say e dey grow by 4 every time.
l-m-h3-b0c36-09.s.s1.explain: The entries na 2, 4, 6, 8, dem dey grow by 2 every time. For the n-th power e be 2n, so for M⁵ e be 10.
l-m-h3-b0c36-09.s.s2.model.0: The entries of M, M², M³, M⁴ na 2, 4, 6, 8, dem dey grow by 2 every time, so for M⁵ e be 10.
l-m-h3-b0c36-09.s.s2.model.1: The upper-right entry of the n-th power look like 2n, so if n=5 e be 10, and the rule hold.

l-m-h3-b0c36-10.title: Sample size and how the sample mean spread
l-m-h3-b0c36-10.goal: Find and state the rule from several cases of how the standard deviation of the sample mean dey change with sample size, then check the rule for one new case.
l-m-h3-b0c36-10.material: For population wey get standard deviation 12, we find the standard deviation of the sample mean for each sample size n. E be 6 for n=4, 4 for n=9, and 3 for n=16.
l-m-h3-b0c36-10.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be the standard deviation of the sample mean when n=36?
l-m-h3-b0c36-10.s.s1.r.b: You assume say the value go half, as if n double.
l-m-h3-b0c36-10.s.s1.r.c: You divide by n instead of √n.
l-m-h3-b0c36-10.s.s1.r.d: You assume say no change dey from the value for n=16.
l-m-h3-b0c36-10.s.s1.explain: The value na 12÷√n. For n=4, 9, 16 e give 6, 4, 3, and for n=36 e be 12÷6=2.
l-m-h3-b0c36-10.s.s2.model.0: When n na 4, 9, 16, the values na 12 divided by 2, 3, 4, so the rule na to divide by √n, and for n=36 e be 12÷6=2.
l-m-h3-b0c36-10.s.s2.model.1: When the sample become 4 times as big, the spread go half, so e dey inversely proportional to √n, and for n=36 e be 2.

l-m-h3-b0c36-11.title: The trail of gradient descent
l-m-h3-b0c36-11.goal: Find and state the rule from several cases of how the position dey change for gradient descent, then check the rule for one new case.
l-m-h3-b0c36-11.material: We dey find the minimum of f(x)=x² with gradient descent. The learning rate na 0.1 and the starting point na x=5, and with each step x change like this: 5 → 4 → 3.2 → 2.56.
l-m-h3-b0c36-11.s.s1.prompt: After the next step (the fourth move), about how big x go be?
l-m-h3-b0c36-11.s.s1.r.a: You assume say dem dey subtract the same amount every time and you estimate without using the pattern.
l-m-h3-b0c36-11.s.s1.r.c: You subtract the last decrease, 0.64, again. But the decrease dey get smaller every time.
l-m-h3-b0c36-11.s.s1.r.d: You think say e dey go down by 1 every time.
l-m-h3-b0c36-11.s.s2.model.0: 5, 4, 3.2, 2.56 each become 0.8 times the one before am, so the next one na 2.56×0.8=2.048.
l-m-h3-b0c36-11.s.s2.model.1: The slope 2x dey get smaller, so the decrease dey get smaller too. Instead of to subtract constant amount, multiply by 0.8 to get 2.048.

l-m-h3-b0c41-11.title: To find the fee rule from parking fee table
l-m-h3-b0c41-11.goal: From several cases of parking fees by parking time, find and state the rule, and check that rule with one new case.
l-m-h3-b0c41-11.material: The first 30 minutes cost 1000 won, 40 minutes cost 1500 won, 50 minutes cost 2000 won, and 60 minutes cost 2500 won. After 30 minutes, the fee dey go up in 10-minute units.
l-m-h3-b0c41-11.s.s1.prompt: Using this rule, how much be the parking fee for 85 minutes?
l-m-h3-b0c41-11.s.s1.r.b: E calculate proportionally without to round up the time wey under 10 minutes.
l-m-h3-b0c41-11.s.s1.r.d: E round 55 minutes down and count only 5 times. The remaining 5 minutes also na one unit.
l-m-h3-b0c41-11.s.s1.explain: If dem round up the 55 minutes after the 30 minutes in 10-minute units, e be 6 times. 1000+6×500=4000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c41-11.s.s2.model.0: The 55 minutes after 30 minutes no be 5.5 times but dem round up to 6 times, so e be 1000+3000=4000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c41-11.s.s2.model.1: The fee dey go up 500 won for every 10 minutes wey pass, and even 5 minutes dem go charge as one unit, so you add 6 times.

l-m-h3-b0c41-12.title: To find the rule for two discounts one after the other
l-m-h3-b0c41-12.goal: From several cases of the total discount rate of consecutive discounts, find and state the rule, and check that rule with one new case.
l-m-h3-b0c41-12.material: If you take 20% off the list price and then take another 10% off, e give total of 28% off, 10% and 10% give 19%, and 50% and 50% give 75% off. Find the rule for consecutive discounts.
l-m-h3-b0c41-12.s.s1.prompt: Using the rule, wetin be the total percent if you take 30% off and then take another 20% off?
l-m-h3-b0c41-12.s.s1.r.a: E add the two discount rates. The extra discount apply to the reduced price.
l-m-h3-b0c41-12.s.s1.r.c: E multiply the discount rates together. You need to multiply the remaining ratios.
l-m-h3-b0c41-12.s.s1.r.d: E read the remaining ratio of 56% as the discount rate.
l-m-h3-b0c41-12.s.s1.explain: Multiply the remaining ratios. 0.7×0.8=0.56, so 56% remain and 44% na discount.
l-m-h3-b0c41-12.s.s2.model.0: If you multiply the remaining ratios e give 0.8×0.9=0.72, wey be 28% off, so 0.7×0.8=0.56, that one mean 44% off.
l-m-h3-b0c41-12.s.s2.model.1: If you add the discount rates e give 20+10=30, wey differ from 28, so the rule of multiplying the remaining ratios correct.

l-m-h3-b0c42-03.material: School P (400, 300, 300 students by grade) pick 100 students as 40, 30, 30. School Q (500, 300, 200 students) pick 50 students as 25, 15, 10. Find di rule for picking.
l-m-h3-b0c42-03.s.s1.prompt: How you go pick 40 students for School R (600, 300, 100 students by grade)?
l-m-h3-b0c42-03.s.s1.r.b: E pick fewer from di larger grade, e assign am for reverse of di headcounts.
l-m-h3-b0c42-03.s.s1.r.c: E use School Q ratio of 5:3:2 as e dey.

l-m-h3-b0c42-03.s.s2.model.0: R grade ratio na 6:3:1, so to divide 40 students for di same ratio give 24, 12, and 4 students.
l-m-h3-b0c42-03.s.s2.model.1: Di previous two schools sample sizes proportional to di grade headcounts too, so dem pick R by di headcount ratio too. 60% of 40 students na 24 students.

l-m-h3-b0c42-13.goal: From several cases of common factor behind two values wey dey change together, find and state the rule, and check that rule with one new case.
l-m-h3-b0c42-13.material: Cases wey dey grow and shrink together: ① vocabulary and height (age) ② air conditioner sales and drink sales (temperature) ③ reading score and shoe size (grade). Apply this rule to 'umbrella sales and the number of late arrivals'.
l-m-h3-b0c42-13.s.s1.prompt: When umbrella sales and the number of late arrivals grow together, which explanation suitable?
l-m-h3-b0c42-13.s.s1.o.a: Dem sell plenty umbrellas, so students dey late
l-m-h3-b0c42-13.s.s1.r.a: E assume say one na the cause of the other.
l-m-h3-b0c42-13.s.s1.o.b: Students dey late, so dem sell plenty umbrellas
l-m-h3-b0c42-13.s.s1.r.b: E assume the cause and effect the wrong way round.
l-m-h3-b0c42-13.s.s1.o.c: The color of the umbrella decide whether you go late
l-m-h3-b0c42-13.s.s1.r.c: E make up new relationship wey no get basis.
l-m-h3-b0c42-13.s.s1.o.d: Rainy days fit don increase the two
l-m-h3-b0c42-13.s.s1.explain: Like the earlier cases, behind two values wey dey change together, 3rd factor fit dey wey affect the two. For here, rain suitable.
l-m-h3-b0c42-13.s.s2.model.0: For ① to ③, 3rd factor like age, temperature, or grade move the two values together, so for umbrellas and late arrivals too, rain fit be the common cause.
l-m-h3-b0c42-13.s.s2.model.1: Before you assume say one cause the other, you must look for factor wey affect the two, so rainy days suitable pass.

l-m-h3-b0c42-19.title: Wetin go happen to the expected value if the prize rule change?
l-m-h3-b0c42-19.topic: How to transform the expected value
l-m-h3-b0c42-19.goal: Look some cases of the expected value of prize rule wey change, talk the rule wey you find, then check am with new case.
l-m-h3-b0c42-19.material: We look the expected value of Y, wey dem make by changing the rule from the prize X. E(X)=3, Y=2X → 6. E(X)=5, Y=X+4 → 9. E(X)=2, Y=3X−1 → 5. Find the rule.
l-m-h3-b0c42-19.s.s1.prompt: When E(X)=10, wetin be the expected value of Y=0.5X+3?
l-m-h3-b0c42-19.s.s1.r.a: Dem leave out the 3 wey dem add.
l-m-h3-b0c42-19.s.s1.r.b: Dem multiply the 3 wey dem add by 0.5 too.
l-m-h3-b0c42-19.s.s1.r.d: Dem leave out the 0.5 wey dem multiply, and add only 3.
l-m-h3-b0c42-19.s.s1.explain: The expected value of Y=aX+b na a×E(X)+b. 0.5×10+3=8.
l-m-h3-b0c42-19.s.s2.model.0: For the cases, 2×3=6, 5+4=9, 3×2−1=5, so dem multiply the number wey dem multiply with the expected value and dem add the number wey dem add, wey give 0.5×10+3=8.
l-m-h3-b0c42-19.s.s2.model.1: The expected value of Y na the same formula wey dem apply to the expected value of X, so if you put 10 e give 0.5×10+3=8.

l-m-h3-b0c42-25.material: From one population we draw samples of size 2 with replacement and find all the sample means wey fit happen. For the population {1,3} the mean of the sample means na 2, and for the population {1,2,6} e na 3.
l-m-h3-b0c42-25.s.s1.prompt: For the population {2,2,8}, wetin be the mean of all the sample means?
l-m-h3-b0c42-25.s.s1.r.a: Dem use the median 2. E no fit the earlier {1,2,6} case.
l-m-h3-b0c42-25.s.s1.r.c: Dem use the middle of the smallest and biggest values (2 and 8).

l-m-h3-b0c42-25.s.s2.model.0: {1,3} give 2 and {1,2,6} give 3, equal to the population mean and different from the median, so {2,2,8} also give mean of 4.
l-m-h3-b0c42-25.s.s2.model.1: We confirm for the two earlier cases the rule say the mean of the sample means equal the population mean, so (2+2+8)÷3=4.
