l-m-h3-b0c43-12.goal: Find and talk one rule from plenty cases of predicted sales for different ad costs, then check the rule with one new case.
l-m-h3-b0c43-12.material: For ad cost of x ten-thousand won, the predicted sales na y ten-thousand won. When x na 0, y na 50; when x na 10, y na 80; when x na 20, y na 110. Find the rule.
l-m-h3-b0c43-12.s.s1.prompt: When the ad cost na 35 ten-thousand won, wetin be the predicted sales?
l-m-h3-b0c43-12.s.s1.r.a: E add the ad cost 35 as e be to the base 50.
l-m-h3-b0c43-12.s.s1.r.b: E only calculate 35×3 and leave the base 50.
l-m-h3-b0c43-12.s.s1.r.d: E add 35×3 again to 110. But 110 don already be the value when the ad cost na 20.
l-m-h3-b0c43-12.s.s1.explain: When ad cost go up by 10, sales go up by 30, so e be 3 for every 1. If you add 3×35 to the base 50 e give 155.
l-m-h3-b0c43-12.s.s2.model.0: Every time x go up by 10, y go up by 30, so e be 3 for every 1, and y na 50 when x na 0. So 50+3×35=155 ten-thousand won.
l-m-h3-b0c43-12.s.s2.model.1: For the cases, y=50+3x fit every value, so if you put 35 e give the prediction 50+105=155.

l-m-h3-b0c43-18.title: How dem dey find di average number of successes?
l-m-h3-b0c43-18.goal: Find and state one rule from some examples of average number of successes for repeated trials, then check di rule with one new example.
l-m-h3-b0c43-18.material: When dem do trial n times and success probability each time na p, di average number of successes na 5 for n=10, p=0.5, 2 for n=20, p=0.1, and 6 for n=30, p=0.2. Find di rule.
l-m-h3-b0c43-18.s.s1.prompt: When n=50 and p=0.04, wetin be di average number of successes?
l-m-h3-b0c43-18.s.s1.r.b: E use di failure probability 0.96 and calculate 50×0.96.
l-m-h3-b0c43-18.s.s1.r.c: E treat probability p itself as di average.
l-m-h3-b0c43-18.s.s1.r.d: E add n and p together.
l-m-h3-b0c43-18.s.s1.explain: Average number of successes na n×p. 10×0.5=5, 20×0.1=2, 30×0.2=6, so 50×0.04=2.
l-m-h3-b0c43-18.s.s2.model.0: All di three examples follow n×p, so when n=50 and p=0.04, na 50×0.04=2.
l-m-h3-b0c43-18.s.s2.model.1: Out of n trials, di share of successes na p, so di average na n multiply by p, and dis rule fit all di three examples.

l-m-h3-b0c44-10.material: For population wey standard deviation na 12, we change sample size n and find the standard deviation of sample average: e be 6 when n=4, 3 when n=16, and 1.5 when n=64.
l-m-h3-b0c44-10.s.s1.prompt: Using the rule, wetin be the value when n=256?

l-m-h3-b0c44-10.s.s1.r.c: No rule dey make the value become 3/4 of the old one when n become 4 times bigger.
l-m-h3-b0c44-10.s.s1.explain: Every time n become 4 times bigger, the value become half. 12÷√256=12÷16=0.75.
l-m-h3-b0c44-10.s.s2.model.0: Every time n become 4 times bigger, the value become half, so na half of 1.5, wey be 0.75.
l-m-h3-b0c44-10.s.s2.model.1: Standard deviation na 12÷√n, so when n=256 e become 12÷16=0.75.

l-m-h3-b0c44-11.goal: Look at some cases of the average and variance of binomial distribution, talk the rule wey you find, and check am with one new case.
l-m-h3-b0c44-11.material: Na binomial distribution where dem repeat one try with success chance 0.2 n times. When n=10 the average na 2 and variance na 1.6; when n=20 the average na 4 and variance na 3.2; when n=30 the average na 6 and variance na 4.8.
l-m-h3-b0c44-11.s.s1.prompt: Using the rule, wetin be the variance when n=40?
l-m-h3-b0c44-11.s.s1.r.a: 4.8 na the variance when n=30. As n dey increase, variance dey increase too.
l-m-h3-b0c44-11.s.s1.r.b: 32 na the average number of failures. E no be variance.
l-m-h3-b0c44-11.s.s1.r.d: 8 na the average when n=40. Variance and average no be the same thing.
l-m-h3-b0c44-11.s.s1.explain: Variance na 0.8 times the average (=1−0.2). When n=40, e be 0.8 times the average 8, wey be 6.4.
l-m-h3-b0c44-11.s.s2.model.0: Variance na 0.8 times the average, so when n=40 e be 0.8 times the average 8, wey be 6.4.
l-m-h3-b0c44-11.s.s2.model.1: Every time n increase by 10, variance increase by 1.6, so add 1.6 to 4.8 and you get 6.4.

l-m-h3-b0c44-12.goal: Look at some cases of standard deviation when dem change scores, talk the rule wey you find, and check am with one new case.
l-m-h3-b0c44-12.material: The average score na 60 and standard deviation na 10. If you add 5 to every score, average go become 65 and standard deviation remain 10; if you multiply every score by 2, average go become 120 and standard deviation go become 20.
l-m-h3-b0c44-12.s.s1.prompt: If you multiply every score by 3 and subtract 4, wetin be the standard deviation?
l-m-h3-b0c44-12.s.s1.r.b: Adding or subtracting values no dey affect the standard deviation.
l-m-h3-b0c44-12.s.s1.r.c: Subtracting a number no dey change the spread. E only change by the number wey you multiply am by.
l-m-h3-b0c44-12.s.s1.r.d: If you multiply, the standard deviation sef go increase by the number wey you multiply by.
l-m-h3-b0c44-12.s.s1.explain: Adding or subtracting no dey change the standard deviation, but multiplication make am bigger by the number wey you multiply by. 10×3=30.
l-m-h3-b0c44-12.s.s2.model.0: Adding or subtracting move all the values together, so the spread remain the same; na only the 3 times wey count, giving 30.
l-m-h3-b0c44-12.s.s2.model.1: When we multiply by 2, the standard deviation sef become 2 times. So for 3 times, e be 30, and subtracting 4 no get effect.

l-m-h3-b0c44-13.goal: Look at some cases of the proportion around the mean for normal distribution, talk about the rule wey you find, then check the rule with one new case.
l-m-h3-b0c44-13.material: Test scores follow normal distribution with mean 70 and standard deviation 10. About 68% of students score between 60 and 80, about 95% between 50 and 90, and about 99.7% between 40 and 100.
l-m-h3-b0c44-13.s.s1.prompt: Using the rule, about wetin percent of students score 90 or more?
l-m-h3-b0c44-13.s.s1.r.a: 5% na the total for 50 or below and 90 or above. You only need find one side.
l-m-h3-b0c44-13.s.s1.r.b: 16% na the proportion of scores wey be 80 or more.
l-m-h3-b0c44-13.s.s1.r.d: 0.15% na the proportion of scores wey be 100 or more.
l-m-h3-b0c44-13.s.s1.explain: 50 to 90 na 95%, so if you split the outside 5% between the two sides, you get about 2.5% for 90 or more.
l-m-h3-b0c44-13.s.s2.model.0: 50 to 90 na 95%, so if you split the outside 5% between the two sides, you get 2.5% for 90 or more.
l-m-h3-b0c44-13.s.s2.model.1: Normal distribution dey balanced for left and right. So 90 or more and 50 or below equal each other and total 5%, making one side 2.5%.

l-m-h3-b0c45-09.title: Pattern dey for sum of rows of Pascal triangle?
l-m-h3-b0c45-09.goal: Find and talk about one pattern from different examples of sum of each Pascal triangle row, then check the pattern with a new example.
l-m-h3-b0c45-09.material: For Pascal triangle, when you add all the numbers for each row, row 1 na 1, row 2 (1 1) na 2, row 3 (1 2 1) na 4, row 4 (1 3 3 1) na 8, and row 5 na 16.
l-m-h3-b0c45-09.s.s1.prompt: As you follow di pattern, wetin be di sum for row 7?
l-m-h3-b0c45-09.s.s1.r.a: Na 2 times di sum for row 5, 16, wey give di sum for row 6.
l-m-h3-b0c45-09.s.s1.r.b: You look am as 7×7. Di sum dey become 2 times for each row.
l-m-h3-b0c45-09.s.s1.r.d: You multiply 2 by itself 7 times. Row 1 na 1, so na only 6 times you go multiply.
l-m-h3-b0c45-09.s.s1.explain: Di sum dey become 2 times for each row. Since row 1 na 1, di sum for row n na 2 wey you multiply (n−1) times, and row 7 na 64.
l-m-h3-b0c45-09.s.s2.model.0: E dey become 2 times each time: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, so row 6 na 32 and row 7 na 64.
l-m-h3-b0c45-09.s.s2.model.1: Di sum for row n na 2 wey you multiply (n−1) times. For row 7, 2 wey you multiply 6 times na 64, so na correct.

l-m-h3-b0c45-10.title: Pattern dey for di sum of one line for magic square?
l-m-h3-b0c45-10.goal: Find pattern from some examples of di sum of one line for magic square, talk am, then check di pattern with new example.
l-m-h3-b0c45-10.material: N×N magic squares dey, wey dem arrange numbers from 1 to n² so say di sum for all rows, columns and diagonals equal. For 3×3, di sum for one line na 15, and for 4×4, na 34.
l-m-h3-b0c45-10.s.s1.prompt: Find di pattern and work out di sum for one line of 5×5 magic square.
l-m-h3-b0c45-10.s.s1.r.a: You add 19, di difference between 15 and 34. Di increase for di sum no dey constant.
l-m-h3-b0c45-10.s.s1.r.c: You guess 5×14. You need divide di total sum by di number of lines.
l-m-h3-b0c45-10.s.s1.r.d: You choose multiple of 5 without reason. Calculate am with di pattern.
l-m-h3-b0c45-10.s.s1.explain: Di sum for one line na di sum of numbers from 1 to n², divided by di number of lines n. For 5×5, 325÷5=65.
l-m-h3-b0c45-10.s.s2.model.0: For 3×3, 45÷3=15, and for 4×4, 136÷4=34, so divide di total sum by n. For 5×5, 325÷5=65.
l-m-h3-b0c45-10.s.s2.model.1: Di sum of all di numbers dey share equally among n lines, so one line na total sum ÷ n. So na 65.

l-m-h3-b0c45-11.title: After how many years di same sexagenary year go come again?
l-m-h3-b0c45-11.goal: Find pattern from some examples of how many years e take make sexagenary names match again for di first time, talk am, then check di pattern with new example.
l-m-h3-b0c45-11.material: Year names dey pair 10 heavenly stems and 12 earthly branches in order. After Gapja come Eulchuk, Byeongin, … 10 years after Gapja year, only di stem still be di same; 12 years after, na only di branch be di same.
l-m-h3-b0c45-11.s.s1.prompt: How many years later go di first year wey get exactly di same stem and branch as Gapja year?
l-m-h3-b0c45-11.s.s1.r.a: You add 10 and 12. You need find di year wey both cycles match for di same time.
l-m-h3-b0c45-11.s.s1.r.b: Di stems dey same but di branches different. Di remainder of 30÷12 na 6.
l-m-h3-b0c45-11.s.s1.r.c: E match for one year, but e no be di first year wey e come round again.
l-m-h3-b0c45-11.s.s1.explain: Every 60 years, wey be di least common multiple of 10 and 12, di stem and branch match together for di first time. Na why dem call am 60-year cycle.
l-m-h3-b0c45-11.s.s2.model.0: Di stems dey repeat every 10 years and di branches every 12 years, so di first year wey both match together na 60 years later, di least common multiple of 10 and 12.
l-m-h3-b0c45-11.s.s2.model.1: 30 years later, na only di stem be di same and di branch dey 6 steps away, so e no work. Na why 60 years later na di first time.

l-m-h3-b0c45-12.goal: Find pattern from some examples of di number of triangles for each stage of Sierpinski triangle, talk am, then check di pattern with new example.

l-m-h3-b0c46-10.material: To pick out prime numbers from 1 to N, cross out multiples of small primes. For 30 or less, up to 2, 3, 5 enough; for 50 or less, up to 2, 3, 5, 7; and for 100 or less, up to 7 still enough.

l-m-h3-b0c46-10.s.s1.r.d: 17²=289 bigger than 200, so we no need 17.
l-m-h3-b0c46-10.s.s1.explain: You only need cross out up to prime p wey p² be N or less. 13²=169≤200<17², so reach 13.
l-m-h3-b0c46-10.s.s2.model.0: Composite number get one prime factor wey square na N or less, so cross out reach 13, the biggest prime with p²≤200.
l-m-h3-b0c46-10.s.s2.model.1: If you cross out only reach 11, 13×13=169 go remain, but 17²=289>200, so 13 enough.

l-m-h3-b0c47-13.title: Every how many years di same stem-branch year dey come again?
l-m-h3-b0c47-13.goal: Find rule from some examples of how stem-branch names of years repeat, state am, then check am with new example.
l-m-h3-b0c47-13.material: Old calendar name each year by pairing 10 heavenly stems and 12 earthly branches in order. 1984 na Gapja, 1985 na Eulchuk, 1986 na Byeongin, and 1987 na Jeongmyo.
l-m-h3-b0c47-13.s.s1.prompt: Which be di first year after 1984 wey go be Gapja again?
l-m-h3-b0c47-13.s.s1.r.a: Na only di stem return to Gap (Gapsul). Di branch never return yet.
l-m-h3-b0c47-13.s.s1.r.b: Na only di branch return to Ja (Byeongja). Di stem never return yet.
l-m-h3-b0c47-13.s.s1.r.c: Di stem na Gap but di branch na Jin (Gapjin).
l-m-h3-b0c47-13.s.s1.explain: Di stems return every 10 years and di branches every 12 years. Dem come together again after 60 years, di least common multiple of 10 and 12.
l-m-h3-b0c47-13.s.s2.model.0: Di stems repeat every 10 years and di branches every 12 years, so di year wey both match for same time na 60 years later, 2044.
l-m-h3-b0c47-13.s.s2.model.1: For 1994 na only trunk match, and for 1996 na only branch match, so 60 years, wey be least common multiple of 10 and 12, must pass.

l-m-h3-b0c48-10.material: Mark n points on circle and connect every pair with line part. For n=2, 3, 4, 5, line parts na 1, 3, 6, 10. Use di rule to predict when n=7.
l-m-h3-b0c48-10.s.s1.prompt: Wetin you get if you predict n=7 with rule wey fit all di examples?
l-m-h3-b0c48-10.s.s1.r.b: When n=3 e give 6, wey no match di 3 for examples.
l-m-h3-b0c48-10.s.s1.r.c: When n=4 e give 5, wey no match di 6 for examples.
l-m-h3-b0c48-10.s.s1.r.d: When n=4 e give 8, wey no match di 6 for examples.
l-m-h3-b0c48-10.s.s1.explain: Each point connect to n−1 other points, but each line part count 2 times, so e na n(n−1)/2. For n=7, e na 21.
l-m-h3-b0c48-10.s.s2.model.0: If you put 4 inside n(n−1)/2, e give 6, and with 5 e give 10, so e fit di examples; n=7 give 21.
l-m-h3-b0c48-10.s.s2.model.1: Each point get n−1 line parts, but each line part count 2 times, so you need divide by 2.

l-m-h3-b0c48-11.title: Wetin rule dey for sum of 4 numbers wey follow one another?
l-m-h3-b0c48-11.goal: Find and state rule from some examples of sum of 4 natural numbers wey follow one another, then check di rule with new example.
l-m-h3-b0c48-11.material: Di sums of 4 natural numbers wey follow one another na 1+2+3+4=10, 2+3+4+5=14, 3+4+5+6=18, and 4+5+6+7=22. Find rule for sum when first number na n.
l-m-h3-b0c48-11.s.s1.r.a: When n=1 e give 4, wey different from 10 for examples.
l-m-h3-b0c48-11.s.s1.o.b: Di sum na 6 more than 4 times n
l-m-h3-b0c48-11.s.s1.o.c: Di sum na 8 more than 2 times n
l-m-h3-b0c48-11.s.s1.r.c: When n=2 e give 12, wey different from 14 for examples.
l-m-h3-b0c48-11.s.s1.r.d: When n=2 e give 20, wey different from 14 for examples.
l-m-h3-b0c48-11.s.s1.explain: n+(n+1)+(n+2)+(n+3)=4n+6. When first number increase by 1, di sum increase by 4.
l-m-h3-b0c48-11.s.s2.model.0: Di sums 10, 14, 18, 22 increase by 4 each time, and when n=1 di sum na 10, so di sum na 4n+6.
l-m-h3-b0c48-11.s.s2.model.1: If you call di 4 numbers n, n+1, n+2, n+3 and add dem, you get 4n+6, so di rule correct.

l-m-h3-b0c48-12.title: Predicting di value at x=6 from di pattern of differences
l-m-h3-b0c48-12.goal: Find and state rule from some examples of how y values for table grow, then check di rule with new example.
l-m-h3-b0c48-12.material: Table: when x=0, 1, 2, 3, 4, y=1, 2, 5, 10, 17. Find di rule from how y change and predict y when x=6.
l-m-h3-b0c48-12.s.s1.prompt: Which rule fit the table, and wetin be prediction for x=6?
l-m-h3-b0c48-12.s.s1.o.a: y dey grow by 7 each time, so 31
l-m-h3-b0c48-12.s.s1.r.a: Differences na 1, 3, 5, 7, so dem change and no be constant.
l-m-h3-b0c48-12.s.s1.r.b: For x=0, e give 0, different from 1 for table.
l-m-h3-b0c48-12.s.s1.r.d: For x=0, e give 2, different from 1 for table.
l-m-h3-b0c48-12.s.s1.explain: Differences 1, 3, 5, 7 increase by 2 each time, so y=x²+1. For x=6, e be 37.
l-m-h3-b0c48-12.s.s2.model.0: Put x=1, 2, 3, 4 inside y=x²+1 and you get 2, 5, 10, 17, so x=6 give 37.
l-m-h3-b0c48-12.s.s2.model.1: Differences increase by 2: 1, 3, 5, 7, so x=5 give 17+9=26, and x=6 give 26+11=37.

l-m-h3-b0c48-13.s.s1.o.a: Number of sum types na 6n, so 30
l-m-h3-b0c48-13.s.s1.r.a: When n=2, e give 12, wey no match 11.

l-m-h3-b0c48-13.s.s1.r.c: When n=1, e give 5, wey no match 6.
l-m-h3-b0c48-13.s.s1.o.d: Sums go from n to 6n, so 26

l-m-h3-b0c49-10.goal: Find and state one rule from several examples of number of squares in grid, then check di rule with new example.
l-m-h3-b0c49-10.material: If you count all squares of different sizes inside n×n grid, 1 dey for n=1, 5 for n=2, 14 for n=3, and 30 for n=4. Use dis rule to predict n=5.
l-m-h3-b0c49-10.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be prediction for n=5 using rule wey fit di examples?
l-m-h3-b0c49-10.s.s1.r.a: For n=2 e give 4, wey different from 5 in di examples.
l-m-h3-b0c49-10.s.s1.r.b: Di differences na 4, 9, 16, so dem no increase by 5.
l-m-h3-b0c49-10.s.s1.r.c: From 5 to 14, dem no multiply by 2.
l-m-h3-b0c49-10.s.s1.o.d: Di differences na 4, 9, 16, so di next difference na 25, giving 55
l-m-h3-b0c49-10.s.s1.explain: New amounts wey dem add na 2², 3², 4², so di next na 5²=25. 30+25=55.
l-m-h3-b0c49-10.s.s2.model.0: Amounts wey dem add na 4, 9, 16, wey be 2², 3², 4², so di next na 5²=25, and 30+25=55.
l-m-h3-b0c49-10.s.s2.model.1: Number of squares for each size na 1², 2², …, so for n=5 e be 1+4+9+16+25=55.

l-m-h3-b0c49-11.s.s1.r.b: Last digit of 7² na 9. E no match di examples.
l-m-h3-b0c49-11.s.s1.o.d: 1: when exponent big, e eventually become 1
l-m-h3-b0c49-11.s.s1.explain: Last digit dey repeat 7, 9, 3, 1 in groups of 4. When you divide 2026 by 4, remainder na 2, so di answer na second one, 9.
l-m-h3-b0c49-11.s.s2.model.0: Last digit of 7⁵ na di same as 7¹, so cycle na 4, and number in position 2026 na second one, 9.
l-m-h3-b0c49-11.s.s2.model.1: 7, 9, 3, 1 dey repeat in groups of 4, and when you divide 2026 by 4 remainder na 2, so last digit na 9.

l-m-h3-b0c49-12.s.s2.model.0: Di sums na 1/2, 2/3, 3/4, 4/5, so sum of n terms na n/(n+1), and nine terms give 9/10.

l-m-h3-b0c49-13.title: Find pattern for money wey dey grow each year
l-m-h3-b0c49-13.goal: Find pattern from some examples of deposit wey grow every year, state am, and check am with new example.
l-m-h3-b0c49-13.material: 100×10,000 won dey grow by fixed rate every year. After 1 year e be 105×10,000 won, after 2 years 110.25×10,000 won, and after 3 years about 115.76×10,000 won. Use dis pattern to predict amount after 10 years.
l-m-h3-b0c49-13.s.s1.prompt: Using pattern wey fit di examples, wetin be prediction for 10 years later?
l-m-h3-b0c49-13.s.s1.r.a: Nothing for di examples support 200 after 10 years.
l-m-h3-b0c49-13.s.s1.o.b: Multiply by 2 every year to get 1024×10,000 won
l-m-h3-b0c49-13.s.s1.r.b: After 1 year e be 105, no be 200.
l-m-h3-b0c49-13.s.s1.o.c: Multiply by 1.05 every year to get about 162.9×10,000 won
l-m-h3-b0c49-13.s.s1.o.d: Add 5×10,000 won every year to get 150×10,000 won

l-m-h3-b0c50-33.s.s2.model.1: Error na 10÷√n, so when n become 4 times bigger, √n become 2 times bigger and error reduce by half.

l-m-h3-b0d10-18.material: For each b, I find length (with sign) of orthogonal projection of b onto direction of a=(3, 4). For b=(1, 0) e na 0.6, for b=(0, 5) na 4, and for b=(5, 5) na 7.
l-m-h3-b0d10-18.s.s1.prompt: How dem determine length of orthogonal projection?
l-m-h3-b0d10-18.s.s1.r.a: For b=(1, 0), 3/1=3, but actual value na 0.6.
l-m-h3-b0d10-18.s.s1.r.b: For b=(1, 0), a·b=3, but actual value na 0.6.
l-m-h3-b0d10-18.s.s1.r.c: For b=(1, 0), e na 5, but actual value na 0.6.
l-m-h3-b0d10-18.s.s1.explain: For all 3 cases e na (a·b)/|a|. 3/5=0.6, 20/5=4, and 35/5=7.
l-m-h3-b0d10-18.s.s2.model.0: (1,0) give 3/5, (0,5) give 20/5, and (5,5) give 35/5, so each na a·b divided by |a|=5.
l-m-h3-b0d10-18.s.s2.model.1: Length of orthogonal projection na |b|cosθ, and a·b=|a||b|cosθ, so e equal a·b divided by |a|.

l-m-h3-b0d10-33.goal: Find and state pattern from examples of radius for circular cross-section wey form when plane cut sphere, then check pattern with new example.
l-m-h3-b0d10-33.material: Cutting sphere x² + y² + z² = 169 with plane z = k make circle. When k = 0 radius na 13, when k = 5 e na 12, and when k = 12 e na 5.
l-m-h3-b0d10-33.s.s1.prompt: How cross-section circle radius r relate to k?
l-m-h3-b0d10-33.s.s1.r.b: When k=5 e give 8, but real value na 12.
l-m-h3-b0d10-33.s.s1.r.c: When k=12 e give 10.6, but real value na 5.
l-m-h3-b0d10-33.s.s1.r.d: When k=0 e give 169, but real value na 13.
l-m-h3-b0d10-33.s.s1.explain: Points on cross-section circle follow x²+y²=169−k². So r=√(169−k²), wey match all three examples.
l-m-h3-b0d10-33.s.s2.model.0: If k=5, √(169−25)=12; if k=12, √(169−144)=5, so e fit every example. Therefore r=√(169−k²).
l-m-h3-b0d10-33.s.s2.model.1: Points on cross-section follow x²+y²+k²=169, so x²+y²=169−k², and radius na its square root.

l-m-h3-b0c35-28.material: One shop sales grow 18% for the first year and 22% for the next year. We wan estimate by how many percent e grow altogether for the two years compared with the start.

l-m-h3-b0c36-14.goal: Estimate the range of the overall approval rate wey dem guess from the sample approval rate, decide suitable size or range, and explain your reasoning.
l-m-h3-b0c36-14.material: Dem choose 400 residents and ask dem, and 240 (60%) approve one policy. The standard error of the sample proportion na about 0.025. Dem estimate the range as sample proportion ± 2×standard error.
l-m-h3-b0c36-14.s.s1.prompt: For which range you go estimate the approval rate of all the residents?
l-m-h3-b0c36-14.s.s1.r.a: You take the standard error 0.025 as something wey too small pass, like 0.005.

l-m-h3-b0c36-14.s.s2.model.0: The margin of error na 2×0.025=0.05, so if you add and subtract 5 percentage points from 60% e give 55% to 65%.
l-m-h3-b0c36-14.s.s2.model.1: Because na sample, the result of the 400 people no be exactly the same as the whole, so you suppose state range of 60% ± 5 percentage points.

l-m-h3-b0c36-15.title: How to estimate the mean of squared errors
l-m-h3-b0c36-15.goal: Estimate the mean of the squared prediction errors (MSE), decide suitable size or range, and explain your reasoning.
l-m-h3-b0c36-15.material: One model predict say the temperatures for three places na 2, 3, and 4 degrees, but the real values na 3, 3, and 6 degrees. The errors (real − predicted) na 1, 0, and 2. Estimate the size of the mean of the squared errors (MSE).

l-m-h3-b0c36-15.s.s1.r.b: You average the errors without squaring dem.

l-m-h3-b0c36-15.s.s1.r.d: You look only the square of the biggest error.
l-m-h3-b0c36-15.s.s1.explain: The squared errors na 1, 0, and 4. If you divide the sum 5 by 3 e give 5/3, about 1.7.
l-m-h3-b0c36-15.s.s2.model.0: If you square the errors e give 1, 0, and 4, and dem divide the sum 5 by the count 3, so e be about 1.7.
l-m-h3-b0c36-15.s.s2.model.1: The biggest square na 4 and the others small, so the mean small well well pass 4, and about 1.7 fit.

l-m-h3-b0c36-16.goal: Estimate the range of accuracy wey you expect from small test, decide suitable size or range, and explain your reasoning.
l-m-h3-b0c36-16.material: Dem use one classification model for 50 test cases and e get 45 (90%) right. The standard error of this accuracy na about 0.04, and dem estimate the range as 90% ± 2×0.04.

l-m-h3-b0c36-16.s.s1.r.c: You carry the number wey e get right for the test data go as e be.
l-m-h3-b0c36-16.s.s1.r.d: The test get only 50 cases, but you treat the error like say e no reach anything.
l-m-h3-b0c36-16.s.s1.explain: 90% ± 8 percentage points na 82% to 98%. Out of 1000 cases, na about 820 to 980 cases.
l-m-h3-b0c36-16.s.s2.model.0: With sample of 50 cases the error na about ±8 percentage points, so for 1000 cases you suppose allow range of 820 to 980.
l-m-h3-b0c36-16.s.s2.model.1: 90% no mean exactly 900, so count the error 2×0.04=0.08 too: 82% to 98%, wey as number of cases na 820 to 980.

l-m-h3-b0c37-13.material: You wan multiply 1000×500 matrix A by 500×200 matrix B. Dem dey get each entry of the result by multiplying 500 pairs of entries and adding dem.

l-m-h3-b0c37-13.s.s1.r.c: You estimate the number of multiplications as 10 times too big.
l-m-h3-b0c37-13.s.s1.explain: The result get 1000×200=200,000 (20×10,000) entries, and each need 500 multiplications, so 20×10,000×500=100 million (1×10⁸).
l-m-h3-b0c37-13.s.s2.model.0: Each of the 200,000 (20×10,000) result entries need 500 multiplications, so 20×10,000×500 na about 100 million (1×10⁸).
l-m-h3-b0c37-13.s.s2.model.1: You multiply the 1000 rows, 200 columns, and inner 500 together, so 1000×200×500 na about 100 million (1×10⁸).

l-m-h3-b0c37-14.s.s1.r.c: Na the share of positives among people wey no be patients be that. No be the share of patients.
l-m-h3-b0c37-14.s.s1.r.d: Na the share of patients before testing be that. E dey change after positive result.
l-m-h3-b0c37-14.s.s1.explain: 16 of the 20 patients and 98 of the 980 non-patients test positive. Among the 114 positives, 16 na patients, so e be about 14%.
l-m-h3-b0c37-14.s.s2.model.0: Among the positives, the patients na 20×0.8=16 people and the non-patients na 980×0.1=98 people, so e be 16/114, about 14%.
l-m-h3-b0c37-14.s.s2.model.1: People wey no be patients pass far, so the 98 false alarms pass the 16 patients, and about 14% of the positives na patients.

l-m-h3-b0c37-15.title: To estimate the number of steps for gradient descent
l-m-h3-b0c37-15.goal: Estimate the number of steps wey gradient descent need until the value small enough, decide suitable size or range, and explain your reasoning.
l-m-h3-b0c37-15.material: If you run gradient descent for f(x)=x² with learning rate of 0.1, x go become 0.8 times as big with each step. If you start for x=10, estimate the number of steps wey e go take for |x| to become less than 1.
l-m-h3-b0c37-15.s.s1.prompt: About how many steps e go take?
l-m-h3-b0c37-15.s.s1.r.b: You assume say dem dey cut x half every time.
l-m-h3-b0c37-15.s.s1.r.c: You assume say e only dey reduce by 0.1 for each step.
l-m-h3-b0c37-15.s.s1.r.d: You think say e go become 10 times smaller at once.
l-m-h3-b0c37-15.s.s1.explain: 0.8¹⁰≈0.107 and 0.8¹¹≈0.086, so 10×0.8¹¹≈0.86<1. E go take about 11 steps.
l-m-h3-b0c37-15.s.s2.model.0: E dey become 0.8 times for each step, so find n wey 10×0.8ⁿ<1. E na 1.07 for n=10 and 0.86 for n=11, so about 11 steps.
l-m-h3-b0c37-15.s.s2.model.1: If e dey shrink by 0.8 times for each step, e go take more than 3 steps just to reach half, so about 10 steps or small more dey needed for 10 to fall under 1.

l-m-h3-b0c38-12.goal: Estimate the probability say product wey dem judge as defective really defective to decide suitable size or range, and explain your reasoning.

l-m-h3-b0c38-12.s.s2.model.0: About 9+89=98 dem judge as defective and only 9 truly defective, so the probability na about 10%.
l-m-h3-b0c38-12.s.s2.model.1: Normal products pass well well, so wrong defect judgments pass true defect judgments, and the probability low, about 10%.

l-m-h3-b0c41-16.title: How to estimate the range of the true value from ruler marks

l-m-h3-b0c41-16.s.s2.model.1: If e differ by more than 0.5mm, dem go read am as different mark, so the range 24.45~24.55cm fit.

l-m-h3-b0c42-08.goal: Estimate di mean commuting time wey you see for frequency table, decide one suitable size or range, then explain di reason.
l-m-h3-b0c42-08.material: Dis na di frequency distribution of commuting times of 30 students. 0-10 min: 6 students, 10-20 min: 14 students, 20-30 min: 8 students, 30-40 min: 2 students. Estimate di mean commuting time without di raw data.

l-m-h3-b0c42-08.s.s1.r.a: E near di end value of di smallest interval, so e too small.

l-m-h3-b0c42-08.s.s2.model.1: The interval wey get the most na 10-20 minutes and 10 students dey 20 minutes or more, so e dey small above 15 minutes, wey make about 17 minutes suitable.

l-m-h3-b0c42-14.goal: Estimate the score prediction by study time, decide suitable size or range, and explain the reason.
l-m-h3-b0c42-14.material: From the data of students wey study 0 to 6 hours, we get the line 'score = 8×hours + 45'. If you put hours 10 inside this e give 125 points.
l-m-h3-b0c42-14.s.s1.prompt: Which statement suitable to predict the score after 10 hours of study?
l-m-h3-b0c42-14.s.s1.o.a: Talk say na 125 points as e be
l-m-h3-b0c42-14.s.s1.r.a: The maximum score na 100, so 125 points no make sense.
l-m-h3-b0c42-14.s.s1.o.b: The line wrong, so dem no fit make prediction

l-m-h3-b0c42-14.s.s1.o.c: After 6 hours no data dey, so e hard to trust
l-m-h3-b0c42-14.s.s1.o.d: Insist say e go be 100 points
l-m-h3-b0c42-14.s.s1.r.d: E insist on 100 points without any data.

l-m-h3-b0c42-26.topic: How to estimate population from sample
l-m-h3-b0c42-26.goal: Estimate the number of fish for pond, decide on the size or range wey fit, then explain your reasons.
l-m-h3-b0c42-26.material: Dem catch 100 fish for pond, mark dem, and release dem. After few days dem catch 50 fish, and 5 of dem get mark.
l-m-h3-b0c42-26.s.s1.prompt: Which one na estimate wey fit of the number of fish for the pond?
l-m-h3-b0c42-26.s.s1.r.a: Dem add am like 100+50−5. Dem no use the ratio.
l-m-h3-b0c42-26.s.s1.r.c: Dem multiply the 45 fish wey no get mark by 100.
l-m-h3-b0c42-26.s.s1.r.d: Dem multiply am like 100×5. That one no match the meaning of ratio.
l-m-h3-b0c42-26.s.s1.explain: The 100 fish wey get mark na about 10% (5÷50) of the whole, so the whole na about 1000 fish.
l-m-h3-b0c42-26.s.s2.model.0: 10% of the 50 fish wey dem catch the second time get mark, so the 100 fish wey get mark na 10% of the whole, wey make about 1000 fish.
l-m-h3-b0c42-26.s.s2.model.1: We treat the ratio for the sample as similar to the ratio for the whole pond, so we estimate 100÷0.1=1000.

l-m-h3-b0c43-25.goal: Estimate the interval wey the sample proportion go fall inside, pick one correct size or range, and explain the reason.
l-m-h3-b0c43-25.material: The proportion of people wey get one particular opinion for the whole group na 0.3. If we randomly survey 100 people, the standard deviation of the sample proportion na about 0.046. Estimate the interval wey the sample proportion go fall inside about 95% of the time.

l-m-h3-b0c43-25.s.s1.r.d: E be every possible value, so e no be estimate.
l-m-h3-b0c43-25.s.s1.explain: About 95% na the mean ±2×standard deviation. 0.3±2×0.046, so e be about 0.21 to 0.39.
l-m-h3-b0c43-25.s.s2.model.0: If you go from 0.3 about 0.09 (2 times the standard deviation) to each side, you go get 0.21 to 0.39, and e cover about 95%, so e correct.
l-m-h3-b0c43-25.s.s2.model.1: 0.29 to 0.31 narrow too much and 0.10 to 0.50 wide too much, so 0.21 to 0.39, wey be 0.3±2×0.046, na the correct one.

l-m-h3-b0c44-14.goal: Estimate the margin of error for poll to choose a suitable size or range, and explain your thinking.
l-m-h3-b0c44-14.material: We ask 400 people we choose at random, and 52% support one policy. We want make rough estimate of the 95% margin of error for the sample proportion.
l-m-h3-b0c44-14.s.s1.prompt: Choose the best estimate for the margin of error.
l-m-h3-b0c44-14.s.s1.r.a: E too wide. Then you no fit tell whether people support am or not.
l-m-h3-b0c44-14.s.s1.r.b: ±10 percentage points na for about 100 people. With 400 people, e go narrower.
l-m-h3-b0c44-14.s.s1.r.c: With 400 people, you no fit get this kind precision.
l-m-h3-b0c44-14.s.s1.explain: 1÷√400=0.05, so e be about ±5 percentage points. More exactly, 1.96×√(0.52×0.48÷400)≈4.9 percentage points.
l-m-h3-b0c44-14.s.s2.model.0: The standard error for the sample proportion na about 0.025, and the margin of error na roughly two times that, so about ±5 percentage points fit well.
l-m-h3-b0c44-14.s.s2.model.1: If the sample na 400, then 1÷√400=0.05, so you fit estimate about ±5 percentage points.

l-m-h3-b0c44-15.goal: Estimate the usual range for the number of heads from coin tosses to choose a suitable size or range, and explain your thinking.
l-m-h3-b0c44-15.material: When you toss fair coin 100 times, people dey treat the number of heads as close to normal distribution with mean 50 and standard deviation 5. Estimate the range wey the number of heads usually fall inside (about 95%).
l-m-h3-b0c44-15.s.s1.prompt: Choose the best range for the number of heads.
l-m-h3-b0c44-15.s.s1.r.b: Na 5 times mean ± standard deviation, and the range too wide well well.
l-m-h3-b0c44-15.s.s1.r.c: Na mean ± one standard deviation, so only about 68% dey inside am.
l-m-h3-b0c44-15.s.s1.r.d: The range narrow so much that results often dey outside am.
l-m-h3-b0c44-15.s.s1.explain: About 95% na mean ± 2 times the standard deviation. Since e be 50±10, the range na 40 to 60 times.
l-m-h3-b0c44-15.s.s2.model.0: 95% dey within 2 standard deviations from the mean, and 2×5=10, so 40 to 60 times fit.
l-m-h3-b0c44-15.s.s2.model.1: 45 to 55 get only about 68%, so to get 95% you need 40 to 60, wey twice as wide.

l-m-h3-b0c44-16.title: Estimating confidence interval for sleep time
l-m-h3-b0c44-16.goal: Estimate the population mean for students' sleep time to choose a suitable size or range, and explain your thinking.
l-m-h3-b0c44-16.material: We survey the daily sleep time of 36 students, and the mean na 7.0 hours. We know the population standard deviation na 1.2 hours. Estimate the 95% confidence interval for the population mean.
l-m-h3-b0c44-16.s.s1.prompt: Choose the best estimate for the confidence interval.
l-m-h3-b0c44-16.s.s1.r.a: With 36 students, you no fit estimate am this precisely.
l-m-h3-b0c44-16.s.s1.r.c: This one use standard deviation 1.2 as e be, and e no consider the sample size.
l-m-h3-b0c44-16.s.s1.r.d: E use only 1 times the standard error, so e too narrow for 95%.
l-m-h3-b0c44-16.s.s1.explain: The standard error na 1.2÷6=0.2, and 1.96×0.2≈0.4, so e be 7.0±0.4.
l-m-h3-b0c44-16.s.s2.model.0: The standard error na 1.2÷√36=0.2, and adding and subtracting about 2 times that, 0.4, gives 6.6 to 7.4 hours.
l-m-h3-b0c44-16.s.s2.model.1: Sample mean no dey spread as much as one person value, so the interval narrow reach about ±0.4, no be ±1.2.

l-m-h3-b0c44-17.s.s1.r.c: To get half, making n 4 times bigger go do.

l-m-h3-b0c44-17.s.s2.model.1: If you make am 2 times bigger, the error reduce to only about 0.71 times, so you need 4 times.

l-m-h3-b0c47-14.goal: Estimate Earth's circumference from distance and angle between two cities, choose suitable size or range, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c47-14.material: One scholar for ancient Greece estimate Earth's circumference from 7.2° difference in midday shadow angles for two cities. The two cities dey same north–south line and about 800km apart.

l-m-h3-b0c47-14.s.s1.r.a: You multiply 800×7.2. 7.2° na only part of 360°.
l-m-h3-b0c47-14.s.s1.r.b: One digit miss. Start by estimating 360÷7.2.
l-m-h3-b0c47-14.s.s1.r.d: You multiply 800×360. You need multiply by 360÷7.2.
l-m-h3-b0c47-14.s.s1.explain: 7.2° na 1/50 of 360°, so circumference na about 50 times 800km, wey be 4×10⁴ km (40,000km).
l-m-h3-b0c47-14.s.s2.model.0: 7.2° na 1/50 of 360°, so Earth's circumference na about 4×10⁴ km (40,000km), wey be 50 times 800km.
l-m-h3-b0c47-14.s.s2.model.1: One full turn of 360° na 50 times 7.2°, so 800×50=40000, and circumference fit estimate as about 4×10⁴ km.

l-m-h3-b0d09-11.s.s2.model.1: x−y=1/(x+y) and x+y≈200, so di difference na about 1/200=0.005.

l-m-h3-b0c33-18.topic: Compound interest calculation (how to work am out)
l-m-h3-b0c33-18.goal: Follow step by step one solution (or one chain of cause and effect) for di interest wen you deposit for 2 years at compound interest, find di first place wey e go wrong, and fix am.
l-m-h3-b0c33-18.material: You deposit 1,000×10,000 won for 2 years at 4% per year compound interest. One student work: ①First-year interest 1,000×0.04=40×10,000 won ②Second-year interest 1,000×0.04=40×10,000 won ③After 2 years 1,000+40+40=1,080×10,000 won
l-m-h3-b0c33-18.s.s1.o.a: ① Di line wey find di first-year interest
l-m-h3-b0c33-18.s.s1.r.a: For di first year di principal na di base, so e correct.
l-m-h3-b0c33-18.s.s1.o.b: ③ Di line wey find di total
l-m-h3-b0c33-18.s.s1.r.b: Di addition correct. Di value for di earlier line wrong.
l-m-h3-b0c33-18.s.s1.r.c: For compound interest, di base for di second year interest dey change.
l-m-h3-b0c33-18.s.s1.o.d: ② Di line wey find di second-year interest
l-m-h3-b0c33-18.s.s1.explain: For compound interest, di base for di second year na 1,040×10,000 won, so di interest na 41.6×10,000 won and di total na 1,081.6×10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c33-18.s.s2.model.0: For compound interest, di second-year interest also base on 1,040×10,000 won, so ② suppose be 1,040×0.04=41.6×10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c33-18.s.s2.model.1: Di interest wey dem add for di first year also dey earn interest like di principal, so di second-year interest big pass 40×10,000 won and di total na 1,081.6×10,000 won.

l-m-h3-b0c33-19.topic: Break-even point (where income and cost equal)
l-m-h3-b0c33-19.title: Where di mistake dey for di break-even solution?
l-m-h3-b0c33-19.goal: Follow step by step one solution (or one chain of cause and effect) for di sales quantity wey cover di fixed cost, find di first place wey e go wrong, and fix am.
l-m-h3-b0c33-19.material: Di selling price for each item na 5,000 won, di variable cost for each item na 3,000 won, and di fixed cost na 200×10,000 won. One student: ①Money wey remain for each item 5,000−3,000=2,000 won ②Fixed cost 2,000,000 won ③Break-even 2,000,000÷5,000=400 items
l-m-h3-b0c33-19.s.s1.o.a: ③ Di line wey find di sales quantity
l-m-h3-b0c33-19.s.s1.o.b: ① Di line wey find di money wey remain for each item
l-m-h3-b0c33-19.s.s1.r.b: To subtract di variable cost from di selling price correct.
l-m-h3-b0c33-19.s.s1.o.c: ② Di line wey use di fixed cost
l-m-h3-b0c33-19.s.s1.r.c: E use di fixed cost wey dem give as e be.
l-m-h3-b0c33-19.s.s1.r.d: Di divisor must be di money wey remain for each item.
l-m-h3-b0c33-19.s.s1.explain: Di 2,000 won wey remain for each item dey cover di fixed cost. 2,000,000÷2,000=1,000 items na di break-even sales quantity.
l-m-h3-b0c33-19.s.s2.model.0: For ③, dem divide by di selling price of 5,000 won, so e wrong; if you divide by di 2,000 won wey remain for each item e give 1,000 items.
l-m-h3-b0c33-19.s.s2.model.1: Di 2,000 won wey remain from each item wey dem sell dey cover di fixed cost as e dey pile up, so dem must correct am to 2,000,000÷2,000=1,000 items.

l-m-h3-b0c33-20.material: Sales rise from 100×10,000 won to 150×10,000 won and then fall back to 100×10,000 won. One student: ①Increase rate 50÷100=50% ②Decrease rate also 50÷100=50% ③So di increase rate and decrease rate na di same
l-m-h3-b0c33-20.s.s1.o.a: ① Di line wey find di increase rate

l-m-h3-b0c33-20.s.s1.r.b: Di conclusion come from di wrong value for di earlier line.
l-m-h3-b0c33-20.s.s1.o.c: ② Di line wey find di decrease rate

l-m-h3-b0c33-20.s.s2.model.0: For ②, dem divide by 100×10,000 won instead of di value before di fall, 150×10,000 won, so e wrong; 50÷150 give about 33.3%.
l-m-h3-b0c33-20.s.s2.model.1: Di decrease rate dey base on di value before di fall, so e no equal di increase rate of 50%; e na about 33.3%.

l-m-h3-b0c34-17.topic: Supply-demand equilibrium (where supply and demand balance)
l-m-h3-b0c34-17.title: Which line go wrong first for di equilibrium price solution?
l-m-h3-b0c34-17.goal: Follow step by step one solution (or one chain of cause and effect) wey set di demand equation equal to di supply equation, find di first place wey e go wrong, and fix am.
l-m-h3-b0c34-17.material: Dis na solution to find di equilibrium price wen di demand na q=100−p and di supply na q=−10+1.5p: ①100−p=−10+1.5p ②110=0.5p ③p=220
l-m-h3-b0c34-17.s.s1.o.a: ① Di line wey set di two equations equal
l-m-h3-b0c34-17.s.s1.r.a: Di quantity demanded must equal di quantity supplied, so e correct.
l-m-h3-b0c34-17.s.s1.o.b: ② Di line wey rearrange di equation
l-m-h3-b0c34-17.s.s1.o.c: ③ Di line wey find p
l-m-h3-b0c34-17.s.s1.r.c: Dis na di result wey come from di wrong equation for di line before.
l-m-h3-b0c34-17.s.s1.r.d: Wen you gather di p terms, di coefficient no be 0.5.
l-m-h3-b0c34-17.s.s1.explain: If you gather p for one side, 100+10=1.5p+p, so 110=2.5p and p=44.
l-m-h3-b0c34-17.s.s2.model.0: For ②, dem calculate di coefficient of p as 0.5, so e wrong; if you correct am to 110=2.5p, then p=44.
l-m-h3-b0c34-17.s.s2.model.1: Wen you move −p to di right side, dem add am to 1.5p and e become 2.5p, so correct am to p=110÷2.5=44.

l-m-h3-b0c34-18.goal: Follow step by step one solution (or one chain of cause and effect) for di expected value of one game where you gain wen you win and lose wen you lose, find di first place wey e go wrong, and fix am.
l-m-h3-b0c34-18.material: Na game where you gain 500 won with 20% chance and lose 100 won with 80% chance. One student write: ①0.2×500=100 ②0.8×(−100)=−80 ③di expected value na 100+80=180 won
l-m-h3-b0c34-18.s.s1.o.a: ① Di line wey find di share wey dem gain
l-m-h3-b0c34-18.s.s1.r.a: Di share of 500 won at 20% chance na 100 won, so e correct.
l-m-h3-b0c34-18.s.s1.o.b: ② Di line wey find di share wey dem lose
l-m-h3-b0c34-18.s.s1.r.b: Di share wey dem lose na −80 won, and even di sign correct.
l-m-h3-b0c34-18.s.s1.r.c: Wen you add −80, you must keep di sign.
l-m-h3-b0c34-18.s.s1.o.d: ③ Di line wey add up di expected value
l-m-h3-b0c34-18.s.s1.explain: −80 na value to subtract, so 100+(−80)=20 won. Because dem add di share wey dem lose, 180 won come out.
l-m-h3-b0c34-18.s.s2.model.0: For ③, dem add −80 won as if na +80 won, so e wrong; di expected value na 100+(−80)=20 won.
l-m-h3-b0c34-18.s.s2.model.1: Di share wey dem lose na negative, so you must subtract 80 from di share wey dem gain, and di expected value na 20 won.

l-m-h3-b0c34-19.material: Dis na solution for di maximum of di profit P(q)=−q²+40q−100: ①P=−(q−20)²+300 ②di vertex of di graph na (300, 20) ③so at q=300 units di maximum profit na 20

l-m-h3-b0c34-19.s.s1.o.b: ① Di line wey change di form
l-m-h3-b0c34-19.s.s1.r.b: −(q−20)²+300, wen you expand am, na di same as di original expression, so e correct.
l-m-h3-b0c34-19.s.s1.r.c: Dis na di conclusion wey come from di wrong vertex for di line before.

l-m-h3-b0c34-19.s.s2.model.0: For ②, dem read di coordinates of di vertex backwards, so e wrong; di vertex of −(q−20)²+300 na (20, 300).
l-m-h3-b0c34-19.s.s2.model.1: Di profit big pass wen q−20=0, so dem suppose correct am to say di maximum profit na 300 at q=20 units.

l-m-h3-b0c35-05.title: Di profit na 1,000 won after discount?
l-m-h3-b0c35-05.goal: Follow di solution, or di chain of cause and effect, for how to find profit from cost, list price, and discounted price step by step, find where e first go wrong, and fix am.
l-m-h3-b0c35-05.material: Dem set di list price by adding 25% profit to cost of 20,000 won, and dem sell di item at 20% discount off di list price. Solution: 1) list price=20,000×1.25=25,000 2) discount=20,000×0.2=4,000 3) selling price=25,000−4,000=21,000 4) profit=21,000−20,000=1,000 won
l-m-h3-b0c35-05.s.s1.r.c: If you use di value from di earlier step, dem calculate 25,000−4,000 correct.
l-m-h3-b0c35-05.s.s1.explain: Di discount dey base on di list price, so e na 25,000×0.2=5,000 won. Di selling price na 20,000 won and di profit na 0 won.
l-m-h3-b0c35-05.s.s2.model.0: Dem must multiply di discount rate by di list price, but dem multiply am by di cost, so step 2 wrong. If 25,000×0.2=5,000, di selling price na 20,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c35-05.s.s2.model.1: Dem choose di base wrongly for step 2. 20% of di list price of 25,000 won na 5,000 won, so di selling price na 20,000 won and di profit na 0 won.

l-m-h3-b0c35-20.title: To solve di expected value of one dice game
l-m-h3-b0c35-20.goal: Follow di solution of di dice game expected value, or im chain of cause and effect, step by step, then find and fix di first place wey e go wrong.
l-m-h3-b0c35-20.material: Roll one die one time. If di number even, you go receive (number)×100 won; if e odd, you go pay 200 won. Solution: 1) Di probabilities of even and odd na 1/2 each 2) When e even, you go receive 400 won on average 3) Expected value=400−200=200 won 4) If you play 100 times, you go earn about 20,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c35-20.s.s1.r.a: 3 even numbers dey and 3 odd numbers dey, so e correct.
l-m-h3-b0c35-20.s.s1.o.b: Step 2: 400 won on average when e even
l-m-h3-b0c35-20.s.s1.r.d: Dis one na calculation wey dem make after dem use di Step 3 value, so e no be di first place wey e go wrong.
l-m-h3-b0c35-20.s.s1.explain: You must multiply by di probabilities. 1/2×400−1/2×200=100 won, and 100 plays go give about 10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c35-20.s.s2.model.0: E wrong because Step 3 no multiply by di probability 1/2 of di two cases; di fix na 200−100=100 won.
l-m-h3-b0c35-20.s.s2.model.1: Expected value na di sum of values times probabilities, so 400×1/2−200×1/2=100 won, and Step 4 go change to 10,000 won too.

l-m-h3-b0c35-26.s.s2.model.0: E wrong because for Step 2 dem add di interest only to di original 200. Add 3% to 206 then fix am to 212.18.
l-m-h3-b0c35-26.s.s2.model.1: Compound interest dey multiply di grown amount by di rate, so after 2 years e na 206×1.03=212.18 and di maturity amount na about 218.5 ×10,000 won.

l-m-h3-b0c35-33.s.s2.model.1: E wrong because dem choose the denominator wrong for Step 3. 50,000÷400,000=0.125, so sales grow by about 12.5%.

l-m-h3-b0c36-19.material: Use gradient descent to find the minimum of f(x)=x²−6x. Find the first line wey go wrong for one solution wey take one step from the starting point x=0 with learning rate 0.25.
l-m-h3-b0c36-19.s.s1.r.a: Dem find the derivative correct. E no wrong.
l-m-h3-b0c36-19.s.s1.o.b: ② Slope for the starting point f'(0)=−6
l-m-h3-b0c36-19.s.s1.r.b: Dem do the substitution correct. E no wrong.
l-m-h3-b0c36-19.s.s1.o.d: ④ x move farther from the minimum point 3
l-m-h3-b0c36-19.s.s1.r.d: This result come from the mistake for ③. One earlier line dey wrong.
l-m-h3-b0c36-19.s.s1.explain: New x = x − learning rate × slope = 0 − 0.25×(−6) = 1.5. Dem add the slope, so e move for opposite direction.
l-m-h3-b0c36-19.s.s2.model.0: Gradient descent must subtract the slope, but dem add am for ③, so x come be −1.5. Correct am to 0−0.25×(−6)=1.5.
l-m-h3-b0c36-19.s.s2.model.1: If the slope na −6, you must go to the right, so x have to big. So dem must correct ③ to 1.5.

l-m-h3-b0c37-19.s.s1.r.d: Na result wey follow ③. One earlier line dey wey wrong.

l-m-h3-b0c50-24.title: Where square root solution go wrong
l-m-h3-b0c50-24.goal: Follow solution or cause-and-effect chain saying √(x²)=x, find first error and fix am.
l-m-h3-b0c50-24.material: Solution: If x=-3, then x²=9. √(x²)=√9=3. But if √(x²)=x, then √(x²)=-3. So 3=-3. This contradiction happen.
l-m-h3-b0c50-24.s.s1.r.c: This result come from earlier error.
l-m-h3-b0c50-24.s.s1.explain: If x negative, √(x²)=-x. Formula always right na √(x²)=|x|, and x=-3 give 3.
l-m-h3-b0c50-24.s.s2.model.0: When x negative, √(x²) positive, so no equal x; therefore √(x²)=x no fit use for every x.
l-m-h3-b0c50-24.s.s2.model.1: Correct formula na √(x²)=|x|, and x=-3 give 3, so contradiction come from wrongly generalizing formula.

l-m-h3-b0d07-02.title: Limit of √(n²+3n)−n: Which Line Wrong?
l-m-h3-b0d07-02.goal: Follow each step of solution, or chain of cause and effect, to find limit of √(n²+3n)−n. Find first place wey e go wrong and correct am.
l-m-h3-b0d07-02.material: Solution of lim(√(n²+3n)−n): (1) Rationalize: 3n/(√(n²+3n)+n) (2) Divide by n: 3/(√(1+3/n)+1) (3) Since 3/n→3, 3/(√4+1)=1 (4) Di limit na 1
l-m-h3-b0d07-02.s.s1.o.b: Line (2): di step wey dem divide by n
l-m-h3-b0d07-02.s.s1.r.b: Expression after dividing numerator and denominator by n correct.
l-m-h3-b0d07-02.s.s1.o.d: Line (4): di step wey dem write conclusion
l-m-h3-b0d07-02.s.s1.r.d: (4) only carry di value from (3), so e no be first wrong step.
l-m-h3-b0d07-02.s.s1.explain: As n→∞, 3/n→0. So correct limit na 3/(1+1)=3/2.
l-m-h3-b0d07-02.s.s2.model.0: As n dey bigger, 3/n dey close to 0, no be 3, so line (3) wrong. Correctly, e be 3/(1+1)=3/2.
l-m-h3-b0d07-02.s.s2.model.1: Denominator of 3/n grow without limit, so di fraction become 0 and √(1+0)=1. Therefore di limit na 3/2.

l-m-h3-b0d07-23.goal: Follow solution steps, or cause-and-result chain, to find slope of tangent at point (1,1) on x²+xy+y²=3. Find first place wey wrong and correct am.
l-m-h3-b0d07-23.material: Solution for slope of tangent at (1,1) on x²+xy+y²=3: (1) Differentiate both sides: 2x+y+xy'+2yy'=0 (2) y'(x+2y)=2x+y (3) y'=(2x+y)/(x+2y) (4) At (1,1), y'=3/3=1
l-m-h3-b0d07-23.s.s1.o.a: Line (1): where dem differentiate both sides
l-m-h3-b0d07-23.s.s1.r.a: E correct, including derivative of xy, y+xy'.

l-m-h3-b0d07-23.s.s1.o.c: Line (3): where dem write y' by dividing
l-m-h3-b0d07-23.s.s1.r.c: (3) come from dividing (2), so na not di first wrong place.
l-m-h3-b0d07-23.s.s1.o.d: Line (4): where dem put in di point
l-m-h3-b0d07-23.s.s1.r.d: Putting (1,1) and calculating correct based on previous line.
l-m-h3-b0d07-23.s.s1.explain: Moving (2x+y) to right side change sign, so y'=−(2x+y)/(x+2y). Slope na −1.
l-m-h3-b0d07-23.s.s2.model.0: Moving 2x+y to right for (1) make sign −, so (2) wrong, and correct slope na −3/3=−1.
l-m-h3-b0d07-23.s.s2.model.1: When only y' terms remain for left side and you move others, sign change, so (2) wrong. Slope na −1, no be 1.

l-m-h3-b0c33-22.goal: Write di total amount (principal plus interest) after 3 years at 5% per year compound interest in another form (expression, table, picture, words), and explain why dem mean di same thing.
l-m-h3-b0c33-22.material: Dem deposit principal P for 3 years at 5% per year compound interest. Find one expression wey mean di same thing as di expression for di total amount after 3 years.

l-m-h3-b0c33-22.s.s1.r.a: E multiply by 1.05 one time and then by 3, so di meaning different.
l-m-h3-b0c33-22.s.s1.r.c: Dis expression leave only small part of di principal.

l-m-h3-b0c33-22.s.s2.model.1: Interest also dey earn interest, wey dey multiply, so you must write power expression, no be di adding expression for simple interest.

l-m-h3-b0c33-23.goal: Write di daily total revenue by price in another form (expression, table, picture, words), and explain why dem mean di same thing.

l-m-h3-b0c33-23.s.s1.prompt: Which expression mean di same thing as di total revenue R?
l-m-h3-b0c33-23.s.s1.r.b: Revenue na product, but e divide.
l-m-h3-b0c33-23.s.s1.r.d: E square only p for di sales-quantity expression. You need to multiply by di price.

l-m-h3-b0c33-23.s.s2.model.0: Total revenue na price × quantity wey dem sell, so if you expand p(100−2p) e give 100p−2p².
l-m-h3-b0c33-23.s.s2.model.1: E multiply di sales quantity of 100−2p items by p won for each item, so R become di quadratic expression 100p−2p² for p.

l-m-h3-b0c34-21.title: Formula for di price before tax from di price wey include tax
l-m-h3-b0c34-21.goal: Rewrite "to remove tax from one price wey include VAT to get di price before tax" in another form (formula, table, picture, words) and explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-h3-b0c34-21.material: One price wey include 10% VAT na 11,000 won. Find di formula wey mean di same thing as to find di price before tax (di supply price).
l-m-h3-b0c34-21.s.s1.prompt: Which formula find di supply price?
l-m-h3-b0c34-21.s.s1.r.a: Dem go add tax one more time, so di price go even big pass.
l-m-h3-b0c34-21.s.s1.r.c: You subtract 10% of di tax-included price. Di tax na 10% of di supply price.
l-m-h3-b0c34-21.s.s1.r.d: To divide by 0.9 give something wey big pass di tax-included price, so e no be di price before tax.
l-m-h3-b0c34-21.s.s1.explain: Supply price × 1.1 = 11,000, so supply price = 11,000 ÷ 1.1 = 10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c34-21.s.s2.model.0: If you add 10% tax to di supply price, e become 1.1 times, wey be 11,000 won, so di supply price na 11,000 ÷ 1.1.
l-m-h3-b0c34-21.s.s2.model.1: Di tax-included price na 1.1 times di supply price, so to go back you no multiply but divide by 1.1.

l-m-h3-b0c34-22.title: To turn di expected-value formula into words
l-m-h3-b0c34-22.goal: Rewrite di expected value, wey dem write as probability times prize, in another form (formula, table, picture, words) and explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-h3-b0c34-22.material: Dem calculate di expected value of one lottery ticket as 0.3×200 + 0.7×0 (di prize na for won). Find di words wey mean di same thing as dis formula.
l-m-h3-b0c34-22.s.s1.prompt: Which words mean di same thing as dis formula?
l-m-h3-b0c34-22.s.s1.r.a: 0.7 na di probability of blank. Blank get prize of 0, so to add am na to add 0.
l-m-h3-b0c34-22.s.s1.o.b: Di average of 200 won and 0 won, wey be 100 won
l-m-h3-b0c34-22.s.s1.r.b: If di probabilities no equal, e no be simple average.
l-m-h3-b0c34-22.s.s1.explain: 0.3 na di 30% probability to win, and di blank part na 0, so di expected value na 30% of 200 won, wey be 60 won.
l-m-h3-b0c34-22.s.s2.model.0: 0.3×200 na 30% of 200 won and 0.7×0 na 0, so di formula mean 30% of 200 won, dat na 60 won.
l-m-h3-b0c34-22.s.s2.model.1: Since di chance to win na 30%, e mean say you fit expect 30% of di 200 won prize on average.

l-m-h3-b0c34-23.title: To turn revenue and cost into one profit formula
l-m-h3-b0c34-23.goal: Rewrite di profit, wey be revenue minus cost, in another form (formula, table, picture, words) and explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-h3-b0c34-23.material: Wen revenue na R(q)=100q won and cost na C(q)=3,000+40q won, simplify di profit P(q)=R(q)−C(q) into one-line formula for q.
l-m-h3-b0c34-23.s.s1.prompt: Which formula mean di same thing as di profit P(q)?
l-m-h3-b0c34-23.s.s1.r.b: Dem must subtract di fixed cost 3,000 too.
l-m-h3-b0c34-23.s.s1.r.c: You add di cost 40q. Dem must subtract cost.
l-m-h3-b0c34-23.s.s1.r.d: You leave out di fixed cost 3,000.
l-m-h3-b0c34-23.s.s1.explain: P=100q−(3,000+40q)=60q−3,000. You dey keep 60 won for each item, and first you must cover di fixed cost of 3,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c34-23.s.s2.model.0: P=100q−(3,000+40q), so if you remove di parentheses e give 60q−3,000.
l-m-h3-b0c34-23.s.s2.model.1: Dem subtract di whole cost, so 40q comot from di revenue to leave 60q, and di fixed cost 3,000 comot too.

l-m-h3-b0c34-24.title: To talk 20% decrease di opposite way
l-m-h3-b0c34-24.goal: Rewrite "one decrease compared with di previous month, wey dem restate with last month as di base" in another form (formula, table, picture, words) and explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-h3-b0c34-24.material: Dis month sales small by 20% pass last month own. Talk di same fact as "last month sales na how many times dis month own".
l-m-h3-b0c34-24.s.s1.prompt: Which expression mean di same thing?
l-m-h3-b0c34-24.s.s1.o.a: Dis month sales na 1.2 times last month own
l-m-h3-b0c34-24.s.s1.r.a: Dis month go down, so e must small pass 1.
l-m-h3-b0c34-24.s.s1.o.b: Last month sales na 1.25 times dis month own
l-m-h3-b0c34-24.s.s1.o.c: Dis month sales na 0.2 times last month own
l-m-h3-b0c34-24.s.s1.o.d: Last month sales na 1.2 times dis month own
l-m-h3-b0c34-24.s.s1.r.d: Dis month na 0.8 times last month, so for di opposite way e na 1.25 times.
l-m-h3-b0c34-24.s.s1.explain: Dis month = last month × 0.8, so last month = dis month ÷ 0.8 = dis month × 1.25.
l-m-h3-b0c34-24.s.s2.model.0: Dis month na 0.8 times last month, so last month na 1 ÷ 0.8 = 1.25 times dis month.
l-m-h3-b0c34-24.s.s2.model.1: To decrease by 20% mean say 80% remain, so to go back you divide by 0.8, wey give 1.25 times.

l-m-h3-b0c35-06.title: To get back one price wey drop 20%
l-m-h3-b0c35-06.topic: Di base of one increase or decrease rate
l-m-h3-b0c35-06.goal: Rewrite "di rate of increase wey restore one price wey drop 20%" in another form (formula, table, picture, words) and explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-h3-b0c35-06.material: Di price of one item drop 20%. Di lowered price na 0.8 times di original price. Think with multiplication about how many percent of di lowered price you must raise am to get back to di original price.
l-m-h3-b0c35-06.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di rate of increase to go from di lowered price back to di original price?
l-m-h3-b0c35-06.s.s1.r.a: You treat di 20% drop as di same size of increase to go back. Di base different.
l-m-h3-b0c35-06.s.s1.r.c: You read di value 0.8 times itself as di rate of increase.
l-m-h3-b0c35-06.s.s1.r.d: You mix up to raise to 1.2 times with to raise by 120%.
l-m-h3-b0c35-06.s.s1.explain: 0.8×(1+r)=1, so 1+r=1.25, dat na, r=25%. Di base change to di lowered price.
l-m-h3-b0c35-06.s.s2.model.0: For 0.8 to become 1 wen you multiply am by some number, e must be 1.25 times, so you must raise am by 25%.
l-m-h3-b0c35-06.s.s2.model.1: Di amount wey dem lower na di same, but di base don small now, 0.8 times di original, so di rate of increase no be 20% but 0.2÷0.8=25%.

l-m-h3-b0c35-14.topic: Break-even point (where income and cost equal)
l-m-h3-b0c35-14.title: To put di break-even point into words
l-m-h3-b0c35-14.goal: Rewrite di break-even point of one product wey get fixed cost of 5,000 won in another form (formula, table, picture, words) and explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-h3-b0c35-14.material: One product get fixed cost of 5,000 won, selling price of 800 won for each item, and variable cost of 300 won for each item. Express in words di number of items (di break-even point) wey total revenue and total cost go become equal.
l-m-h3-b0c35-14.s.s1.prompt: Which explanation mean di same thing as di break-even point?
l-m-h3-b0c35-14.s.s1.o.a: Di number of items wey, if you earn 800 won each, go cover 5,000 won
l-m-h3-b0c35-14.s.s1.r.a: You no subtract di variable cost of 300 won.
l-m-h3-b0c35-14.s.s1.o.b: Di number of items wey, if 500 won remain each, go cover di fixed cost of 5,000 won
l-m-h3-b0c35-14.s.s1.o.c: Di number of items wey, if 300 won remain each, go cover 5,000 won
l-m-h3-b0c35-14.s.s1.r.c: You mistake di variable cost for profit.
l-m-h3-b0c35-14.s.s1.o.d: Di number of items wey revenue reach 5,000 won
l-m-h3-b0c35-14.s.s1.r.d: You only look revenue without you compare am with di total cost.
l-m-h3-b0c35-14.s.s1.explain: Di money wey remain for each item na 800−300=500 won. At 5,000÷500=10 items, revenue and cost equal at 8,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c35-14.s.s2.model.0: Each item wey you sell leave 800−300=500 won, so you need 10 items to cover 5,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c35-14.s.s2.model.1: Total revenue 800x and total cost 5,000+300x must equal, so 500x=5,000 and x=10.

l-m-h3-b0c35-21.s.s1.o.a: If you buy one ticket, you go always lose 200 won
l-m-h3-b0c35-21.s.s1.r.a: Expected value na average, no be di result of one single try.
l-m-h3-b0c35-21.s.s1.o.b: If you buy plenty plenty tickets, you go lose 200 won for each ticket on average

l-m-h3-b0c35-21.s.s1.r.d: Dem read di average as result wey dey always happen.
l-m-h3-b0c35-21.s.s1.explain: Expected value na di average of plenty tries. One single try fit win, but on average you go lose 200 won for each ticket.
l-m-h3-b0c35-21.s.s2.model.0: Expected value na average, no be di result of one try, so you fit talk am another way say if you buy plenty, you go lose 200 won for each ticket on average.

l-m-h3-b0c35-27.title: To turn cost table into formula
l-m-h3-b0c35-27.topic: Tables and formulas of one function
l-m-h3-b0c35-27.goal: Change di cost table by production quantity to another form (formula, table, picture, words), then explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-h3-b0c35-27.material: Na table of how many things one workshop produce and the total cost. For 0 items e na 8,000 won, for 10 items 8,600 won, for 20 items 9,200 won, and for 30 items 9,800 won.
l-m-h3-b0c35-27.s.s1.prompt: Which formula (x na the number of items) mean the same thing as the table?
l-m-h3-b0c35-27.s.s1.r.a: E read the increase of 600 for every 10 items as the increase for 1 item.
l-m-h3-b0c35-27.s.s1.r.b: The cost for 0 items no be 0 won. The fixed cost no dey inside.
l-m-h3-b0c35-27.s.s1.r.d: E use the value for 10 items as the fixed cost.
l-m-h3-b0c35-27.s.s1.explain: E dey grow by 600 won every 10 items, wey mean 60 won for 1 item, and e na 8,000 won for 0 items, so C=8,000+60x.
l-m-h3-b0c35-27.s.s2.model.0: E na 8,000 won for 0 items and e dey grow by 600 won every 10 items, wey be 60 won for each item, so C=8,000+60x.
l-m-h3-b0c35-27.s.s2.model.1: If you put x=20 e give 8,000+1,200=9,200, wey match the table, so this formula show the table exactly.

l-m-h3-b0c36-21.title: To write system of equations with matrices
l-m-h3-b0c36-21.goal: Change the system of equations 2x+3y=7, x−y=1 to another form (equation, table, picture, words), and explain why e get the same meaning.
l-m-h3-b0c36-21.material: We wan write the system 2x+3y=7, x−y=1 as matrix product. Write the coefficients as matrix, and the unknowns and the right-hand side as column vectors.
l-m-h3-b0c36-21.s.s1.prompt: Choose the matrix equation wey get the same meaning.
l-m-h3-b0c36-21.s.s1.r.a: The sign of the coefficient for the second equation different, so e become −x+y=1.
l-m-h3-b0c36-21.s.s1.r.b: Dem swap the rows and columns of the coefficient matrix, so e become different equation.
l-m-h3-b0c36-21.s.s1.r.c: Dem write the coefficient −1 of y as 1, so e become x+y=1.
l-m-h3-b0c36-21.s.s1.explain: Each row dey show the coefficients of one equation. The first row (2 3) na 2x+3y, and the second row (1 −1) na x−y.
l-m-h3-b0c36-21.s.s2.model.0: The first row of the matrix product na 2x+3y and the second row na x−y, so both equations match the right-hand side (7; 1).
l-m-h3-b0c36-21.s.s2.model.1: If you multiply each row coefficients by the column vector (x; y) and add, e give the original equations, so e get the same meaning.

l-m-h3-b0c36-22.title: To change probability wey dem state for words into symbols
l-m-h3-b0c36-22.goal: Change "the probability of being actually sick among people wey test positive" to another form (equation, table, picture, words), and explain why e get the same meaning.
l-m-h3-b0c36-22.material: Event D na "actually sick" and event T na "test positive". We wan write the sentence "the probability of being actually sick among people wey dem judge positive" for symbols.
l-m-h3-b0c36-22.s.s1.prompt: Choose the symbols wey get the same meaning as the sentence.
l-m-h3-b0c36-22.s.s1.r.b: This na the probability of being positive among the sick, so dem swap the condition and the result.
l-m-h3-b0c36-22.s.s1.r.c: This na the overall proportion wey be positive and sick together, no be the proportion among the positives.
l-m-h3-b0c36-22.s.s1.r.d: This na only the probability of being positive; e no include whether the person dey sick.
l-m-h3-b0c36-22.s.s1.explain: "Among people wey test positive" na the condition T, and wetin we wan know na D, so e be P(D|T).
l-m-h3-b0c36-22.s.s2.model.0: "Among the positives" na the condition and the event wey we wan find na to dey sick, so we write P(D|T), and the condition go to the right of the vertical bar.
l-m-h3-b0c36-22.s.s2.model.1: Dem narrow the range to only the people wey test positive, so T become the condition, and the proportion wey sick inside that group na P(D|T).

l-m-h3-b0c36-23.title: To change gradient descent into formula
l-m-h3-b0c36-23.goal: Change one step of gradient descent to another form (equation, table, picture, words), and explain why e get the same meaning.
l-m-h3-b0c36-23.material: For words, one step of gradient descent na "from the current position, move for the direction wey opposite the slope, by the slope multiply by the learning rate η".
l-m-h3-b0c36-23.s.s1.prompt: Which formula get the same meaning as this description?
l-m-h3-b0c36-23.s.s1.r.a: This one dey move for the direction of the slope, go where the value dey big.
l-m-h3-b0c36-23.s.s1.r.b: Dem use the position x instead of the slope f'(x).
l-m-h3-b0c36-23.s.s1.r.d: Dem no count the current position x.
l-m-h3-b0c36-23.s.s1.explain: To go opposite the slope mean to subtract, and the size of the move na η·f'(x), so e be x−η·f'(x).
l-m-h3-b0c36-23.s.s2.model.0: You must go opposite the slope, so you subtract, and the amount wey you move na η multiply by f'(x), so e become x−η f'(x).
l-m-h3-b0c36-23.s.s2.model.1: To start from the current position x and subtract η f'(x) make the same move as the description, so e get the same meaning.

l-m-h3-b0c36-24.title: To talk am another way as the proportion of sick people wey dem miss
l-m-h3-b0c36-24.goal: Change "the proportion wey dem miss among people wey really sick" to another form (equation, table, picture, words), and explain why e get the same meaning.
l-m-h3-b0c36-24.material: Out of 100 tests, 30 sick people dem find correct as sick, 10 sick people dem miss, 5 healthy people dem call sick, and 55 healthy people dem find correct.
l-m-h3-b0c36-24.s.s1.prompt: Which one na "the proportion wey dem miss among people wey really sick"?
l-m-h3-b0c36-24.s.s1.r.a: You use all 100 tests as the denominator. The denominator suppose be the number of sick people.
l-m-h3-b0c36-24.s.s1.r.c: This na the proportion wey dem find, no be the proportion wey dem miss.
l-m-h3-b0c36-24.s.s1.r.d: You calculate based on the healthy people wey dem call sick.
l-m-h3-b0c36-24.s.s1.explain: 30+10=40 people really sick, and dem miss 10 of dem. 10/40=25%, wey be wetin remain from the recall of 75%.
l-m-h3-b0c36-24.s.s2.model.0: Dem miss 10 of the 40 people wey really sick, so e be 10/40=25%, wey equal 1 minus the proportion wey dem find, 75%.
l-m-h3-b0c36-24.s.s2.model.1: The denominator must be 40, the number of people wey really sick, so write 10/40=25%, no be 10/100.

l-m-h3-b0c37-21.title: How to write table as matrix
l-m-h3-b0c37-21.goal: Change the table of fruit stock by store to another form (expression, table, picture, words), then explain why e mean the same thing.
l-m-h3-b0c37-21.material: Store A get 3 apples and 2 pears, and Store B get 1 apple and 4 pears. Write am as matrix with the rows as the stores (for the order A, B) and the columns as the fruits (for the order apple, pear).
l-m-h3-b0c37-21.s.s1.prompt: Choose the matrix wey show the same information.
l-m-h3-b0c37-21.s.s1.r.a: Dem mix up the positions of the entries, so Store A pears dem read as 4.
l-m-h3-b0c37-21.s.s1.r.b: Dem swap the rows and columns, so the first row become the apple stock.
l-m-h3-b0c37-21.s.s1.r.c: Dem swap the order of the columns, so the first column become the pear stock.
l-m-h3-b0c37-21.s.s1.explain: The first row na Store A (3 apples, 2 pears) and the second row na Store B (1 apple, 4 pears), so e be (3 2; 1 4).
l-m-h3-b0c37-21.s.s2.model.0: For the first row, write 3 and 2, Store A apples and pears for that order, and for the second row, write Store B 1 and 4, so e mean the same as the table.
l-m-h3-b0c37-21.s.s2.model.1: The rows na the stores and the columns na the fruits, so each entry match one cell of the table, wey make am the same information.

l-m-h3-b0c37-22.title: How to put the meaning of expected value into words
l-m-h3-b0c37-22.goal: Change the expected value 3.5 of die roll to another form (expression, table, picture, words), then explain why e mean the same thing.
l-m-h3-b0c37-22.material: The expected value of the number wey show when you roll one fair die na 3.5. You wan put wetin this number really mean into everyday words.
l-m-h3-b0c37-22.s.s1.prompt: Choose the sentence wey mean the same as the expected value 3.5.
l-m-h3-b0c37-22.s.s1.o.a: If you roll am once, 3.5 go show
l-m-h3-b0c37-22.s.s1.r.a: Die no get face wey be 3.5. E no be the result of one roll.
l-m-h3-b0c37-22.s.s1.o.b: 3.5 na the face wey show pass
l-m-h3-b0c37-22.s.s1.r.b: 3.5 no be face, and all the faces get the same probability.
l-m-h3-b0c37-22.s.s1.r.c: Other faces fit show too. The expected value na average size.
l-m-h3-b0c37-22.s.s1.o.d: If you roll am many times and take the average, e go near 3.5
l-m-h3-b0c37-22.s.s1.explain: The expected value no be the result of one roll but the value wey the average go near when you repeat many times.
l-m-h3-b0c37-22.s.s2.model.0: The average of the faces na (1+2+…+6)/6=3.5, and the more times you roll, the more the average go near this value, so e mean the same.
l-m-h3-b0c37-22.s.s2.model.1: The expected value na about the average of repeated rolls, no be one single face, so the sentence wey talk say the average go near 3.5 na the correct one.

l-m-h3-b0c38-06.title: To write system of equations again as matrix equation
l-m-h3-b0c38-06.goal: Write the matrix-product form of one system of equations again for another representation (equation, table, picture, words), and explain why e mean the same thing.
l-m-h3-b0c38-06.material: We wan write the system of equations 2x+y=5, x−y=1 again as matrix equation for the form (coefficient matrix)(x; y)=(right side). Semicolon (;) mark new row of matrix.
l-m-h3-b0c38-06.s.s1.prompt: Which matrix equation mean the same as the original system of equations?
l-m-h3-b0c38-06.s.s1.r.a: The coefficient of y for the second row na -1, but dem write am as +1.
l-m-h3-b0c38-06.s.s1.r.b: Dem swap the order of 5 and 1 for the right side.
l-m-h3-b0c38-06.s.s1.explain: Write the coefficients of each equation for one row, and write the right side for column for the same order. x=2, y=1 satisfy both equations.
l-m-h3-b0c38-06.s.s2.model.0: The first row get coefficients 2, 1, the second row get 1, -1, and the right side na 5, 1, so e be [2 1; 1 -1][x; y]=[5; 1].
l-m-h3-b0c38-06.s.s2.model.1: If you put x=2, y=1 inside the matrix equation, e give 5 and 1 for the rows, so e mean the same as the original system of equations.

l-m-h3-b0c38-15.material: Quiz score X dey come out as 1 point with probability 0.2, 2 points with 0.5, and 3 points with 0.3. The expected value na E(X)=1×0.2+2×0.5+3×0.3=2.1. Choose another expression wey get the same meaning.
l-m-h3-b0c38-15.s.s1.prompt: Which expression get the same meaning as E(X)?
l-m-h3-b0c38-15.s.s1.o.a: The midpoint between the score wey get the biggest probability and the one wey get the smallest
l-m-h3-b0c38-15.s.s1.r.a: You no fit find middle value from the sizes of the probabilities.
l-m-h3-b0c38-15.s.s1.o.b: The score wey dey come out most often, 2 points
l-m-h3-b0c38-15.s.s1.r.b: Na the mode be that. The expected value na weighted average.
l-m-h3-b0c38-15.s.s1.o.c: Di simple average of 1, 2, and 3 points, 2 points
l-m-h3-b0c38-15.s.s1.r.c: Dat one na simple average wey probability no weigh.
l-m-h3-b0c38-15.s.s1.o.d: Di average when 2, 5, and 3 out of 10 people get 1, 2, and 3 points
l-m-h3-b0c38-15.s.s1.explain: If out of 10 people 2 get 1 point, 5 get 2 points, and 3 get 3 points, di average na (2+10+9)÷10=2.1, di same.
l-m-h3-b0c38-15.s.s2.model.0: If you turn di probabilities to proportions of people, e go be (1×2+2×5+3×3)÷10=2.1, so e mean di same as di expected value.
l-m-h3-b0c38-15.s.s2.model.1: Di expected value na average wey probability weigh, so e give di same value as di average of 10 people for di same proportions.

l-m-h3-b0c38-23.title: To put mean squared error into words
l-m-h3-b0c38-23.goal: Rewrite di mean squared error (1/n)Σ(prediction−actual)² for another representation (equation, table, picture, words), then explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-h3-b0c38-23.material: Di mean squared error (MSE) na (1/n)Σ(predicted value−actual value)². For predictions [2,5,4] and actual values [3,5,2], e na (1+0+4)÷3=5/3. Make we put dis formula into words.
l-m-h3-b0c38-23.s.s1.prompt: Which expression get di same meaning as MSE?
l-m-h3-b0c38-23.s.s1.o.a: Di mean of di sum of all di errors
l-m-h3-b0c38-23.s.s1.r.a: Di signs of di errors dey cancel out. Di squaring no dey.
l-m-h3-b0c38-23.s.s1.o.b: Di sum of di squares of all di errors
l-m-h3-b0c38-23.s.s1.r.b: Di mean, wey you go get when you divide by di count n, no dey.
l-m-h3-b0c38-23.s.s1.o.c: Di mean of di squares of di errors
l-m-h3-b0c38-23.s.s1.o.d: Di square of di sum of di errors
l-m-h3-b0c38-23.s.s1.r.d: You must square each error then add. Di order different.
l-m-h3-b0c38-23.s.s1.explain: Square each error then take di mean. Di signs no dey cancel and big errors count more.
l-m-h3-b0c38-23.s.s2.model.0: Di formula dey square di errors and divide by n, so e na di mean of di squared errors.
l-m-h3-b0c38-23.s.s2.model.1: If you just add di errors −1 and 2, dem go cancel, so square first then take di mean.

l-m-h3-b0c38-31.s.s1.prompt: Which explanation get the same meaning?
l-m-h3-b0c38-31.s.s1.o.a: The more data dey, the bigger the error go become
l-m-h3-b0c38-31.s.s1.r.a: From the numbers alone you no fit know the relationship between the amount of data and the error.
l-m-h3-b0c38-31.s.s1.o.b: E never learn well, since e no fit even fit the training data
l-m-h3-b0c38-31.s.s1.r.b: The training error small for 2%, so e no dey under-learn.
l-m-h3-b0c38-31.s.s1.o.c: E fit the training data well but e weak for new data
l-m-h3-b0c38-31.s.s1.o.d: The validation data easy pass the training data
l-m-h3-b0c38-31.s.s1.r.d: The validation error bigger, so na the harder side for real.

l-m-h3-b0c41-25.title: To write the cost per item again with other words
l-m-h3-b0c41-25.goal: Write another expression wey show the cost of 2,000 won per item for another form (expression, table, picture, or words), and explain why dem mean the same thing.
l-m-h3-b0c41-25.material: To make 20 mugs cost 36,000 won for materials and 4,000 won for packaging. The cost per item na 40,000÷20=2,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c41-25.s.s1.prompt: Which expression mean the same as cost of 2,000 won per item?
l-m-h3-b0c41-25.s.s1.o.a: Material cost of 36,000 won divided by 20
l-m-h3-b0c41-25.s.s1.r.a: The packaging cost miss. This one na 1,800 won.

l-m-h3-b0c41-25.s.s1.r.c: E multiply instead of to divide by the number of items.
l-m-h3-b0c41-25.s.s1.o.d: Add material cost per item, 1,800 won, and packaging cost per item, 200 won
l-m-h3-b0c41-25.s.s1.explain: 36,000÷20=1,800 and 4,000÷20=200, and the sum na 2,000 won. Na the same value as total cost÷number of items.
l-m-h3-b0c41-25.s.s2.model.0: To divide the total cost by 20 na the same as to divide the material cost and the packaging cost each by 20 and add dem, so dem mean the same thing.
l-m-h3-b0c41-25.s.s2.model.1: Since 1,800+200=2,000, the sum of the material cost per item and the packaging cost per item equal the cost per item.

l-m-h3-b0c42-28.material: Test scores get mean of 50 and standard deviation of 10. The means of samples of 25 students wey dem choose at random dey distribute with mean 50 and standard deviation 2. Write this fact in words.

l-m-h3-b0c42-31.s.s2.model.1: The relative expression "2 times" fit rewrite as 3 people wey become 6 for every 1 group of 10,000, and the increase na 3 people, so this sentence correct.

l-m-h3-b0c43-26.material: For one test, dem reject the “hypothesis say no effect dey” for 5% significance level. Put this result inside normal everyday words.
l-m-h3-b0c43-26.s.s1.o.a: The probability say the hypothesis of no effect correct na 5%

l-m-h3-b0c43-26.s.s1.o.d: The size of the effect na 5%
l-m-h3-b0c43-26.s.s1.r.d: 5% no be the size of the effect; na the standard for judging.

l-m-h3-b0c43-26.s.s2.model.1: 5% no be the probability say the hypothesis correct; na the standard for how rare the result be under the assumption, so this sentence mean the same thing.

l-m-h3-b0c49-26.title: Thinking of Average as Total
l-m-h3-b0c49-26.goal: Turn average condition into total condition: show am in different form (formula, table, picture, words) and explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-h3-b0c49-26.material: For 7 days, you walk average of 6000 steps each day. Think of average as total to find how many steps you need walk on day 8 so daily average through day 8 go be 6500 steps.

l-m-h3-b0c49-26.s.s1.r.a: Total for 8 days na 52000 steps, so 13000 steps too much.

l-m-h3-b0c49-26.s.s1.r.b: If na only day 8 be 6500 steps, average go be around 6060 steps.
l-m-h3-b0c49-26.s.s1.o.c: Total for 7 days na 42000 steps and total for 8 days na 52000 steps, so 10000 steps
l-m-h3-b0c49-26.s.s1.r.d: Finding average of averages no tell you day-8 steps.
l-m-h3-b0c49-26.s.s1.explain: Average×days na total. If you subtract 7-day total 42000 from 8-day total 52000, you get 10000 steps.
l-m-h3-b0c49-26.s.s2.model.0: Total for 8 days na 8×6500=52000 and for 7 days na 42000, so you need walk 10000 steps on day 8.
l-m-h3-b0c49-26.s.s2.model.1: Average na total divided by number of days, so if you turn am into total, you fit add di missing amount all at once.

l-m-h3-b0d07-32.title: Turn series limit into definite integral

l-m-h3-b0d07-32.s.s2.model.0: Gathering n pieces with width 2/n give length 2, x=1+2k/n go 1 to 3, so ∫₁³ f(x)dx.
l-m-h3-b0d07-32.s.s2.model.1: When k=1, x just above 1; when k=n, x=3, so interval [1,3]. That equal this integral.

l-m-h3-b0d09-38.title: Showing Center and Radius in Sphere Equation
l-m-h3-b0d09-38.goal: Change expanded sphere equation to another form (equation, table, picture, words), and explain why dem mean same thing.
l-m-h3-b0d09-38.material: Sphere equation expanded as x² + y² + z² − 2x + 4y − 6z + 5 = 0. Rewrite am so center and radius dey clear at first look.
l-m-h3-b0d09-38.s.s1.r.a: Signs of center coordinates turn opposite.
l-m-h3-b0d09-38.s.s1.r.b: Right side na radius squared, so e be 9, no be 3.
l-m-h3-b0d09-38.s.s1.r.c: Dem get right side wrong by adding constant term 5.

l-m-h3-b0d09-38.s.s2.model.1: Move right side 9 to left and expand to get −2x+4y−6z and constant 1+4+9−9=5, so e same as original equation.

l-m-h3-b0d10-10.material: Ellipse equation dey written expanded as 4x² + 9y² − 16x + 18y − 11 = 0. Rewrite am to show center and lengths of major and minor axes.

l-m-h3-b0d10-10.s.s2.model.1: When you expand dis equation, you get 4x²+9y²−16x+18y+25=36, wey match original equation, so na same ellipse.

l-m-h3-b0c33-26.goal: Compare two methods or claims about di order to apply one coupon and one discount, choose di one wey better, and explain your reasons.
l-m-h3-b0c33-26.material: You wan buy shoes wey get list price of 20,000 won. You fit use both 5,000-won coupon and extra 10% discount, and you fit decide which one to apply first.
l-m-h3-b0c33-26.s.s1.prompt: Which way you fit take pay less?
l-m-h3-b0c33-26.s.s1.o.a: To use only di coupon cheap pass: 15,000 won

l-m-h3-b0c33-27.title: Sure 8,000 won versus coin toss for 20,000 won
l-m-h3-b0c33-27.goal: Compare two methods or claims about how to compare two choices by expected value, choose di one wey better, and explain your reasons.
l-m-h3-b0c33-27.material: Choice A give you sure 8,000 won. Choice B na coin toss: heads give 20,000 won and tails give 0 won. Compare dem by expected value only.
l-m-h3-b0c33-27.s.s1.prompt: Which judgment better based on expected value?
l-m-h3-b0c33-27.s.s1.o.a: B: di best outcome na 20,000 won
l-m-h3-b0c33-27.s.s1.r.a: Dat one only look di good outcome. Di 0 won from tails must enter di average too.
l-m-h3-b0c33-27.s.s1.o.c: Dem na di same: di average na 8,000 won
l-m-h3-b0c33-27.s.s1.r.c: Di average for B na (20,000+0)÷2=10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c33-27.s.s1.r.d: To be sure na about risk preference. B get bigger expected value.
l-m-h3-b0c33-27.s.s1.explain: Di expected value of B na 0.5×20,000+0.5×0=10,000 won, wey big pass A own 8,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c33-27.s.s2.model.0: Di expected value of B na 0.5×20,000+0.5×0=10,000 won, so e big pass A at 8,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c33-27.s.s2.model.1: Di expected value na di sum of each outcome times im probability, so even if you include di 0 won from tails, B still dey 2,000 won more.

l-m-h3-b0c33-28.material: Shop A sales go from 100 × 10,000 won to 200 × 10,000 won, and Shop B own go from 1,000 × 10,000 won to 1,500 × 10,000 won. We wan compare how fast di two shops grow.

l-m-h3-b0c33-28.s.s1.o.a: Compare dis year sales: B big pass
l-m-h3-b0c33-28.s.s1.r.a: Dis year value alone no tell us how much e grow.
l-m-h3-b0c33-28.s.s1.o.b: Compare di starting sales: B big pass
l-m-h3-b0c33-28.s.s1.r.b: Di starting value no be how much e grow.
l-m-h3-b0c33-28.s.s1.o.c: Compare increase amounts: B 500 × 10,000 won > A 100 × 10,000 won
l-m-h3-b0c33-28.s.s1.r.c: Di shops get different sizes, so di amount of increase alone no fit tell us who grow faster.

l-m-h3-b0c33-28.s.s2.model.0: Di growth rate na ratio to di starting value: A na 100% and B na 50%, so A grow faster.
l-m-h3-b0c33-28.s.s2.model.1: Di two shops get different size, so e fair pass to compare by di ratio to di starting value than by di amount of increase.
