l-m-h3-b0c34-25.title: Interest rate 3.5% (dem collect tax) versus 3.0% (no tax)
l-m-h3-b0c34-25.goal: Compare di two methods or claims about di interest wey remain after tax, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain di evidence.
l-m-h3-b0c34-25.material: Two 1-year deposits dey. Account A pay 3.5% every year, and dem collect 15.4% of di interest as tax. Account B pay 3.0% every year and no tax dey. If you deposit di same amount, choose di one wey leave you more interest.
l-m-h3-b0c34-25.s.s1.o.a: A: di interest rate of 3.5% high pass
l-m-h3-b0c34-25.s.s1.r.a: After dem collect tax, A rate drop to about 2.96%.
l-m-h3-b0c34-25.s.s1.o.b: No fit tell: nobody know di principal
l-m-h3-b0c34-25.s.s1.r.b: If di principal na di same, you only need to compare di rates, so you no need to know di principal.
l-m-h3-b0c34-25.s.s1.o.c: Di same: tax no affect di interest
l-m-h3-b0c34-25.s.s1.r.c: Dem collect tax from di interest, so di interest wey you keep go small.
l-m-h3-b0c34-25.s.s1.explain: A keep 3.5%×(1−0.154)≈2.96%, wey small pass B own 3.0%. If di principal na di same, B give more.
l-m-h3-b0c34-25.s.s2.model.0: A after-tax rate na 3.5%×0.846, about 2.96%, so e leave less interest than B own 3.0%.
l-m-h3-b0c34-25.s.s2.model.1: You must compare di rates after dem collect tax, so even with lower rate, B wey no tax dey leave more.

l-m-h3-b0c34-26.s.s1.r.b: 2-year subscription na 480,000 won, wey different from to buy.
l-m-h3-b0c34-26.s.s1.o.c: Subscription: e easy to stop wen you want
l-m-h3-b0c34-26.s.s1.r.c: If you plan to use am for 2 years, you must compare by total cost.

l-m-h3-b0c34-26.s.s2.model.0: Di subscription na 20,000 won×24 months=480,000 won and to buy na 360,000 won, so to buy cost less if you use am for 2 years.
l-m-h3-b0c34-26.s.s2.model.1: Even if di monthly amount small, e dey add up over long time, so compare by total cost, and after 18 months to buy na di better deal.

l-m-h3-b0c34-27.title: Salary up 4%, prices up 6%: who correct?
l-m-h3-b0c34-27.topic: Real purchasing power (wetin your money fit really buy)
l-m-h3-b0c34-27.goal: Compare di two methods or claims about di salary increase rate and di price increase rate, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain di evidence.
l-m-h3-b0c34-27.material: Salary go up 4% and prices go up 6% for di same period. A talk say, "Salary go up, so life don better." B talk say, "Prices go up more, so wetin we fit buy don reduce."
l-m-h3-b0c34-27.s.s1.o.a: B: because prices rise more than salary
l-m-h3-b0c34-27.s.s1.o.b: A: because salary no go down
l-m-h3-b0c34-27.s.s1.r.b: Even if di amount grow, if prices rise more, di amount wey you fit buy go down.
l-m-h3-b0c34-27.s.s1.r.c: Even if di raise look big, e small pass di 6% rise for prices.
l-m-h3-b0c34-27.s.s1.o.d: No fit compare: because di units different
l-m-h3-b0c34-27.s.s1.r.d: Both na growth rates (%), so dem fit compare directly.
l-m-h3-b0c34-27.s.s1.explain: Salary go up 4% and prices go up 6%. 1.04÷1.06≈0.98, so wetin you fit buy go down by about 2%.
l-m-h3-b0c34-27.s.s2.model.0: Prices rise more than salary, so with di same salary you fit really buy less.
l-m-h3-b0c34-27.s.s2.model.1: Di salary growth rate of 4% small pass di price increase rate of 6%, so we fit talk say real purchasing power don drop by about 2%.

l-m-h3-b0c34-29.title: You suppose buy di extended warranty? Think am through with expected value
l-m-h3-b0c34-29.goal: Compare di two methods or claims about di sign-up fee and di expected repair cost, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain di evidence.
l-m-h3-b0c34-29.material: If you pay 3 × 10,000 won for extended warranty on one home appliance, dem go waive repair cost of 20 × 10,000 won if e spoil. Di chance say e go spoil within 1 year na 10%. Decide whether to sign up based only on di expected repair cost.
l-m-h3-b0c34-29.s.s1.o.a: Sign up: because 20 × 10,000 won plenty if e spoil
l-m-h3-b0c34-29.s.s1.r.a: You only look di size of di amount and you no multiply by di 10% chance say e go spoil.
l-m-h3-b0c34-29.s.s1.o.b: Sign up: because 10% chance no low
l-m-h3-b0c34-29.s.s1.r.b: Dem must multiply di probability by di repair cost and compare am as expected value.
l-m-h3-b0c34-29.s.s1.o.c: E no matter: di expected value equal 3 × 10,000 won
l-m-h3-b0c34-29.s.s1.r.c: Di expected repair cost na 20 × 10,000 won × 0.1 = 2 × 10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c34-29.s.s1.o.d: No sign up: expected repair cost 2 × 10,000 won < 3 × 10,000 won
l-m-h3-b0c34-29.s.s1.explain: Di expected repair cost na 20 × 10,000 won × 0.1 = 2 × 10,000 won, wey small pass di sign-up fee of 3 × 10,000 won. If you look expected value alone, you no suppose sign up.
l-m-h3-b0c34-29.s.s2.model.0: Di expected repair cost na 20 × 10,000 won × 0.1 = 2 × 10,000 won, and di sign-up fee of 3 × 10,000 won big pass, so by expected value e better make you no sign up.
l-m-h3-b0c34-29.s.s2.model.1: Even if e spoil, you save only 2 × 10,000 won on average, so to pay 3 × 10,000 won na loss by expected value.

l-m-h3-b0c35-07.title: Between 4% simple interest and 3.8% compound interest
l-m-h3-b0c35-07.topic: To compare simple and compound interest
l-m-h3-b0c35-07.goal: Compare di two methods or claims about simple and compound interest on one 3-year deposit, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain di evidence.
l-m-h3-b0c35-07.material: You deposit 100 × 10,000 won for 3 years. A na 4% every year simple interest and B na 3.8% every year compound interest. People dey talk say compound interest better, but di rates different. Compare by di amount after 3 years.
l-m-h3-b0c35-07.s.s1.prompt: Which explanation fit, if you judge by di amount after 3 years?
l-m-h3-b0c35-07.s.s1.r.b: You no calculate di value after 3 years by yourself.
l-m-h3-b0c35-07.s.s1.r.c: You estimate di effect of compound interest as bigger than wetin e really be.
l-m-h3-b0c35-07.s.s1.o.d: B get more because na compound interest
l-m-h3-b0c35-07.s.s1.r.d: You only look di name "compound interest" and you no consider di difference for di rates.
l-m-h3-b0c35-07.s.s1.explain: A na 100+4×3=112 × 10,000 won and B na 100×1.038³≈111.84 × 10,000 won, so A big small pass.
l-m-h3-b0c35-07.s.s2.model.0: A na 4%×3=12%, wey be 112 × 10,000 won, and B na 1.038³≈1.118, wey be 111.8 × 10,000 won, so A big small pass.
l-m-h3-b0c35-07.s.s2.model.1: Di effect of compound interest dey get bigger over long period, and 3 years short, so A, wey im rate high by 0.2%p, come out ahead.

l-m-h3-b0c35-15.goal: Compare di two methods or claims about two tax systems wey base on income, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain di evidence.
l-m-h3-b0c35-15.material: Plan A charge 12% of income. Plan B charge 5% on income up to 2,000 ×10,000 won, and 20% on di part wey pass 2,000 ×10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c35-15.s.s1.prompt: At wetin income A tax low pass B own?
l-m-h3-b0c35-15.s.s1.r.a: B pay 75 ×10,000 won and A pay 180 ×10,000 won, so B pay less.
l-m-h3-b0c35-15.s.s1.r.b: B pay 200 ×10,000 won and A pay 300 ×10,000 won, so B pay less.
l-m-h3-b0c35-15.s.s1.r.c: B pay 400 ×10,000 won and A pay 420 ×10,000 won, so B pay less.
l-m-h3-b0c35-15.s.s1.explain: If income pass 3,750 ×10,000 won, A pay less. At 4,500 ×10,000 won, A pay 540 and B pay 600 (×10,000 won).
l-m-h3-b0c35-15.s.s2.model.0: At 4,500 ×10,000 won, A pay 540 ×10,000 won and B pay 100+500=600 ×10,000 won, so A pay less.
l-m-h3-b0c35-15.s.s2.model.1: Di two plans equal at 3,750 ×10,000 won, and na only wen income high pass dat one B 20% go get big effect, so 4,500 ×10,000 won na di correct answer.

l-m-h3-b0c35-22.title: To compare expected value and risk together
l-m-h3-b0c35-22.goal: Compare two ways or claims about di expected value and risk of two products, choose di one wey suit pass, then explain di reason.
l-m-h3-b0c35-22.material: A get half chance each of return of +10% or −2%, and B get half chance each of +30% or −20%. Compare di range of variation too, no be only di expected value.
l-m-h3-b0c35-22.s.s1.o.a: A get higher expected value, so e better for every way
l-m-h3-b0c35-22.s.s1.r.a: A na 4% and B na 5%, so B get higher expected value.
l-m-h3-b0c35-22.s.s1.o.b: A riskier because im chance of loss different
l-m-h3-b0c35-22.s.s1.r.b: Both products get di same 50% chance of loss.
l-m-h3-b0c35-22.s.s1.o.c: B, wey get higher expected value, get lower risk too
l-m-h3-b0c35-22.s.s1.r.c: B fit drop reach −20%, so im risk actually big pass.
l-m-h3-b0c35-22.s.s1.o.d: B get 1%p higher expected value and bigger range of variation
l-m-h3-b0c35-22.s.s1.explain: Di expected values na 4% for A and 5% for B, and di return ranges na −2 to 10% for A and −20 to 30% for B, so B dey swing more.
l-m-h3-b0c35-22.s.s2.model.0: A na 0.5×10−0.5×2=4% and B na 0.5×30−0.5×20=5%, so B get higher expected value but e fit fall reach −20%.
l-m-h3-b0c35-22.s.s2.model.1: Both get di same 50% chance of loss, so di difference na di size of di loss, and B riskier even though im average high pass.

l-m-h3-b0c35-30.title: How to compare interest after dem don comot tax
l-m-h3-b0c35-30.goal: Compare two ways or claims about deposit interest before and after tax, choose the one wey fit pass, then explain the reason.
l-m-h3-b0c35-30.material: You deposit 1,000 ×10,000 won for 1 year. A dey pay 3.0% every year with no tax for the interest. B dey pay 3.4% every year, but dem go take 15.4% of the interest wey you receive as tax.
l-m-h3-b0c35-30.s.s1.prompt: Which one give more interest wey you actually keep?
l-m-h3-b0c35-30.s.s1.r.b: E forget to subtract the tax from B interest.
l-m-h3-b0c35-30.s.s1.o.c: B, about 31 ×10,000 won even after tax
l-m-h3-b0c35-30.s.s1.r.c: E estimate the tax as much smaller than how e really be.
l-m-h3-b0c35-30.s.s1.r.d: E no calculate the interest after tax directly.
l-m-h3-b0c35-30.s.s1.explain: B tax na 34×0.154≈5.2 (×10,000 won), so the interest wey you keep na about 28.8 ×10,000 won, wey small pass A own 30 ×10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c35-30.s.s2.model.0: Dem take about 5.2 ×10,000 won, wey be 15.4% of 34 ×10,000 won, from B, e remain about 28.8 ×10,000 won, so A own 30 ×10,000 won pass.
l-m-h3-b0c35-30.s.s2.model.1: Even though the rate look like say e high by 0.4%p, dem dey take tax from the interest, so after tax B go end lower.

l-m-h3-b0c36-25.title: The two vectors dey point the same direction?
l-m-h3-b0c36-25.goal: Compare two ways or claims about the directions of the vectors (1,2) and (2,4), choose the one wey fit pass, and explain your reasoning.
l-m-h3-b0c36-25.material: Two claims dey about the directions of vectors u=(1,2) and v=(2,4). Claim A: The entries different, so the directions different. Claim B: v na 2 times u, so the directions na the same.
l-m-h3-b0c36-25.s.s1.o.a: A: The entries different, so the directions different
l-m-h3-b0c36-25.s.s1.r.a: You miss say vectors fit get different sizes and still point the same way.
l-m-h3-b0c36-25.s.s1.o.b: B: E be 2 times relation, so the same direction
l-m-h3-b0c36-25.s.s1.o.c: Both correct: any direction fit work
l-m-h3-b0c36-25.s.s1.r.c: The direction don settle as just one. Two claims wey dey fight each other no fit both correct.
l-m-h3-b0c36-25.s.s1.o.d: The sizes must equal before the directions go equal
l-m-h3-b0c36-25.s.s1.r.d: You mix up size and direction. Dem dey decide direction separate from size.
l-m-h3-b0c36-25.s.s1.explain: If v=2u, then v na u wey dem stretch for the same direction. Only the size different and the direction na the same.
l-m-h3-b0c36-25.s.s2.model.0: v=(2,4)=2×(1,2), so na u wey dem stretch to twice the length for the same direction, and the entries different because the sizes different.
l-m-h3-b0c36-25.s.s2.model.1: Vectors wey dey the same direction na positive multiples of each other, so B, wey get 2 times relation, correct, and A take difference for size as difference for direction.

l-m-h3-b0c36-26.title: Which survey result we suppose trust?
l-m-h3-b0c36-26.goal: Compare two ways or claims about the results of two surveys wey get different sample sizes, choose the one wey fit pass, and explain your reasoning.
l-m-h3-b0c36-26.material: About the same policy, for Survey A 30 of 50 people (60%) approve, and for Survey B 280 of 500 people (56%) approve. The two surveys choose people the same way.
l-m-h3-b0c36-26.s.s1.prompt: Which one pass for trust to guess the overall approval rate?
l-m-h3-b0c36-26.s.s1.o.a: Same: the two proportions near each other
l-m-h3-b0c36-26.s.s1.r.a: Even if the proportions near each other, how far you fit trust dem depend on the sample size.
l-m-h3-b0c36-26.s.s1.o.b: A: The approval rate come out higher
l-m-h3-b0c36-26.s.s1.r.b: Higher value no mean say e pass for trust.
l-m-h3-b0c36-26.s.s1.o.c: A: E accurate because the number of respondents small
l-m-h3-b0c36-26.s.s1.r.c: The smaller the sample, the more chance go affect am.
l-m-h3-b0c36-26.s.s1.o.d: B: The sample big, so the margin of error small
l-m-h3-b0c36-26.s.s1.explain: The bigger the sample, the closer the sample proportion go dey to the population proportion, so the margin of error go shrink. So Survey B pass for trust.
l-m-h3-b0c36-26.s.s2.model.0: Sample wey big 10 times get smaller standard error, so di 56% of Survey B fit near di overall approval rate more.
l-m-h3-b0c36-26.s.s2.model.1: With 50 people, di proportion dey change well well if just small people differ, so you fit trust di result from 500 people more.

l-m-h3-b0c36-27.title: To compare learning rates 1.0 and 0.1
l-m-h3-b0c36-27.goal: Compare two ways or claims about gradient descent with different learning rates, choose di one wey suit pass, then explain your reasoning.
l-m-h3-b0c36-27.material: Do gradient descent on f(x)=x² from di starting point x=4. With learning rate 1.0, x go 4 → −4 → 4 → …, and with learning rate 0.1 e change 4 → 3.2 → 2.56 → ….
l-m-h3-b0c36-27.s.s1.prompt: Which one suit pass to find di minimum for x=0?
l-m-h3-b0c36-27.s.s1.o.a: Learning rate 1.0: e dey move plenty at once
l-m-h3-b0c36-27.s.s1.r.a: E dey move plenty, but e dey jump pass di minimum and just dey go back and forth for one place.
l-m-h3-b0c36-27.s.s1.o.b: Learning rate 0.1: e dey near 0 more and more
l-m-h3-b0c36-27.s.s1.o.c: Both na di same: dem use di same formula
l-m-h3-b0c36-27.s.s1.r.c: Even with di same formula, di result dey different depending on di learning rate.
l-m-h3-b0c36-27.s.s1.o.d: Learning rate 1.0: e pass 0 and near am even more
l-m-h3-b0c36-27.s.s1.r.d: After e pass 0, e just dey go back and forth between 4 and −4. E no dey near.
l-m-h3-b0c36-27.s.s1.explain: Learning rate 1.0 just dey go back and forth between −4 and 4 and e no dey near 0 at all. With 0.1, di value dey shrink to 0.8 times each time and e dey near 0.
l-m-h3-b0c36-27.s.s2.model.0: Learning rate 1.0 dey only repeat 4 and −4, so e no fit near di minimum, while with 0.1 di value dey shrink and near 0.
l-m-h3-b0c36-27.s.s2.model.1: If one step too big, e go jump pass di minimum and dey go back and forth, so di small learning rate 0.1 suit pass.

l-m-h3-b0c36-28.title: We suppose trust di model wey get high training score?
l-m-h3-b0c36-28.goal: Compare two ways or claims about two models wey training and test scores different, choose di one wey suit pass, then explain your reasoning.
l-m-h3-b0c36-28.material: Model P get 99% accuracy for di training data and 80% for di test data wey e never see before. Model Q get 88% for training and 86% for di test. Dem measure both for di same way.
l-m-h3-b0c36-28.s.s1.prompt: Which model dem fit trust pass for new data?
l-m-h3-b0c36-28.s.s1.o.a: P: E get di highest training accuracy
l-m-h3-b0c36-28.s.s1.r.a: Even with high training score, e drop for data wey e never see before.
l-m-h3-b0c36-28.s.s1.o.b: P: E be 99% for training, so 80% na by chance
l-m-h3-b0c36-28.s.s1.r.b: Di test score of 80% dey tell us more about di performance for new data.
l-m-h3-b0c36-28.s.s1.o.c: Same: di averages of di two scores similar
l-m-h3-b0c36-28.s.s1.r.c: Di average no dey tell us di performance for new data.
l-m-h3-b0c36-28.s.s1.o.d: Q: Di gap between training and test scores small
l-m-h3-b0c36-28.s.s1.explain: P lean too much to di training data (overfitting) and e drop well well for di test. Q, wey im test score high and im gap small, dem fit trust pass.
l-m-h3-b0c36-28.s.s2.model.0: P get big gap of 19 percentage points between training and test, so e lean to di training data, and Q, wey get 86% for di test, dem fit trust pass.
l-m-h3-b0c36-28.s.s2.model.1: Di test score dey show di performance for new data, so Q wey get 86% better pass P wey get 80%, and im gap small too.

l-m-h3-b0c36-29.goal: Compare two ways or claims about di probability after streak of results for coin tossing, choose di one wey suit pass, then explain your reasoning.
l-m-h3-b0c36-29.material: Dem toss one fair coin and heads show 5 times one after di other. Claim A: Now di probability of tails big pass. Claim B: Di probability say di next toss go be tails still be 1/2.
l-m-h3-b0c36-29.s.s1.o.a: A: Heads show plenty, so e go balance out
l-m-h3-b0c36-29.s.s1.r.a: Coin no dey remember past results.
l-m-h3-b0c36-29.s.s1.o.b: B: Each toss no dey depend on di others
l-m-h3-b0c36-29.s.s1.o.c: A: 5 one after di other rare, so tails go show first
l-m-h3-b0c36-29.s.s1.r.c: 5 one after di other rare, but di probability of di next single toss no dey change.
l-m-h3-b0c36-29.s.s1.o.d: Both wrong: di next one na heads for sure
l-m-h3-b0c36-29.s.s1.r.d: Even after 5 one after di other, you no fit sure of di next result.
l-m-h3-b0c36-29.s.s1.explain: Di results of di tosses no dey depend on each other, so di previous 5 no dey change di next probability. Di probability of tails still be 1/2.
l-m-h3-b0c36-29.s.s2.model.0: Each toss no dey depend on di others, so di previous 5 no dey affect di next probability, and tails still be 1/2.
l-m-h3-b0c36-29.s.s2.model.1: Coin no dey remember past results, so Claim A, say tails go show more to balance things, no correct.

l-m-h3-b0c37-25.title: Book recommendations: dot product and cosine similarity
l-m-h3-b0c37-25.goal: Compare two methods of how to pick books wey get similar taste, choose the one wey fit pass, then explain how you reason am.
l-m-h3-b0c37-25.material: The taste na s=(1,2), Book X=(1,2), and Book Y=(6,0). Method A dey pick the book wey get bigger dot product, and Method B dey pick the book wey get bigger cosine similarity cosθ=(a·b)/(|a||b|). The goal na book wey get the same 'direction' as the taste.
l-m-h3-b0c37-25.s.s1.prompt: Which method fit pass for the goal to find book wey get the same direction?
l-m-h3-b0c37-25.s.s1.o.a: A: Pick the book wey get the biggest dot product
l-m-h3-b0c37-25.s.s1.r.a: Dot product dey get bigger the bigger the vectors be, so e no fit compare direction alone.
l-m-h3-b0c37-25.s.s1.r.b: Method A pick Y and Method B pick X, so dem differ.
l-m-h3-b0c37-25.s.s1.o.c: B: Divide by the sizes and compare only the direction
l-m-h3-b0c37-25.s.s1.o.d: A: Book wey get bigger size always better
l-m-h3-b0c37-25.s.s1.r.d: The size no get anything to do with how e fit the taste.
l-m-h3-b0c37-25.s.s1.explain: X get the same direction as s, so cos=1, and Y na about 0.45. The dot product rate Y, wey bigger for size, higher, so e no fit the goal of direction.
l-m-h3-b0c37-25.s.s2.model.0: Cosine similarity dey divide by the sizes and compare only direction, so e pick X, wey get the same direction as s, and e fit the goal.
l-m-h3-b0c37-25.s.s2.model.1: The dot product come out high for 6 because Y big, but im direction different, so if direction na the goal, B na the one wey fit.

l-m-h3-b0c37-26.title: How we suppose choose who to survey?
l-m-h3-b0c37-26.goal: Compare two sampling methods to find out how the whole school satisfy with school lunch, choose the one wey fit pass, then explain how you reason am.
l-m-h3-b0c37-26.material: You wan know how all 600 students for the school satisfy with school lunch. Method A dey randomly pick 60 students from the student list. Method B dey ask 60 students wey e meet for front of the lunchroom.
l-m-h3-b0c37-26.s.s1.prompt: Which method fit pass to estimate how the whole school satisfy?
l-m-h3-b0c37-26.s.s1.o.a: B: To ask for the spot dey more accurate
l-m-h3-b0c37-26.s.s1.r.a: E dey meet only students wey chop lunch, so e fit lean to one side.
l-m-h3-b0c37-26.s.s1.o.b: Both same: the number of students same, 60
l-m-h3-b0c37-26.s.s1.r.b: Even when the number of people same, the bias go differ depending on how dem pick am.
l-m-h3-b0c37-26.s.s1.o.c: A: Every student get the same chance to dem pick am
l-m-h3-b0c37-26.s.s1.o.d: B: E dey finish quick, so the error small
l-m-h3-b0c37-26.s.s1.r.d: To finish quick no get anything to do with the size of the error.
l-m-h3-b0c37-26.s.s1.explain: With random sampling, everybody get the same chance to dem pick am, so the sample resemble the whole group. For front of the lunchroom, e lean towards students wey dey chop lunch.
l-m-h3-b0c37-26.s.s2.model.0: If you pick randomly from the list, every student get the same chance, so the sample represent the whole school.
l-m-h3-b0c37-26.s.s2.model.1: For front of the lunchroom, you go meet only students wey dey chop lunch, so the satisfaction lean to one side, and A fit pass.

l-m-h3-b0c37-27.title: MSE and MAE: how to catch big mistakes
l-m-h3-b0c37-27.goal: Compare two ways to measure error, MAE and MSE, choose the one wey suitable pass, and explain your reasoning.
l-m-h3-b0c37-27.material: The errors of Model P na (2,2,2,2) and the errors of Model Q na (0,0,0,8). The mean of the absolute errors (MAE) of the two models na 2. We especially wan avoid big mistakes.
l-m-h3-b0c37-27.s.s1.prompt: Which measure suitable pass to separate the two models?
l-m-h3-b0c37-27.s.s1.o.a: MAE: The two models the same, so e dey enough
l-m-h3-b0c37-27.s.s1.r.a: The values the same, so e no fit pick out the model wey get big mistake.
l-m-h3-b0c37-27.s.s1.o.b: MAE: E weak against outliers, so dem no fit use am
l-m-h3-b0c37-27.s.s1.r.b: MAE just dey punish big errors less. No be measure wey dem no fit use.
l-m-h3-b0c37-27.s.s1.o.c: MSE: The sums of the errors the same, so e no fit separate dem
l-m-h3-b0c37-27.s.s1.r.c: MSE na 4 for P and 16 for Q, wey different, so dem fit separate dem.
l-m-h3-b0c37-27.s.s1.o.d: MSE: Dem square Q big error and e show
l-m-h3-b0c37-27.s.s1.explain: MSE na 4 for P and 16 for Q. E dey square big errors so dem count pass, so e pick out Q, wey get big mistake.
l-m-h3-b0c37-27.s.s2.model.0: MAE na 2 for the two, so e no fit separate dem, but MSE na 4 and 16, wey different, and e pick out Q wey get the big error 8, so MSE na the suitable one.
l-m-h3-b0c37-27.s.s2.model.1: The goal na to avoid big mistakes, so MSE, wey dey square errors and punish big values more, na the suitable one.

l-m-h3-b0c37-28.title: Wetin spam filter suppose look more?
l-m-h3-b0c37-28.goal: Compare two ways to evaluate spam filter, precision and recall, choose the one wey suitable pass, and explain your reasoning.
l-m-h3-b0c37-28.material: Spam filter dey sort mail as spam. The biggest problem na when important mail enter spam folder and you no fit see am. Claim A: we suppose look recall more. Claim B: we suppose look precision more.
l-m-h3-b0c37-28.s.s1.prompt: Which claim suitable pass for this goal?
l-m-h3-b0c37-28.s.s1.o.a: A: E must no miss even one spam
l-m-h3-b0c37-28.s.s1.r.a: To miss spam na only small wahala. You no go lose important mail.
l-m-h3-b0c37-28.s.s1.o.b: A: Higher recall means normal mail safer
l-m-h3-b0c37-28.s.s1.r.b: If you call more mail spam to raise recall, more normal mail go enter net.
l-m-h3-b0c37-28.s.s1.o.c: We no need any of dem: accuracy dey enough
l-m-h3-b0c37-28.s.s1.r.c: If spam few, even high accuracy no fit tell you how much normal mail you lose.
l-m-h3-b0c37-28.s.s1.o.d: B: Wetin e call spam must really be spam
l-m-h3-b0c37-28.s.s1.explain: If dem wrongly sort normal mail as spam, precision go drop. To protect important mail, the precision of the spam calls matter.
l-m-h3-b0c37-28.s.s2.model.0: Dem must no sort normal mail as spam, so you need to look precision, the share of real spam among wetin dem call spam.
l-m-h3-b0c37-28.s.s2.model.1: If you call more mail spam to raise recall, important mail go enter net, so B, wey look precision more, suitable.

l-m-h3-b0c37-29.title: Which of the two lines fit the data better
l-m-h3-b0c37-29.goal: Compare two line models wey dem fit to the same points, choose the one wey suitable pass, and explain your reasoning.
l-m-h3-b0c37-29.material: Dem fit two lines to the points (1,2), (2,4), and (3,5). Model A: y=2x. Model B: y=1.5x+0.5. The smaller the mean of the squared differences between the predictions and the real values (MSE), the better.
l-m-h3-b0c37-29.s.s1.o.a: A: E pass exactly through two points, so e better
l-m-h3-b0c37-29.s.s1.r.a: B also pass exactly through two points. You must compare the error for the remaining point.
l-m-h3-b0c37-29.s.s1.o.b: A: Only one error of 1 dey, so e smaller
l-m-h3-b0c37-29.s.s1.r.b: The error 1 squared na 1, wey big pass B own 0.25.
l-m-h3-b0c37-29.s.s1.o.c: Dem no fit tell: only 3 points dey
l-m-h3-b0c37-29.s.s1.r.c: Even with 3 points, you fit calculate and compare the MSE.
l-m-h3-b0c37-29.s.s1.o.d: B: The mean of the squared errors small, about 0.08
l-m-h3-b0c37-29.s.s1.explain: A get errors (0,0,−1), so MSE=1/3, and B get (0,0.5,0), so MSE=0.25/3≈0.08. B smaller.
l-m-h3-b0c37-29.s.s2.model.0: A na the one error 1 squared and divided by 3, about 0.33, and B na 0.5²=0.25 divided by 3, about 0.08, so B smaller.
l-m-h3-b0c37-29.s.s2.model.1: The two models hit two points exactly, so when you compare the errors for the remaining point, 1 and 0.5, B suitable pass.

l-m-h3-b0c38-07.title: Which user get similar taste pattern?
l-m-h3-b0c38-07.goal: Compare two methods or claims for choosing users wey get similar taste pattern, pick the one wey fit pass, and explain your reasoning.
l-m-h3-b0c38-07.material: Rating vectors for three movies: P=(1,2,3), Q=(2,4,6), R=(3,2,1). Q just dey give more generous scores than P, but the order of wetin dem like na the same. We wan compare the pattern, no be the size of the scores.
l-m-h3-b0c38-07.s.s1.prompt: Who get taste pattern wey most similar to P, and wetin be the reason?
l-m-h3-b0c38-07.s.s1.o.a: Q, the two vectors get the same direction
l-m-h3-b0c38-07.s.s1.o.b: R, the sum of the ratings na the same as P
l-m-h3-b0c38-07.s.s1.r.b: Even if the sums equal, the order of the movies wey dem like na opposite.
l-m-h3-b0c38-07.s.s1.o.c: R, the distance to P near pass
l-m-h3-b0c38-07.s.s1.r.c: The size of the scores dey shake distance. E fit miss the pattern.
l-m-h3-b0c38-07.s.s1.o.d: Q, the sum of the ratings big pass P
l-m-h3-b0c38-07.s.s1.r.d: Bigger sum no be reason to say dem similar.
l-m-h3-b0c38-07.s.s1.explain: Q=2P, so the direction na the same and the cosine similarity na 1. Even though R near for distance, the order of preference na opposite.
l-m-h3-b0c38-07.s.s2.model.0: Q na 2 times P, so the direction na the same and the cosine similarity na 1, wey mean say we fit see the preference patterns as the same.
l-m-h3-b0c38-07.s.s2.model.1: How generous people dey give scores dey affect distance, so when you dey compare patterns, cosine, wey dey look direction, fit pass.

l-m-h3-b0c38-16.title: Wetin we suppose use as di representative value of response times?
l-m-h3-b0c38-16.goal: Compare two methods or claims to choose one value wey represent di response time, pick di one wey suit pass, then explain your reasoning.
l-m-h3-b0c38-16.material: 6 server response times (ms): 12, 13, 12, 14, 13, 400. Di mean na about 77.3 and di median na 13. Decide which value to use for di report as di 'typical response time'.
l-m-h3-b0c38-16.s.s1.prompt: Which value represent di typical response time well, and wetin be di reason?
l-m-h3-b0c38-16.s.s1.o.a: Mean 77.3, e reflect all di values
l-m-h3-b0c38-16.s.s1.r.a: Di single 400 pull di mean up well well, far from most of di values.
l-m-h3-b0c38-16.s.s1.o.b: Median 13, extreme values no dey shake am too much
l-m-h3-b0c38-16.s.s1.o.c: 400, di slowest value na wetin matter
l-m-h3-b0c38-16.s.s1.r.c: Di maximum no be 'typical' but di worst case.
l-m-h3-b0c38-16.s.s1.o.d: Mean 77.3, e stable because 6 values dey
l-m-h3-b0c38-16.s.s1.r.d: Di fewer di values, di bigger di effect of extreme value.
l-m-h3-b0c38-16.s.s1.explain: Di single 400 raise di mean plenty, so e move far from most of di values (12 to 14). Di median 13 represent di typical value better.
l-m-h3-b0c38-16.s.s2.model.0: Most values na 12 to 14, but di single 400 make di mean 77.3, so di median 13, wey no too sensitive to extreme values, suit.
l-m-h3-b0c38-16.s.s2.model.1: Outliers dey drag di mean and e dey spoil di typical value. So I judge say di median, di middle of di order, suit pass.

l-m-h3-b0c38-24.title: If big mistake dey dangerous, which model?
l-m-h3-b0c38-24.goal: Compare two methods or claims for di standard to choose model when dem must avoid big errors, pick di one wey suit pass, then explain your reasoning.
l-m-h3-b0c38-24.material: 5 error sizes for two models. Model A: 3,3,3,3,3 (mean absolute error 3, MSE 9). Model B: 1,1,1,1,10 (mean absolute error 2.8, MSE 20.8). Na service wey one big error dey dangerous.
l-m-h3-b0c38-24.s.s1.prompt: Which model you go choose, and wetin be di reason?
l-m-h3-b0c38-24.s.s1.o.a: A, di MSE smaller, so big errors no too be problem
l-m-h3-b0c38-24.s.s1.o.b: B, error of 1 na di one wey dey happen pass
l-m-h3-b0c38-24.s.s1.r.b: Even if small errors plenty, one big error dey dangerous.
l-m-h3-b0c38-24.s.s1.o.c: Dem similar, di sums of di errors na di same
l-m-h3-b0c38-24.s.s1.r.c: Di sums of di errors no be di same: 15 and 14.
l-m-h3-b0c38-24.s.s1.o.d: B, di mean absolute error smaller
l-m-h3-b0c38-24.s.s1.r.d: Di mean small, but e miss di single error of 10.
l-m-h3-b0c38-24.s.s1.explain: MSE dey count big errors more. A get 9 and B get 20.8, so A suit to avoid big mistakes.
l-m-h3-b0c38-24.s.s2.model.0: B MSE big at 20.8 because of di single error of 10, so if big mistakes dey dangerous, A, wey get MSE of 9, suit.
l-m-h3-b0c38-24.s.s2.model.1: MSE dey square big errors so dem count plenty, so for situation wey you want avoid big mistakes, to choose A correct.

l-m-h3-b0c38-32.material: Model X: training accuracy 98%, validation accuracy 80%. Model Y: training 90%, validation 88%. Dem no use the validation data for training. Choose the model wey go do better for new data.

l-m-h3-b0c38-32.s.s2.model.0: Dem no use the validation data for training, so e near performance for new data, and Y, wey get the higher score, fit.

l-m-h3-b0c39-27.goal: Compare two methods or claims about the two records, 3.2 kg and 3.20 kg, choose the one wey suitable pass, and explain your reasoning.
l-m-h3-b0c39-27.material: A write the weight as 3.2 kg and B write 3.20 kg. A scale get smallest mark of 0.1 kg, and B scale get 0.01 kg. The numerical value na the same.
l-m-h3-b0c39-27.s.s1.prompt: Which one correctly state the difference between the two records?
l-m-h3-b0c39-27.s.s1.r.a: If you know the marks, you fit compare with the error limit.
l-m-h3-b0c39-27.s.s1.o.b: A more precise (because e get fewer digits)

l-m-h3-b0c39-27.s.s1.r.c: The marks different, so the range wey you fit trust different.
l-m-h3-b0c39-27.s.s1.explain: The error limit na half of the smallest mark. A na ±0.05 kg and B na ±0.005 kg, so B more precise.
l-m-h3-b0c39-27.s.s2.model.0: B error limit na ±0.005 kg and A own na ±0.05 kg, so even though the values the same, B more precise.
l-m-h3-b0c39-27.s.s2.model.1: 3.20 mean say dem trust the last digit, so e be more precise record than 3.2. The marks fine pass by 10 times.

l-m-h3-b0c39-28.title: Which of the two fertilizer solutions strong pass?
l-m-h3-b0c39-28.goal: Compare two methods or claims about the strength of fertilizer solutions A and B, choose the one wey suitable pass, and explain your reasoning.
l-m-h3-b0c39-28.material: Fertilizer solution A mix 1 container of fertilizer with 3 containers of water, and B mix 2 containers of fertilizer with 5 containers of water. You wan compare which one strong pass with the same standard.
l-m-h3-b0c39-28.s.s1.prompt: Which one strong pass, and why?
l-m-h3-b0c39-28.s.s1.r.a: The total amounts wey dem mix different, so you no fit compare by the amount of water alone.
l-m-h3-b0c39-28.s.s1.o.b: B: the fertilizer ratio 2/7 big pass A own 1/4
l-m-h3-b0c39-28.s.s1.o.c: Dem the same: because the two get more water than fertilizer
l-m-h3-b0c39-28.s.s1.r.c: A na 25% of the whole and B na about 28.6%, so dem different.
l-m-h3-b0c39-28.s.s1.o.d: A: because the number of containers of fertilizer small pass
l-m-h3-b0c39-28.s.s1.r.d: You no fit know the strength from the number of containers alone. Look the ratio to the whole.
l-m-h3-b0c39-28.s.s1.explain: The fertilizer ratio to the whole na 1/4=25% for A and 2/7, about 28.6%, for B. B strong pass.
l-m-h3-b0c39-28.s.s2.model.0: A get 1 container of fertilizer out of 4 containers total, wey be 25%, and B get 2 out of 7 containers total, wey be about 28.6%, so B strong pass.
l-m-h3-b0c39-28.s.s2.model.1: The total amounts different, so you must compare by the ratio to the whole, no be the amount of water. 2/7 big pass 1/4.

l-m-h3-b0c39-29.title: You fit just average the delivery rates of the two routes?
l-m-h3-b0c39-29.goal: Compare two methods or claims about the two ways to combine the on-time delivery rates of two routes, choose the one wey suitable pass, and explain your reasoning.
l-m-h3-b0c39-29.material: Delivery route A deliver 98% of 1,000 orders on time, and route B deliver 90% of 200 orders on time. Method 1 na (98+90)÷2=94%, and Method 2 find am by combining the numbers of orders.
l-m-h3-b0c39-29.s.s1.prompt: Which one na the method wey suitable pass for the combined delivery rate?
l-m-h3-b0c39-29.s.s1.o.a: Method 1: because the average of the two ratios dey enough
l-m-h3-b0c39-29.s.s1.r.a: The numbers of orders differ by 5 times, but dem count dem equal, so e go wrong.
l-m-h3-b0c39-29.s.s1.o.b: Method 2: add up the on-time orders and divide by the total
l-m-h3-b0c39-29.s.s1.o.c: Method 1: because the calculation simple pass
l-m-h3-b0c39-29.s.s1.r.c: Even if e simple, if you ignore the difference in the numbers of orders, the value go wrong.
l-m-h3-b0c39-29.s.s1.o.d: The two the same: because na average
l-m-h3-b0c39-29.s.s1.r.d: Method 1 give 94% and Method 2 give about 96.7%, so dem different.
l-m-h3-b0c39-29.s.s1.explain: The on-time orders na 980 and 180, for sum of 1,160. If you divide by the total of 1,200 e give about 96.7%, wey be the combined delivery rate.
l-m-h3-b0c39-29.s.s2.model.0: Two ratios wey get different numbers of orders carry different weights depending on the number of orders, so you no suppose just average dem. Method 2, wey dem find by 1,160÷1,200, correct.
l-m-h3-b0c39-29.s.s2.model.1: Because A get far more cases, the combined delivery rate suppose be about 96.7%, wey close to 98% pass 94%.

l-m-h3-b0c39-30.title: To know accurate methods from precise methods
l-m-h3-b0c39-30.goal: Compare two methods or claims for measuring length wey im true value na 2.00 m, choose the one wey suitable pass, and explain your reasons.
l-m-h3-b0c39-30.material: Dem measure rod wey im true length na 2.00 m three times with each method. Method A: 2.05, 2.05, 2.06 m. Method B: 1.97, 2.03, 2.00 m.
l-m-h3-b0c39-30.s.s1.prompt: Which method get average wey close to the true value pass (more accurate)?
l-m-h3-b0c39-30.s.s1.o.a: A: because the three values close together
l-m-h3-b0c39-30.s.s1.r.a: To dey close together na precision; whether e close to the true value, you must check am separate.
l-m-h3-b0c39-30.s.s1.o.b: Same: the two near the true value
l-m-h3-b0c39-30.s.s1.r.b: The average of A na about 2.053 m, wey off from the true value by more than 0.05.
l-m-h3-b0c39-30.s.s1.o.c: Dem no fit tell: because dem measure only three times
l-m-h3-b0c39-30.s.s1.r.c: You fit compare the difference from the true value with the averages wey dem give.
l-m-h3-b0c39-30.s.s1.o.d: B: im average na 2.00 m, the same as the true value
l-m-h3-b0c39-30.s.s1.explain: The average of A na about 2.053 m and the average of B na 2.00 m. The values of A close together, but dem lean to one side.
l-m-h3-b0c39-30.s.s2.model.0: The average of B na (1.97+2.03+2.00)÷3=2.00 m and that of A na about 2.053 m, so B close to the true value pass.
l-m-h3-b0c39-30.s.s2.model.1: Even though the values of A close to each other, dem all lean high, so A no accurate. B, wey im average equal the true value, accurate.

l-m-h3-b0c39-31.title: 3 people for 4 days or 4 people for 3 days: which one cheap pass?
l-m-h3-b0c39-31.goal: Compare the total costs of two staffing plans for the same job, choose the one wey suitable pass, and explain your reasons.
l-m-h3-b0c39-31.material: 3 people fit do the same job in 4 days or 4 people fit do am in 3 days. 1 person daily wage na 100,000 won (10×10,000), and the equipment rental fee na 30,000 won (3×10,000) per day.
l-m-h3-b0c39-31.s.s1.prompt: Which method cost less in total, and why?
l-m-h3-b0c39-31.s.s1.o.a: 3 people, 4 days: because fewer people dey
l-m-h3-b0c39-31.s.s1.r.a: The person-days wey dem work the same, 12 for both, so the labor cost the same.
l-m-h3-b0c39-31.s.s1.o.b: Same: because the labor cost the same
l-m-h3-b0c39-31.s.s1.r.b: Dem rent the equipment for different numbers of days, 4 and 3.
l-m-h3-b0c39-31.s.s1.o.c: 4 people, 3 days: same labor cost and fewer rental days
l-m-h3-b0c39-31.s.s1.o.d: 3 people, 4 days: because to use the equipment longer na gain
l-m-h3-b0c39-31.s.s1.r.d: The rental fee dey grow with the number of days wey dem use, so 4 days cost more.
l-m-h3-b0c39-31.s.s1.explain: The labor cost the same: 12 person-days × 100,000 won (10×10,000) = 1,200,000 won (120×10,000). Equipment na 90,000 won (9×10,000) for 3 days and 120,000 won (12×10,000) for 4 days, so 4 people for 3 days cheap by 30,000 won (3×10,000).
l-m-h3-b0c39-31.s.s2.model.0: The two plans na 12 person-days, so the labor cost the same, 1,200,000 won (120×10,000), but the equipment rental na 90,000 won (9×10,000) for 3 days and 120,000 won (12×10,000) for 4 days, so 4 people for 3 days cheap pass.
l-m-h3-b0c39-31.s.s2.model.1: Since the labor cost the same, the difference come from the number of equipment rental days. 3 days cost 30,000 won (3×10,000) less than 4 days.

l-m-h3-b0c40-26.title: Length wey dem measure by walking and length wey dem measure by laser
l-m-h3-b0c40-26.goal: Compare di two methods or claims for to measure one side of workshop, choose di one wey suit pass, then explain di reasons.
l-m-h3-b0c40-26.material: Measure one side of workshop in two ways. A use stride (0.7 m per step, error ±0.1 m) for 12 steps. B use laser distance meter (error ±2 mm) and get 8.40 m.
l-m-h3-b0c40-26.s.s1.prompt: Which method suit pass for di length wey dem go use for quote?
l-m-h3-b0c40-26.s.s1.o.a: A: because you fit measure while you dey waka
l-m-h3-b0c40-26.s.s1.r.a: E easy, but di error limit big reach ±1.2 m.
l-m-h3-b0c40-26.s.s1.o.b: Dem na di same, because both na 8.4 m
l-m-h3-b0c40-26.s.s1.r.b: Even if di values na di same, di range wey you fit trust different.
l-m-h3-b0c40-26.s.s1.o.c: A: because di error go disappear if you waka many times
l-m-h3-b0c40-26.s.s1.r.c: Di bias for one step dey add up with di number of steps.
l-m-h3-b0c40-26.s.s1.o.d: B: di error limit small well well, ±2 mm
l-m-h3-b0c40-26.s.s1.explain: For A, di error dey build up over 12 steps to at most ±1.2 m, and for B e na ±2 mm. For quote, B, wey get smaller error, suit pass.
l-m-h3-b0c40-26.s.s2.model.0: For A, error of 0.1 m per step dey build up 12 times to as much as ±1.2 m, so B, wey be ±2 mm, dey reliable far pass.
l-m-h3-b0c40-26.s.s2.model.1: Even though di two values na di same, di error limits different by about 600 times, so B suit pass for di length wey dem go use for quote.

l-m-h3-b0c40-27.title: If dem divide profit by di ratio of hours, how much each person go get?
l-m-h3-b0c40-27.goal: Compare di two methods or claims for to share profit between two workers wey work different hours, choose di one wey suit pass, then explain di reasons.
l-m-h3-b0c40-27.material: Two workers work on di same job for 12 hours and 8 hours, and dem share profit of 100,000 won. Method 1 split am equally, and Method 2 split am by di ratio of hours wey dem work.
l-m-h3-b0c40-27.s.s1.prompt: Which method reflect di amount of work, and how much each person get?
l-m-h3-b0c40-27.s.s1.o.a: Method 1: 50,000 won each, because e dey di same for everybody
l-m-h3-b0c40-27.s.s1.r.a: Since di hours wey dem work different, to split equally make di share per hour different.
l-m-h3-b0c40-27.s.s1.r.b: Dis values no reflect di time ratio 12:8=3:2.
l-m-h3-b0c40-27.s.s1.r.d: Dem split am backwards, so di person wey get fewer hours go get more.
l-m-h3-b0c40-27.s.s1.explain: 12:8 na 3:2, so to split 100,000 won for di ratio 3:2 give 60,000 won and 40,000 won. Both get 5,000 won per hour.
l-m-h3-b0c40-27.s.s2.model.0: 12:8 na 3:2, and to split 100,000 won for di ratio 3:2 give 60,000 won and 40,000 won, so both people get 5,000 won per hour.
l-m-h3-b0c40-27.s.s2.model.1: To split equally make di share per hour different, at about 4,167 won and 6,250 won, so Method 2, wey split by di ratio of hours, suit pass.

l-m-h3-b0c40-28.title: Which explanation read di amount of increase too?
l-m-h3-b0c40-28.goal: Compare di two methods or claims for to read table of cumulative shipments by weekday, choose di one wey suit pass, then explain di reasons.
l-m-h3-b0c40-28.material: Cumulative shipments by weekday: Mon 3, Tue 7, Wed 10, Thu 12, Fri 13 items. Explanation A na "shipments dey grow faster and faster," and Explanation B na "dem dey keep growing, but di amount of increase dey get smaller."
l-m-h3-b0c40-28.s.s1.prompt: Which explanation fit di table better, and why?
l-m-h3-b0c40-28.s.s1.o.a: A: because di values dey keep getting bigger
l-m-h3-b0c40-28.s.s1.r.a: Values wey dey get bigger and di amount of increase wey dey get bigger na different things.
l-m-h3-b0c40-28.s.s1.o.b: B: di amount of increase dey shrink as 4, 3, 2, 1
l-m-h3-b0c40-28.s.s1.o.c: Both correct: because e dey keep increasing
l-m-h3-b0c40-28.s.s1.r.c: A talk say di amount of increase dey get bigger, and dat one no match di table.
l-m-h3-b0c40-28.s.s1.o.d: A: because Friday get di biggest value
l-m-h3-b0c40-28.s.s1.r.d: If you look only di last value, e no go tell you how fast e dey change.
l-m-h3-b0c40-28.s.s1.explain: Di increase per day dey shrink as 4, 3, 2, 1 items. E dey keep growing, but di amount of increase dey get smaller.
l-m-h3-b0c40-28.s.s2.model.0: 7−3=4, 10−7=3, 12−10=2, 13−12=1, so di increases dey shrink, and dat one make Explanation B correct.
l-m-h3-b0c40-28.s.s2.model.1: Even though di values dey keep getting bigger, di amount of increase dey get smaller, so e no dey grow faster and faster. Na why B suit.

l-m-h3-b0c40-29.title: Between diameters of 20 mm and 150 mm, which one more accurate?
l-m-h3-b0c40-29.goal: Compare di two methods or claims about di accuracy of to measure di diameters of two parts, choose di one wey suit pass, then explain di reasons.
l-m-h3-b0c40-29.material: Part A, wey get diameter of 20 mm, dem measure am with error of ±0.2 mm, and Part B, wey get diameter of 150 mm, dem measure am with error of ±0.9 mm. We want compare which one more accurate for relative terms.
l-m-h3-b0c40-29.s.s1.prompt: Which measurement more accurate for relative terms?
l-m-h3-b0c40-29.s.s1.o.a: A: because im error of 0.2 mm smaller
l-m-h3-b0c40-29.s.s1.r.a: Dis one look only di absolute error. A na 1% and B na 0.6%.
l-m-h3-b0c40-29.s.s1.o.b: B: im relative error of 0.6% smaller than A 1%
l-m-h3-b0c40-29.s.s1.o.c: Dem na di same: both get errors of 1 mm or less
l-m-h3-b0c40-29.s.s1.r.c: Dem na di same for to be 1 mm or less, but di relative errors different, 1% and 0.6%.
l-m-h3-b0c40-29.s.s1.o.d: No fit tell: because di parts different
l-m-h3-b0c40-29.s.s1.r.d: To use relative error let you compare even when di lengths different.
l-m-h3-b0c40-29.s.s1.explain: A relative error na 0.2÷20=1%, and B own na 0.9÷150=0.6%. B more accurate for relative terms.
l-m-h3-b0c40-29.s.s2.model.0: A na 0.2÷20=1% and B na 0.9÷150=0.6%, so B, wey get smaller relative error, more accurate.
l-m-h3-b0c40-29.s.s2.model.1: Because di lengths different, you suppose compare by relative error, di error wey dem divide by di measured length. 0.6% small pass 1%, so B better.

l-m-h3-b0c40-30.title: Make am ourselves, or outsource am?
l-m-h3-b0c40-30.goal: Compare di two methods or claims for to make 100 parts, choose di one wey suit pass, then explain di reasons.
l-m-h3-b0c40-30.material: We need 100 parts. To make dem ourselves cost 30,000 won for equipment setup plus 500 won per part, and outsourcing cost 700 won per part.
l-m-h3-b0c40-30.s.s1.prompt: Which one cheap pass to get 100 parts, and why?
l-m-h3-b0c40-30.s.s1.o.a: Dem na di same: because di difference per part na only 200 won
l-m-h3-b0c40-30.s.s1.r.a: With quantity of 100, di totals different: 70,000 won and 80,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c40-30.s.s1.o.b: Make ourselves: because once you buy di equipment, you go keep dey use am
l-m-h3-b0c40-30.s.s1.r.b: Dis time you must compare am for di case of to make only 100.
l-m-h3-b0c40-30.s.s1.o.c: Outsource: 70,000 won in total, wey cheap pass 80,000 won for to make ourselves
l-m-h3-b0c40-30.s.s1.o.d: Make ourselves: because 500 won per part cheap pass
l-m-h3-b0c40-30.s.s1.r.d: Dem leave out di 30,000 won setup cost. To make dem ourselves cost 80,000 won in total.
l-m-h3-b0c40-30.s.s1.explain: To make dem ourselves na 30,000+500×100=80,000 won, and outsourcing na 700×100=70,000 won. For 100 parts, outsourcing cheap pass.
l-m-h3-b0c40-30.s.s2.model.0: To make dem ourselves cost 80,000 won with di setup cost added, and outsourcing cost 70,000 won, so for 100 parts outsourcing cheap pass.
l-m-h3-b0c40-30.s.s2.model.1: If you look only di price per part, to make dem ourselves cheap pass, but because of di 30,000 won setup cost, outsourcing cheap pass by 10,000 won for 100 parts.

l-m-h3-b0c41-26.title: Two products wey get different volumes: how to compare?
l-m-h3-b0c41-26.goal: Compare two methods or claims for comparing the prices of two products wey get different volumes, choose the one wey fit pass, and explain the reason.
l-m-h3-b0c41-26.material: Juice na 1,800 won for 500 mL and 2,550 won for 750 mL. Method 1 pick the one wey get lower total price, and Method 2 pick the one wey get lower price per 100 mL.
l-m-h3-b0c41-26.s.s1.prompt: Which comparison method fit pass, and why?
l-m-h3-b0c41-26.s.s1.o.a: The results of the two methods always na the same
l-m-h3-b0c41-26.s.s1.r.a: This time the results different. Method 1 give 500 mL and Method 2 give 750 mL.
l-m-h3-b0c41-26.s.s1.r.b: Even with larger volume, the unit price fit high.
l-m-h3-b0c41-26.s.s1.o.c: Method 1: The lower total price cheaper
l-m-h3-b0c41-26.s.s1.r.c: The volumes different, so the total price alone no tell which one cheaper.
l-m-h3-b0c41-26.s.s1.o.d: Method 2: Volumes differ, so compare unit prices
l-m-h3-b0c41-26.s.s1.explain: 500 mL na 360 won per 100 mL and 750 mL na 340 won. By unit price, 750 mL cheaper.
l-m-h3-b0c41-26.s.s2.model.0: The prices per 100 mL na 360 won and 340 won, so for products wey get different volumes, Method 2, wey compare by unit price, fit.
l-m-h3-b0c41-26.s.s2.model.1: Dem no fit compare total prices when the amounts different, so you must change dem to the price for the same amount and compare.

l-m-h3-b0c41-27.title: Which representative value fit daily wage data?
l-m-h3-b0c41-27.goal: Compare two methods or claims for choosing representative value for work team daily wage data, choose the one wey fit pass, and explain the reason.
l-m-h3-b0c41-27.material: The daily wages of 5 workers for one team (for ten-thousand won) na 12, 12, 13, 13, 60. The 60 na the value of one person wey receive special allowance. We wan state the team usual daily wage.
l-m-h3-b0c41-27.s.s1.prompt: Which value fit pass to represent the team daily wage?
l-m-h3-b0c41-27.s.s1.r.a: Na one person value, so e no represent the whole team.
l-m-h3-b0c41-27.s.s1.o.b: Median 13 ten-thousand won: extreme values no affect am well
l-m-h3-b0c41-27.s.s1.o.c: Mean 22 ten-thousand won: e reflect all values
l-m-h3-b0c41-27.s.s1.r.c: The single value 60 pull the mean up and put am far from most of the values.
l-m-h3-b0c41-27.s.s1.r.d: Na just one person value and e no tell the team usual value.
l-m-h3-b0c41-27.s.s1.explain: The mean na 22 ten-thousand won, wey big pass most values. The median of 13 ten-thousand won near the usual value pass.
l-m-h3-b0c41-27.s.s2.model.0: The single value 60 raise the mean to 22, but extreme values no shake the median 13, so e fit represent the team.
l-m-h3-b0c41-27.s.s2.model.1: 4 out of 5 people get 12-13 ten-thousand won, so 13 ten-thousand won fit pass to state the usual daily wage.

l-m-h3-b0c41-28.goal: Compare two methods or claims for the quantity of material wey dem need to cover the required length, choose the one wey fit pass, and explain the reason.
l-m-h3-b0c41-28.material: Dem need 38 m of rebar, and each piece na 6 m. Method 1 order 6 pieces, wey round 38÷6=6.33 to the nearest whole number. Method 2 order 7 pieces, wey round up.

l-m-h3-b0c41-28.s.s1.r.d: 6 pieces make 36 m, so e short by 2 m.

l-m-h3-b0c41-28.s.s2.model.1: For problems wey dem must cover the required length, shortage no must dey even if some remain, so dem dey round up.

l-m-h3-b0c42-04.goal: Compare two methods or claims, two question sentences wey ask about school lunch satisfaction, choose di one wey suit pass, then explain di reason.
l-m-h3-b0c42-04.material: Dis na two questions from school lunch satisfaction survey. A: 'How dissatisfied you be with di bad-tasting school lunch?' B: 'How satisfied you be with today school lunch? (Choose from very dissatisfied to very satisfied)'
l-m-h3-b0c42-04.s.s1.prompt: Which question suit pass to find out satisfaction?
l-m-h3-b0c42-04.s.s1.o.a: A, because e show dissatisfaction better
l-m-h3-b0c42-04.s.s1.r.a: Di question assume dissatisfaction for advance and e lead di answer to one side.
l-m-h3-b0c42-04.s.s1.o.b: A, because di sentence short pass
l-m-h3-b0c42-04.s.s1.r.b: To be neutral matter pass how long e be.
l-m-h3-b0c42-04.s.s1.o.c: Both questions na di same, because di topic na di same
l-m-h3-b0c42-04.s.s1.r.c: Even with di same topic, di sentence fit lead di answer.
l-m-h3-b0c42-04.s.s1.o.d: B, because dem word am neutrally and e get choices for both sides
l-m-h3-b0c42-04.s.s1.explain: If question lead di answer to one side, di results go lean. With neutral wording and choices for both sides, you fit find out wetin people really think.
l-m-h3-b0c42-04.s.s2.model.0: A decide for advance say di lunch taste bad, so answers go lean toward dissatisfaction, and dat one make di neutral B suit pass.
l-m-h3-b0c42-04.s.s2.model.1: B better because respondents fit choose anywhere from very dissatisfied to very satisfied, so their real thoughts go show.

l-m-h3-b0c42-10.title: Variance and standard deviation: which one to write for the notice?
l-m-h3-b0c42-10.goal: Compare two methods or claims, two values wey tell the spread of scores, choose the one wey suitable pass, and explain the reason.
l-m-h3-b0c42-10.material: One test get mean of 60 points, variance of 36 (points²), and standard deviation of 6 points. Choose the spread value wey you go write together with the mean for the notice wey dem send to students.
l-m-h3-b0c42-10.s.s1.prompt: Which value suitable pass to write next to the mean?
l-m-h3-b0c42-10.s.s1.o.a: Standard deviation 6 points, because e get the same unit as the scores
l-m-h3-b0c42-10.s.s1.o.b: The larger of the two, because the spread look bigger
l-m-h3-b0c42-10.s.s1.r.b: Dem choose am by impression, no be by purpose.
l-m-h3-b0c42-10.s.s1.o.c: Variance 36, because na the value wey dem use for the calculation
l-m-h3-b0c42-10.s.s1.r.c: The unit na points², so e hard to compare am directly with the scores.
l-m-h3-b0c42-10.s.s1.o.d: Variance 36, because the number more accurate
l-m-h3-b0c42-10.s.s1.r.d: The variance no more accurate; the unit just different.
l-m-h3-b0c42-10.s.s1.explain: The standard deviation get the same unit as the scores, so you fit read am right away, like 'mean 60 points, spread about 6 points'.
l-m-h3-b0c42-10.s.s2.model.0: The standard deviation of 6 points get the same unit as the scores, so you fit read am side by side with the mean of 60 points, wey make am suitable pass.
l-m-h3-b0c42-10.s.s2.model.1: The variance get the unit points², wey make am hard to compare directly with scores, so use the standard deviation, wey get the same unit.

l-m-h3-b0c42-17.goal: Compare two analyses of scatter plot wey get outlier, choose the one wey suitable pass, and explain your reasons.
l-m-h3-b0c42-17.material: For scatter plot of study time and scores for 15 students, one student far from the rest, with 10 hours of study and score of 95. With this student inside the correlation coefficient na 0.8, and without this student e na 0.3.
l-m-h3-b0c42-17.s.s1.prompt: Which one na the most suitable way to write this for report?
l-m-h3-b0c42-17.s.s1.o.a: Write only 0.8, because dem use all the data
l-m-h3-b0c42-17.s.s1.r.a: E hide the fact say one point dey affect the result greatly.
l-m-h3-b0c42-17.s.s1.o.b: Write only 0.3, because dem suppose throw away the point wey dey stick out
l-m-h3-b0c42-17.s.s1.r.b: To delete point without reason mean to dey pick and choose the data.
l-m-h3-b0c42-17.s.s1.r.c: To average different results dey make dem meaningless.
l-m-h3-b0c42-17.s.s1.o.d: Write the two and talk say one point get large effect
l-m-h3-b0c42-17.s.s1.explain: The fact say one point change the result greatly na important information. You suppose report the results with and without am, together with im effect.
l-m-h3-b0c42-17.s.s2.model.0: Because of one student the result change greatly, to 0.8 and 0.3, so e honest to write the two results and talk say this point get large effect.
l-m-h3-b0c42-17.s.s2.model.1: To delete or hide point without reason dey distort the result, so e more suitable to show the two and explain why.

l-m-h3-b0c42-32.title: Approval rating 20→25%: wetin we suppose write?
l-m-h3-b0c42-32.goal: Compare two newspaper headlines about change for approval rating, choose the one wey fit pass, and explain your reasons.
l-m-h3-b0c42-32.material: The approval rating go from 20% to 25%. Headline A: "Approval rating up 5%" Headline B: "Approval rating up 5%p (25% increase)"
l-m-h3-b0c42-32.s.s1.o.a: A, e go up by 5, so no wahala
l-m-h3-b0c42-32.s.s1.r.a: "5%" fit be read as 5% of 20, wey be increase of 1.
l-m-h3-b0c42-32.s.s1.o.b: B, e separate %p from the rate of increase
l-m-h3-b0c42-32.s.s1.r.c: Dem be expressions wey dey measure different things, so to use dem together no wrong.
l-m-h3-b0c42-32.s.s1.o.d: Dem two na the same thing
l-m-h3-b0c42-32.s.s1.r.d: 5%p increase and 5% increase mean different things.
l-m-h3-b0c42-32.s.s1.explain: From 20% to 25% na increase of 5%p, and as ratio e be 5÷20=25% increase. "5%" fit be read as 5% of 20 (=1).
l-m-h3-b0c42-32.s.s2.model.0: Percentage point na the difference between rates, and 25% increase na the rate of change compared to 20, so B, wey separate the two, correct pass.
l-m-h3-b0c42-32.s.s2.model.1: A's 5% fit be read as 5% of 20%, wey be 1%p, so B, wey separate 5%p and 25%, dey cause less misunderstanding.

l-m-h3-b0c42-33.title: Wetin the 20 successful people get in common, na the secret be that?
l-m-h3-b0c42-33.goal: Compare two ways to interpret wetin successful cases get in common, choose the one wey fit pass, and explain your reasons.
l-m-h3-b0c42-33.material: Dem talk say all 20 successful entrepreneurs dey wake up by 5 a.m. A: "To wake up for dawn na the secret of success." B: "If we no know wetin time failed entrepreneurs dey wake up, we no fit call am the secret."
l-m-h3-b0c42-33.s.s1.prompt: Which statement fit pass if na only this data we get?
l-m-h3-b0c42-33.s.s1.o.a: A, all 20 same, so e sure
l-m-h3-b0c42-33.s.s1.r.a: E look only successful cases and e no check the ones wey fail.
l-m-h3-b0c42-33.s.s1.o.b: A, people wey dey wake up for dawn dey work hard
l-m-h3-b0c42-33.s.s1.r.b: Dem never show say to work hard na the cause of success.
l-m-h3-b0c42-33.s.s1.o.c: B, dem prove say to wake for dawn no get anything to do with success
l-m-h3-b0c42-33.s.s1.r.c: Dem no prove say e no get connection; na say we no fit know.
l-m-h3-b0c42-33.s.s1.o.d: B, no failed group dey to compare with, so we no fit conclude
l-m-h3-b0c42-33.s.s1.explain: If we collect only successful people, we no fit know whether the same habit dey common among people wey fail too. So we no fit conclude say na the secret.
l-m-h3-b0c42-33.s.s2.model.0: If failed entrepreneurs also dey wake for dawn, e no be secret, so B fit pass A, wey conclude without comparison group.
l-m-h3-b0c42-33.s.s2.model.1: If you collect only successful cases, you no fit know whether wetin dem get in common connect to success, so B, wey talk the limit of the evidence, fit pass.

l-m-h3-b0c43-06.title: Which value suppose describe how scores spread?
l-m-h3-b0c43-06.goal: Compare two values wey show how the data spread, choose the one wey fit pass, and explain your reasons.
l-m-h3-b0c43-06.material: For one math test, most of the 20 students scores na 70 to 80 points, and only one student score 20 points. The range na 60 points and the interquartile range na 8 points. Choose the value wey go describe how most students spread.
l-m-h3-b0c43-06.s.s1.prompt: Which value fit pass to describe how most students spread?
l-m-h3-b0c43-06.s.s1.o.a: Range 60 points, because e show the biggest difference
l-m-h3-b0c43-06.s.s1.r.a: That one student 20 points make the range big well well.
l-m-h3-b0c43-06.s.s1.o.b: Range 60 points, because e use all the data
l-m-h3-b0c43-06.s.s1.r.b: The range dey use only two values, the maximum and the minimum.
l-m-h3-b0c43-06.s.s1.o.c: Dem two na the same, because dem measure spread
l-m-h3-b0c43-06.s.s1.r.c: If outlier dey, the two values go differ well well.
l-m-h3-b0c43-06.s.s1.o.d: Interquartile range 8 points, because na the width of the middle half
l-m-h3-b0c43-06.s.s1.explain: The one value of 20 points shake the range well well. The interquartile range na the width of the middle half, so e represent most students well.
l-m-h3-b0c43-06.s.s2.model.0: Because of one student 20 points the range become 60 points, so the interquartile range of 8 points, wey be the width of the middle half, show how most students spread better.
l-m-h3-b0c43-06.s.s2.model.1: The range dey use only the smallest and largest values, so outliers dey shake am well well, but the interquartile range hardly shake, so e fit pass.

l-m-h3-b0c43-16.goal: Compare two methods or claims about whether to use correlation coefficient and scatter plot together, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain di reason.
l-m-h3-b0c43-16.material: Di correlation coefficients for four sets of data all be di same, about 0.8. But di scatter plots different: one get straight-line shape, one curved shape, one shape wey one outlier make, and one ordinary scatter.
l-m-h3-b0c43-16.s.s1.prompt: Which method better to use for report?
l-m-h3-b0c43-16.s.s1.o.a: Write only correlation coefficient 0.8, because e simple
l-m-h3-b0c43-16.s.s1.r.a: Even when di value na di same, di scatter plots get different shapes.
l-m-h3-b0c43-16.s.s1.o.b: Put only di scatter plots and no write any number
l-m-h3-b0c43-16.s.s1.r.b: Di number still summarize how strong di relationship be, so e even better to use both.
l-m-h3-b0c43-16.s.s1.o.c: Write say all four na di same data
l-m-h3-b0c43-16.s.s1.r.c: Di scatter plots different, so you no fit talk say na di same data.
l-m-h3-b0c43-16.s.s1.o.d: Put di correlation coefficient and scatter plot together
l-m-h3-b0c43-16.s.s1.explain: Even with di same correlation coefficient, di shapes different. Di number show how strong di relationship be, and di scatter plot show di shape and outliers, so e good to put both.
l-m-h3-b0c43-16.s.s2.model.0: Even with di same correlation coefficient, di data fit curve or get outlier, so you need check di shape with scatter plot. Na why e good to put both.
l-m-h3-b0c43-16.s.s2.model.1: One number only tell di strength of di relationship, so to show scatter plot too na wetin go show di shape and outliers well.

l-m-h3-b0c43-20.title: Two prize draws: which one better?
l-m-h3-b0c43-20.goal: Compare two methods or claims about two prize draws for amusement park, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain di reason.
l-m-h3-b0c43-20.material: A: Pay 500 won and get 3000 won with probability 0.2. B: Pay 300 won and get 2500 won with probability 0.1. Compare dem by expected amount received minus amount paid.
l-m-h3-b0c43-20.s.s1.r.a: E look only the amount paid and leave out di expected amount received.
l-m-h3-b0c43-20.s.s1.o.b: A, because e dey earn 100 won on average
l-m-h3-b0c43-20.s.s1.o.c: A, because di chance to win higher
l-m-h3-b0c43-20.s.s1.r.c: E look only di probability and no consider di prize and di amount paid together.
l-m-h3-b0c43-20.s.s1.o.d: Both na di same, because person fit win
l-m-h3-b0c43-20.s.s1.r.d: If you calculate am, dem different: 100 won and −50 won.
l-m-h3-b0c43-20.s.s1.explain: Expected value for A na 0.2×3000−500=100 won, and for B na 0.1×2500−300=−50 won.
l-m-h3-b0c43-20.s.s2.model.0: A dey earn 0.2×3000−500=100 won, and B dey lose 0.1×2500−300=−50 won, so A better.
l-m-h3-b0c43-20.s.s2.model.1: You need calculate di chance to win, di prize, and di amount paid together, so A, wey dey earn 100 won on average, na di correct choice.

l-m-h3-b0c43-27.title: If 8 out of 10 people don better, e mean say the effect na 80%?
l-m-h3-b0c43-27.goal: Compare two ways to understand new medicine effect, pick the one wey correct pass, and explain the reason.
l-m-h3-b0c43-27.material: 8 out of 10 people wey take the new medicine don better. A: “This na medicine wey get 80% effect.” B: “We no fit talk about the effect unless we know the recovery rate of comparison group wey no take the medicine.”
l-m-h3-b0c43-27.s.s1.o.a: B, because dem don prove say the medicine no get effect
l-m-h3-b0c43-27.s.s1.r.a: E no prove say no effect dey; e just say we no fit know.
l-m-h3-b0c43-27.s.s1.o.b: A, because 10 people na big enough sample
l-m-h3-b0c43-27.s.s1.r.b: 10 people na sample wey small enough to lean one side by chance.
l-m-h3-b0c43-27.s.s1.o.c: B, we no fit know the effect without comparison group
l-m-h3-b0c43-27.s.s1.o.d: A, because 8 people don better, so the effect sure
l-m-h3-b0c43-27.s.s1.r.d: E make strong claim without knowing how many people go better even without the medicine.
l-m-h3-b0c43-27.s.s1.explain: Some people dey better even if dem no take medicine. Only if we compare with the recovery rate of comparison group, na then we fit talk about the medicine effect.
l-m-h3-b0c43-27.s.s2.model.0: If about 8 people fit better even without the medicine, e no be the effect of the medicine, so B correct pass A, wey make strong claim without comparison group.
l-m-h3-b0c43-27.s.s2.model.1: 10 people fit lean one side by chance and no standard dey to compare with, so B, wey talk say we no fit know the effect, correct pass.

l-m-h3-b0c43-32.title: Which one lean one side more, big hospital or small hospital?
l-m-h3-b0c43-32.topic: Sample size and how e dey change
l-m-h3-b0c43-32.goal: Compare two methods or claims about how much the proportion dey change depending on hospital size, pick the one wey correct pass, and explain the reason.
l-m-h3-b0c43-32.material: One small hospital dey where on average 10 babies dey born every day and one big hospital where 100 dey born. Inside one year, which hospital go get more days wey 70% or more of the babies wey dem born that day be boys? A talk say the big hospital, and B talk say the small hospital.
l-m-h3-b0c43-32.s.s1.prompt: Which claim and reason correct pass?
l-m-h3-b0c43-32.s.s1.o.a: A, because more babies dey born
l-m-h3-b0c43-32.s.s1.r.a: The more babies wey dey, the more the proportion dey stable for real.
l-m-h3-b0c43-32.s.s1.o.b: Dem be the same, because the probability of boy na the same
l-m-h3-b0c43-32.s.s1.r.b: Even if the probability na the same, the proportion dey swing more when the daily sample small.
l-m-h3-b0c43-32.s.s1.o.c: B, because more boys dey born for the small hospital
l-m-h3-b0c43-32.s.s1.r.c: No evidence dey say more boys dey born.
l-m-h3-b0c43-32.s.s1.o.d: B, because the smaller the sample, the more the proportion dey swing
l-m-h3-b0c43-32.s.s1.explain: The probability say 7 or more out of 10 na boys na about 17%, but 70 or more out of 100 almost never happen. The small sample dey swing more.
l-m-h3-b0c43-32.s.s2.model.0: With 10 babies, the probability of 7 or more boys na about 17%, and with 100 babies, 70 or more almost never happen, so the small hospital get more of such days.
l-m-h3-b0c43-32.s.s2.model.1: The smaller the sample, the more the proportion dey swing and the more extreme proportions dey show, so B, wey choose the small hospital, correct.

l-m-h3-b0c44-27.title: Typical income for village: mean or median?
l-m-h3-b0c44-27.goal: Compare two ways or claims about representative values for skewed data, choose the better one, and explain your reason.
l-m-h3-b0c44-27.material: The monthly income (for millions of won) for 5 households for one village na 3, 3, 4, 4, 50. To describe the village 'typical income,' compare mean, 12.8, with median, 4.
l-m-h3-b0c44-27.s.s1.prompt: Choose the representative value wey fit better and the reason.
l-m-h3-b0c44-27.s.s1.o.a: Median 4: the extreme value 50 no affect am too much
l-m-h3-b0c44-27.s.s1.o.b: Mean 12.8: e use all the values, so e dey accurate pass every time
l-m-h3-b0c44-27.s.s1.r.b: The one 50 push the mean up plenty and carry am far from typical.
l-m-h3-b0c44-27.s.s1.o.c: Mean 12.8: e near the income of most households
l-m-h3-b0c44-27.s.s1.r.c: 12.8 big pass the income for 4 households (3 to 4) plenty.
l-m-h3-b0c44-27.s.s1.o.d: Maximum 50: the household wey get pass money represent the village
l-m-h3-b0c44-27.s.s1.r.d: One household no fit represent wetin typical for the whole village.
l-m-h3-b0c44-27.s.s1.explain: The extreme value 50 push mean reach 12.8. The median, 4, show income for most households well.
l-m-h3-b0c44-27.s.s2.model.0: Because of the one 50, mean rise reach 12.8 and move far from typical household, so median, 4, better pass.
l-m-h3-b0c44-27.s.s2.model.1: Median na the value for middle, so extreme values hardly shake am; na why e fit describe typical income.

l-m-h3-b0c44-28.title: Correlation and cause: which sentence better?
l-m-h3-b0c44-28.goal: Compare two ways or claims, two sentences about correlation and cause, choose the better one, and explain your reason.
l-m-h3-b0c44-28.material: After we analyze the data, we find say students wey spend more time on games tend to get lower grades (correlation coefficient −0.5). A: Students wey play longer tend to get lower grades. B: Games dey lower grades.
l-m-h3-b0c44-28.s.s1.prompt: Choose the sentence wey fit this observation data better, and the reason.
l-m-h3-b0c44-28.s.s1.o.a: B: If correlation na −0.5, dem don confirm the cause
l-m-h3-b0c44-28.s.s1.r.a: Correlation coefficient by itself no fit prove cause.
l-m-h3-b0c44-28.s.s1.o.b: A and B mean the same thing, so any one good
l-m-h3-b0c44-28.s.s1.r.b: Tendency and cause no be the same kind of claim.
l-m-h3-b0c44-28.s.s1.o.c: B: Game time happen first, so na the cause
l-m-h3-b0c44-28.s.s1.r.c: Time order by itself no fit rule out other causes, like sleep.
l-m-h3-b0c44-28.s.s1.o.d: A: Dem only confirm correlation, and the cause no known
l-m-h3-b0c44-28.s.s1.explain: With observation data, you fit only talk say things tend to happen together. To say one cause the other, you need control other factors.
l-m-h3-b0c44-28.s.s2.model.0: Observation data only confirm tendency, so A wey talk about tendency fit better pass B wey claim say na cause.
l-m-h3-b0c44-28.s.s2.model.1: Other things, like sleep time, fit affect both grades and game time, so A better.

l-m-h3-b0c44-29.title: Compare report sentences when p-value na 0.2
l-m-h3-b0c44-29.goal: Compare two ways or claims about how to report test result wey no significant, choose the better one, and explain your reason.
l-m-h3-b0c44-29.material: We test how new study method affect result, and p-value na 0.2, wey no significant (significance level 0.05). A: Dem prove say no effect dey. B: We no get enough evidence say effect dey.
l-m-h3-b0c44-29.s.s1.prompt: Choose the sentence wey fit better and the reason.
l-m-h3-b0c44-29.s.s1.o.a: B: p-value na 0.2, so effect dey
l-m-h3-b0c44-29.s.s1.r.a: Big p-value no be evidence say effect dey.
l-m-h3-b0c44-29.s.s1.o.b: A: 0.2 big pass 0.05, so the effect na 0
l-m-h3-b0c44-29.s.s1.r.b: If sample small, you fit miss real effect.
l-m-h3-b0c44-29.s.s1.o.c: B: Evidence no reach, but this no prove say no effect dey
l-m-h3-b0c44-29.s.s1.o.d: A: If p-value big, e don settle say no effect dey
l-m-h3-b0c44-29.s.s1.r.d: Even if p-value big, e never settle say no effect dey.
l-m-h3-b0c44-29.s.s1.explain: Not significant mean evidence say effect dey no reach. E no mean dem prove say no effect dey.
l-m-h3-b0c44-29.s.s2.model.0: Big p-value mean evidence no reach, e no mean dem prove say no effect dey, so B fit.
l-m-h3-b0c44-29.s.s2.model.1: If sample small, you fit miss effect even when e really dey, so A wey claim say no effect dey no fit.

l-m-h3-b0c44-30.title: Compare error for two surveys wey get different sample size
l-m-h3-b0c44-30.goal: Compare two ways or claims about margin of error for two surveys wey get different sample size, choose the better one, and explain your reason.
l-m-h3-b0c44-30.material: Support rate for the same policy na 50% for both polls. Poll A randomly ask 100 people and Poll B randomly ask 400 people. Compare their 95% margins of error.
l-m-h3-b0c44-30.s.s1.o.a: B margin of error na about half of A own
l-m-h3-b0c44-30.s.s1.o.b: A and B get the same margin of error
l-m-h3-b0c44-30.s.s1.r.b: Even if support rate na the same, the error different when sample size different.
l-m-h3-b0c44-30.s.s1.o.c: B margin of error na about 4 times A own
l-m-h3-b0c44-30.s.s1.r.c: The bigger the sample, the smaller the error. E no dey grow.
l-m-h3-b0c44-30.s.s1.o.d: B margin of error na about 1/4 of A own
l-m-h3-b0c44-30.s.s1.r.d: When n become 4 times bigger, error become 1/2, e no be 1/4.
l-m-h3-b0c44-30.s.s1.explain: Margin of error follow 1÷√n. A na about ±10 percentage points and B na about ±5 percentage points, so B half.
l-m-h3-b0c44-30.s.s2.model.0: Margin of error follow 1÷√n and n na 4 times bigger, so B margin of error na half of A own.
l-m-h3-b0c44-30.s.s2.model.1: A na about ±10 percentage points and B na about ±5 percentage points, so B margin of error na half of A own.

l-m-h3-b0c45-27.title: Which one closer to π, 22/7 or 3.14?
l-m-h3-b0c45-27.goal: Compare di two methods or claims, 22/7 and 3.14, as approximations for π, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain di reason.
l-m-h3-b0c45-27.material: Archimedes show say π bigger than 3 10/71 and smaller than 3 1/7. π dey about 3.14159. Compare approximations 22/7 (= 3 1/7) and 3.14.
l-m-h3-b0c45-27.s.s1.o.a: 3.14: na decimal, so e more accurate
l-m-h3-b0c45-27.s.s1.r.a: To write am as decimal no make am more accurate.
l-m-h3-b0c45-27.s.s1.o.c: Dem get exactly di same error
l-m-h3-b0c45-27.s.s1.r.c: 22/7 and 3.14 different from π by different amounts.
l-m-h3-b0c45-27.s.s1.o.d: 22/7: e smaller than π, so e farther away
l-m-h3-b0c45-27.s.s1.r.d: 22/7 bigger than π. Compare dem by di size of di error.
l-m-h3-b0c45-27.s.s1.explain: 22/7≈3.14286, and di error na about 0.0013. Di error for 3.14 na about 0.0016, so 22/7 small-small closer.
l-m-h3-b0c45-27.s.s2.model.0: Since π≈3.14159, di difference from 22/7 na about 0.0013 and from 3.14 na about 0.0016, so 22/7 closer.
l-m-h3-b0c45-27.s.s2.model.1: When you subtract am directly, di 22/7 side smaller, so e closer. You no fit say decimal more accurate just because e decimal.

l-m-h3-b0c45-28.goal: Compare di two methods or claims about preference rankings wey 100 people give for three candidates, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain di reason.
l-m-h3-b0c45-28.material: 100 people rank three candidates, A, B, and C. A>B>C: 40 people, B>C>A: 35 people, C>B>A: 25 people. With one vote, A (40 votes) dey 1st place, but if only A and B compete, B win with 60 votes.
l-m-h3-b0c45-28.s.s1.prompt: Who fit be called di winner wey get stronger support?
l-m-h3-b0c45-28.s.s1.o.a: Rankings no mean anything, so anybody na di same
l-m-h3-b0c45-28.s.s1.r.a: When you look rankings, more people prefer B.
l-m-h3-b0c45-28.s.s1.o.b: You no fit trust runoff votes
l-m-h3-b0c45-28.s.s1.r.b: You fit calculate 1-on-1 comparisons from di ranking information.
l-m-h3-b0c45-28.s.s1.o.c: B: e win 1-on-1 against either A or C
l-m-h3-b0c45-28.s.s1.o.d: A: e get di most first choices
l-m-h3-b0c45-28.s.s1.r.d: A lose 40:60 when e go 1-on-1 with B.
l-m-h3-b0c45-28.s.s1.explain: B beat A 60:40 and C 75:25. If you count only first choices, dis information disappear.
l-m-h3-b0c45-28.s.s2.model.0: B beat A 60:40 and C 75:25, so against either of di two candidates, more people prefer B.
l-m-h3-b0c45-28.s.s2.model.1: A get plenty first choices, but 60 people prefer B, so when you also look 1-on-1 comparisons, B na di winner with stronger support.

l-m-h3-b0c45-29.s.s1.prompt: Which value better to represent di income?

l-m-h3-b0c46-28.goal: Compare two methods or claims for sharing 7 seats according to vote share, choose the better one, and explain why.

l-m-h3-b0c46-28.s.s1.r.b: Rounding add up to 6, so e no work.

l-m-h3-b0c46-28.s.s1.explain: Rounding give 3+2+1=6, so one seat remain. C, wey get biggest decimal part (0.40), get am, making 3, 2, 2.
l-m-h3-b0c46-28.s.s2.model.0: With Method 1, 3+2+1=6, so total no match; with Method 2, C wey get bigger decimal part get the seat wey remain, so total become 7.

l-m-h3-b0c47-26.s.s1.explain: Di differences from π=3.14159 na about 0.0189 for Egypt and about 0.0166 for Babylon, so Babylonian value small-small closer.

l-m-h3-b0c47-26.s.s2.model.1: 3.125 smaller than π and 3.1605 bigger than π. When you compare how far each one miss am, Babylon one miss am less, so e closer.

l-m-h3-b0c47-27.goal: Compare note wey you get by stacking 5ths 12 times with note 7 octaves higher, choose di claim wey fit pass, and explain how you reason am.
l-m-h3-b0c47-27.material: Stack one note go up 12 times by frequency ratio 3:2 (a 5th). Note 7 octaves higher na 2⁷=128 times. Claim A say dem exactly di same, and Claim B say dem different. (3/2)⁴≈5.06 and (3/2)⁸≈25.6.
l-m-h3-b0c47-27.s.s1.prompt: Calculate am, then choose di claim wey fit pass.
l-m-h3-b0c47-27.s.s1.o.a: A: Value after stacking 12 times equal 128 times
l-m-h3-b0c47-27.s.s1.r.a: (3/2)¹² na about 129.7, so e no equal 128.
l-m-h3-b0c47-27.s.s1.o.b: B: Value after stacking 12 times small-small pass 128 times
l-m-h3-b0c47-27.s.s1.o.c: B: Value after stacking 12 times small-small lower than 128 times
l-m-h3-b0c47-27.s.s1.r.d: You fit compare am by calculating (3/2)⁸×(3/2)⁴.
l-m-h3-b0c47-27.s.s2.model.0: 25.6×5.06≈129.7 pass 128, so note wey dem stack 12 times slightly higher than note 7 octaves up.
l-m-h3-b0c47-27.s.s2.model.1: (3/2)¹²≈129.7, so e no equal 128 but e bigger. So claim say value stacked 12 times slightly bigger correct.

l-m-h3-b0c47-28.s.s1.prompt: Which rectangle closer to golden ratio?
l-m-h3-b0c47-28.topic: The golden ratio and comparing ratios
l-m-h3-b0c47-28.goal: Compare two ways to find which rectangle closer to golden ratio, choose di one wey fit better, and explain how you reason am.
l-m-h3-b0c47-28.material: Golden ratio na ratio wey long side ÷ short side dey about 1.618. Rectangle A na 21×13 and Rectangle B na 20×12 (cm). For both rectangles, difference between long side and short side na 8.
l-m-h3-b0c47-28.s.s1.r.b: 1.667 dey about 0.049 away from 1.618, and A dey about 0.003 away.
l-m-h3-b0c47-28.s.s1.o.c: Both get difference of 8, so dem equally close
l-m-h3-b0c47-28.s.s1.r.c: Even if di differences same, di ratios different. Dem judge golden ratio with ratio.
l-m-h3-b0c47-28.s.s1.r.d: None of di ratios exactly equal 1.618.
l-m-h3-b0c47-28.s.s1.explain: Long side ÷ short side na 1.615 for A and 1.667 for B. Even if di differences same, di ratios different.
l-m-h3-b0c47-28.s.s2.model.0: 21÷13≈1.615 dey about 0.003 from 1.618, while 20÷12≈1.667 dey about 0.049 away, so A closer.
l-m-h3-b0c47-28.s.s2.model.1: Both rectangles get side difference of 8, but golden ratio na ratio, so you must compare di ratios, and A ratio closer.

l-m-h3-b0c47-29.material: Fence wey long 120m dey surround land. Design A na square with sides 30m, and Design B na circle. (Use 3.14 for pi.)

l-m-h3-b0c47-29.s.s1.r.d: Square na 900m² and circle na about 1,146m², wey bigger.

l-m-h3-b0c47-29.s.s2.model.0: Square na 30×30=900m² and circle wey radius about 19.1m na about 1,146m², so circle bigger.
l-m-h3-b0c47-29.s.s2.model.1: If perimeter same, circle get bigger area than square, so when you compare about 1,146m² and 900m², circle bigger.

l-m-h3-b0c47-30.title: Which one easier to divide equally, 60 or 100?
l-m-h3-b0c47-30.goal: Compare two ways of choosing unit, 60 or 100, to see which one easier to divide equally, choose di one wey fit better, and explain how you reason am.
l-m-h3-b0c47-30.material: Babylonians use 60 as one unit, and nowadays we often use 100 as one unit. Compare how easy to divide each unit equally by counting its divisors.
l-m-h3-b0c47-30.s.s1.prompt: Which one get more divisors, so e easier to divide?
l-m-h3-b0c47-30.s.s1.o.a: 100: e bigger number, so e get more divisors
l-m-h3-b0c47-30.s.s1.r.a: 100 get 9 divisors and 60 get 12. Bigger number no always get more divisors.
l-m-h3-b0c47-30.s.s1.o.b: 60: e get 12 divisors, more than 100 wey get 9
l-m-h3-b0c47-30.s.s1.o.c: Both get di same number of divisors
l-m-h3-b0c47-30.s.s1.r.c: 60 get 12 and 100 get 9, so dem different.
l-m-h3-b0c47-30.s.s1.r.d: You fit compare dem by counting all di divisors.
l-m-h3-b0c47-30.s.s1.explain: 60 get 12 divisors and 100 get 9. You fit also divide 60 exactly into 3, 4, or 6 equal parts.
l-m-h3-b0c47-30.s.s2.model.0: 60 get 12 divisors and 100 get 9, so 60 easier to divide equally.
l-m-h3-b0c47-30.s.s2.model.1: When you divide 100 by 3, remainder dey, but 60 divide evenly by 3, 4, and 6, so e easier to share.
