l-m-h3-b0c48-27.title: How we suppose compare effect of study methods?
l-m-h3-b0c48-27.goal: Compare two methods or claims to test effect of new study method, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain di reason.
l-m-h3-b0c48-27.material: We wan find out whether new study method raise scores. Method 1: Compare only one class scores before and after dem use di method. Method 2: From two similar classes, only one use di new method, then compare score changes for both classes.
l-m-h3-b0c48-27.s.s1.prompt: Which method test di effect in more reliable way?
l-m-h3-b0c48-27.s.s1.o.a: Method 1: Na di same class, so di conditions na di same
l-m-h3-b0c48-27.s.s1.r.a: Even inside di same class, other things fit change as time pass.
l-m-h3-b0c48-27.s.s1.o.b: Method 2: Compare two classes to separate other influences
l-m-h3-b0c48-27.s.s1.o.c: Both na di same: if scores go up, na di effect
l-m-h3-b0c48-27.s.s1.r.c: Test difficulty or study time fit also raise scores.
l-m-h3-b0c48-27.s.s1.o.d: Method 1: Few people dey in di survey, so e more accurate
l-m-h3-b0c48-27.s.s1.r.d: To get few participants no make am more accurate.
l-m-h3-b0c48-27.s.s1.explain: With control class, you fit filter other influences like test difficulty and study time together.
l-m-h3-b0c48-27.s.s2.model.0: Method 2 better because you fit see whether control class also change during di same period, wey tell you whether new method cause am.
l-m-h3-b0c48-27.s.s2.model.1: If you look only one class, score wey rise because test become easier go still look like effect, so Method 2 more reliable.

l-m-h3-b0c48-29.title: Linear model or quadratic model: which one to trust?
l-m-h3-b0c48-29.goal: Compare two methods to choose model wey fit 5 days of data, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain di reason.
l-m-h3-b0c48-29.material: Across 5 days, visitor numbers na 3, 5, 8, 12, 17. Model A na y=3.5x−1 (line), and Model B na y=0.5x²+0.5x+2. B fit all five values exactly, and A miss small-small each time. We wan predict day 6.
l-m-h3-b0c48-29.s.s1.prompt: Which model and reason more suitable to predict day 6?
l-m-h3-b0c48-29.s.s1.o.a: A: Equation simple, so e always more reliable
l-m-h3-b0c48-29.s.s1.r.a: Simplicity alone no explain di curve shape inside di data.
l-m-h3-b0c48-29.s.s1.o.b: Both na di same: we no fit know day 6
l-m-h3-b0c48-29.s.s1.r.b: We fit compare how well each one match di data.
l-m-h3-b0c48-29.s.s1.o.c: B: Equation complicated, so you no fit trust am
l-m-h3-b0c48-29.s.s1.r.c: You no fit reject model wey match exactly just because e complicated.
l-m-h3-b0c48-29.s.s1.o.d: B: E explain di increase pattern 2,3,4,5
l-m-h3-b0c48-29.s.s1.explain: Di increases 2,3,4,5 go up by 1 each time, wey B explain. For day 6, B give 23 and A give 20.
l-m-h3-b0c48-29.s.s2.model.0: Di increases na 2,3,4,5, and B follow dem exactly, so 23 for day 6 more reliable.
l-m-h3-b0c48-29.s.s2.model.1: Line A assume say di increase stay constant, so e miss di curve shape of di data, and B better.

l-m-h3-b0c48-30.title: Two strategies to find counterexample
l-m-h3-b0c48-30.goal: Compare two strategies to find counterexample, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain di reason.
l-m-h3-b0c48-30.material: Claim: Sum of two irrational numbers always irrational. Strategy 1: Add many different pairs of irrational numbers, like √2+√3 and √2+π. Strategy 2: Plan pairs of irrational numbers on purpose so their sum rational.
l-m-h3-b0c48-30.s.s1.prompt: Which strategy and reason more suitable to find counterexample?
l-m-h3-b0c48-30.s.s1.o.a: Strategy 1: Di more you try, di more likely you go find one
l-m-h3-b0c48-30.s.s1.r.a: If cases wey fail rare, random trying fit no find dem.
l-m-h3-b0c48-30.s.s1.o.b: Both no useful: dem don prove di claim
l-m-h3-b0c48-30.s.s1.r.c: To collect plenty examples still no make general proof.
l-m-h3-b0c48-30.s.s1.o.d: Strategy 2: Build am to target structure wey go break di claim
l-m-h3-b0c48-30.s.s1.explain: √2 and −√2 both irrational, but their sum na 0. If you design structure wey break di claim, counterexample go show quick.
l-m-h3-b0c48-30.s.s2.model.0: √2+(−√2)=0 na rational, so Strategy 2, wey design sum to be rational, produce counterexample straight away.
l-m-h3-b0c48-30.s.s2.model.1: Numbers wey dem add randomly mostly go still be irrational, so even after plenty tries counterexample fit no show. Na why Strategy 2 better.

l-m-h3-b0c48-31.goal: Compare two hypotheses to see which one more suitable to test, choose di better one, and explain di reason.
l-m-h3-b0c48-31.material: Hypothesis A: “If you exercise plenty, your body go better.” Hypothesis B: “Students wey walk at least 3 hours each week get resting heart rate wey average 3 beats lower.” Compare how easy e be to test both hypotheses.
l-m-h3-b0c48-31.s.s1.prompt: Which hypothesis and reason more suitable to test?
l-m-h3-b0c48-31.s.s1.o.a: B: E get numbers, so e must be true
l-m-h3-b0c48-31.s.s1.r.a: To get numbers no mean say e true. E only mean say person fit test am.
l-m-h3-b0c48-31.s.s1.o.b: A: Everybody agree with am, so e easy to test
l-m-h3-b0c48-31.s.s1.r.b: To agree with am and to test am different. Wetin to measure never clear.

l-m-h3-b0c49-31.goal: Compare two methods to show claim say √2 irrational, choose better one and explain why.

l-m-h3-b0c49-31.s.s1.o.a: Method 1: e enough if the 20 digits no repeat
l-m-h3-b0c49-31.s.s1.r.a: You only check limited digits, so e fit repeat after that.

l-m-h3-b0c49-31.s.s1.o.c: Method 2: assuming fraction na only guess, so no fit trust am
l-m-h3-b0c49-31.s.s1.r.c: If one assumption lead to contradiction, e prove the assumption wrong.
l-m-h3-b0c49-31.s.s1.o.d: Method 2: e check all fractions p/q at once

l-m-h3-b0c49-31.s.s2.model.1: Writing am as p/q give p²=2q², making p and q both even, contradiction, so Method 2 prove am.

l-m-h3-b0d07-06.title: Limit of √(n²+n)−n: whose solution correct?
l-m-h3-b0d07-06.goal: Compare two methods or claims about limit of √(n²+n)−n, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain how you reason am.
l-m-h3-b0d07-06.material: A: “Since √(n²+n) dey close to n, di difference na 0.” B: “Rationalizing give n/(√(n²+n)+n), so limit na 1/2.” Compare di two solutions.
l-m-h3-b0d07-06.s.s1.prompt: Which explanation of di two solutions correct?
l-m-h3-b0d07-06.s.s1.o.a: A correct. Di two terms become almost equal.
l-m-h3-b0d07-06.s.s1.r.a: When n=1000, di difference na about 0.4999, wey no be 0.
l-m-h3-b0d07-06.s.s1.o.b: B correct. Difference between two close terms no always equal 0.
l-m-h3-b0d07-06.s.s1.o.c: Both correct. Na only di methods different.
l-m-h3-b0d07-06.s.s1.r.c: Di conclusions different, 0 and 1/2, so both no fit be correct.
l-m-h3-b0d07-06.s.s1.r.d: Di difference dey close to 1/2, so limit dey.
l-m-h3-b0d07-06.s.s1.explain: When n=1000, √(n²+n)−n na about 0.4999. Rationalizing give 1/(√(1+1/n)+1)→1/2.
l-m-h3-b0d07-06.s.s2.model.0: Both terms grow big, so you no fit say di difference na 0, and rationalizing give 1/(√(1+1/n)+1)→1/2, so B correct.
l-m-h3-b0d07-06.s.s2.model.1: When n=1000, value na about 0.4999, so e no be 0 and dey close to 1/2, making B solution correct.

l-m-h3-b0d07-11.material: A: “Even if 9s continue forever, e no ever become 1, so 0.999…<1.” B: “0.9+0.09+0.009+… get first term 0.9 and common ratio 0.1, so sum na 0.9/(1−0.1)=1.”

l-m-h3-b0d07-11.s.s1.r.b: 0.999…<1 and 0.999…=1 no fit both be true at same time.
l-m-h3-b0d07-11.s.s1.o.c: B correct. Limit of partial sums na 1.
l-m-h3-b0d07-11.s.s1.o.d: Person no fit decide. Na matter of convention.
l-m-h3-b0d07-11.s.s1.r.d: Dem define series sum by limit of partial sums, so value na 1.

l-m-h3-b0d07-11.s.s2.model.0: Limit of partial sums determine infinite decimal, and 0.9/(1−0.1)=1, so 0.999…=1, making B correct.
l-m-h3-b0d07-11.s.s2.model.1: Partial sum na 1−(0.1)ⁿ, wey dey come close to 1 as n grow, so sum na 1 and B claim correct.

l-m-h3-b0d07-27.material: A say lim(x→0)(e^(3x)−1)/x na 3; B say e na 1. A: Let 3x=t, changing expression to 3·(eᵗ−1)/t. B: Since (eʰ−1)/h→1, answer simply 1.
l-m-h3-b0d07-27.s.s1.o.a: B correct. Apply limit formula directly.
l-m-h3-b0d07-27.s.s1.r.a: Denominator na x, so e no match form (eʰ−1)/h.
l-m-h3-b0d07-27.s.s1.o.d: A correct. Denominator must match 3x too.

l-m-h3-b0d07-27.s.s2.model.0: Denominator must be 3x to make (eʰ−1)/h form, so multiply and divide by 3 to get 3·1=3, meaning A correct.
l-m-h3-b0d07-27.s.s2.model.1: When x=0.001, (e^0.003−1)/0.001≈3.0045, near 3; so B's 1 wrong and A's 3 right.

l-m-h3-b0d07-33.s.s2.model.1: Since 1/x² always positive, integral no fit negative; A contradict, and B point correct.

l-m-h3-b0d08-06.s.s2.model.0: Putting 1/n−1/(n+2) over common denominator give 2/{n(n+2)}, 2 times original term, so B solution, wey multiply by 1/2, correct.
l-m-h3-b0d08-06.s.s2.model.1: A split expression na 2 times original, so sum too become 2 times bigger, 3/2, wey wrong; B sum na 3/4, matching partial-sum table.

l-m-h3-b0d09-07.material: Ellipse x²/16 + y²/4 = 1 and point (3, 1) dey. A: Use tangent formula 3x/16 + y/4 = 1 straightaway. B: First put point inside to check whether e dey on ellipse.

l-m-h3-b0d09-25.topic: Magnitude and Dot Product of Vectors
l-m-h3-b0d09-25.goal: Compare 2 ways to expand magnitude of vector difference, or 2 claims, choose di better one, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0d09-25.material: X write |a−b| as |a|−|b|, and Y write |a−b|²=|a|²−2a·b+|b|². Put a=(1,0), b=(0,1) to check which correct.
l-m-h3-b0d09-25.s.s1.o.a: Y: Dot product na 0, so formula no hold
l-m-h3-b0d09-25.s.s1.r.a: Even when dot product na 0, formula hold because |a|²+|b|²=2.
l-m-h3-b0d09-25.s.s1.r.c: Even if e simple, value must be correct. For dis example, 0≠√2.
l-m-h3-b0d09-25.s.s1.o.d: X: You find vector magnitude by subtracting
l-m-h3-b0d09-25.s.s1.r.d: You find magnitude of difference from components, no be as |a|−|b|.
l-m-h3-b0d09-25.s.s1.explain: |a−b|²=|(1,−1)|²=2, and |a|²−2a·b+|b|²=1−0+1=2. X expression give 0, so e different.
l-m-h3-b0d09-25.s.s2.model.0: Y expression hold as 2=1−0+1, but X expression give √2=1−1=0, wey wrong, so Y correct.
l-m-h3-b0d09-25.s.s2.model.1: Magnitude of difference no be |a|−|b|, so X wrong. Y method of squaring and using dot product always work.

l-m-h3-b0d09-26.material: Find k so a=(k, 2) and b=(3, −6) perpendicular. X: a·b=0, meaning 3k−12=0. Y: a real-number multiple of b, meaning k/3 = 2/(−6).

l-m-h3-b0d09-26.s.s1.o.b: Y: Di ratios must equal, so k=−1
l-m-h3-b0d09-26.s.s1.r.b: k=−1 na value wey make a parallel to b.

l-m-h3-b0d09-26.s.s1.explain: Perpendicular mean dot product na 0. From 3k+2·(−6)=0, k=4. Real-number multiple condition na for parallel and give k=−1.
l-m-h3-b0d09-26.s.s2.model.0: If perpendicular, a·b=0, so 3k−12=0 give k=4. Y use condition for parallel, so e no suitable.
l-m-h3-b0d09-26.s.s2.model.1: If k=−1, a=(−1,2) na −1/3 times b, so dem parallel. Perpendicular mean dot product 0, so X correct.

l-m-h3-b0d10-11.title: Method you fit trust for asymptote slope
l-m-h3-b0d10-11.goal: Compare two methods or claims about finding hyperbola asymptotes, choose di more suitable one, and explain how you reason am.
l-m-h3-b0d10-11.material: Two students find asymptotes for hyperbola x²/4 − y²/9 = 1. X: Change 1 on right to 0, giving x²/4 − y²/9 = 0, so y = ±3x/2. Y: Take point (10, 14.7) on curve, giving y = 1.47x.
l-m-h3-b0d10-11.s.s1.prompt: Whose method more reliable, and why?
l-m-h3-b0d10-11.s.s1.o.a: Y: E use real point, so e more accurate
l-m-h3-b0d10-11.s.s1.r.a: Point on curve no be point on asymptote, so slope different.
l-m-h3-b0d10-11.s.s1.o.b: X: Setting right side to 0 give exact slope
l-m-h3-b0d10-11.s.s1.o.c: Y: Di bigger x be, di farther slope go from 3/2
l-m-h3-b0d10-11.s.s1.r.c: Di bigger x be, di closer slope go to 3/2.
l-m-h3-b0d10-11.s.s1.o.d: X: E correct because equation short
l-m-h3-b0d10-11.s.s1.r.d: To be short no make am correct; judge am by what equation mean.
l-m-h3-b0d10-11.s.s1.explain: When x big, −1 no matter much, so y²/9≈x²/4, meaning y≈±3x/2. Changing 1 to 0 give these exact lines.
l-m-h3-b0d10-11.s.s2.model.0: When x very big, for x²/4−y²/9=1, 1 no matter much and left side dey close to 0, so X lines, wey dem get by changing 1 to 0, exact.
l-m-h3-b0d10-11.s.s2.model.1: Y point dey on curve, so e differ small-small from asymptote and give slope 1.47, but X one na limiting line, so e be 3/2.

l-m-h3-b0d10-12.title: If major axis 2 times as long, ellipse similar shape?
l-m-h3-b0d10-12.goal: Compare two methods or claims about whether two ellipses similar shapes, choose di more suitable one, and explain how you reason am.
l-m-h3-b0d10-12.material: Ellipse A: x²/16 + y²/4 = 1, Ellipse B: x²/64 + y²/8 = 1. X: B major axis 2 times A, so B na enlarged, similar version of A. Y: Major-axis to minor-axis ratio must be di same for dem to be similar.
l-m-h3-b0d10-12.s.s1.o.a: X: If major axis 2 times as long, minor axis too 2 times as long
l-m-h3-b0d10-12.s.s1.r.a: B minor axis no be 2 times A; e be √2 times.
l-m-h3-b0d10-12.s.s1.o.b: X: If both na ellipses, dem always similar shapes
l-m-h3-b0d10-12.s.s1.r.b: Ellipses fit differ in how flat dem be, so dem fit no be similar.
l-m-h3-b0d10-12.s.s1.o.c: Y: Ratios different: 2 for A and about 2.8 for B
l-m-h3-b0d10-12.s.s1.o.d: Y: You fit judge by major-axis ratio alone
l-m-h3-b0d10-12.s.s1.r.d: If you only look major axis, you miss difference in flatness.
l-m-h3-b0d10-12.s.s1.explain: For A major axis to minor axis na 4:2, and for B e be 8:2√2. Ratios na 2 and about 2.8, wey different, so dem no be similar.
l-m-h3-b0d10-12.s.s2.model.0: Major axis become 2 times as long, from 4 to 8, but minor axis go from 2 to 2√2, only √2 times, so ratios different and shapes no similar.
l-m-h3-b0d10-12.s.s2.model.1: Major-to-minor ratio na 2 for A and 8/2.83≈2.8 for B, so shapes different and Y correct.

l-m-h3-b0d10-25.title: If one angle acute, triangle acute?
l-m-h3-b0d10-25.goal: Compare 2 methods or claims about 3 angles of triangle, choose more suitable one, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0d10-25.material: For A(0, 0), B(4, 0), C(1, 1), X say AB·AC = 4 > 0, so triangle ABC acute. Y say you must check all 3 angles.
l-m-h3-b0d10-25.s.s1.o.a: Y: Another vertex fit be obtuse
l-m-h3-b0d10-25.s.s1.o.b: X: If one angle acute, others too acute
l-m-h3-b0d10-25.s.s1.r.b: Even if one triangle angle acute, another one fit be obtuse.
l-m-h3-b0d10-25.s.s1.o.c: X: If dot product positive, triangle form
l-m-h3-b0d10-25.s.s1.r.c: Dot product sign tell type of one angle, no be whether triangle dey.
l-m-h3-b0d10-25.s.s1.o.d: Y: Dot product no get anything to do with angle size, so you no fit trust am
l-m-h3-b0d10-25.s.s1.r.d: Dot product sign tell type of angle at that vertex.
l-m-h3-b0d10-25.s.s1.explain: Angle at A acute, but CA·CB=−2<0, so angle at C obtuse. You no fit judge from one vertex alone.
l-m-h3-b0d10-25.s.s2.model.0: CA·CB=(−1)(3)+(−1)(−1)=−2<0, so C obtuse and triangle no be acute. Na why you must check all angles.
l-m-h3-b0d10-25.s.s2.model.1: AB·AC positive only mean angle at A acute, so Y right to check other 2 angles too.

l-m-h3-b0d10-26.title: Di 2 orthogonal projection lengths same?
l-m-h3-b0d10-26.goal: Compare 2 methods or claims about orthogonal projection lengths of 2 vectors, choose better one and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0d10-26.material: a=(3, 4) and b=(1, 0). X: Length of orthogonal projection of b onto direction of a same as projection of a onto direction of b. Y: Di 2 lengths fit different.
l-m-h3-b0d10-26.s.s1.o.a: X: Both get dot product 3, so dem equal
l-m-h3-b0d10-26.s.s1.r.a: Dot products same, but magnitudes wey dem divide by (|a|, |b|) different.
l-m-h3-b0d10-26.s.s1.o.b: X: Orthogonal projection always symmetric, so dem equal
l-m-h3-b0d10-26.s.s1.r.b: Length of orthogonal projection depend on which vector direction you project onto.
l-m-h3-b0d10-26.s.s1.r.c: Di lengths na 0.6 and 3, and neither bigger than 3.
l-m-h3-b0d10-26.s.s1.explain: Length of projection of b onto direction of a na 3/5=0.6, and a onto direction of b na 3/1=3. Dot products same, but magnitudes dem divide by different.
l-m-h3-b0d10-26.s.s2.model.0: If you divide dot product 3 by |a|=5, e give 0.6; dividing by |b|=1 give 3, so di 2 lengths different and Y correct.
l-m-h3-b0d10-26.s.s2.model.1: Projection length na dot product divided by magnitude of vector wey give direction, so if |a|≠|b| dem different.

l-m-h3-b0d10-41.title: If line parallel to line on α, e too parallel to α?
l-m-h3-b0d10-41.goal: Compare 2 ways or claims to decide if line and plane parallel, choose better one and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0d10-41.material: Line l parallel to line m on plane α. Gap: Then l always parallel to α. Eul: l parallel to α only if l no dey on α.
l-m-h3-b0d10-41.s.s1.o.a: Eul: If e lie on α, e no parallel but contained
l-m-h3-b0d10-41.s.s1.o.b: Gap: If e parallel to m, e no fit meet α
l-m-h3-b0d10-41.s.s1.r.b: If l dey inside α, e meet α at every point.
l-m-h3-b0d10-41.s.s1.o.c: Gap: Parallel lines mean planes too parallel
l-m-h3-b0d10-41.s.s1.r.c: Even if lines parallel, whether their planes parallel na separate matter.
l-m-h3-b0d10-41.s.s1.o.d: Eul: E must perpendicular to α, no be m, to be parallel
l-m-h3-b0d10-41.s.s1.r.d: Parallel condition no get anything to do with perpendicularity.
l-m-h3-b0d10-41.s.s1.explain: Even if l parallel to m, if l lie on α, e contained, no be parallel. E parallel only when e outside.
l-m-h3-b0d10-41.s.s2.model.0: If l∥m and l dey outside α, e no meet α, so e parallel; but if e lie on α, e contained, so Eul correct.
l-m-h3-b0d10-41.s.s2.model.1: Gap statement wrong because e miss case where l same line as m, and Eul add condition, so Eul correct.

l-m-h3-b0d10-42.title: Wetin needed for 2 planes to be perpendicular?
l-m-h3-b0d10-42.goal: Compare 2 ways or claims to decide if 2 planes perpendicular, choose better one and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0d10-42.material: Decide if planes α and β perpendicular. Gap: If one line on α perpendicular to β, then α⊥β. Eul: Every line on α must perpendicular to β for α⊥β.
l-m-h3-b0d10-42.s.s1.o.a: Eul: Every line must perpendicular, so e strict
l-m-h3-b0d10-42.s.s1.r.a: Inside α usually get lines wey no perpendicular to β.
l-m-h3-b0d10-42.s.s1.o.b: Gap: If one line parallel to β dey, dem perpendicular
l-m-h3-b0d10-42.s.s1.r.b: Having parallel line different from being perpendicular.
l-m-h3-b0d10-42.s.s1.o.c: Eul: α and β no suppose get intersection line to be perpendicular
l-m-h3-b0d10-42.s.s1.o.d: Gap: One line perpendicular to β enough
l-m-h3-b0d10-42.s.s1.explain: If one line on α perpendicular to β, then α⊥β. Inside α get lines wey no perpendicular to β, like intersection line, so every-line rule wrong.
l-m-h3-b0d10-42.s.s2.model.0: Even for 2 perpendicular planes, α get lines wey no perpendicular to β, like intersection line, so Eul condition too strict and Gap correct.
l-m-h3-b0d10-42.s.s2.model.1: If α contain line wey perpendicular to β, α stand upright on β, so just one such line make α⊥β.

l-m-h3-b0c33-30.s.s2.model.0: 7,200 won na 1.2 times di cost, so e keep di 20% profit, e na at most 8,000 won, and na di lowest candidate, so e correct.
l-m-h3-b0c33-30.s.s2.model.1: 7,000 won no reach for profit and 8,500 won pass di competing price, so di lowest price wey meet both conditions na 7,200 won.

l-m-h3-b0c33-32.title: One item wey cost 100 × 10,000 won: how we suppose split di payments?
l-m-h3-b0c33-32.goal: For one choice where di monthly burden limit and di total burden clash, weigh all di conditions wey dey clash, choose di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c33-32.material: You wan buy one item wey cost 100 × 10,000 won. Conditions: ① you fit pay at most 12 × 10,000 won every month ② inside dat limit, choose di one wey get di smallest total burden.
l-m-h3-b0c33-32.s.s1.r.a: You for pay 100 × 10,000 won dis month, wey pass 12 × 10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c33-32.s.s1.o.b: 6 months, no interest: about 16.7 × 10,000 won every month
l-m-h3-b0c33-32.s.s1.r.b: E na about 16.7 × 10,000 won every month, wey pass 12 × 10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c33-32.s.s1.o.c: 10 months, no interest: 10 × 10,000 won every month
l-m-h3-b0c33-32.s.s1.o.d: 12 months, with interest: 9.2 × 10,000 won every month
l-m-h3-b0c33-32.s.s1.r.d: Di monthly burden fit, but you pay more for total: 110.4 × 10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c33-32.s.s1.explain: Di 10-month no-interest plan na 10 × 10,000 won every month and 100 × 10,000 won for total. Di 12-month plan with interest na 110.4 × 10,000 won for total.
l-m-h3-b0c33-32.s.s2.model.0: Di 10-month no-interest plan keep di limit at 10 × 10,000 won every month and e cost least for total at 100 × 10,000 won, so e correct.
l-m-h3-b0c33-32.s.s2.model.1: Di 12-month plan keep di limit but e cost more for total at 110.4 × 10,000 won, so inside di monthly limit, di plan wey get di smallest total burden na di 10-month one.

l-m-h3-b0c33-33.title: Expected return and loss limit: which investment plan?
l-m-h3-b0c33-33.goal: For investment plans wey wan get returns while dem limit losses, weigh all di conditions wey dey clash, choose di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c33-33.material: Choose one investment plan. Conditions: ① expected return of at least 6% every year ② worst-case loss inside 5%. Plan A na expected 4% and worst −1%, B na 8% and −10%, C na 7% and −3%, and D na 9% and −15%.
l-m-h3-b0c33-33.s.s1.r.a: Di expected return na 4%, wey no reach 6%.
l-m-h3-b0c33-33.s.s1.r.c: Di worst-case loss na 10%, wey pass 5%.
l-m-h3-b0c33-33.s.s1.r.d: Di worst-case loss na 15%, wey pass 5%.
l-m-h3-b0c33-33.s.s1.explain: Only C meet both: expected return of 7% (at least 6%) and worst-case loss of 3% (inside 5%).
l-m-h3-b0c33-33.s.s2.model.0: C get expected return of 7%, wey be at least 6%, and worst-case loss of 3%, wey dey inside 5%, so e meet both conditions.
l-m-h3-b0c33-33.s.s2.model.1: A get too small expected return, and B and D get big losses, so C na di only plan wey meet both conditions.

l-m-h3-b0c33-34.goal: For one choice where one income goal and work hours clash, weigh all di conditions wey dey clash, choose di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c33-34.material: You need to earn at least 40 × 10,000 won for one month (4 weeks) and work at most 12 hours every week. Among di plans wey meet dis conditions, choose di one wey get di shortest work time.
l-m-h3-b0c33-34.s.s1.o.a: Hourly wage 9,000 won, 12 hours every week
l-m-h3-b0c33-34.s.s1.r.a: E meet di conditions, but plan dey wey work with 10 hours every week.
l-m-h3-b0c33-34.s.s1.o.b: Hourly wage 12,000 won, 10 hours every week
l-m-h3-b0c33-34.s.s1.o.c: Hourly wage 10,000 won, 14 hours every week
l-m-h3-b0c33-34.s.s1.r.c: E na 14 hours every week, wey pass di 12-hour limit.
l-m-h3-b0c33-34.s.s1.o.d: Hourly wage 12,000 won, 8 hours every week
l-m-h3-b0c33-34.s.s1.r.d: Dat one na 38.4 × 10,000 won every month, wey no reach 40 × 10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c33-34.s.s1.explain: At 12,000 won every hour for 10 hours every week, you earn 48 × 10,000 won every month, wey meet di conditions, and e get di shortest time among di plans wey meet dem.
l-m-h3-b0c33-34.s.s2.model.0: At 12,000 won every hour for 10 hours every week, you earn 48 × 10,000 won every month, wey be at least 40 × 10,000 won, and di hours na at most 12, so e meet di conditions.
l-m-h3-b0c33-34.s.s2.model.1: 9,000 won every hour for 12 hours also meet di conditions, but di work time long pass, so di shortest plan, 10 hours, na di correct one.

l-m-h3-b0c34-30.goal: For setting one price where di sales condition and profit conflict, weigh all di conditions wey conflict, choose di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c34-30.material: Sales na q=200−2p (items) and di cost na 20 won for each item. Conditions: ① sales of 90 items or more ② inside dat one, di price wey get di biggest profit (p−20)×q
l-m-h3-b0c34-30.s.s1.prompt: Which price na di best one wey meet both conditions?
l-m-h3-b0c34-30.s.s1.r.a: E meet di condition, but di profit of 3,000 won small pass di 3,150 won at 55 won.
l-m-h3-b0c34-30.s.s1.r.c: Sales go be 80 items, so e fail di condition of 90.
l-m-h3-b0c34-30.s.s1.r.d: Sales go be 60 items, so e fail di condition of 90.
l-m-h3-b0c34-30.s.s1.explain: Wit sales of 90 or more, p≤55. At 50 won di profit na 3,000 won, and at 55 won e na 90 items×35 won=3,150 won, so 55 won na di best.
l-m-h3-b0c34-30.s.s2.model.0: Di prices wey meet di sales condition na 55 won or less, and di profit at 55 won na 3,150 won, more than di 3,000 won at 50 won, so di answer na 55 won.
l-m-h3-b0c34-30.s.s2.model.1: Di profit at 60 won big pass, but sales go be 80 items, wey break di condition, so choose 55 won, di biggest inside di condition.

l-m-h3-b0c34-31.title: To repay 600 × 10,000 won: monthly burden and total repayment
l-m-h3-b0c34-31.topic: Loan repayment (how to pay back loan)
l-m-h3-b0c34-31.goal: For choosing one period where di monthly repayment limit and di total repayment conflict, weigh all di conditions wey conflict, choose di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c34-31.material: You dey choose how long to take repay 600 × 10,000 won. Conditions: ① monthly repayment of 30 × 10,000 won or less ② inside dat one, di lowest total repayment. Di total repayment by period na 624 × 10,000 won for 12 months, 630 × 10,000 won for 18 months, 648 × 10,000 won for 24 months, and 684 × 10,000 won for 36 months.
l-m-h3-b0c34-31.s.s1.r.d: E meet di limit, but di total of 684 × 10,000 won pass di one for 24 months.
l-m-h3-b0c34-31.s.s1.explain: Di periods wey get monthly payment of 30 × 10,000 won or less na 24 and 36 months, and among dem, di one wey get lower total repayment na 24 months (648 × 10,000 won).
l-m-h3-b0c34-31.s.s2.model.0: Di only periods wey get monthly repayment of 30 × 10,000 won or less na 24 and 36 months, so 24 months, wey get lower total repayment between di two, na di best.
l-m-h3-b0c34-31.s.s2.model.1: 12 and 18 months pass di monthly limit, so dem comot, and from di remaining two choose 24 months, wey get lower total.

l-m-h3-b0c34-32.goal: For one allocation where di loss limit and di expected profit conflict, weigh all di conditions wey conflict, choose di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c34-32.material: You split 200 × 10,000 won between one safe asset (2% every year) and one risky asset (expected 8% every year, worst case −10%). Conditions: ① di maximum loss from di risky asset na 10 × 10,000 won or less ② inside dat one, di allocation wey get di biggest expected profit
l-m-h3-b0c34-32.s.s1.prompt: Which allocation na di best one wey meet both conditions?
l-m-h3-b0c34-32.s.s1.r.a: E meet di condition, but di expected profit of 4 × 10,000 won low pass.
l-m-h3-b0c34-32.s.s1.r.b: E meet di condition, but di expected profit of 7 × 10,000 won low pass di one for 100 × 10,000 won allocation.
l-m-h3-b0c34-32.s.s1.r.d: Di worst-case loss na 15 × 10,000 won, wey pass di limit of 10 × 10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c34-32.s.s1.explain: Di worst-case loss for risky asset of 100 × 10,000 won na 10 × 10,000 won, and di expected profit na 8+2=10 × 10,000 won, di biggest inside di limit.
l-m-h3-b0c34-32.s.s2.model.0: Wit risky asset of 100 × 10,000 won, di worst-case loss na 10 × 10,000 won, wey fit di limit, and di expected profit of 10 × 10,000 won na di biggest, so na di best.
l-m-h3-b0c34-32.s.s2.model.1: 150 × 10,000 won pass di loss limit, and 0 and 50 × 10,000 won get smaller expected profit, so 100 × 10,000 won na di biggest inside di limit.

l-m-h3-b0c34-33.goal: For one choice where di lunch budget and preparation time conflict, weigh all di conditions wey conflict, choose di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c34-33.material: Dis na lunches for di 20 weekdays of one month. To buy lunch cost 8,000 won, and packed lunch cost 2,500 won for ingredients and 30 minutes to prepare. l-m-h3-b0c34-33.s.s1.r.c: E meet di conditions, but di preparation time of 5 hours long pass di one for 8 days.
l-m-h3-b0c34-33.s.s1.r.d: Di preparation time na 7 hours, wey pass 6 hours.
l-m-h3-b0c34-33.s.s1.explain: Wit 8 days, di lunch cost na 116,000 won and di preparation na 4 hours, so e meet di conditions, and among di options wey meet dem, im preparation time na di shortest.
l-m-h3-b0c34-33.s.s2.model.0: Wit 8 days, di lunch cost na 116,000 won, wey be 12 × 10,000 won or less, and di preparation time of 4 hours na 6 hours or less and di shortest, so na di best.
l-m-h3-b0c34-33.s.s2.model.1: Wit 6 days di lunch cost too high and e pass di limit, and wit 10 days di time long pass, so di answer na 8 days, wey get di shortest time inside di conditions.

l-m-h3-b0c35-08.s.s1.r.c: E pass di condition of 30,000 won every month or less.

l-m-h3-b0c35-08.s.s2.model.1: "Or less" and "or more" include di same value, so di option wey get 30,000 won and 20GB meet all di conditions.

l-m-h3-b0c35-16.title: To raise di price to balance profit and sales
l-m-h3-b0c35-16.goal: Weigh every condition wey conflict for setting one price, choose di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c35-16.material: One product cost 1,000 won each, and im daily sales na 800−0.3P units wen di price na P won. Choose di price wey keep daily sales at 200 or more and give di biggest daily profit.
l-m-h3-b0c35-16.s.s1.prompt: Among di prices wey meet di conditions, which one give di biggest profit?
l-m-h3-b0c35-16.s.s1.r.a: Sales na 350 units and profit na 175,000 won, but option dey wey get bigger profit.
l-m-h3-b0c35-16.s.s1.r.c: Sales na 200 units and profit na 200,000 won, wey small pass di one at 1,800 won.
l-m-h3-b0c35-16.s.s1.r.d: Sales na only 140 units, wey break di 200-unit condition.
l-m-h3-b0c35-16.s.s1.explain: 2,200 won break di sales condition. Among di rest, 1,800 won, wey get profit of 208,000 won, na di biggest.
l-m-h3-b0c35-16.s.s2.model.0: 2,200 won sell only 140 units and e break di condition, so dem don rule am out. Among di rest, 1,800 won, wey get profit of 208,000 won, na di biggest.
l-m-h3-b0c35-16.s.s2.model.1: When price go up, profit for each unit go grow but sales go fall, so if you weigh di two conditions, 1,800 won na di best.

l-m-h3-b0c35-23.material: Di way to go school must cost 60,000 won a month or less, take 45 minutes or less one way, and fit work for any weather. Options: bus, subway, shared bicycle, subway+bus pass.

l-m-h3-b0c35-32.title: How to choose between premium and coverage
l-m-h3-b0c35-32.goal: Think about every condition wey dey clash when you wan buy insurance, choose the best compromise, then explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c35-32.material: Big accident fit cause loss of 300 ×10,000 won. Find insurance wey get yearly premium of 20 ×10,000 won or less and coverage of 300 ×10,000 won or more. E no suppose cheap reach the point wey coverage no go reach.
l-m-h3-b0c35-32.s.s1.r.a: The premium fit, but the coverage no reach 300 ×10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c35-32.s.s1.r.d: The premium fit, but the coverage no reach 300 ×10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c35-32.s.s1.r.c: The coverage don enough, but the premium pass 20 ×10,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c35-32.s.s1.explain: 18 ×10,000 won no pass 20 ×10,000 won, and the coverage of 300 ×10,000 won no small pass the loss of 300 ×10,000 won, so e meet the two conditions.
l-m-h3-b0c35-32.s.s2.model.0: If you choose am just because e cheap, 200 ×10,000 won coverage no go cover loss of 300 ×10,000 won, so the option of 18 ×10,000 won wey meet the two conditions na the correct one.
l-m-h3-b0c35-32.s.s2.model.1: Dem remove 25 ×10,000 won because, even though the coverage big pass, e pass the premium condition, so the option of 18 ×10,000 won with 300 ×10,000 won coverage remain.

l-m-h3-b0c36-30.title: To decide di number of columns for taste vector
l-m-h3-b0c36-30.goal: Weigh all di conditions wey dey fight each other on di number of columns wey dem use write user taste as vector, choose di compromise wey suit pass, then explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c36-30.material: For movie recommendation, dem write taste as vector with d entries. Conditions: ① to show each of 4 kinds of taste with one entry, d≥4; ② one person get only 12 ratings, so d na 6 or less; ③ di lighter di calculation, di better.
l-m-h3-b0c36-30.s.s1.prompt: Which d suit pass wey keep all three conditions?
l-m-h3-b0c36-30.s.s1.r.a: E no fit show each of di 4 kinds with one entry.
l-m-h3-b0c36-30.s.s1.r.c: E keep di conditions, but more entries dey, so di calculation heavy pass.
l-m-h3-b0c36-30.s.s1.r.d: You use all 12 ratings as entries, and dat one break di condition of 6 or less.
l-m-h3-b0c36-30.s.s1.explain: d must be at least 4 and at most 6, and di value wey get di lightest calculation among dem na 4.
l-m-h3-b0c36-30.s.s2.model.0: To show di 4 kinds we need d≥4, and because of di number of ratings d≤6, so inside dat range 4, wey get di lightest calculation, suit.
l-m-h3-b0c36-30.s.s2.model.1: d=3 get too few entries and d=12 too many for di number of ratings, so choose di light d=4, wey keep both conditions.

l-m-h3-b0c36-31.title: Between di number of survey respondents and di budget
l-m-h3-b0c36-31.goal: Weigh all di conditions wey dey fight each other on di number of people wey dem go get answers from for survey, choose di compromise wey suit pass, then explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c36-31.material: To know di approval rate inside error of ±5 percentage points (95% confidence), at least 385 people dey needed. Di cost na 2000 won for 1 response and di budget na 900,000 won (90×10,000).
l-m-h3-b0c36-31.s.s1.prompt: Among di numbers of people wey keep both conditions, which one suit pass?
l-m-h3-b0c36-31.s.s1.r.a: E fit di budget, but di error pass 5 percentage points.
l-m-h3-b0c36-31.s.s1.r.b: E small pass 385, so di error big pass 5 percentage points.
l-m-h3-b0c36-31.s.s1.r.c: E cost 1,200,000 won (120×10,000), wey pass di budget of 900,000 won (90×10,000).
l-m-h3-b0c36-31.s.s1.explain: E must be at least 385 people and at most 900,000 (90×10,000)÷2000=450 people. Among di choices, di one wey dey inside dis range na 400 people.
l-m-h3-b0c36-31.s.s2.model.0: E must be at least 385 people make di error dey inside ±5 percentage points, and di budget allow up to 450 people, so 400 people fit both conditions.
l-m-h3-b0c36-31.s.s2.model.1: 300 people break di error condition and 600 people break di budget, so 400 people, wey keep both, suit.

l-m-h3-b0c36-32.title: To choose learning rate
l-m-h3-b0c36-32.goal: Weigh all di conditions wey dey fight each other as you dey choose di learning rate for gradient descent, choose di compromise wey suit pass, then explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c36-32.material: For f(x)=x², from di starting point x=5, x dey become (1−2η) times for each step. Conditions: ① after 3 steps |x|≤1; ② di sign of x no dey change (η<0.5); ③ di learning rate suppose dey di safe, small side.
l-m-h3-b0c36-32.s.s1.prompt: Which η suit pass wey keep all di conditions?
l-m-h3-b0c36-32.s.s1.r.a: After 3 steps x≈2.56, so e no keep di condition of 1 or less.
l-m-h3-b0c36-32.s.s1.r.b: E keep di conditions, but di smaller 0.3 don do.
l-m-h3-b0c36-32.s.s1.r.d: 1−2η=−0.8, so di sign change and e break ②.
l-m-h3-b0c36-32.s.s1.explain: If (1−2η)³×5≤1, then η na at least about 0.21, and η<0.5. Among di choices, di smallest such value na 0.3.
l-m-h3-b0c36-32.s.s2.model.0: With η=0.1, x na 2.56 after 3 steps so ① no dey kept, and 0.9 change di sign, so among di choices wey keep both, di smaller one na 0.3.
l-m-h3-b0c36-32.s.s2.model.1: With 0.3, x dey shrink to 0.4 times each step, so after 3 steps e na 0.32, wey be 1 or less and keep di condition, and e small pass 0.45, so e safer.

l-m-h3-b0c36-33.title: To decide di test criterion (threshold)
l-m-h3-b0c36-33.goal: Weigh all di conditions wey dey fight each other for di criterion wey dem use decide positive result for disease test, choose di compromise wey suit pass, then explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c36-33.material: Recall R and precision P for each threshold: 0.3: R 0.96, P 0.40 / 0.5: R 0.92, P 0.55 / 0.7: R 0.85, P 0.70 / 0.9: R 0.60, P 0.90. Di conditions na R≥0.9 and P≥0.5.
l-m-h3-b0c36-33.s.s1.r.a: R don do, but P na 0.40, wey no reach 0.5.
l-m-h3-b0c36-33.s.s1.r.c: P don do, but R na 0.85, wey no reach 0.9.
l-m-h3-b0c36-33.s.s1.r.d: P high, but R na 0.60, so plenty sick people dem miss.
l-m-h3-b0c36-33.s.s1.explain: Di only one wey satisfy both R≥0.9 and P≥0.5 na 0.5 (R 0.92, P 0.55).
l-m-h3-b0c36-33.s.s2.model.0: For 0.3, P na 0.40, and for 0.7 and 0.9, R dey below 0.9, so 0.5 na di only one wey keep both conditions.
l-m-h3-b0c36-33.s.s2.model.1: If you lower di threshold for recall, e dey cut into precision, so 0.5, wey pass both standards, na di suitable compromise.

l-m-h3-b0c36-34.title: To split data into training, validation, and test sets
l-m-h3-b0c36-34.goal: Weigh all di conditions wey dey fight each other for di ratio to split 1000 pieces of data, choose di compromise wey suit pass, then explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c36-34.material: Split 1000 pieces of data into training/validation/test. Conditions: training at least 600, validation at least 100, test at least 150, and inside dat one, train on as much as possible.
l-m-h3-b0c36-34.s.s1.prompt: Among di choices wey keep di conditions, which split suit pass?
l-m-h3-b0c36-34.s.s1.r.a: Di test get only 100, so e break di condition of at least 150.
l-m-h3-b0c36-34.s.s1.r.b: Training get only 500, so e break di condition of at least 600.
l-m-h3-b0c36-34.s.s1.r.d: Validation and test too small, so e break two conditions.
l-m-h3-b0c36-34.s.s1.explain: Di only choice wey keep training ≥600, validation ≥100, and test ≥150 na 700/150/150.
l-m-h3-b0c36-34.s.s2.model.0: For 800/100/100 di test dey under 150, and for 500/250/250 di training dey under 600, so only 700/150/150 keep di conditions.
l-m-h3-b0c36-34.s.s2.model.1: E leave di validation and test shares for or above di minimum and make training big, so 700/150/150 na di suitable compromise.

l-m-h3-b0c37-30.title: How to choose image resolution
l-m-h3-b0c37-30.goal: Consider all the conditions wey dey conflict for the number of pixels per side when dem write black-and-white image as vector, choose the best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c37-30.material: Shrink black-and-white image to n×n pixels to make vector with n² entries. Conditions: ① the number of entries n² na 4000 or less, ② to recognize the letters, n na 40 or more, ③ within that, make am as sharp as possible (the larger n).
l-m-h3-b0c37-30.s.s1.prompt: Which n na the best one wey meet all the conditions?
l-m-h3-b0c37-30.s.s1.r.a: n²=784 meet ①, but e less than 40, so e break ②.
l-m-h3-b0c37-30.s.s1.r.b: E meet two conditions, but sharper n dey (③).
l-m-h3-b0c37-30.s.s1.r.d: n²=6400 pass 4000, so e break ①.
l-m-h3-b0c37-30.s.s1.explain: If 40≤n and n²≤4000, then n≤63. The largest value among the choices na n=60 (3600 entries).
l-m-h3-b0c37-30.s.s2.model.0: From n²≤4000, n na 63 or less, and n≥40, so 60, the sharpest among the choices for this range, na the suitable one.
l-m-h3-b0c37-30.s.s2.model.1: With 28 you no fit recognize the letters, and with 80 too many entries dey, 6400, so choose 60, the largest wey meet the two conditions.

l-m-h3-b0c37-31.title: How to choose confidence level and interval width
l-m-h3-b0c37-31.goal: Consider all the conflicting conditions for how to choose the confidence level of estimation interval, choose the best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c37-31.material: When the standard error of the sample mean na 2, the margins of error by confidence level na 80%: ±2.6, 90%: ±3.3, 95%: ±3.9, and 99%: ±5.2. Conditions: ① confidence level 95% or more, ② margin of error ±5 or less.
l-m-h3-b0c37-31.s.s1.prompt: Which confidence level meet the two conditions?
l-m-h3-b0c37-31.s.s1.r.a: The margin of error small, but the confidence level dey under 95%.
l-m-h3-b0c37-31.s.s1.r.b: The confidence level no reach 95%, so e break ①.
l-m-h3-b0c37-31.s.s1.r.c: The margin of error na ±5.2, wey pass ±5.
l-m-h3-b0c37-31.s.s1.explain: Because of ①, 95% and 99% remain, and because of ②, 99% (±5.2) drop out. The one wey meet the two conditions na 95%.
l-m-h3-b0c37-31.s.s2.model.0: Anything under 95% break ①, and 99% break ② with margin of error of 5.2, so only 95% meet the two conditions.
l-m-h3-b0c37-31.s.s2.model.1: If you raise the confidence level, the interval go wide, so 95%, with ±3.9, na the compromise wey be 5 or less and also 95% or more.

l-m-h3-b0c37-32.material: For f(x)=x² with learning rate of 0.2, x go become 0.6 times as big with each step. Start for x=8. Conditions: ① |x|≤0.5 when you stop, ② the calculation na 8 steps or fewer, ③ within that, as few steps as possible.
l-m-h3-b0c37-32.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be the best number of steps wey meet all the conditions?
l-m-h3-b0c37-32.s.s1.r.a: x≈1.73, wey big pass 0.5, so e break ①.
l-m-h3-b0c37-32.s.s1.r.b: x≈0.62, wey big pass 0.5, so e break ①.
l-m-h3-b0c37-32.s.s1.r.d: E meet ①, but e break ②, wey talk say 8 steps or fewer.
l-m-h3-b0c37-32.s.s1.explain: 5 steps give 0.62, wey no reach, and 6 steps give 0.37, wey be 0.5 or less. 9 steps pass the 8-steps-or-fewer condition.
l-m-h3-b0c37-32.s.s2.model.0: With 6 steps, x≈0.37 meet ①, and e na 8 steps or fewer, so e meet ② too. The smaller 5 steps give 0.62, so e no work.
l-m-h3-b0c37-32.s.s2.model.1: 3 steps and 5 steps no reach the error condition, and 9 steps pass the number of steps, so 6 steps na the one wey meet the two.

l-m-h3-b0c37-33.goal: Consider all the conflicting conditions for how to choose model complexity (the degree of polynomial), choose the best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c37-33.material: The errors (training/test) of polynomial models of degree d na d=1: 9/10, d=3: 2/3, d=4: 1.5/3.2, and d=6: 0.2/8. Conditions: ① test error 3.5 or less, ② the gap between training and test errors na 2 or less, ③ the simplest model.
l-m-h3-b0c37-33.s.s1.prompt: Which degree na the best one wey meet all three conditions?
l-m-h3-b0c37-33.s.s1.r.a: Na the simplest, but test error of 10 pass 3.5.
l-m-h3-b0c37-33.s.s1.r.c: E meet two conditions, but e more complex than d=3, so e lose for ③.
l-m-h3-b0c37-33.s.s1.r.d: The training error small, but test error of 8 break ①.
l-m-h3-b0c37-33.s.s1.explain: d=3 and 4 meet ① and ②, and among dem, the simpler d=3 na the suitable one. d=6 na model wey lean toward the training data only.
l-m-h3-b0c37-33.s.s2.model.0: d=1 and d=6 get test errors wey pass 3.5, and d=3 and 4 meet the conditions, so choose the simpler d=3.
l-m-h3-b0c37-33.s.s2.model.1: For d=4 the test error actually go up to 3.2, so the simplest d=3, wey meet the two conditions, na the suitable one.

l-m-h3-b0c37-34.title: Sampling method and budget
l-m-h3-b0c37-34.goal: Consider all the conflicting conditions for the sampling method of opinion poll, choose the best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c37-34.material: You dey survey the opinions of the residents of one city. Conditions: ① pick randomly from list to reduce bias, ② budget of 500,000 won or less (50 man won), ③ sample of 250 people or more. The number of people and the cost different for each choice.
l-m-h3-b0c37-34.s.s1.prompt: Which method meet all three conditions?
l-m-h3-b0c37-34.s.s1.o.a: 100 people picked at random from list (150,000 won; 15 man won)
l-m-h3-b0c37-34.s.s1.r.a: E random and e dey inside the budget, but e no reach 250 people.
l-m-h3-b0c37-34.s.s1.o.b: 400 people wey dem meet for street (200,000 won; 20 man won)
l-m-h3-b0c37-34.s.s1.r.b: The number of people and the budget work, but e no random, so e fit get bias.
l-m-h3-b0c37-34.s.s1.o.c: 600 people picked at random (950,000 won; 95 man won)
l-m-h3-b0c37-34.s.s1.r.c: E random and e get enough people, but e pass the budget of 500,000 won (50 man won).
l-m-h3-b0c37-34.s.s1.o.d: 300 people picked at random (400,000 won; 40 man won)
l-m-h3-b0c37-34.s.s1.explain: The only method wey random, get 250 people or more, and cost 500,000 won (50 man won) or less na 300 people at random from the list.
l-m-h3-b0c37-34.s.s2.model.0: 100 people break the number-of-people condition, 400 break the random condition, and 600 break the budget condition, so 300, wey meet all three conditions, na the suitable one.
l-m-h3-b0c37-34.s.s2.model.1: To reduce bias e must random, and the one wey fit the number of people and the budget inside that na 300 people at random from the list, so na this method.

l-m-h3-b0c38-25.title: How we suppose choose di learning rate?
l-m-h3-b0c38-25.goal: Consider all di conditions wey dey fight each other for di learning rate of gradient descent, pick di compromise wey suit pass, then explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c38-25.material: Di loss na f(w)=w², and di start na w=1. With each update, w dey become (1−2×learning rate) times as big. Conditions: inside 100 updates di loss must drop below 0.01, and di sign of w must no change.
l-m-h3-b0c38-25.s.s1.prompt: Which learning rate meet both conditions?

l-m-h3-b0c38-25.s.s1.r.c: Di multiplier na −0.8, so di sign of w dey change every time.
l-m-h3-b0c38-25.s.s1.r.d: Di multiplier na −1.2, so di sign dey change and di value dey keep growing.
l-m-h3-b0c38-25.s.s1.explain: With 0.1 di multiplier na 0.8, so di sign stay di same and di loss dey drop quick. 0.01 slow, and 0.9 and 1.1 dey change di sign.
l-m-h3-b0c38-25.s.s2.model.0: With 0.1 di multiplier na 0.8, wey positive, so di sign no change, and after 100 updates di loss small pass 0.01 well well, so e suit.
l-m-h3-b0c38-25.s.s2.model.1: 0.01 too slow, and for 0.9 and 1.1 di multiplier become negative, so only 0.1 meet both conditions.

l-m-h3-b0c38-33.title: How we suppose set the threshold for spam detection?
l-m-h3-b0c38-33.topic: How to set the classification threshold
l-m-h3-b0c38-33.goal: Think about all the conditions wey dey clash for spam-filter threshold, choose the compromise wey fit pass, then explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c38-33.material: By threshold (normal emails wey dem wrongly send to spam / spam wey dem miss): 0.3 na 20/2, 0.5 na 8/6, 0.7 na 4/15, 0.9 na 1/40. Conditions: normal emails wey dem wrongly send must be 5 or fewer, and among those, spam wey dem miss must be the fewest.
l-m-h3-b0c38-33.s.s1.prompt: Which threshold fit the conditions pass?
l-m-h3-b0c38-33.s.s1.r.a: Dem wrongly send 20 normal emails, wey pass 5.
l-m-h3-b0c38-33.s.s1.r.b: Dem wrongly send 8 normal emails, wey pass 5.
l-m-h3-b0c38-33.s.s1.r.d: E meet the condition, but dem miss 40 spam emails, wey pass wetin 0.7 get.
l-m-h3-b0c38-33.s.s1.explain: The thresholds wey get 5 or fewer na 0.7 (4) and 0.9 (1), and 0.7 miss fewer spam emails, 15.
l-m-h3-b0c38-33.s.s2.model.0: Na only 0.7 and 0.9 get 5 or fewer normal emails wey dem wrongly send, and 0.7 miss fewer spam emails, 15, so the answer na 0.7.
l-m-h3-b0c38-33.s.s2.model.1: Dem remove 0.3 and 0.5 because dem wrongly send more than 5 normal emails, and for the rest, dem choose 0.7 because e miss fewer.

l-m-h3-b0c39-33.material: You wan hang 4 shelves, each 55 cm wide, for wall wey long 240 cm. The gap between shelves must be at least 3 cm, and the margin for each end must be at least 4 cm. All the gaps the same.

l-m-h3-b0c41-31.title: To choose packing box: cost and breakage
l-m-h3-b0c41-31.goal: Think about all the conditions wey dey fight each other for the compromise between packing cost and breakage risk, choose the compromise wey fit pass and explain the reason.
l-m-h3-b0c41-31.material: Box A cost 400 won each with 5% breakage rate, Box B cost 520 won with 1%, and Box C cost 900 won with 0.5%. The item worth 3,000 won, and if e break, the item value lost. The breakage rate must be 2% or less, and the lower the total cost per item (packing cost + loss), the better.
l-m-h3-b0c41-31.s.s1.prompt: Which box keep both conditions and fit pass?
l-m-h3-b0c41-31.s.s1.r.a: The total cost per item na 550 won, but e break the condition of 2% breakage rate.
l-m-h3-b0c41-31.s.s1.o.b: Use A and B mix half and half
l-m-h3-b0c41-31.s.s1.r.b: The average breakage rate na 3%, so e break the condition of 2% or less.
l-m-h3-b0c41-31.s.s1.r.d: E meet the conditions, but the total cost per item of 915 won na the highest.
l-m-h3-b0c41-31.s.s1.explain: The total costs na 550 won for A (dem remove am because of the 5% rate), 520+30=550 won for B, and 900+15=915 won for C. Inside the conditions, B na the lowest.
l-m-h3-b0c41-31.s.s2.model.0: Dem remove A from the conditions by its 5% breakage rate, B na 550 won, and C na 915 won, so B, wey meet the conditions, cheapest.
l-m-h3-b0c41-31.s.s2.model.1: Even if you add the breakage loss of 30 won, B na 550 won, so e meet the condition of 2% or less and get the lowest cost.

l-m-h3-b0c41-32.title: How many printers we suppose rent?
l-m-h3-b0c41-32.goal: Think about all the conditions wey dey fight each other for the number of machines wey must keep both the deadline and the budget, choose the compromise wey fit pass and explain the reason.
l-m-h3-b0c41-32.material: Dem must print 150 posters inside 3 hours, and the budget na 45,000 won. 1 printer dey print 30 sheets per hour, and the rental fee na 8,000 won per 1 printer for 1 hour, wey dem charge by rounding up to whole hours.
l-m-h3-b0c41-32.s.s1.prompt: Which option keep both conditions and fit pass?
l-m-h3-b0c41-32.s.s1.r.a: E take 5 hours, wey pass the 3-hour deadline.
l-m-h3-b0c41-32.s.s1.r.b: 2.5 hours round up to 3 hours, wey make 48,000 won, and e pass the budget.
l-m-h3-b0c41-32.s.s1.r.c: 1.25 hours round up to 2 hours, wey cost 64,000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c41-32.s.s1.explain: 5 printers finish inside 1 hour and cost 40,000 won. 2 printers cost 48,000 won and 4 printers cost 64,000 won, and dem pass the budget.
l-m-h3-b0c41-32.s.s2.model.0: 5 printers finish 150 sheets inside 1 hour and cost 40,000 won, so dem keep both the deadline and the budget.
l-m-h3-b0c41-32.s.s2.model.1: 2 printers and 4 printers pass di budget of 45,000 won because of di rental time wey dem round up, and 1 printer miss di deadline, so 5 printers suit.

l-m-h3-b0c41-33.material: One truck dey move 100 boxes wey weigh 18 kg each. For safety, each load must be 450 kg or less, and dem must move everything inside 4 trips.
l-m-h3-b0c41-33.s.s1.r.a: E na 450 kg or less, but 5 trips pass 4.
l-m-h3-b0c41-33.s.s1.r.b: 4 trips carry only 96, so 4 boxes remain.
l-m-h3-b0c41-33.s.s1.r.d: 27×18=486 kg pass di safe load of 450 kg.

l-m-h3-b0c41-33.s.s2.model.1: 24 per load carry only 96 for 4 trips, and 27 na 486 kg, so each one break one condition.

l-m-h3-b0c41-34.title: To decide di mix when only 12 L of Color A dey
l-m-h3-b0c41-34.goal: For di compromise between di mixing ratio and di stock limit, consider all di conditions wey dey fight each other, choose di compromise wey suit pass, then explain di reason.
l-m-h3-b0c41-34.material: Dem must mix paint Color A and Color B 3:2 so di color no go change. Only 12 L of Color A dey for stock, and plenty Color B dey. Make as much as possible.
l-m-h3-b0c41-34.s.s1.prompt: Which option make di most while e keep di conditions?
l-m-h3-b0c41-34.s.s1.o.a: Color A 15 L + Color B 10 L (25 L)
l-m-h3-b0c41-34.s.s1.r.a: Dem no fit make am because e pass di Color A stock of 12 L.
l-m-h3-b0c41-34.s.s1.o.b: Color A 12 L + Color B 8 L (20 L)
l-m-h3-b0c41-34.s.s1.o.c: Color A 9 L + Color B 6 L (15 L)
l-m-h3-b0c41-34.s.s1.r.c: E keep di conditions, but dem fit make more.
l-m-h3-b0c41-34.s.s1.o.d: Color A 12 L + Color B 13 L (25 L)
l-m-h3-b0c41-34.s.s1.r.d: 12 : 13 no be 3 : 2, so di color go change.
l-m-h3-b0c41-34.s.s1.explain: If you match A at 12 L, B na 12÷3×2=8 L. 12:8=3:2, so dem fit make 20 L.
l-m-h3-b0c41-34.s.s2.model.0: 12:8 na 3:2, di same ratio, and e use up all 12 L of A wey dey for stock, so e make di most.
l-m-h3-b0c41-34.s.s2.model.1: A na only 12 L, so dem must set B to 12÷3×2=8 L make di ratio no change.

l-m-h3-b0c42-05.title: How we go pick so that even small region no go miss?
l-m-h3-b0c42-05.goal: As dem dey divide di sample size by region, consider all di conditions wey dey fight each other, choose di compromise wey suit pass, then explain di reason.
l-m-h3-b0c42-05.material: Pick 100 people from 800 for big city, 150 for mid-sized and small cities, and 50 for rural and fishing areas. Conditions: ① at least 10 for each region ② inside dat one, as close as possible to di population ratio (80:15:5).
l-m-h3-b0c42-05.s.s1.prompt: Which allocation (big city, mid-sized/small, rural/fishing) suit pass for di conditions?
l-m-h3-b0c42-05.s.s1.r.a: E match di ratio, but rural and fishing areas get 5 people, so e no keep ①.
l-m-h3-b0c42-05.s.s1.r.c: E keep ①, but e far from di ratio pass 75, 15, 10.
l-m-h3-b0c42-05.s.s1.r.d: E keep ①, but e too far from di population ratio.
l-m-h3-b0c42-05.s.s1.explain: 75, 15, 10, wey raise rural and fishing areas from 5 to 10 people while e reduce only di big city by 5, na di closest to di ratio.
l-m-h3-b0c42-05.s.s2.model.0: Rural and fishing areas must get at least 10, so add 5 but take 5 away only from di big city, and dat one give 75, 15, 10, di closest to di ratio.
l-m-h3-b0c42-05.s.s2.model.1: 80, 15, 5 break ①, and 34, 33, 33 and 70, 20, 10 far from di ratio pass, so 75, 15, 10 suit.

l-m-h3-b0c42-23.title: How many lunchboxes dem suppose prepare?
l-m-h3-b0c42-23.topic: How to decide with the expected value
l-m-h3-b0c42-23.goal: When demand no sure, think about all the conditions wey dey clash as you dey decide how many lunchboxes to prepare, choose the compromise wey fit pass, then explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c42-23.material: Lunchbox dey earn profit of 2000 won if dem sell am and loss of 1000 won if dem no sell am. Demand na 10 lunchboxes with probability 0.3, 20 with 0.5, and 30 with 0.2. Think about the risk of say dem no go sell together with the chance of say dem go miss out.
l-m-h3-b0c42-23.s.s1.prompt: Which number wey dem prepare give the biggest expected value?
l-m-h3-b0c42-23.s.s1.r.a: Dem always sell finish for 20000 won, but you miss the chance to sell more.
l-m-h3-b0c42-23.s.s1.r.c: The expected value na 29000 won, wey small pass wetin 20 get.
l-m-h3-b0c42-23.s.s1.r.d: The loss from leftovers big, so the expected value lower, for 27000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c42-23.s.s1.explain: The expected values by number wey dem prepare na 10: 20000 won, 20: 31000 won, 25: 29000 won, 30: 27000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c42-23.s.s2.model.0: If you find the expected value for each number wey dem prepare, 20 biggest for 31000 won, so 20 fit.
l-m-h3-b0c42-23.s.s2.model.1: 10 safe but e miss chances, and with 25 or 30 the loss from leftovers big and the expected value low, so 20 good.

l-m-h3-b0c42-29.title: How many questions the survey suppose get?
l-m-h3-b0c42-29.goal: To decide the number of survey questions, look all the conditions wey dey fight each other, choose the compromise wey fit pass, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c42-29.material: 25 questions dey wey dem must get. By number of questions, the share wey answer reach the end na 90% for 20, 85% for 25, 78% for 30, and 60% for 40. Conditions: ① put all the 25 necessary questions ② at least 80% answer reach the end.
l-m-h3-b0c42-29.s.s1.prompt: Which number of questions meet both conditions?
l-m-h3-b0c42-29.s.s1.r.a: The share wey answer high, but the 25 necessary questions no fit enter.
l-m-h3-b0c42-29.s.s1.r.c: The share wey answer na 78%, e no reach 80%.
l-m-h3-b0c42-29.s.s1.r.d: The share wey answer na 60%, e far from reach 80%.
l-m-h3-b0c42-29.s.s1.explain: 25 questions get all the necessary questions and the share wey answer na 85%, so both conditions meet.
l-m-h3-b0c42-29.s.s2.model.0: 25 questions get all the necessary questions and the share wey answer na 85%, so both conditions meet.
l-m-h3-b0c42-29.s.s2.model.1: 20 get too few questions, and for 30 and 40 the share wey answer dey lower than 80%, so 25 fit.

l-m-h3-b0c42-34.title: Where we suppose set the test cutoff?
l-m-h3-b0c42-34.goal: For the cutoff of a diagnostic test, look all the conditions wey dey fight each other, choose the compromise wey fit pass, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c42-34.material: For each cutoff, these na the number of patients wey dem miss and the number of healthy people wey test positive (false alarms). 40: 1·30, 50: 3·18, 60: 6·9, 70: 10·4. Condition: inside 5 or fewer missed, make the false alarms be the fewest.
l-m-h3-b0c42-34.s.s1.r.a: Only 1 dem miss, but the false alarms na the most at 30.
l-m-h3-b0c42-34.s.s1.r.c: False alarms na 9, but 6 dem miss, wey pass 5.
l-m-h3-b0c42-34.s.s1.explain: Cutoffs wey get 5 or fewer missed na 40 and 50, and between dem, 50 (18 false alarms) get fewer, so e fit.
l-m-h3-b0c42-34.s.s2.model.0: The only cutoffs wey keep missed to 5 or fewer na 40 and 50, and 50 get fewer false alarms at 18, so na 50.
l-m-h3-b0c42-34.s.s2.model.1: 60 and 70 miss more than 5 so dem no work, and between 40 and 50, 50 get fewer false alarms and meet both conditions, so e fit.

l-m-h3-b0c43-21.title: How many minutes early we suppose leave?
l-m-h3-b0c43-21.goal: Think about all di conditions wey dey conflict between di chance to arrive late and departure time, choose di best balance, and explain di reason.
l-m-h3-b0c43-21.material: Di time to reach school follow normal distribution with mean 25 minutes and standard deviation 5 minutes. Keep di chance of arriving late at 5% or less, and leave as late as possible. P(Z>1)=0.16, P(Z>1.6)=0.055, P(Z>2)=0.023, P(Z>3)=0.001.
l-m-h3-b0c43-21.s.s1.prompt: How many minutes before school start time you suppose leave?
l-m-h3-b0c43-21.s.s1.r.a: Di chance to arrive late na about 16%, wey pass 5%.
l-m-h3-b0c43-21.s.s1.r.b: Di chance to arrive late na about 5.5%, wey pass 5%.
l-m-h3-b0c43-21.s.s1.r.d: Di chance to arrive late low, but you go need leave earlier.
l-m-h3-b0c43-21.s.s1.explain: If you leave 35 minutes before, (35−25)÷5=2, so di chance to arrive late na about 2.3%. Among di choices of 5% or less, na di latest departure.
l-m-h3-b0c43-21.s.s2.model.0: If you leave 35 minutes before, z=2 and di chance to arrive late na about 2.3%, wey be 5% or less. Leaving 33 minutes before gives 5.5%, wey no dey allowed, so 35 minutes before na di latest choice.
l-m-h3-b0c43-21.s.s2.model.1: If you leave 30 or 33 minutes before, di chance to arrive late go pass 5%, so dem no dey allowed. Among di choices of 5% or less, di latest one, 35 minutes before, na di correct one.

l-m-h3-b0c43-22.title: How many items we suppose check from one box?
l-m-h3-b0c43-22.goal: Think about all di conditions wey dey conflict when deciding how many items to inspect for defects, choose di best balance, and explain di reason.
l-m-h3-b0c43-22.material: We wan catch box wey get 10% defect rate with probability at least 80%. Choose n items from di box, and reject di box if even one item get defect. Probability to catch am na 1−0.9ⁿ, inspection cost na 400 won for each item, and budget na 7000 won.
l-m-h3-b0c43-22.s.s1.prompt: How many items we suppose inspect to meet both conditions well?
l-m-h3-b0c43-22.s.s1.r.a: Di probability to catch am na about 65%, wey no reach 80%.
l-m-h3-b0c43-22.s.s1.r.b: Di probability to catch am na about 77%, wey no reach 80%.
l-m-h3-b0c43-22.s.s1.r.d: Di probability na about 88%, but inspection cost na 8000 won, wey pass di budget.
l-m-h3-b0c43-22.s.s1.explain: With 16 items, di probability na about 81.5% and di cost na 6400 won, so both conditions dey met. With 14 items di probability no reach, and with 20 items di cost pass di limit.
l-m-h3-b0c43-22.s.s2.model.0: With 16 items, di probability to catch am na about 81.5% and inspection cost na 6400 won, wey dey within budget, so both conditions dey met.
l-m-h3-b0c43-22.s.s2.model.1: With 10 or 14 items, di probability no reach 80%, and with 20 items e cost 8000 won, wey pass budget, so 16 items na di right number.

l-m-h3-b0c43-28.title: Where we go set the test standard?
l-m-h3-b0c43-28.topic: How to balance the two kinds of error
l-m-h3-b0c43-28.goal: Think about all the conditions wey dey fight each other for setting the test standard, pick the best compromise, and explain the reason.
l-m-h3-b0c43-28.material: The risk to conclude say effect dey when e no dey (A) and the risk to miss effect when e dey (B) different for each standard. 1: A 1%, B 30%; 2: A 5%, B 12%; 3: A 10%, B 7%; 4: A 20%, B 2%. Condition: keep A at 5% or less, and make B small as e fit be.
l-m-h3-b0c43-28.s.s1.r.a: A good at 1%, but B big pass for 30%.
l-m-h3-b0c43-28.s.s1.r.c: B small at 7%, but A na 10%, wey pass 5%.
l-m-h3-b0c43-28.s.s1.explain: The standards wey A dey 5% or less na 1 and 2, and among dem, Standard 2, wey B small pass, na the correct one.
l-m-h3-b0c43-28.s.s2.model.0: The only standards wey A dey 5% or less na 1 and 2, and among dem B small pass at 12%, so Standard 2 correct.
l-m-h3-b0c43-28.s.s2.model.1: Standards 3 and 4 no allowed because A pass 5%, and Standard 2 better pass Standard 1 because the risk to miss effect small pass.

l-m-h3-b0c43-33.material: Divide 40 scores into classes. Conditions: ① at least 4 classes ② even the smallest frequency at least 3. Width 50: 2 classes. Width 25: 4 classes, smallest frequency 4. Width 10: 10 classes, smallest frequency 1. Width 5: 20 classes, smallest frequency 0.

l-m-h3-b0c43-33.s.s1.r.c: The smallest frequency na 1, so e no meet ②.
l-m-h3-b0c43-33.s.s1.r.d: The smallest frequency na 0, so e no meet ②.
l-m-h3-b0c43-33.s.s1.explain: Only width 25 get at least 4 classes and smallest frequency of 4, wey be 3 or more.
l-m-h3-b0c43-33.s.s2.model.0: Width 25 get 4 classes and smallest frequency of 4, so e meet both conditions.
l-m-h3-b0c43-33.s.s2.model.1: Width 50 no get enough classes, and widths 10 and 5 get frequencies wey small too much, so only width 25 meet both conditions.

l-m-h3-b0c43-34.title: For sensitive survey, which method we suppose use?
l-m-h3-b0c43-34.goal: Think about all the conditions wey dey fight each other for choosing the method for sleep-time survey, pick the best compromise, and explain the reason.
l-m-h3-b0c43-34.material: Pick one method for the sleep-time survey. Conditions: ① dem no fit know names ② response rate at least 70% ③ among those, the fewest false answers. Named interview: response rate 95%, false answers 3%. Anonymous paper: 75%, 10%. Anonymous link: 82%, 6%. Anonymous survey wey take only volunteers: 40%, 4%.
l-m-h3-b0c43-34.s.s1.prompt: Which method fit the conditions best?
l-m-h3-b0c43-34.s.s1.r.a: Dem go know the names, so e no meet ①.
l-m-h3-b0c43-34.s.s1.r.b: E meet the conditions, but false answers na 10%, more than the link.
l-m-h3-b0c43-34.s.s1.o.d: Anonymous survey wey take only volunteers
l-m-h3-b0c43-34.s.s1.r.d: The response rate na 40%, so e no meet ②.
l-m-h3-b0c43-34.s.s1.explain: The ones wey meet ① and ② na the anonymous paper and the anonymous link, and among dem, the anonymous link, wey get fewer false answers, na the correct one.
l-m-h3-b0c43-34.s.s2.model.0: The only methods wey anonymous and get response rate of at least 70% na paper and the link, and among dem the link get fewer false answers at 6%, so the link correct.
l-m-h3-b0c43-34.s.s2.model.1: The named interview no anonymous and the volunteer survey get low response rate, so dem out, and you go pick the link, wey get fewer false answers than paper.

l-m-h3-b0c44-31.s.s1.r.b: The cost fit, but margin of error na about ±10 percentage points, e wide pass the target.
l-m-h3-b0c44-31.s.s1.r.c: The cost fit, but margin of error na about ±4.9 percentage points, wey pass 3 percentage points.
l-m-h3-b0c44-31.s.s1.r.d: The error small enough, but e cost 400×10,000 won, wey pass the budget.

l-m-h3-b0c44-32.title: Do survey without bias inside 3 days
l-m-h3-b0c44-32.goal: For survey method wey time limit dey conflict with fair representation, weigh all conditions wey dey conflict, choose the best balance, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c44-32.material: We need survey wetin all 600 students for the school want for after-school activity inside 3 days. Conditions: results no suppose favor one side, and response rate suppose high too.
l-m-h3-b0c44-32.s.s1.prompt: Choose the method wey go meet both conditions best.
l-m-h3-b0c44-32.s.s1.o.a: Pick 120 students by chance from school register and make dem answer during class
l-m-h3-b0c44-32.s.s1.o.b: Post link for school website and collect answers
l-m-h3-b0c44-32.s.s1.r.b: E go favor students wey volunteer, and response rate go low too.
l-m-h3-b0c44-32.s.s1.o.c: Ask 120 students wey you meet for hallway during break
l-m-h3-b0c44-32.s.s1.r.c: E go favor students for hallway, and no be everybody get chance to be chosen.
l-m-h3-b0c44-32.s.s1.o.d: Ask only the 20 class presidents, one from each class
l-m-h3-b0c44-32.s.s1.r.d: Class presidents opinion fit different from opinion of all students.

l-m-h3-b0c44-32.s.s2.model.0: Random sampling reduce bias and answering during class increase response rate, so both conditions fit.
l-m-h3-b0c44-32.s.s2.model.1: Link survey dey favor volunteers, and hallway survey give people different chance to get picked, so dem no meet the conditions; na why the first method fit.

l-m-h3-b0c44-33.title: Salary report wey short but no mislead
l-m-h3-b0c44-33.topic: Traps when people dey understand statistics
l-m-h3-b0c44-33.goal: For one way to report salary wey represent people well, weigh all the conditions wey dey conflict, choose the best balance, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c44-33.material: Among monthly salaries for 10 workers (unit na 10,000 won), 9 get 280 and 1 get 3,000. Mean na 552 and median na 280. The introduction suppose be 1 or 2 sentences, but e must tell salary of most workers and no hide say one salary high well well.

l-m-h3-b0c45-33.title: How we suppose divide di 365 days of one year?
l-m-h3-b0c45-33.goal: As you divide one new calendar into months, consider all di conditions wey clash, choose di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c45-33.material: You dey design new calendar. Conditions: ① every month get di same length, a multiple of 7, so each weekday fall on di same date every month ② one year get 365 days. Any days left after you divide am into months fit stay outside di months.

l-m-h3-b0c45-33.s.s1.r.b: 31 no be multiple of 7, and e pass 365 days.
l-m-h3-b0c45-33.s.s1.r.c: E na multiple of 7, but e short by 15 days from 365 days.
l-m-h3-b0c45-33.s.s1.o.d: 13 months of 28 days plus one day outside di months
l-m-h3-b0c45-33.s.s1.explain: 28×13=364, and one day remain. If you no put dat day for any month, both conditions fit work.
l-m-h3-b0c45-33.s.s2.model.0: 28×13=364 leave one day. If you keep dat day outside di months, both conditions fit work.
l-m-h3-b0c45-33.s.s2.model.1: 30 days×12 months na 360 days, and 31 days×12 months na 372 days; dem no fit 365 days. So 13 months of 28 days, wey be multiple of 7, na di best choice.

l-m-h3-b0c46-32.title: Tuning keyboard instrument: wetin we suppose give up?
l-m-h3-b0c46-32.goal: Weigh all conflicting conditions for tuning keyboard instrument, choose best balance, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c46-32.material: For just intonation, 5th interval for one key exactly 3:2 and sound clear, but changing to another key make intervals out of tune. 12-tone equal temperament use same ratio for every semitone, so e sound similar for all keys. Its 5th na about 1.498:1.
l-m-h3-b0c46-32.s.s1.prompt: Which method best for keyboard instrument wey play in all keys?
l-m-h3-b0c46-32.s.s1.o.a: Tune each note anyhow you like
l-m-h3-b0c46-32.s.s1.r.a: No rule for intervals, so chords no blend well.
l-m-h3-b0c46-32.s.s1.o.b: 12-tone equal temperament: fit use all keys, with small errors
l-m-h3-b0c46-32.s.s1.o.c: Just intonation tuned for one key
l-m-h3-b0c46-32.s.s1.r.c: Only that key sound clear, and e no meet condition to play all keys.
l-m-h3-b0c46-32.s.s1.r.d: After stacking 12, e no match octave exactly and e go out of tune.
l-m-h3-b0c46-32.s.s1.explain: (3/2)¹² no equal 2⁷, so if every 5th tune exactly, octave go out. Equal temperament share the small error among all notes.
l-m-h3-b0c46-32.s.s2.model.0: Condition to play all keys clash with clear intervals, so 12-tone equal temperament wey share the small error na better choice.
l-m-h3-b0c46-32.s.s2.model.1: The 5th, 1.498, almost equal 3:2, so ear hardly notice difference, and equal temperament wey fit move to any key better.

l-m-h3-b0c47-33.material: Make new calendar. Conditions: ① every month get same number of days, ② number of days in one month na multiple of 7 (so each weekday fall at same place every month), ③ number of days for one year dey closest to 365.
l-m-h3-b0c47-33.s.s1.prompt: Choose design wey meet di three conditions best.
l-m-h3-b0c47-33.s.s1.r.a: 28 na multiple of 7, but 336 days dey 29 days away from 365.
l-m-h3-b0c47-33.s.s1.r.b: 30 no be multiple of 7, so e break ②.
l-m-h3-b0c47-33.s.s1.r.c: 35 na multiple of 7, but 350 days dey 15 days away from 365.
l-m-h3-b0c47-33.s.s1.explain: Among plans wey keep ②, 364 days dey closest to 365 days.
l-m-h3-b0c47-33.s.s2.model.0: 13 months × 28 days better because 28 na multiple of 7 and 364 days only dey 1 day away from 365 days.
l-m-h3-b0c47-33.s.s2.model.1: 360 days no work because 30 no be multiple of 7, and among di remaining 336, 350, and 364 days, 364 days dey closest.

l-m-h3-b0c47-34.title: How we suppose divide 10 seats based on vote share?
l-m-h3-b0c47-34.goal: Think about all di conditions wey dey conflict when dividing 10 seats based on vote share, choose di best balance, and explain how you reason am.
l-m-h3-b0c47-34.material: Four parties win 52%, 27%, 14%, and 7% of di votes. Divide 10 seats. Conditions: ① total na 10 seats, ② every party get at least 1 seat, ③ each seat count differ from vote share×10 by less than 1 seat, ④ total of di differences must be di smallest.
l-m-h3-b0c47-34.s.s1.prompt: Choose division wey meet all four conditions.
l-m-h3-b0c47-34.s.s1.r.b: Total of di differences na 0.8+0.7+0.4+0.3=2.2. For 5, 3, 1, 1 e na 1.2.
l-m-h3-b0c47-34.s.s1.r.c: Di last party get 0 seats, so e break ②.
l-m-h3-b0c47-34.s.s1.r.d: Total of di differences na 1.8. Dat pass 1.2 for 5, 3, 1, 1.
l-m-h3-b0c47-34.s.s1.explain: Vote share×10 na 5.2, 2.7, 1.4, 0.7. For 5, 3, 1, 1, total difference na 1.2, di smallest.
l-m-h3-b0c47-34.s.s2.model.0: 5, 3, 1, 1 add up to 10, every party get at least 1 seat, and di differences add up to 0.2+0.3+0.4+0.3=1.2, di smallest, so e fit.
l-m-h3-b0c47-34.s.s2.model.1: 6, 2, 1, 1 get difference sum 2.2; 5, 2, 2, 1 get 1.8; and 5, 3, 2, 0 no work because of di 0 seats, so 5, 3, 1, 1 fit.

l-m-h3-b0c48-32.title: How many people we suppose survey?
l-m-h3-b0c48-32.goal: Think about all di conditions wey dey conflict when you decide survey size, choose most suitable balance, and explain di reason.
l-m-h3-b0c48-32.material: Every person surveyed cost 2000 won, and budget na 200,000 won (20 × 10,000). We wan keep error (roughly 1/√n) within 10 percentage points. We need decide number of people n.
l-m-h3-b0c48-32.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di most suitable number of people wey meet both conditions?
l-m-h3-b0c48-32.s.s1.r.a: E fit budget, but error na about 14 percentage points, over 10 percentage points.
l-m-h3-b0c48-32.s.s1.r.b: E fit budget, but error na about 11 percentage points, over 10 percentage points.
l-m-h3-b0c48-32.s.s1.r.d: Error small, but cost na 300,000 won (30 × 10,000), wey pass budget.
l-m-h3-b0c48-32.s.s1.explain: With 100 people, cost na 200,000 won (20 × 10,000), and error na 1/√100=10 percentage points, exactly meeting both conditions.
l-m-h3-b0c48-32.s.s2.model.0: With 100 people, 2000×100=200,000 won (20 × 10,000), and error na 10 percentage points, so both conditions dey met.
l-m-h3-b0c48-32.s.s2.model.1: Fewer people make error bigger, and more people pass budget, so 100 na di number wey meet both conditions.

l-m-h3-b0c48-33.title: Model better when e simple or when e more accurate?
l-m-h3-b0c48-33.goal: Think about all di conditions wey dey conflict when choosing model complexity, choose di most suitable balance, and explain di reason.
l-m-h3-b0c48-33.material: Predict di value for next day from data for 12 days. Error sums na 30 for line, 4 for quadratic (degree 2), and 0 for degree-11 polynomial. Degree-11 polynomial miss new values by plenty, and e complicated too. Our goal na prediction, and we must also explain am for presentation.
l-m-h3-b0c48-33.s.s1.r.a: Di error big at 30, so e miss di curved pattern.
l-m-h3-b0c48-33.s.s1.o.b: One average value: easiest to explain
l-m-h3-b0c48-33.s.s1.r.b: E no catch di trend, so you no fit use am for prediction.
l-m-h3-b0c48-33.s.s1.o.c: Quadratic (degree 2): di error small and e easy to explain
l-m-h3-b0c48-33.s.s1.o.d: Degree-11 polynomial: e fit all 12 data points perfectly
l-m-h3-b0c48-33.s.s1.r.d: E only fit di data, miss new values, and hard to explain.
l-m-h3-b0c48-33.s.s1.explain: Di best model na di simplest one wey reduce error enough, while e still fit predict and explain new values.
l-m-h3-b0c48-33.s.s2.model.0: Di degree-2 polynomial reduce di error to 4 and get few coefficients, so e fit new values well too, and dis make am suitable for both conditions.
l-m-h3-b0c48-33.s.s2.model.1: Di degree-11 polynomial fit 12 points perfectly but miss new values and hard to explain, so e hard to choose.

l-m-h3-b0c48-34.title: How many decimal places we suppose write for measurement result?
l-m-h3-b0c48-34.goal: As you choose how many digits to report for measured average, consider all di conditions wey clash, choose di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c48-34.material: Dem use tape measure wey get marks each 1cm to measure same length 10 times, and average na 12.43cm. E wrong to pretend say measurement precise pass wetin e be, but if e too rough you throw away information. Decide how to report am.
l-m-h3-b0c48-34.s.s1.prompt: Which way of reporting keep both conditions?
l-m-h3-b0c48-34.s.s1.r.a: E use digits wey much smaller than di marks, so e pretend say e precise.
l-m-h3-b0c48-34.s.s1.r.b: With tape measure marked in 1cm, you no fit trust even di second decimal place.
l-m-h3-b0c48-34.s.s1.r.d: E throw away decimal information wey average of 10 measurements give.
l-m-h3-b0c48-34.s.s1.explain: Averaging allow you trust digits smaller than one mark, but unit of 0.01cm no get meaning.
l-m-h3-b0c48-34.s.s2.model.0: Average of 10 measurements more precise than di marks, so 12cm throw information away, but hard to trust second decimal place, so 12.4cm suitable.
l-m-h3-b0c48-34.s.s2.model.1: Di marks na 1cm, so if you write up to second decimal place, you go pretend say e precise. Na why first decimal place suitable.

l-m-h3-b0c48-35.title: Choosing Number of Trials and Variables for Falling Experiment
l-m-h3-b0c48-35.goal: As you choose number of repeats and variables for falling experiment, consider all di conditions wey clash, choose di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c48-35.material: We dey investigate wing length of paper helicopter and how long e take fall. One measurement take 2 minutes, and we get 30 minutes. Keep every other condition di same except length, repeat 3 times for each length, and compare as many lengths as possible.
l-m-h3-b0c48-35.s.s1.prompt: Which plan best fit all 3 conditions?
l-m-h3-b0c48-35.s.s1.o.a: Change wing length and weight together, 3 times each
l-m-h3-b0c48-35.s.s1.r.a: If you change 2 things together, you no fit tell which one cause di effect.
l-m-h3-b0c48-35.s.s1.r.b: E take 36 minutes, wey pass 30 minutes.
l-m-h3-b0c48-35.s.s1.r.c: If you no repeat am, you no fit remove chance error.
l-m-h3-b0c48-35.s.s1.explain: 5×3=15 times, and 15×2 minutes=30 minutes, so e use all di time, change only one variable, and repeat 3 times each.
l-m-h3-b0c48-35.s.s2.model.0: E be 5×3=15 times, 2 minutes each, total 30 minutes, so e compare di most lengths within di time and still repeat dem.
l-m-h3-b0c48-35.s.s2.model.1: 6 lengths pass di time, and if you change weight too, you no go know di cause, so 5 lengths with 3 repeats each suitable.

l-m-h3-b0c49-32.title: Flower bed beside wall: choose between area and wall length
l-m-h3-b0c49-32.goal: Look at all conflicting conditions for width and length of wire-fenced flower bed, choose best balance, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c49-32.material: Make rectangular flower bed against wall using 24m wire fence. Side along wall no need fence, and length y must be at most 10m because wall. Call short side x and make bed as big as possible.
l-m-h3-b0c49-32.s.s1.prompt: Which plan (x,y) biggest and still meet both conditions?
l-m-h3-b0c49-32.s.s1.r.b: E meet conditions but much smaller.
l-m-h3-b0c49-32.s.s1.r.c: E meet conditions but smaller than (7, 10).
l-m-h3-b0c49-32.s.s1.r.d: Biggest, but y=12, pass the 10m wall length.
l-m-h3-b0c49-32.s.s1.explain: Area x(24−2x) biggest at x=6, but y≤10 mean x≥7. At x=7, area 70 na biggest allowed.
l-m-h3-b0c49-32.s.s2.model.0: x=6 give y=12, over 10, so no allowed. For x=7 or more, area biggest at x=7, giving 70, so (7, 10).
l-m-h3-b0c49-32.s.s2.model.1: Area dey shrink when x pass 6, so 7, the smallest x wey meet wall condition, na right choice.

l-m-h3-b0c49-33.material: More questions give more information, but fewer people finish answer. Dem send am to 100 people; 80% finish 10-question survey, 55% finish 20 questions, 35% finish 30, and 20% finish 40. (Information gained = responses × questions)

l-m-h3-b0c49-34.title: Wetin size class interval suppose be?
l-m-h3-b0c49-34.goal: Think about conflicting conditions for class interval in frequency table, choose best balance, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c49-34.material: The 40 data values get minimum 12 and maximum 88. For frequency table, too few classes hide shape, too many make am jagged, so 5 to 8 classes good. Classes suppose start at 10.
l-m-h3-b0c49-34.s.s1.prompt: Which class interval meet both conditions?
l-m-h3-b0c49-34.s.s1.r.a: Too many classes make am jagged.

l-m-h3-b0c49-34.s.s2.model.0: With class interval 10, there are 8 classes from 10–20 to 80–90, inside 5 to 8.
l-m-h3-b0c49-34.s.s2.model.1: 5 gives 16 classes, too many; 20 and 40 give 4 and 2, too few, so 10 fit.

l-m-h3-b0c49-35.title: Choose measurement count between average error and time
l-m-h3-b0c49-35.goal: Think about conflicting conditions for number of fall-time measurements, choose best balance and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c49-35.material: If error (standard deviation) for one timing na 2 seconds, error for average of n timings na about 2/√n seconds. You want average error 0.5 seconds or less, but one timing take 3 minutes and you get 60 minutes. Use as little time as possible.
l-m-h3-b0c49-35.s.s1.prompt: Which measurement count best meets conditions?
l-m-h3-b0c49-35.s.s1.r.a: Error na 2/3≈0.67 seconds, more than 0.5 seconds.

l-m-h3-b0c50-06.topic: Scope and conditions of a study
l-m-h3-b0c50-06.goal: Think about all di conditions wey dey conflict when deciding survey size, choose di best balance, and explain why.
l-m-h3-b0c50-06.material: 3 surveyors dey do survey for 10 weekdays. 1 person fit survey up to 10 people for one day, and for results to be trusted, sample must get at least 100 people. Target na all 900 students for school.
l-m-h3-b0c50-06.s.s1.prompt: Which plan meet all di conditions best?
l-m-h3-b0c50-06.s.s1.o.a: Survey all 900 students for di school
l-m-h3-b0c50-06.s.s1.r.a: You fit survey no more than 300 people, so e no possible.
l-m-h3-b0c50-06.s.s1.r.b: E under 100, and choosing only friends go make results biased.
l-m-h3-b0c50-06.s.s1.o.c: Survey 120 people wey dem choose randomly
l-m-h3-b0c50-06.s.s1.o.d: Survey 350 people wey dem choose randomly
l-m-h3-b0c50-06.s.s1.r.d: Maximum na 300, so e no fit finish within di period.
l-m-h3-b0c50-06.s.s1.explain: Maximum possible na 3×10×10=300 people. Di only random sample wey be at least 100 and at most 300 na 120 people.
l-m-h3-b0c50-06.s.s2.model.0: Up to 300 people possible and you need at least 100, so random sample of 120 meet both conditions and represent di school.
l-m-h3-b0c50-06.s.s2.model.1: 900 or 350 pass 300 and no possible, while 40 less than 100, so 120 most suitable.
